president of the commission. − mr president, the questions were in fact all addressed, understandably, to the prime minister and the acting presidency of the council. the right to answer those questions is a privilege i will not take away from her. let me use this minute to reiterate the need to concentrate this semester on supplementing our important efforts in terms of fiscal consolidation with growth-enhancing measures. i believe the danish presidency will be a very effective partner in this matter, in delivering pragmatically, in trying to find solutions. prime minister, you have heard parliament and i think we can say that there is broad support in this parliament for your programme. you can count on this parliament. you can also certainly count on the commission. we can therefore make this semester not a semester of more empty announcements and delay, but a semester of decisions and concrete implementation. we wish you all the best.
president-in-office of the council. − mr president of the european parliament, mr president of the european commission, leaders of the political groups, honourable members of this house, thank you very much for your remarks. it has been a real pleasure to take part in this lively debate that we have had today. what i take away from the debate today is a clear conviction that, yes, not all of us agree – i will come back to that – but also a solid and robust confirmation that we have support for the danish presidency programme and i thank you for that. we will do everything we can to live up to this support. many topics have been raised. time is limited, but allow me to address a few of the issues that you have raised. mr barroso and mr daul raised the question of the mff. we will be very serious in dealing with this during the danish presidency. i can assure you that it will be a top priority for the danish presidency to get as far as we can in terms of the multiannual financial framework. we will do that with the purpose of modernising our financial perspective and in such a way that we can use our common resources to create new jobs and new growth. in this context let me also make a remark on the financial transaction tax, which has been raised by mr callanan and others. i want to raise this to avoid any misunderstandings. the danish presidency will handle this dossier in a loyal and professional manner and as an honest broker. i am tempted also to draw attention to the wider agenda of the financial regulation, which we will intend to strengthen in our presidency. many have raised the question of hungary, namely mr verhofstadt, ms harms and mr moraes. as everyone knows, there is a debate on hungary taking place in the plenary later this afternoon. let me be brief: the commission plays a vital role as a guardian of our treaties. they have found grounds for initiating an infringement procedure on at least three counts against hungary. we must of course take that very seriously. we are in full support of the way the commission has handled this crisis. they have used what everyone is talking about today, the rules that we have, the treaties and – let us be clear – the community method. we are behind the commission in this. all member states are under the obligation to abide by our laws. that is an integral part of the way we do things in the union. many have addressed the debt crisis. the downgrading of a number of european member states underlines the need for european answers in this crisis but, before everyone decides that this is a crisis of europe, i would like to remind this house that the reason why we have a debt crisis in the european union is because member states have not watched their own budgets. this is at the core of why we have a problem. we need to focus on european solutions, but let us not forget that the reason why we have an economic crisis is because the member states did not abide by our rules. this takes me to the downgrading of some of the member states. mr verhofstadt referred to the wording and quoted, i believe, standard and poor’s. i have also noted what standard and poor’s are saying, because they were specifically referring to the lack of growth and employment perspectives in the european member states when they downgraded the countries. what they said was not said by a social democrat or the european left. standard and poor’s said that austerity also has to be followed up by growth initiatives. (applause) that brings me to the discussion about growth and employment. many have touched upon that – mr swoboda, ms harms, mr søndergaard, ms turunen, mr bendtsen, mr johansson and many other speakers. let me state very clearly that the european economies must consolidate. they need to do that and, for that reason, the danish presidency and denmark will support the fiscal compact. but let me also be very clear that it is not enough to focus on consolidation alone. we have to give a push in the right direction to growth and employment. young people all across europe are expecting that from us. we need to create european jobs now. i agree with the speakers who have suggested we go back to one of the biggest successes that the european union have had over the years: the single market. it is the internal market that has created growth and employment. that is why we want to finalise the work of the single market. therefore the president of the european council and i have agreed not to forget the issue of growth and employment. that is why we have agreed that at our meeting on 30 january 2012 we will emphasise this point and make sure that, not only do we discuss consolidation, but we also discuss growth and employment. this is what we want to do. many of you have mentioned the energy efficiency directive. mr turmes mentioned this as rapporteur and i appreciate that. i can only repeat and stress to you that, if we want to see clear results on the green agenda, we must make haste. this is an opportunity. we have a european parliament that wants to do that and we have a presidency that wants to focus on that. let us make it happen over the next six months. we can only do that if we all cooperate. (applause) many of you have addressed the question of european unity and the community method: mr daul, mr rohde and others. let me be clear, what sets europe apart is our commitment to solidarity with each other, to our unity as a union, but also to our commitment to the community method. i know that if citizens across europe are listening to this debate, they will look at us and ask what is this community method? what do they mean by the community method? i will state today that it is still worth defending because what the community method really means is that europe is no longer ruled by the strongest, but that europe is now ruled by law and democracy. friends, that is worth defending. (applause) it is worth defending not only for the smaller member states but for all of us. the community method and european unity must be an overarching goal for our endeavour. with your help, dear former colleagues, friends, honourable members of the european parliament, let us make it happen, let us work together and let us produce some tangible, real results for our european citizens. i am convinced that we can do that. if we do, we will also create a path out of the european crisis to a more prosperous future. (applause)

the author. − if we speak of the european union as an association of equal states, then this is the policy of equality that we should consistently pursue. direct payments to farmers producing agricultural products in the european union cannot be 2, 3 or even 4 times different, because it is precisely these differences that program problems that will never bring us to a balance in the food supply chain. costs in the food production and supply chain are increasing for a variety of reasons: increased requirements in phytosanitary, animal welfare, environmental, hygiene and food safety, all of which are the same in all member states. however, the different levels of payments in the european union countries push food producers into a situation where fair competition is not possible, as in mars. another important issue to be addressed is that the food market is currently dominated by large distribution companies and that prices paid to farmers in the food supply chain are constantly being lowered. meanwhile, production costs continue to rise. farmers do not receive sufficient income from their produce, and large commercial monopolies make huge profits at the expense of farmers. the large difference between the price paid to farmers and the final price paid by consumers, as well as the lack of transparency, the disparity in the competitive conditions and, in some cases, the abuse in the food supply chain, make it unprofitable to engage in agricultural activities and put farmers' survival at serious risk. i believe that the first task for the commission and the member states today is to ensure that the rules of competition, operating on the basis of the principle of equal treatment, are respected at all stages of the food chain, both at the level of the suppliers and at the level of the consumers.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. food waste has reached such levels that it can be considered a global problem. since the 1970's, the world's population has increased by over 50 percent. food is wasted everywhere - in the fields during harvest, in the processing industry and, most importantly, in the homes of consumers. in this unholy rivalry, europe and north america are undeniably the leaders. people on both continents waste up to 115 kg of food per person per year. in the european union alone, the figure is even higher. according to the european commission's statistics, the average european throws away 179 kg of food, which amounts to some 89 million tonnes of irreversibly wasted food per year. it is not overproduction of food, as is commonly believed, that is the main cause of food waste and consequently of hunger, but poor stock management and misguided marketing strategies aimed solely at maximizing profits. however, the biggest impact on waste growth seems to be the use of a single 'use by' date on the labels. manufacturers should be encouraged to include two particulars, with one additional: 'use for'. the term 'use before' refers to the quality of the product, while the term 'use after' refers to its safety. this will help consumers make informed choices and, most importantly, prevent food that is still fit to eat from being thrown away.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report, which is a technical adjustment to the provisions on airport transit visas. as indicated in the submission, this adjustment will not change the practice of eu member states. the european parliament's present report therefore only proposes technical amendments, since the amendment to the regulation provides for the exemption from the requirement to hold an airport transit visa for third-country nationals who hold a valid visa or a valid residence permit issued by a member state which does not (yet) apply all the provisions of the schengen acquis (united kingdom, ireland, cyprus, bulgaria and romania). the european parliament considers that such an adjustment is logical, as it is pointless to check a person who already has a visa or residence permit again if this person has already been checked before and has been found not to pose a risk of illegal immigration. in addition, the proposal should also reduce the administrative burden on member states.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i consider it inappropriate and unnecessary to repeat the control procedures on a third-country national who already has a valid visa or residence permit, since it has already been established during the initial check that he does not pose a risk of illegal immigration. in addition, in order to ensure legal certainty and transparency and the effective application of the provisions on airport transit visas, the exemptions from the requirement to hold an airport transit visa must be clearly and unambiguously laid down and applied in accordance with strict requirements. it is also very important to underline that the new provisions of this regulation will benefit not only individual travellers and air carriers but also member states, as they will reduce the administrative burden.

in writing. - i voted for this document. international air links between member states and third countries have traditionally been established by bilateral air services agreements. in 2002, the court of justice of the eu ruled that national appointment clauses in bilateral agreements were in breach of eu law. they shall allow a third party to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisation or the authorisation of an air carrier designated by a member state but not majority owned by that member state or its national entity and not effectively controlled by them. this was seen as discrimination against eu air carriers which are established in one member state but owned and controlled by another member state. the commission has negotiated an agreement to replace certain provisions in the existing 19 bilateral air services agreements between the eu member states and indonesia. the aim of this agreement is to ensure that all eu air carriers can benefit from air routes between the relevant eu member states and indonesia without discrimination and to prohibit anti-competitive activities.

in writing. − the objective of the memorandum of cooperation is to shape and strengthen relations and cooperation between the eu and the international civil aviation organisation (icao). it was signed in montreal on 28 april 2011 and in brussels on 4 may 2011 and has been provisionally applied since then. the icao was established by the 1944 chicago convention as a specialized agency of the united nations. its 190 current member states cooperate in the fields of aviation safety, aviation security, air traffic management and environmental protection. most icao standards and requirements are taken into account in eu legislation or even substantially transposed into european law (e.g. aircraft environmental standards). the eu therefore has a strong interest in contributing to the icao policy-making process, in particular with a view to the competitiveness of its own civil aviation industry. i supported the conclusion of a memorandum which will ensure greater harmonisation of standards, better coordination of the relevant actions and better use of limited resources.

in writing. - i voted for this document. biocidal products are necessary for the eradication of organisms harmful to human or animal health and organisms which damage natural or manufactured products. directive 98/8/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 16 february 1998 concerning the placing of biocidal products on the market ('the directive') establishes a harmonised system for the authorisation and placing on the market of biocidal products and for the establishment and regulation of the list of active substances authorised for use in biocidal products. the provisions of the directive require that, seven years after its entry into force, the commission draw up a report and submit it to the council. the review of the application of the directive has shown that the simplified procedure provided for in the directive has no real impact on the evaluation of active substances, in particular those used in low-risk biocidal products, and that the data requirements and provisions on the non-requirement of data may be unclear or inconsistent or, in certain cases, may be disproportionately burdensome. the new regulation aims to improve the existing regulatory framework without compromising the high level of protection of the environment and human and animal health, to ensure the free movement of biocidal products on the union market and to reduce the administrative burden on companies and public authorities.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because of the recent volatility in food and basic commodity prices, the growing concern about the functioning of european and global food supply chains, and the increased uncertainty about farmers' incomes and long-term investment. in addition, the income problem for farmers continues to deepen and the price consumers pay for their products is not reflected in the price farmers pay for their production, which prevents farmers from investing and innovating, which may lead to the decision of most farmers to leave agriculture. the imbalance problem in the food supply chain is therefore of european importance and requires specific measures at european level. attention should be paid to the fact that agricultural policy must enable small and medium-sized farms, including family farms, to earn a decent income, to produce sufficient quantities of food of appropriate quality at affordable prices, to create jobs, to promote rural development and to ensure environmental protection and sustainability. the european parliament therefore calls on national and european competition authorities and other regulators of production and trade to take action against the abuse of buyer power by dominant wholesalers and retailers, which systematically puts farmers at a very disadvantage in negotiations.
in writing. − there are several weak links in the food supply chain that need to be addressed more seriously. while the consumer's interest in safe products is already, so to speak, protected by the various legislation on product labelling, the price-fixing aspects are not yet favourable to either the consumer or the producer. one of the elements of eu competition policy is the regulation of entities in a monopoly or dominant position, ensuring the functioning of the free market. on the other hand, such regulation should not lead to a return to the days of price regulation. i therefore support the resolution in principle, but i think that there is still a long way to go before legislation is adopted in this area.
in writing. - i support this resolution because only joint efforts can eliminate imbalances in the food supply chain. in particular, it is necessary to ensure fair and transparent relations between food producers, suppliers, processors and distributors and to establish an effective regulatory mechanism. it is essential that farmers are paid fair and profitable prices for agricultural products and that the highest profit margins for large trading centres are established. this will promote the fair distribution of added value in the food supply chain. i support the proposal that the commission should maintain the system of production quotas, which must be adapted to the needs of each country.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's contribution to the development of the european union's space policy, which is one of the most important areas of eu industrial policy. the european space industry generates a consolidated turnover of eur 5.4 billion and employs more than 31 000 highly qualified people. it is estimated that 6-7% of gdp in the west (around eur 800 billion in the european union) is currently dependent on satellite navigation, which requires the creation of a legal and institutional environment for space policy to continue to develop successfully in the european union, and space services markets are growing rapidly. in its report, parliament proposes that the commission should clarify and include the assessment of the technical feasibility and the associated costs and benefits of all space programmes. it is also necessary to establish a clear governance of space policy with effective monitoring and coordination mechanisms in order to align priorities and resources from national funds and the european union. in its report, parliament also asks the commission to complement the legal and financial framework of the galileo programme appropriately, in particular by establishing the multiannual financial perspective for 2014-2020.
in writing. − i support this resolution on the creation of a space strategy for the european union that is beneficial to citizens and that would contribute to the establishment of the objectives of the eu's digital agenda. space is a source of growth and innovation, contributing to increased prosperity and opening up opportunities to meet the eu's socioeconomic and security needs. in this context, space policy must be real policy, and therefore awareness of the importance of space must be increased. europe must also preserve its independence in the use of space. i believe that support for european space infrastructure and research needs to be strengthened. it is also essential to ensure that the european space programme focuses on those areas which provide the greatest added value for europe as a whole.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. every year, more and more healthy and edible food is lost throughout the food supply chain in europe (some estimates put the figure as high as 50%). according to a study published by the commission, some 89 million tonnes or 179 kg of food waste per capita are generated each year in the 27 member states. in the european union, 79 million people still live below the poverty line. i agree that more investment is needed in ways to reduce food waste, to reduce the losses suffered by agri-food businesses and to reduce food prices, thereby improving access to food for poorer populations. in order to ensure a high level of consumer protection, member states should be able to take appropriate measures to ensure that the use of such products is not disproportionate to the risks posed by the products concerned. the commission should also identify measures and actions to encourage greater involvement of agri-food businesses, wholesale markets, shops, distribution networks, public and private catering establishments and restaurants, public administrations and non-governmental organisations in the fight against food waste.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the first important step in the fight against hunger in the world is to reduce food waste, to address the problems of the growth in demand forecast by the food and agriculture organisation (fao) and to improve the nutritional level of the population. every year, more and more healthy and edible food is wasted throughout the food supply chain in europe, and in some cases, even after food reaches the consumer, it becomes waste. food waste also has ethical, economic, social and nutritional consequences, as well as health and environmental consequences, as food waste contributes to global warming and food waste produces methane gas, which is 21 times more greenhouse gas-intensive than carbon dioxide. the european parliament therefore calls on the council, the commission, the member states and the actors in the food supply chain to urgently address the problem of food waste throughout the supply and consumption chain and to establish guidelines and support ways of improving the efficiency of the food supply chain in each sector. the european parliament also calls on the commission to assess and support advance measures to reduce food waste at the beginning of the chain, such as labelling with two expiry dates (sell by and consume by ) and selling expired or damaged products at a lower price.
in writing. − food depletion in the developed world and food scarcity in the developing world are both topical and closely interrelated issues. the european union, one of the most developed regions in the world, with its overproduction-promoting common agricultural policy, is also, unfortunately, a major contributor to the fact that a large proportion of food products do not reach those who need them most, but are thrown away or otherwise destroyed. we propose to address the problem by developing strategies and concrete measures. but i suggest that we start with ourselves -- spend twice as much time in the grocery store next time, but think twice about whether we're actually going to use this or that product instead of throwing it away when it's expired.
in writing. - i support this resolution because food waste is a global problem and a food waste chain has already developed alongside food production. to address this problem, strategies for improving the efficiency of the food chain must be developed at eu level. the fight against food waste must be a priority on the eu's political agenda. in this context, it is necessary to increase the efficiency of the food chain, raise public awareness and information. i believe that the commission should assess as soon as possible the possibilities of a coercive policy on food waste and set specific food waste prevention targets. i support the proposal that, in the context of public procurement rules for catering and hotel services, priority should be given to those undertakings which ensure the free distribution of unused products. in addition, low-income consumers must be able to buy high-quality food at lower prices.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, first of all i would like to thank the house for a very lively, interesting debate which raised a lot of new ideas. i think it underlies the clear sentiment that this summit was very important and crucial because, after a certain period of time, the primary focus was on growth. it was very important for us to address the greatest concern of our citizens, which is growth and employment, in this way. of course a very important element of the summit was to continue our work on guaranteeing stronger economic and fiscal governance. i would like to use this opportunity to thank parliament’s negotiators, mr verhofstadt, mr gualtieri and mr brok, for an excellent job and for the good cooperation with the european commission. coming back to the outcome of the summit – and i believe mr van rompuy would testify to this – i think there was a consensual approach to the discussion on growth and to the importance of growth and of streamlining our policy to achieve that goal. i cannot agree with those who believe that we can create new jobs by dismantling the european social model. we had such a situation here in europe in the 17th and 18th centuries; let us not go back, please. as regards the focus on youth, i think that the measures adopted during the european council to help our young generation – those 7.5 million young people who are not employed, not in education and not in training – are absolutely crucial. action on this is immediate: letters have been sent to the eight member states, the joint action teams will meet in february, funds are mobilised and these new job plans for the young generation should be debated by the european spring council. i believe we cannot act any faster; what we need is your support and good cooperation from the member states. turning to the very important issue of economic and fiscal governance, i think it was quite clear from this debate, and i think this is echoed by the european council, that we cannot have consolidation without growth. last year we were very much breaking new ground when we were trying to save the euro; trying to save the european monetary union. now we are moving beyond that. we see a certain stabilisation. we can focus on growth, which will bring hope to many families in the european union. there is one thing which it is important to underline. when i was listening to the debate some of the speakers were describing the outcome in much bleaker terms than it really deserved. i think that parliament and the commission acting together have been instrumental in upholding the community method and guaranteeing that the european parliament would be involved in economic governance, that the european institutions would be central in economic governance, that we will have no new european institutions and that this treaty will be incorporated in european law within five years. i think these are very important positive gains and we should look at them in this positive light. some very quick remarks on the specific questions. i absolutely agree with mr daul as regards the importance of the services directive. the full implementation of this directive would increase trade in commercial services by 45%. it would increase foreign direct investment by 20%. it can bring about an increase of 0.5 to 1.5% in gdp. where else can we find such an easy potential for growth? it is lamentable that this directive is not yet in operation; we have started infringement procedures against the remaining two member states which have yet to transpose it correctly. mr verhofstadt mentioned patents. i can assure you that this was highlighted very forcefully by me in the general affairs council and also by the president of the commission in the european council. it is true that, having the chance to decrease costs by 80%, we should do it as soon as possible. we have been discussing the patent for decades, and i am pleased that we now have a deadline and that we should definitely solve this issue before the june european council. i would plead with the three countries which cannot agree where the seat will be to find a solution, because our innovation community, our scientists, are really waiting for it. as regards mr swoboda’s comment on the financial transactions tax and mr verhofstadt’s comments on the eurobonds, the financial transaction tax is a very important proposal. i would like to assure you that the commission is not going to give up. we had one difficult political debate on this issue and it was definitely not conclusive but, if we gave up after each difficult political debate at council level, there would be no european law. we are going to continue and we will need your support. i believe that in the end, in all member states, they will realise how useful this measure can be, the kind of fair burden-sharing it could bring from the financial sector, and the kind of healthy regulatory effect it could have on the financial industry. i believe in rational arguments and these arguments are very rational. i believe they will prevail. as regards eurobonds and stability bonds, you know that the commission believes that this is an excellent stabilising and investment tool and a very good instrument. i think this was clearly shown in our options paper and now we see that the discussion is ongoing. it is very difficult, but i believe that these new efforts in fiscal consolidation will actually increase mutual confidence among the member states in how responsible we are in managing our public finances. i personally believe that we will see the day when we will use the eurobonds, the stability bonds, as a very important financial and investment tool in the european union. coming to the last piece of information: co-financing. i agree with mr verhofstadt that this is a very important tool in helping countries in distress. as you probably know, we have already increased the co-financing rate from 75% to 85% – at first temporarily for latvia, greece, portugal and romania and we did something similar for ireland. now we have increased it even further: 95% in the case of greece. moreover we are helping the greek authorities to better absorb these funds on the ground.
the european council - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as i said in my introduction, growth and employment policy is a policy at different levels. there is the short term, there is the long term, there is the economic aspect, there is the aspect which is purely a matter of employment policy, there is what can be done at the level of the member states, there is what can be done at the level of the union. as far as the short term is concerned, i hope i shall be brief. firstly, we must not forget that we are, of course, experiencing a period of stagnation, of recession, but that we are coming out of two years of positive growth of about 2% in the euro zone and indeed throughout the union. we tend to forget that and think that the period we have left behind is a recession. this is not the case, despite the consolidation efforts that have been made on average. of course, there are countries that are under programmes and those that are subject to market pressure. but, overall, when i average out the years 2010 and 2011 as good for growth and employment. in a country i know better than others, belgium, we even created 100,000 jobs in 2010 and 2011. we lost 7,000 in the crisis year of 2009. even this year, 2012, growth is positive. i know there are problems in a lot of countries and in a lot of regions. but i also want to emphasize that we have also had positive developments in the last two years. for short-term growth, the most important thing we can do - everyone agrees on this - is to foster renewed confidence in the euro area. if confidence returns to the euro area, consumers and businesses will have more confidence and that will lead to more economic growth. we saw in 2009, once confidence returned, once confidence in the banks was restored, there was a renewed economic growth and an increase in employment. so we have to work on that. the last few months have not been as catastrophic as some people try to make out. for example, the spreads relative to germany have decreased substantially for italy and spain: 1.6 for spain and portugal compared to the highest level of the spread a few months ago. i'm not saying we've reached the goal, i'm just saying there's a positive turnaround. i am not even mentioning ireland where there is a decrease compared to the bund - there is about 7%. is that enough? no, you can't! is there a turning point? i know! i hope we will continue along this path. in the short term, spending more and increasing deficits is not the answer. this is not the answer, we tried it, we failed. even outside the european union, those who have practised this policy of fiscal stimulus must now return to a more orthodox policy. and even under the golden rule, if there is a small deficit that can be tolerated, it is a structural deficit. so there is room for manoeuvre: it is structural, it is not nominal or a deficit of 0.5% at any time. there's an appreciation and there's this structural effect that we have to take into account. in the short term, every disadvantage has an advantage, the recent depreciation of the euro is a help to our exports and there are even studies that prove that this can happen very quickly. in the long term, there is the europe 2020 strategy. we don't care, we compare it to the lisbon strategy. i believe that now we are taking it very seriously and have integrated the europe 2020 strategy into the european semester and the six-pack. there is also a much stronger commitment from this parliament than in the past to work on this. we also have commitments for employment in the euro plus pact. of course, all this must be carried out. but i think we have made all the arrangements necessary to make this long-term strategy a success this time. i share your disappointment about the european patent. i look at it but it's my character from a perspective that has positive elements. i started my political career with a prime minister in the 1970s who said: 'we have not succeeded in reaching agreement on the european patent at the european council.' i'm talking about the year 1978. we are now much later and, under the belgian presidency, and even with a minister for economic affairs whom some know better than others, we have managed to make a breakthrough through enhanced cooperation. now we have to take the final step; it will take a few weeks, but i am sure that the danish presidency - and we are helping it a lot - will find a solution to this problem. as regards the social aspect, the specific employment policy, it must be recognized that a great deal can be done at european level. we can work in the single market. we can mobilise european funds, and we are doing so: we have reduced the co-financing rate, and the vice-president of the commission has done well to mention this. so we can do all of this, there are project bonds, but we have to admit that the biggest work has to be done at the national level. we can influence national governments and parliaments. we can encourage them. we can ask for commitments. in some ways, they can even be punished. all this is planned in the european semester. but the bulk of the work has to be done by national governments and parliaments, otherwise we cannot explain the difference between germany, austria, the netherlands and some other parts of europe in terms of unemployment rates. for example, for young people, the rate may be quite low, around 8%, while in other cases it approaches 50%. there are huge differences which are due to the policy that has been pursued in the past. what we are going to do now is to encourage national governments and member states to follow the good examples, including the austrian example, through financial and other incentives. the commission's recommendations will be very important and our conclusions in the european council are in that direction. i won't belittle them as much as some have. so there is this economic side and this social side and of course, as i have just mentioned, what can be done at the level of the union and what can be done at the level of the member states. as regards the treaty, ladies and gentlemen, when i compare everything that was said before it was concluded with what is now being said, i think we have done a good job. we have worked well with the help of many people, including and especially in this parliament. a great deal of work has been done to integrate this intergovernmental treaty into the philosophy of the european union treaties. we must make an effort - it will be the task of our successors, at any rate of mine - to incorporate this treaty into the treaty itself as such within a few years. we have also made sure that there is more coherence in the european union. at one point, some felt that we were heading towards a two-speed europe. we got a deal for 25. unfortunately, not 27, but 25, which means that there are eight countries outside the euro zone that have shown solidarity with those who have a common currency. and we have reached an agreement that those who are not in the euro zone, but who ratify the treaty, can participate in key moments in the deliberations of the euro zone summits and of course be associated with all the subjects that are agreed in the treaty. the cohesion of the union has thus been safeguarded as far as possible. once again, when i compare what was said before the negotiations and listen carefully to what is now being said about the treaty, we have come a long and interesting way, and i am glad of that.
in writing. it is now more important than ever what message the european parliament will send to the half billion people in the european union (eu). we must show a united position in the european parliament's resolution on the conclusions of this week's european council. i think we have to advocate for saving wisely, for the efficient use of eu funds, but it is very important to stress that saving alone will not help to overcome the eu crisis. it is also worth noting that in some member states, the excessive use of funds has led to an even greater increase in poverty and social exclusion in recent years. in some member states, the response has been emigration, especially among young people. in the european parliament we must stress that the crisis can only be overcome by promoting economic growth, increasing employment, supporting small and medium-sized enterprises and other concrete measures. unfortunately, at this week's european council, the declaration on growth and jobs was relegated to the background, as the focus was on institutional matters and disagreements between some member states over a crossborder agreement on the treaty. we must be in favour of not dividing the eu into euro-zone and non-euro-zone countries, because that is how we divide the community, people's trust in the european union as a united, responsible and solidary community.

mr president, i welcome the eu decision to place an embargo on iranian oil imports, ban new contracts and freeze iranian central bank assets, because the recent eu decision, coupled with existing american measures, will come close to imposing the ‘crippling sanctions’ referred to by the us secretary of state, hillary clinton. it is important to note that the eu, as a block, is iran’s second largest customer, taking about a quarter of iranian exports. the latest set of eu and us sanctions goes beyond targeting the persons and institutions involved in the nuclear programme. hopefully those sanctions will achieve their aim, but more important is that the eu member states are perfectly aware of the possible consequences and that the respective governments are prepared to deal with them. the european parliament, in its resolution, makes a strong statement in support of the eu’s dual-track approach for the negotiations with iran, which offers both rewards and punishments. what is clear is that we are far away from trusting the current iranian regime and, at the same time, we would wish iran to become a country like japan, which has the capability to become a nuclear power quickly if need be, but which has rejected taking the final steps to possessing nuclear weapons. finally, in this context, what could give negotiations and diplomacy a chance is the ever-changing situation in iran and in the region, including the move towards democracy in the middle east.
we often say that the european union lacks a unified voice in foreign policy, so it is really very gratifying that european member states, which are experiencing economic difficulties and importing iranian oil, have been able to reach an agreement and decide on broader sanctions against iran. this is a serious signal to the iranian government first and foremost. the iranian regime's verbal claims that its atomic weapons are peaceful are unfounded and unconvincing. meanwhile, the european union's policy remains one of duplicity, leaving it up to the iranian authorities to impose further constraints on the country's economic development. the primary objective of sanctions is to ensure that a substantial threat to global security and regional stability in the middle east is eliminated. it is a pity that some countries with global ambitions are unable to transcend narrow national interests and take a stand for global security - i am talking about russia and china. however, i think we need to set very clear conditions and criteria for the lifting of the sanctions announced.
on behalf of the ecr group. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the increasing political and economic importance of brazil, russia, india, china and south africa requires the development of a coherent and effective union policy towards those countries. it should not be based on our fears or our fear of the emergence of new powers, but on cooperation and mutual trust. relations with the bric countries should be based on a real partnership, but also, and importantly, on shared values. the union must take due account of the new political and economic importance of the emerging powers in order to maintain its own international standing. for these reasons, several of the priorities in mr saryusz-wolski's report need to be highlighted and supported. the concept of bilateral strategic partnerships with each of these countries will strengthen the union's position. the renewed partnership with brazil on the basis of the eu-mercosur association, which will be the most important agreement signed by the union so far, should be supported. brazil can also be a great example for us to build energy self-sufficiency by supporting the production of biofuels. the role of the strategic partnership with russia in promoting peace and security in europe should also be emphasised. finally, i would like to express the hope that the union will properly appreciate the importance of china as a major economic power of the future and take the lead in engaging with china in order to revive the economy of our continent.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. energy services affect all aspects of people's lives and livelihoods. without free access to these services, societies are forced to live in poverty. about 1.3 billion people in the world have no access to electricity. this is a big problem in the third world. but there is another problem, affecting the people of the european union itself, and especially its new member states, which is limited access to electricity because of its high price. this is particularly true in rural areas, which is why it is so important to strengthen the eu energy fund to support marginalised rural areas and dispersed households. the promotion of and investment in renewable energy sources should become the main union action in this area. the goal is clear: to provide affordable energy services to the poor, especially in rural areas. in central and eastern europe, including countries such as lithuania, many hectares of land are uncultivated. by supporting biofuel energy initiatives, we would have a triple benefit: cheaper energy, a return to agricultural production and a reduction in unemployment by creating new jobs in the agricultural sector. the union should develop clear guidelines on the criteria for financing and supporting the production of biofuels and alternative energy sources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu foreign policy towards brics which makes recommendations, identifying key areas of reform, where the eu could seek to streamline its action and institutional architecture and thereby increase its potential and effectiveness as a global actor. i agree with the rapporteur that the overall coordination of eu foreign policy towards the brics and other emerging powers should be ensured by the commission, that better linking of foreign and security policy with eu sectoral policies should be implemented by the following actions: increasing the participation of the ep in bilateral summits between the eu and its strategic partners, increasing the role of the brics in international development policy that better reflects their share in global gdp, strengthening the strategic dialogue between eu and usa on global governance and reform of international organisations. we, members of european parliament, conclude that the eu should take into account the new weight in political and economic terms of the brics and other emerging powers and use its political leverage to continue promoting universal values in the looming new multi-polar system of global governance and be at the forefront of the process of reform of the international governance system.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the growing demographic gap between the west and the brics and other emerging market economies in the near future threatens to change the established balance of power in the international arena and the very system of global governance. the seven emerging market economies (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, mexico and turkey) are projected to have larger economies than all the g7 countries (the united states, japan, canada, the united kingdom, germany, france and italy) by 2050. china is projected to become the world's largest economy by gross domestic product by 2020 and india could become the world's fastest growing economy by 2050. these countries will become increasingly important economically and politically on the international stage, especially in addressing global challenges such as the fight against climate change, international terrorism, the distribution of resources and rare earths, global political stability, etc. the eu needs to strengthen cooperation with the brics and other emerging market economies in the global governance framework and in international organisations. i agree with what needs to be considered at eu level, how to increase the role, influence and voting power of the eu in international forums and how to achieve smoother coordination and a more coherent position among eu member states in these forums.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the european union must define a common foreign policy objective and strategy for regions with rapid economic development, such as the so-called brics countries (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, mexico and turkey). on the basis of current data, brics economic growth is projected to continue strong and even surpass the g7 (the united states, japan, canada, the united kingdom, germany, france and italy) combined by 2050. the european union will therefore have to take due account in the conduct of its foreign policy in the future of the new economic and political strength of these emerging market economies and to act as one strong political and economic entity. this is particularly important if, as a region of the world, we are to continue to lead the reform of international governance and play a key role in finding a global solution to transnational challenges such as climate change, access to raw materials and rare earth metals, terrorism and global political stability and security.
in writing. − in 2050, the economies of the seven emerging market economies (brazil, russia, india, china, indonesia, mexico and turkey) will be larger than the combined economies of the g7 (usa, japan, canada, uk, germany, france and italy). it is projected that china will become the world's largest economy by gdp by 2020 and india may become the fastest growing economy by 2050. i supported this document because addressing international challenges such as climate change, global governance issues, access to raw materials and rare minerals, terrorism, the fight against radical non-state movements, sustainable development, global political stability and security will require a rules-based, integrative approach based on partnership, shared values and common consensus, comprehensive consultation and cooperation with new emerging market economies. efficient solutions to international problems will have to be found through concerted efforts. i also agree that the eu can and should take the initiative in this area.
in writing. − universal values such as human rights and freedoms must be and remain the central dimension of international relations and global structures. in the context of changing global economic and political realities, the european union must take a leading role and promote the strengthening of universal values in the emerging multilateral system of international relations by developing bilateral and multilateral relations with the brics countries based on democracy, mutual respect and shared values. growing economic power allows for the creation of additional poles of power in the global system, but increasing political and economic weight also means increasing global responsibilities. it is important that these countries choose the path of cooperation, rather than confrontation, in addressing issues of global security, stability and prosperity. the eu can and must contribute to creating a world of tomorrow where no one doubts that they are supporting a tyrant or a murderer.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which sets out the eu's foreign policy objectives and future strategy towards brics and other rapidly developing countries. the rules-based approach to integration and continued and constructive cooperation with new emerging market economies are needed to address the current and pressing global challenges. it should be noted that the eu's foreign policy must take into account and assess the interests and role of each individual brics country, rather than the collective interests of these countries as a group of countries. in addition, in order to reform financial and economic governance institutions globally and contribute to the consolidation of the multilateral order, the eu needs to strengthen its political dialogue with the brics countries and to better align its policies with the us.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution where the ep recommends to the council a consistent policy towards regimes against whom the eu applies restrictive measures when their leaders exercise their personal and commercial interests for their personal wealth within eu borders. i agree with the rapporteur on the proposed clearer criteria for eu sanctions, in order to enhance the consistency, transparency and credibility of their application. i also agree that an annual report should be made on the implementation of sanctions, the european parliament should be fully and regularly associated in the review process and the evaluation of sanctions should be done in dialogue with the people and civil society organisations of the targeted countries, with the aim of developing and strengthening the respect for democracy and human rights. the eu member states would have to declare when persons on sanctions lists have physical or financial assets within their borders, to apply financial sanctions or restrictive measures in case of any financial intervention. we, members of european parliament, believe that measures clearly targeted to the accountable regimes and eu coordinated action will strive to minimise the adverse impact on the civil population, in particular the most vulnerable.
in writing. - i voted for the report. it is estimated that over the past two decades, more than $150 billion (u.s.) has been taken out of north africa - algeria, morocco, and tunisia. the application of sanctions or restrictive measures, such as arms embargoes, trade sanctions, financial and economic sanctions, account freezes, flight bans, admission restrictions, diplomatic sanctions, boycotts of sporting and cultural events and suspensions of cooperation with third countries, can only be effective if they are applied jointly at eu level. disagreement between member states often leads to inconsistent application of restrictive measures, which undermines the credibility of the eu and adversely affects the effectiveness of these measures. i agree with the european parliament's recommendations that an effective eu-wide sanctions policy should be developed by establishing clear criteria for the application of sanctions, with clear objectives, the form and guidelines for the assessment of the sanctions to be applied and a review procedure, which would allow for improved cooperation and interaction between member states and ensure that no double standards are applied when deciding on restrictive measures or sanctions.
in writing. − the european union is attractive to many authoritarian leaders and those associated with them as a source of investment, wealth, banking and healthcare, and as a place where they enjoy the freedom to travel and spend their often dubiously earned money. i voted in favour of the document because decisions on sanctions should be taken by the eu only after a full assessment of how democratic change can be most effectively achieved in the country concerned, and each decision should be duly justified. sanctions themselves should be used only to influence the elite responsible for repressive or criminal regimes and the responsible non-state actors in failed states and to ensure that restrictive measures and sanctions are not applied inaccurately, are proportionate to the objective pursued and minimise the negative impact on the civilian population, in particular the most vulnerable. it is therefore necessary to improve cooperation and interaction between the 27 eu member states in this area, and we must speak with one voice and in a consistent manner.
in writing. − the eu must strengthen the effectiveness and coherence of restrictive measures and sanctions against authoritarian regimes, while maintaining flexibility. it is necessary to ensure that the impact of these measures on ordinary citizens is minimised. this requires common criteria and standards for the imposition and removal of sanctions. the effectiveness of restrictive measures will be enhanced by the full involvement of both countries belonging to the european economic area and countries seeking eu membership. the application of sanctions should also be binding on all persons and entities, including third-country persons and entities, operating on the eu market and on eu nationals and economic operators operating outside the eu. i believe that the immediate publication of all such cases would have a major preventive effect in discouraging the access of representatives of authoritarian and criminal regimes to the european union market, financial institutions and structures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu must pursue a consistent policy towards regimes subject to restrictive measures. first, it is essential to ensure that every decision taken by the eu is properly reasoned. in addition, clear and precise criteria for the application of restrictive measures and an effective sanctions policy must be established. each restrictive measure and sanction shall be applied in a targeted and proportionate manner, following a detailed analysis of the economic and social situation in the country concerned. it should be noted that a coherent policy towards authoritarian regimes must be pursued not only outside the eu but also within the eu. in this respect, a special role is assigned to the member states, which must ensure that restrictive measures are effectively applied against the leaders of authoritarian regimes when they pursue their personal and commercial interests within the eu.
in writing. - colleagues, the eu must learn from its mistakes. there have been many examples - some of which are mentioned in this report - of leaders of ruthless dictatorships who have increased their wealth by helping other eu member states. what's even more shocking is that it's been done so openly for so long. for example, the gaddafi regime was valued at billions of dollars in assets across the eu, particularly private property in the uk. the assets of egyptian president hosni mubarak and his family amounted to almost $70 million, most of which was invested by the eu and the us. at the very least, there is an urgent need to strengthen restrictive measures against recognised authoritarian regimes by targeting their personal and commercial activities in the eu. i agree with the main point of the report that we need a coherent policy towards authoritarian regimes. but we must go further. we also need a consistent policy towards those member states which break the rules. last week, human rights watch released a report condemning the eu and its member states for showing a reluctance to address human rights abuses within the eu, despite speaking out about the importance of human rights and freedoms during the arab spring.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution requesting the commission to submit swiftly a proposal for a directive on the cross-border transfer of company seats. currently, there is a lack of consistency in legislation on procedures for transferring the registered office or real head office of an existing company from one member state to another within the single market. the transfer of company seats is often accompanied by administrative difficulties, high costs, social implications and the lack of legal certainty. we, members of the european parliament, agree that the process within the eu should be harmonised, the directive should apply to limited liability companies and allow companies to exercise their right of establishment by migrating to a host member state without losing their legal personality. the transfer should not circumvent legal, social and fiscal conditions. any company against which proceedings for winding-up, liquidation, insolvency or suspension of payments or other similar proceedings have been brought should not be allowed to undertake a cross-border transfer of seat. this legal harmonisation will strengthen competitiveness at eu level.
in writing. − articles 49 and 54 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union guarantee freedom of establishment for all enterprises and companies. cross-border corporate migration and the possibility of relocating companies to other member states are among the most important factors in the completion of a well-functioning internal market. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the directive on the transfer of business between member states. in the public consultations launched back in 2004, a majority of participants considered that it would be useful to adopt a company law directive on the relocation of company headquarters to another member state, which would ensure a harmonised regime in all member states. i therefore support the european parliament's recommendation that the commission submit a proposal for a directive on the relocation of companies to another member state.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a report in which the european parliament, in the exercise of its newly acquired right of legislative initiative, which previously belonged exclusively to the european commission, asks the latter to submit a proposal for a directive on the relocation of the headquarters of companies to another member state of the european union. the european parliament has exercised this right because it considers that the commission's inaction on this issue is wrong, since it does not remove the obstacles to the exercise by companies of one of their fundamental eu rights the freedom to establish companies throughout the european union. the european parliament's opinion was based on the results of numerous public consultations and also on the conclusions of the european court of justice that there are still too many differences in the national laws of the member states applicable to the establishment of companies, which hinder the exercise of the freedom of establishment and therefore require a harmonised regime throughout the eu. such unification of the legal regime applicable to the establishment of companies throughout the eu would remove many administrative obstacles and reduce social and tax costs for a company seeking to establish itself in another member state.
in writing. - 2 february 2012 i voted in favour of the document because companies still face administrative obstacles and social and tax costs in implementing mobility policies. it is therefore necessary to lay down appropriate measures to give effect to the freedom of undertakings to move their head offices. the commission should submit a proposal for a directive on the relocation of company headquarters to another member state, taking into account the need to guarantee freedom of establishment for all firms and companies. the transfer of the head office should preserve the continuity of the legal personality of the undertaking or company concerned and thus ensure its proper functioning. the transfer should not affect the rights of the interested parties (small shareholders, employees and creditors) which they enjoyed before the transfer. legal specificity is required, with full respect for the legal, social and fiscal conditions. it should also be noted that the relocation of the company's headquarters is one of the most important elements in the creation of the internal market.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it will facilitate the exercise of the right of establishment by limited liability companies and their migration to the host member state without losing their legal personality. the companies will thus be able to be restructured under the law of the host state without being liquidated and at the same time ensuring that they have the right conditions for their activities. moreover, the transfer of undertakings from one member state to another will give due regard to the interests of workers, respect their rights and protect them against dismissal. in view of the benefits of this directive, i consider it appropriate to oblige the commission to submit as soon as possible a proposal for a directive on the relocation of company head offices to another member state, as cross-border corporate migration is one of the most important factors in the creation of an effectively functioning internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which outlines the efficiency and effectiveness of the echo control, monitoring and supervision system, in particular when it comes to framework partnership agreement (fpa) partners or to international organisations (such as the un). the eu (the commission together with the member states) is the world’s largest donor of humanitarian aid. the eu’s total contribution of aid, including the member states, in 2010, was eur 2 957 million. the average budget managed by dg echo for its humanitarian aid activities between 2006 and 2010 is eur 889 million annually. in 2010 the budget was reinforced to eur 1 115 million to respond to crisis and disasters (haiti, pakistan). we, members of the european parliament, agree that there is additional need for sustainability, coherence and complementarity of humanitarian actions.
in writing. − in recent years, the world has witnessed a dramatic increase in the frequency, scale and severity of humanitarian disasters, affecting an increasing number of countries. in 2010 alone, the two major disasters in haiti and pakistan demonstrated some of the inefficiencies and lack of coordination needed to respond effectively to disasters. it is also necessary to ensure adequate control and transparency of the use of eu funds and to increase the accountability of beneficiaries, preventing misuse of funds. i believe that in order to strengthen audits and increase the credibility of the checks carried out, it is important to take account of the court's recommendation to monitor better the allocation and post-allocation of funds and to reach an agreement with the un agencies that jointly manage humanitarian aid with the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the need to make the delivery of humanitarian aid by the european union more transparent and efficient. also, strengthen the control of the use of funds when the eu provides humanitarian aid in a joint management with other partners the united nations and other international organisations. in the case of joint management of humanitarian projects, budget implementation and control are delegated to international organisations, with the european commission performing only monitoring and verification tasks on the spot. in the context of the discharge procedure, the court and parliament have repeatedly criticised the way in which international organisations are managed jointly. the criticism was prompted by a lack of consistency, rigorousness and various sources of confusion arising from the many additional levels of legislation that lead to the most errors. the weaknesses in the control of eu funds and monitoring of progress have also been widely criticised. this report therefore proposes to replace the joint management method with indirect management, which would allow the budgetary authorities to be more accountable to the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the document because there has been a dramatic increase in the frequency, scale and severity of humanitarian disasters, affecting more countries in the world. the eu's key role as a global humanitarian provider and the increasing number and frequency of interventions in and outside the eu, as well as the current budgetary constraints, highlight the importance of sound financial management in accordance with the principles of economy, efficiency and effectiveness. the massive disasters in haiti and pakistan have once again demonstrated the need to improve the eu's response capabilities in terms of efficiency, speed and coordination. the most important thing is that the most vulnerable groups receive timely and effective assistance.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as the dramatic increase in the number of humanitarian disasters makes it particularly important to ensure sound financial management based on the principles of economy, efficiency and effectiveness. the eu is the largest provider of humanitarian aid and the european commission's directorate-general for humanitarian aid and civil protection needs to be adequately equipped with financial and human resources to fulfil its mandate. the effectiveness and efficiency of eu humanitarian aid depends on an objective and consistent assessment of needs. in addition, the aid must be implemented using innovative methods and the continuous involvement of beneficiaries in the planning and management of the aid must be encouraged. in view of the constant increase in the number of different large-scale natural disasters, the eu needs to strengthen its response capacity. it is important to note that in order to achieve these objectives, it is essential that a realistic humanitarian aid budget is finally established.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which addresses the exchange of views on the commission’s public consultation examining possibilities for introducing a system of collective judicial recourse (‘collective redress’) at european level. the report highlights the principle that anyone who has suffered damage must have the right to receive compensation but that those bringing collective actions must not be in a better position than individual claimants. the eu legal tradition is directed towards solving disputes between individuals rather than through a collective entity. some member states’ legal systems have developed differing approaches to the issue of collective redress. it is in this context that the commission must put forward evidence that, pursuant to the principle of subsidiarity, an action at eu level is opportune. we, members of the european parliament, agree on the need for this new legal initiative and on initially proposed horizontal procedural actions and safeguards which should be further analysed, tested and developed.
in writing. − the commission's consumer policy strategy sets the objective of creating an efficient internal retail market by 2013 and enabling consumers and retailers to feel as safe as they do when buying in their own country. cross-border trade in the eu is developing very slowly because consumers are not assured that their rights will be protected and that they will receive compensation for damage if problems arise. the integration of european markets and the resulting intensification of cross-border activities have created the need for a common european concept of collective redress. the commission has made considerable efforts in this area, which is still regulated at member state level. i believe that a clear impact assessment must be provided and that possible measures must be identified to improve the current eu regulatory framework at eu level, to compensate those who have suffered damage as a result of breaches of eu law, and thus to strengthen consumer confidence and ensure the smoother functioning of the internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament (ep) report because in a european area of justice, eu citizens and businesses must not only have rights, but also the possibility of actually exercising those rights effectively. in addition, all eu citizens should be guaranteed the right to a fair trial. it should be noted that the system of collective actions for damages can complement the legal protection of individuals, but cannot replace it. the european parliament welcomes the commission's work towards a common european concept of collective actions. the ep asks the commission to demonstrate in its impact assessment that, in line with the principle of subsidiarity, action at eu level is needed to improve the current eu regulatory framework in order to compensate those who have suffered damage as a result of breaches of eu law, thereby enhancing consumer confidence and ensuring the smoother functioning of the internal market. the european parliament also welcomes the efforts made by member states to strengthen the rights of victims of unlawful activities when they adopt or plan to adopt legislation aimed at facilitating the redress process and avoiding an abusive litigation culture. however, it also recognises that national collective redress mechanisms differ widely, in particular in their scope and procedural features, which may impede the exercise of rights by citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because in a european area of justice, citizens and businesses must be able to exercise their rights under eu law effectively and efficiently. in the case of mass or dispersed damage, victims of the unlawful activity may indeed not have a right to claim compensation, as the costs of individual redress may be disproportionate to the damage suffered. in this respect, the concept of european collective redress can be useful, as it may be important for victims of unlawful activities to pool their claims which would otherwise have to be brought separately, and for undertakings to have a single dispute settled or a single court decision to provide legal certainty on the matter in question.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which establishes a uniform concept of european collective redress. such a concept will allow for the resolution of cross-border disputes and ensure the effectiveness of consumer redress and enforcement measures. it should be noted that the importance of the institution of collective redress in the protection of consumer rights is undeniable. mandatory eu-level collective redress mechanisms will ensure the highest level of protection of eu consumer rights and a more competitive internal market. i believe that the role of consumer organisations in collective redress should be encouraged and strengthened in order to achieve the objectives pursued. in addition, a european-level remedy for collective actions must be available to consumers at both national and eu level.
in writing. − the labelling of products and the indication of the nutritional value on food packaging are intended to increase consumer awareness of the composition and nutritional value of food. eu legislation on food labelling and nutrition labelling aims to provide information to the consumer in a clear and simple manner and to prevent any misuse, ambiguity or misleading use of such information. currently, information on food packaging indicating that a product is light or dietary can mislead the consumer and influence his choice of a particular food, even though such information is often not linked to the true nutritional value of the product. i voted in favour of the european parliament's position against the commission's proposed claim of a 10% lower nutritional content, as this claim can be confusing and incomprehensible to the average consumer, and i supported the call for a new draft proposal with new and clearer wording.
in writing. − i believe that the most important objective we have to pursue in the adoption of legislation on food labelling is consumer safety, which is impossible without ensuring that consumers are adequately informed. it is therefore a wrong practice to allow the same property (in this case the reduction of substances) to be described by several statements. in particular, where these claims can be used even if other conditions expected by the consumer (e.g. reduction in calories after reduction in sugar) are not met. as it is a regulation on the provision of information to consumers, it may even be liable to mislead consumers.
in writing. − i think it is appropriate to disagree with the commission's new regulation which proposes to amend the list of nutrition claims in foodstuffs. in particular, nutrition and health claims made on foods must not be ambiguous or misleading. consumers must be provided with accurate and specific information on foodstuffs, their origin, characteristics and properties. it should be noted that comprehensive and accurate information on the product allows comparison with other foodstuffs and the selection of the most appropriate foodstuff without any health risk. the amended list of nutrition claims currently in force will not only have a negative impact on consumers, but will also distort competition in relation to products with the currently used claims.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as fiscal stability is not only one of the key tools for overcoming the crisis, but also strengthens solidarity and ensures sustainable growth and employment. in this context, it is necessary not only to apply existing measures but also to develop new measures to stimulate the economic recovery. it is therefore appropriate to establish a debt repayment fund, develop a draft of bonds, a guideline for stability bonds and introduce a financial transaction tax at european level. i believe that member states whose currency is not the euro should be given full participation rights in all euro-related summits, not just those on competitiveness, the overall structure of the euro area and the basic rules. it is welcome that the international agreement on a fiscal stability union will take due account of and pursue the objectives of sustainable growth, employment, competitiveness and social cohesion. it is also essential that the content of the agreement is incorporated into the eu legal framework within five years.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution concerning the conclusions of the informal european council meeting of 30 january 2012. i support the criticising opinion of the european parliament and i agree upon the proposed improvements to the final text of the conclusions. i agree with the common concerns that the uk maintains its objection on the final text of the treaty on stability, coordination and governance in the economic and monetary union. the economic recovery requires measures to strengthen solidarity and boost sustainable growth and employment and insist that the european council decides on concrete and far-reaching measures. i support the ep request for a further series of measures to ensure fiscal stability, and calls now for the establishment of a redemption fund, project bonds, a road map for stability bonds and the introduction of an ftt at european level, for which the commission has already made a proposal. we members of european parliament point out that some further important elements are missing from the new agreement, such as the avoidance of double standards between the norms in the agreement and those in the lisbon treaty and contained in the acquis communautaire. we also insist and reiterate that ep participation in these negotiations is further extended.
