in writing. - i voted for this resolution. fiscal stability in the eu and in the member states is an important component of the solution to the current crisis, and the new fiscal treaty will provide the basis for new principles for the coordination and surveillance of the economies of the eu member states. the european parliament succeeded in getting very important provisions, in particular on the participation of non-euro area member states in euro area summits, included in the final text of the treaty. so far, agreement has been reached on the right to participate in those meetings which concern competitiveness, the general structure of the euro area and the basic rules which will apply to these member states in the future, but i believe that non-euro area countries should not be restricted from participating in other meetings. in addition to this agreement, other urgent measures are needed, including the introduction of a financial transaction tax at eu level as soon as possible and the establishment of an eu credit rating agency.
in writing. − i voted for this european parliament resolution because it is very important what message we send to the half billion people in the european union about the state of the eu, the economic situation and better governance. the european parliament (ep) recognises that fiscal stability is an important component of the solution to the current crisis, but stresses that measures to strengthen solidarity and to promote sustainable growth and employment are needed to achieve economic recovery. the ep welcomes the fact that the european council recognises this, but insists that concrete and far-reaching measures are needed. it is important to realise that austerity alone will not solve the european union's crisis. in order to ensure fiscal stability, the european parliament proposes to use not only the series of measures envisaged but also the drafting of a bond, the guidelines for stability bonds and the introduction at european level of a financial transaction tax, which has already been proposed by the commission. the ep also urges the contracting parties to fully honour their commitment to incorporate the stability, coordination and governance treaty into the eu treaties within five years at the latest, and to take this opportunity to address the remaining shortcomings of the lisbon treaty.
in writing. −fiscal stability is an important component of the solution to the current crisis, but the recovery of the economy requires measures to strengthen solidarity and to promote sustainable growth and employment. it is good that the european council recognises this, but it does not take concrete and far-reaching measures. i therefore abstained. the new agreement also lacks a number of other important elements: first, the desire to avoid double standards between the agreement and the lisbon treaty and the rules of the acquis communautaire; second, all contracting parties to the agreement, current and future euro area members, should have the same right to participate fully in all euro-related summits. euro-area summit meetings should be held in an expanded format. we must all work towards fiscal stability, economic recovery, strengthening solidarity and sustainable growth and employment for our citizens.
in writing. − eu foreign ministers agreed on additional restrictive measures against iran in a number of sectors. gradual embargoes on crude oil imports to the eu have been imposed, measures have been taken against the central bank of iran, further export restrictions have been imposed. these measures reflect serious and growing concerns about the possible military aspects of iran's nuclear programme. there is no effective dialogue between the west and iran and tensions have risen dangerously in the gulf region. however, the eu remains committed to a comprehensive and lasting solution that would strengthen the international community's confidence in iran's peaceful nuclear programme. i agree that the solution to this issue should be to seek by all means a diplomatic solution to the nuclear crisis and to avoid military conflict, and that the humanitarian consequences of additional sanctions against iran should be carefully assessed and monitored.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the proliferation risk associated with iran's nuclear programme remains a major concern for the eu. it is of concern that the iaea report makes the claim that there is credible information that iran has engaged in activities related to the development of a nuclear explosive device. iran's enrichment activities may be in violation of six unsc resolutions and eleven iaea council resolutions. this is evidenced by the recent start of an operation to enrich uranium to 20% at an underground facility in the fordovo area near como. iran must immediately halt its development of enrichment technologies, which go far beyond the need to ensure the security of fuel supply for civilian purposes and show disregard for international concerns about covert military intent. it is necessary to engage in meaningful and constructive discussions in order to address substantially the concerns raised by the nuclear programme.
in writing. the atena report has sent a distress signal to the world. the military dimension of iran's nuclear programme poses a direct threat to the middle east region, in particular to israel, and to world peace and security. iran is a member of the nuclear non-proliferation treaty and the existence of a military dimension would be a serious breach of international law. in the absence of cooperation from iran, the 27 eu member states unanimously agreed to new sanctions and continue to call on iran to return to the negotiating table. iran shall immediately provide all answers to the questions raised, resume negotiations and fully open documents, sites, infrastructure and persons to iaea inspections. those members of the un security council who supply nuclear technology and expertise to iran must freeze such exports, renouncing narrow economic and political interests, assuming their responsibility as guardians of world peace before the world, because they are very likely to be collaborating in the creation of a new source of global threat.
in writing. − i believe that the eu must take a firm stand and that all issues concerning iran and its nuclear programme must be resolved peacefully. we can't cross that line, there's no going back. the use of military force and means is not an effective way to resolve the conflict. it will not bring results but will only exacerbate disagreements and increase tensions. military force cannot be used as a means of political pressure, especially now that the world is still experiencing economic instability. in this context, constructive negotiations and mutually beneficial decisions are necessary to ensure a reliable supply of energy resources. it is also essential to ensure that the strict penalties which should be applied as a measure of last resort are effective, adequate and proportionate to the objective pursued.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution giving the ep reaction on the european commission’s communication on sport of 18 january 2011, which is the first contribution to define new eu competences for sport. i support the commission position as the proposed policy promotes an increase in the social role and a healthy lifestyle, combats doping and violence, gives benefits to the economy and will ensure better governance in sport. furthermore, the report stresses the fact that sport can contribute to the strategic objectives of the european union, given its educational and cultural value. however, in the future, the european union has to create a future specific programme on sport with a view to defining and supporting a real european dimension in sport. we, members of european parliament, believe in actions at eu level such as a focus on doping, trafficking, mobility of athletes, racism and violence and on the fight against criminal activities such as money laundering, match-fixing, human trafficking and exploitation of minors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. sport generates a high added value across the eu, contributing to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth and having a significant positive impact on social inclusion, education and training and public health. sport also helps to reduce social security and healthcare costs, as it improves health, increases productivity and ensures a better quality of life. i support the objectives set out in the commission's communication, in particular the inclusion of compulsory sport in all schools, increased support for organisations seeking to integrate people through sport, in particular those at risk of social exclusion and people with disabilities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because sport is a very fast-growing sector not only in the european union but also beyond. the data show that increased sporting activity creates around 15 million jobs in the eu. the sports sector employs 5.4% of the active population and has an annual turnover of around €407 billion, or 3.65% of european gdp. sport plays a major role in society and contributes to social well-being by promoting employment and integration, contributing to society and social education. the european union has recently been given new competence in the field of sport and is invited to contribute to the promotion of sport. in response to the commission communication 'strengthening the role of eu action in sport', the european parliament proposes that the eu focus on issues of international concern such as doping, illicit trafficking, athlete mobility, racism and violence in sport. the commission is also proposing to examine and deal with money laundering, match fixing, human trafficking and the exploitation of minors. it is also proposed to establish a european register of persons who have shown aggressive behaviour during matches in the past as a result of illness. the discussion of such problems at eu level could make a significant contribution to their solution and would create real added value for action at eu level in the sport sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it calls on the commission to propose, in the context of the public health benefits of sport and its social, cultural and economic benefits, an ambitious budget for a specific sport policy under the future mff. sport for people of all ages is an important area with great potential to improve the overall health of europeans and the eu and the member states are therefore encouraged to promote participation in sport and to promote healthy lifestyles, making full use of the opportunities offered by sport, as this will ultimately reduce healthcare costs. it is welcome that attention is being paid to persons with disabilities by encouraging them to take part in sporting activities and by providing adequate funding for the development of disabled sport and competition, in particular by providing access to sport and equal opportunities for disabled people to participate in sport and to use a free sports facility adapted to the needs of disabled athletes. sport plays an important role in ensuring social inclusion, public health and volunteering across borders, and the promotion of physical and sporting activities makes a significant contribution to public health cost savings.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because sport is not only a key public health tool, but also a social and cultural phenomenon and a dynamic economic sector. sport is also an important tool for development policy. in this context, it is also necessary to coordinate joint action at eu level in the sports sector. an ambitious budget must be earmarked to achieve this objective. given the benefits of sport, both the eu as a whole and each member state must encourage citizens to participate in sport and promote healthy lifestyles. particular attention shall be paid to the integration of disabled persons into sporting activities. i support the proposal to regulate the profession of sports agent and to establish a european register of agents to help protect athletes from the risk of conflicts of interest. furthermore, in order to prevent doping and other forms of manipulation at sporting events, member states should be encouraged to exchange information, experience and good practice on a regular basis.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur that sport can encourage our citizens to contribute to society and help to strengthen a sense of social inclusion. we can learn a lot from sport: the recent eurobasket in lithuania demonstrated the enthusiasm, purpose and unity that are sadly lacking in lithuanian politics and public life. in lithuania, sports are very poorly funded. this is understandable in view of the economic crisis that has struck my country. but we can't blame the economic crisis for the lack of funding for sports. another problem is the weak administration of the lithuanian sports system. last year lithuania's sports budget was 39 million litas (just over 11 million euros). for example, the sports budget in latvia is almost double that. greater transparency and better governance are needed. part of the problem is the distribution of funds - while some of the larger lithuanian sports federations receive the bulk of the funding, a few dozen federations are left without incentives. the issue of sustainable financing of lithuanian sports should be further examined.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution initiated by the ep (epp group) based on fact-finding visits and petitions of european citizens to the parliament concerning the environment, in particular the inappropriate application by the member states of the waste management directive (new plants, landfills and incinerators). three main problems were identified: a lack of a sound environmental impact assessment and public consultations in the permission procedure for landfills; incorrect operation of waste management facilities and deficiencies in waste management systems. i agree that the ep, at eu level, should urge the member states to speed up the transposition of the waste framework directive into national law, that there should be reinforcement of the existing european environment agency for monitoring purposes rather than creating new instances, and that the member states should be recommended to impose, in accordance with the polluter-pays principle, adequate and dissuasive fines and penalties for illegal disposal of waste, especially with regard to toxic and hazardous waste.
in writing. − the european parliament's committee on petitions receives an increasing number of complaints about the inability of the public authorities in many member states to deal adequately with the problem of waste management. failure to address these problems and to prioritise them negatively affects not only human health and well-being but also the prospects for the planet. waste management is becoming a major political and social issue, and people are looking to the european union to solve it. i agree that the commission needs to take a much bigger role and be much more active in identifying persistent shortcomings in the implementation of the waste directives by member states and taking action against member states if they fail to properly comply with their obligations under eu law.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament report because a large number of citizens of the european union are petitioning about the non-disposal of waste, and most of the petitions are related to waste treatment plants. citizens' petitions show that they believe the authorities are not in control of the situation and in some cases are not prepared to make the effort needed to find solutions, and that trust has been shaken, open confrontation has occurred and a deadlock has arisen, which has impeded action. in addition, most eu citizens expect public authorities to provide effective and efficient public services in the areas of health, education, transport and security. the apparent inability of public authorities in many member states to deal adequately with the problem of waste management is thus a determining factor in the increasing number of petitions. the european parliament calls on the eu member states to transpose the waste framework directive into their national law without delay and to ensure that all the requirements set out therein are met, in particular the requirement to draw up and implement detailed waste management plans, as well as to amend in a timely manner all the targets set under eu legislation. in addition, the commission should closely monitor the transposition of the eu directive on the protection of the environment through criminal law in the member states to ensure that this is done in a timely and effective manner.
in writing. − i supported the report because most european citizens expect public authorities to provide effective and efficient public services in the areas of health, education, transport and security. however, in many countries the apparent inability of the authorities to deal adequately with the problem of waste management is a determining factor in the increasing number of petitions. member states must ensure that any decision on a new waste management, in particular on the incineration or methane production of a facility or, in the worst case, the installation or construction of a new landfill, is subject to a full and mandatory environmental impact assessment. the commission is invited to propose clearer and more specific criteria for the location of landfills, taking into account the distance to local dwellings, schools or health facilities, in order to provide greater guarantees for the protection of human health and the environment against potential hazards, bearing in mind that there are many variable and site-specific circumstances that need to be taken into account. i believe that the achievement of the recycling and prevention objectives set out in the legislation requires the active involvement of civil society, the increased involvement of stakeholders and better information for the public. the recommendations in this report should help to improve the implementation of waste management policies in the future.
in writing. − in the resolution adopted today, we have highlighted two very important aspects. first, the need for the commission and the member states to pay greater attention to informing the public about the necessity and benefits of waste management. currently, in some member states, sorting is slowing down, mainly because of a lack of public confidence in its benefits. secondly, the specific impact of the environmental impact assessment process on the transparency of waste management. it is the lack of clarity and public awareness in the design and construction of waste management facilities (in particular incineration plants and landfills) that leads to waste crises and even disasters during the rdp (as shown by real examples in italy, spain and other countries). therefore, in the next review of the ppp directive, we need to make more efforts to ensure that the public is properly and effectively involved in the consultation, that their views are taken into account and that the process itself is transparent and independent.
in writing. - i support this resolution. in particular, in order to properly implement the waste management directive and other related legislation and to develop effective waste management strategies, it is necessary to allocate appropriate funding from the cohesion fund or the european investment bank for the installation of infrastructure and facilities. in addition, member states must carry out monitoring, inspections and other necessary actions at all stages of the waste management chain. i believe that common eu standards for the colour labelling of waste by category should be established for the sorting and recycling of waste. it is also essential to ensure that environmental impact assessments are mandatory before any decision is taken on a new waste facility, in particular the installation or construction of a new landfill. in addition, local authorities should engage in a constructive dialogue with local populations in order to reduce their resistance. local residents must be assured that the licensing and operating authorities are transparent and properly compliant. i think the commission should impose dissuasive penalties for illegal waste disposal. in addition, greater attention should be paid to the impact of all forms of organised crime on environmental crime.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution reporting the daphne programme’s success and suggesting a number of improvements to correct imbalances that have arisen, e.g. in the breakdown of projects between member states. i agree that this eu initiative running from 1997 was undoubtedly beneficial to eu citizens and, therefore, the daphne objectives in the new programme should be maintained. i agree to the proposal to maintain the daphne programme for smaller ngos and also to the list of programme intervention in recital k containing a list of types of violence against women and children, including sexual abuse, rape, domestic violence, prostitution, trafficking and violation of women’s health and reproductive rights. the success of this programme over 15 years indicates how extremely important for eu, and especially lithuanian, citizens is the continuity of the programme.
in writing. − the daphne programme, established in 1997, aims to combat violence against children, young people and women. given the success, effectiveness and popularity of the daphne programme, its continuity and adequate funding must be ensured. the new generation programme will focus on women, children and young people who are at particular risk of violence due to social exclusion. i support the call for member states to collect data on violence against women on a regular basis in order to understand the scale of the problem in the eu, and for the commission to provide more funding for projects aimed at informing the public, and in particular people at risk of violence, about the new forms of violence associated with the increasing use of online social networks (threats, psychological pressure, victims, child pornography on the internet). this type of violence is more disguised than other forms of violence, but it can be just as traumatic physically and psychologically.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament report because the daphne programme is the only programme of its kind aimed at combating violence against women, children and young people throughout the european union. since its launch in 1997, the programme has been a real success: firstly, it has been popular with stakeholders (beneficiaries, public and academic institutions, non-governmental organisations) and, secondly, the projects financed by the programme have been implemented effectively. it is therefore essential to ensure continued funding for the daphne programme in order to continue the implementation of the measures currently in place and to introduce new measures that are effective in combating all forms of violence against children, young people and women. the daphne programme is a crucial tool to promote greater public awareness of violence against women and to provide women's organisations and other relevant stakeholders with the opportunity to develop their activities and concrete actions in this area. the daphne programme will be integrated into the rights and citizenship programme from 2014, but it is essential to ensure that the objectives of the programme, in particular the objective to combat violence against women, remain within the objectives of the new rights and citizenship programme for the period 2014-2020. moreover, given the success, effectiveness and popularity of this programme, the next generation programme should continue to ensure its high funding.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document as it seeks to strengthen the impact of the programme and asks the commission to continue to pay particular attention to women, children and young people who are particularly at risk of violence because of social exclusion and marginalisation. i also agree with the need to increase funding for projects aimed at informing young people in particular about the new forms of violence associated with increased use of online social networks (threats, psychological pressure, bullying, child pornography on the internet). this type of violence is more disguised than other forms of violence, but it can be just as traumatic physically and psychologically. the aim of european, national and all of our policies is to prevent and combat violence against women, children and young people.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which looks at the achievements and future prospects of the daphne programme. it is important to note that this programme is of great importance and is necessary to prevent violence against women, children and young people throughout the european union. it should be noted that such violence includes all forms of human rights violations. in this context, there is a need to continuously improve the dissemination of the programme in the member states, as well as the cooperation between different organisations. in addition, the prevention and reduction of gender-based violence inevitably requires legislation at european level and substantial funding.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i am very much in favour of the daphne initiative, which aims to combat violence against young people and women, even with a small amount of money and the sharing of experience. i am therefore very concerned that the report shows that certain member states, including lithuania, are very poorly represented in the daphne programme. according to data provided by lithuanian non-governmental organisations (ngos), 63% of lithuanian women have experienced physical or sexual violence or threats. the vast majority of these women said that the experience had made them feel hated and powerless. most disturbingly, only 10.6 percent of all victims reported serious incidents to the police. according to the lithuanian women's information center, police and courts avoid domestic violence cases unless the victim is severely beaten or killed. police resources against criminals are often limited. the network of crisis centres provides inadequate assistance to victims of violence. in 2011, there were 15 crisis centres and 6 shelters for battered women in lithuania, but they do not cover the whole country and only 2 of them are financed by municipalities. this is too big a problem to leave to ngos. politicians should take decisive action.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament report because sexual violence mass rape, trafficking in human beings and other forms of sexual violence against women and children are still unacceptably used as a tactic of war in conflict regions around the world. in addition, the lack of governance in post-conflict areas may lead to a deterioration in the situation of women and girls, as was the case in libya and egypt. sexual violence in conflict has devastating consequences for victims, including physical (risk of infertility, transmission of sexually transmitted diseases, etc.) and psychological consequences, as victims are often condemned, rejected, abused, shamed, and often ostracized from the community, and sometimes even killed. the families of the victims also suffer greatly, as sexual violence is considered degrading. the impunity of perpetrators of sexual violence is also a major concern, as illustrated by the armed conflict in colombia, where sexual violence against women is systematic and covert, with perpetrators escaping virtually all punishment. this form of violence should therefore be considered a war crime. to improve this situation, the post of eusr for women, peace and security should be created. the creation of such an office would make all policies and actions more coherent and effective, and would provide the united nations with a focal point through which to cooperate in more similar ways.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because i believe that women in peacekeeping operations play an important role in military and/or civilian organisations, as role models, as mediators between cultures and as promoters of greater empowerment for women, and as breakers of stereotypes for local men. gender considerations should be addressed from the very beginning of the planning of civilian and security missions. history has repeatedly shown that warfare is a highly male-dominated activity and therefore it is to be expected that the particular capacities of women to engage in dialogue and non-violent action can make a significant contribution to the peaceful prevention and management of conflicts. the commission, the eeas and parliament's delegations must find ways to encourage developing countries that have not yet done so to sign, ratify and implement the 1998 rome statute (relating to the international criminal court), as this is a necessary step to protect women's rights in war situations and to avoid impunity for criminals.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because in armed conflicts women and children are often the first civilian victims of the belligerents. i am thinking in particular of the use of mass rape as a weapon of war, and of sexual violence which often goes unpunished. this report emphasises the role and place of women in military and civilian peacekeeping operations, particularly the role they can play in conflict and peace negotiations. the report also calls for zero tolerance for sexual violence and sexual exploitation of children and women in armed conflict and refugee camps. it strongly condemns the use of sexual violence against women as a weapon of war, equating this form of violence to a "war crime". we call for an end to impunity for perpetrators of sexual violence and for women who have been victims of abuse and violence to be able to bring complaints before international courts under conditions compatible with their dignity.
in writing. − in armed conflict, women and girls are often easy targets. violence against women has long-term consequences for the victims themselves, their families, communities and ultimately societies. in some parts of the world, sexual crimes and other forms of violence against women are war tactics and demoralising tactics, and are justified, deliberate and encouraged. the definition of war crimes should therefore be supplemented in order to treat sexual crimes as any other war crime and to eliminate the possibility of avoiding responsibility for such crimes. the positive role of women in conflict prevention and reconciliation is not sufficiently recognised and exploited. i therefore voted in favour of the report, which highlights the diversity of the problem and sets out a number of proposals which, if implemented, i believe would make greater progress in protecting women and children from sexual violence in armed conflict.
in writing. − i believe that we must make every effort to prevent sexual violence in all its forms in conflict regions around the world. in this context, it is necessary to provide for specific provisions to enable women to be more effectively protected against various forms of sexual offences. appropriate funding must be allocated to these objectives. in addition, discrimination against women and stereotypes in promotion policies and in job-promotion companies must be prevented. each person, irrespective of his or her sex, shall be appointed to the appropriate post in accordance with his or her abilities and competence. it is important to note that not only the eu but also developing countries must take certain steps to protect women's rights in war situations and to end impunity for criminals. these countries must sign, ratify and implement the rome statute as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution aiming to support the objective of universal energy access by 2030 bringing greater attention to how the international community could generate funding (usd 756 billion by 2032) for central and more sustainable forms of energy generation across the world. i agree that the debate on sustainable energy access and consumption should be in parallel with the eradication of poverty with the establishment of a specific ‘energy and development’ programme within eu development cooperation policy. moreover, the use of renewable energy resources should be at the heart, as they can offer an economic solution in developing countries with benefits to health, the environment and local development, as well as the fight against climate change. we, members of european parliament, call on the developing countries to commit seriously to the goal of universal energy access, and recommend increased assistance to ministries of energy in developing countries to enable them to make the case for support, including the development of long-term sustainable energy strategies and improved regional cooperation in energy matters.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i agree that energy services affect all aspects of human life and livelihood and that without access to these services, entire communities are condemned to poverty. the european union must therefore, in contributing to the millennium development goals, continuously seek ways to contribute as effectively as possible to the accessibility of energy services for all. the european parliament stresses in its resolution the need to increase the use of renewable energy sources and calls for eu financial support to be directed specifically to promoting the use of these resources. the european parliament also notes that the european energy fund is one of the few financial mechanisms operating on an international scale and that it is therefore necessary to review the effectiveness and efficiency of the mechanism in the preparation of the new multiannual financial perspective (2014-2020). in its report, parliament also stressed that an effective partnership between the public sector, the private sector, communities and local authorities will be needed to expand access to sustainable energy services. parliament also recognises that the public sector alone cannot meet all the financing needs needed to expand access to electricity, and therefore draws attention to the importance of private investors and market-oriented reforms in the energy sector.
in writing. − i voted for this document because access to modern energy services is essential to reduce poverty and promote sustainable social development of people. unless decisive action is taken to improve the situation, some 67% of the population will still be without access to electricity in 2015. over the past decade, access to energy resources for the poor has been modestly funded. bilateral cooperation between eu member states in energy aid has been directed primarily at economic growth and environmental objectives, rather than at the access of the poor to energy resources. transparent, democratic participation of civil society, local authorities and regulators in the energy sector is important to enable them to monitor the implementation of universal energy access, to ensure good governance and fair competition and to curb corruption.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as access to modern energy services is a prerequisite for reducing poverty and ensuring sustainable social development. each country is responsible for ensuring access to universal services, but not every developing country is able to ensure access to energy resources for poor people on its own. the eu's contribution in this area must therefore be very strong and substantial, including funding, capacity building, technology transfer and governance reform. the eu needs to develop clear and precise guidelines on environmental sustainability criteria and other initiatives to ensure that modern sustainable energy services are available to all. it is worth noting that developing countries are currently under-represented and under-funded in terms of increasing access to energy resources for the poor.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the report contains important measures to combat the lack of local electricity and the high levels of poverty in the developing world. some of the projections made by the rapporteur raise concerns in 2015, some 67% of sub-saharan africa is still likely to be without access to electricity. maybe not, but ordinary lithuanians are going through a hard time too. according to eurostat, the highest price jump for electricity in lithuania between the second half of 2009 and last year was 31%. meanwhile, the eu price of electricity increased by 5,1% over the same period. since 1 january 2012, the price of electricity in lithuania has increased by 1,4 ct/kwh. the closure of the ignalina nuclear power plant was one of the conditions for accession to the eu, which significantly changed the structure of electricity production in lithuania. our leaders lack a comprehensive and realistic electricity strategy for lithuania. in early 2010, prime minister kubilius said that nothing bad would happen if the plant was closed. we're prepared to supply as much power as we need. although no harm was done, the situation of most lithuanians with regard to electricity deteriorated.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution concerning the ep annual report on taxation issues. the report focuses on the tax initiatives taken by the commission during 2011 and on areas where further initiatives are necessary in order to improve the functioning of the single market and to create a more competitive europe. the report also stresses that improvement of the single market and eventually some tax harmonisation could be key factors for encouraging growth and job creation; that tax policies must aim to foster european competitiveness and lower costs for european business, namely for small and medium enterprises. i agree with the rapporteur’s proposal that the ep should ask the commission and member states to cooperate further on their respective tax policies against double taxation, tax fraud and tax evasion in order to increase transparency and reduce loopholes and uncertainties for businesses and citizens with regard to tax collection. to make the taxation process more coherent, i support the ep call upon the commission in cooperation with the european parliament to establish an eu definition and list – taking into account, as a first step, the oecd definition and list of tax havens or secrecy jurisdictions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is the first time that the european parliament has published its annual report on taxation, with the aim of contributing to the european commission's work in this area. indeed, the current economic and financial crisis has led to a significant increase in the debt of member states, and robust fiscal consolidation and a fairer and more accurate distribution of the tax burden are therefore essential to ensure fiscal sustainability. in this context, where both cost reductions and tax increases are needed, it is crucial that growth-oriented tax changes are prioritised. it is also crucial to remember that in these circumstances, now more than ever, we need to ensure that, alongside austerity measures, automatic stabilisers of the social security system are in place in all countries to ensure growth and social cohesion. the european parliament therefore calls for closer coordination of tax policies in the european union, which would reduce costs and administrative burdens for citizens and businesses, and stresses the need to simplify the procedure for paying vat in order to eliminate double taxation and red tape for employers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i believe that low taxes are necessary not only for the welfare of social families and households, but also for the competitiveness of new jobs. however, it is also important to control and use public expenditure efficiently and to pursue stable public finances. the commission's taxation proposals should contribute to the eu's competitiveness by removing the distortions of competition that arise from the different tax systems in place. the commission and the member states should continue to cooperate in developing their respective tax policies aimed at combating double taxation, tax fraud and tax evasion, in order to increase transparency and reduce gaps and uncertainties for businesses and citizens in relation to tax collection, in particular with regard to their respective administrative procedures for filing tax returns. member states should aim to reduce the costs of tax compliance for smes by simplifying procedures and reducing red tape where possible. it is clear that member states have different corporate tax bases, which in practice can become cross-border barriers to trade, hindering growth and employment.
in writing. − low taxes are necessary not only for social welfare but also for competitiveness of new jobs. it should be noted that taxation is a matter of national sovereignty. in this context, each member state should aim to reduce the tax burden, paying particular attention to smes. it is also essential that tax policies, both in the eu and in the member states, are directed against double taxation, tax fraud, tax evasion and abuse. i believe that the commission's taxation proposals should first and foremost increase the competitiveness of the eu and ensure the efficient functioning of the single market, but should in no way increase the tax burden. the vat payment procedure should also be simplified and bureaucracy reduced. taking into account the interests of citizens and businesses, a clear, transparent and stable tax environment should be established, which would eliminate the cross-border tax obstacles, discrimination and double taxation of citizens and businesses that currently still exist.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution welcoming the commission report on competition policy 2010. to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the report on competition policy, this year’s edition begins with an overview of the major developments of competition policy and enforcement over the past 40 years. i agree with the rapporteur that eu competition policy has brought numerous benefits in terms of consumer welfare and has been an essential tool to eliminate obstacles to the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital. i agree on the emphasis that the ongoing consolidation in the banking sector has actually increased the market share of several major financial institutions and, therefore, the commission has to maintain a close watch on the sector in order to enhance competition in european banking markets. we, members of european parliament, recall the parliament’s invitation to the commission during the early steps of the implementation of the third energy package to closely monitor the level of competition; it also asks the commission to intensify the efforts that it is making in order to open up competition in the credit rating agencies sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because competition policy is an essential tool for the european union to create a dynamic, efficient and innovative internal market and to be competitive on the global stage. the european parliament welcomes the commission's prompt and reasonable response to the crisis by adopting specific state aid rules and using competition policy as a crisis management tool. the large amount of state aid provided during the crisis, for example in the form of guarantee schemes, recapitalisation schemes and additional liquidity support provided by banks, contributed to the large imbalances in public finances. the commission should further investigate the competitive situation in the retail sector, in particular in relation to the alleged abuse of market power by dominant retail chains to the detriment of small retailers and producers in the agri-food market. the european parliament also believes that competition policy should contribute to the promotion of open standards and to the application and interoperability of activities, in order to avoid that the small number of market participants prevents consumers and customers from participating in the development of technologies.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as protectionism and non-compliance with competition rules would only deepen and prolong the crisis, and competition policy is an essential tool for the eu to create a dynamic, efficient and innovative internal market and to be competitive on the global stage. despite all efforts to combat the economic crisis, cartels remain a major threat to competition, consumer welfare and the proper functioning of markets and cannot be tolerated, especially in times of economic crisis. eu competition policy has brought many benefits to consumer welfare and remains the main instrument for removing barriers to the free movement of goods, services, persons and capital. competition policy remains the main instrument for safeguarding the single market and protecting consumers' interests. only by combining strong principles with flexible procedures can competition policy be a constructive and stabilising factor in the eu's financial system and the real economy in general. i believe that greater price transparency is essential to promote competition in the single market and to give consumers real choice.
in writing. − competition policy is an important crisis management tool for shipping. it also helped to create the single market and to boost the eu's economic growth. in view of its contribution, a new, permanent framework for the regulation of state aid rules, operating under stronger and stricter rules, especially in the case of aid to the banking sector, must be established. however, it is essential that the state aid does not distort competition but encourages entrepreneurship. in addition, competition policy must be conducted on the basis of a comprehensive approach to the internal market, with particular attention to citizens, consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises. i believe that the commission must develop as a matter of urgency a system for solving the problems of europe's troubled banks, which would allow it to respond quickly to the difficulties it faces and to take more effective decisions.
in writing. the european commission's move to channel the remaining eu structural funds to support smes and tackle youth unemployment is welcome. this eur 82 million injection is expected to help tackle youth unemployment by finding ways to reduce the rate of youth unemployment rapidly. it is great that we are talking about efforts to develop internship opportunities or incentives for employers to hire young people. but this financial injection and momentary attention or measures are far from the panacea. even now, with youth unemployment high on the political agenda, it is necessary to look for targeted measures that are truly effective in a fast-moving and dynamic eu market. we have been saying for many years that we need to strengthen the link between business and education and to promote cooperation between them in order to bridge the gap between them. it is the gap between business and education that is the main cause of the huge youth unemployment: employers constantly stress that young people lack specific skills and practical skills and that their expectations of pay do not correspond to reality. another concern is that the eu education system does not focus on the development of young people's entrepreneurship, their ability not only to take up jobs but also to create them. it is to be hoped that the ec experts, in consultation with the member states, will pay due attention not only to the current youth unemployment crisis but also to the search for integrated solutions in the education, social affairs and economic sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal related to the management of the european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy in order to fight against infringements of intellectual property rights, increase the awareness of public and private sectors of the impact of counterfeiting and piracy and inform consumers of the dangers related to the purchase of fake products. i supported adjusting the observatory’s title to its more extended role by changing its name from ‘european observatory on counterfeiting and piracy’ to ‘european observatory on infringements of intellectual property rights’. i also supported the proposal to clarify the scope of the regulation in line with directive 2004/48.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the europe 2020 strategy is based on a smart growth foundation, which consists of promoting creativity, knowledge and innovation. over the next decade, it is necessary to improve the eu's research performance and to ensure a greater uptake of smart products and services in the market. the successful establishment of the single market for research will depend on the effective protection of intellectual property rights. the increasing number of intellectual property infringements in recent years (a study in 2010 shows that piracy in the music, film, television and software sectors cost the eu some eur 10 billion and led to the loss of over 185 000 jobs in 2008) is undermining investment in innovation, destroying jobs, threatening the health and safety of european consumers and preventing the expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises. i agree that the office for harmonization in the internal market should be strengthened to this end, with certain tasks relating to the protection of intellectual property rights, which would help to better understand the extent of infringements of intellectual property rights and to respond to them more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is the european parliament's position on the european commission's proposal to combat piracy and infringements of intellectual property rights. the commission has proposed to the european parliament to merge the management of two separate bodies set up respectively to collect information on intellectual property and trade marks and to combat infringements of intellectual property rights. this will make them more efficient and save money. this proposal was very well received by the european parliament, which had already asked the commission in 2010 to strengthen the role of the european observatory on infringements of intellectual property rights, and this will be possible by entrusting the office for harmonisation in the internal market, which was established in 1996, with certain additional resource-intensive tasks. the new structure of the european observatory on infringements of intellectual property rights, with additional resources, will therefore include: more transparent governance based on a clear, predefined methodology; greater accountability to the european parliament, the commission and civil society; and a balanced representation of the interests of industry, consumers, small businesses and independent creators. it is important to note that the european monitoring centre for infringements of intellectual property rights will not retain any functions that could be equated to the role of law enforcement authorities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because the economic prosperity of the union depends on sustainable creativity and innovation. effective measures to protect them are therefore necessary to ensure their future welfare. intellectual property rights are a vital part of business assets they help to ensure that creators and innovators are properly remunerated for their work and that their investments in research and new ideas are protected. we need a sound, coherent and progressive approach to intellectual property rights. the ever-increasing scale of infringements of intellectual property rights poses a real threat not only to the union's economy but also, often, to the health and safety of consumers in the union. therefore, effective and coordinated action at national, european and global levels is urgently needed to successfully combat this phenomenon. taking into account the need to protect intellectual property rights the council invited the commission to set up a european monitoring centre on counterfeiting and piracy. the centre should be the main centre for the collection, monitoring and presentation of information and data relating to all infringements of intellectual property rights. it should become a platform for cooperation between national authorities and stakeholders to exchange ideas and expertise on best practices and to provide policy-makers with recommendations on common rights strategies.
in writing. − i support this resolution as it is necessary to promote greater cooperation between member states and the eu institutions. in particular, private-public cooperation should be encouraged by improving cooperation in the field of law enforcement. it should be noted that no legal regulation should create an additional administrative burden. in order to promote economic growth, employment and cultural diversity, it is necessary to develop new competitive business models that expand the legitimate supply of cultural and creative content. the ipr monitoring centre should therefore become a platform for cooperation between national authorities and stakeholders to help prevent infringements of intellectual property rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the proposed directive because there is an increasing demand for access to information on companies in a cross-border context, either for commercial purposes or to facilitate access to justice. cross-border groups, as well as many restructuring operations such as mergers and divisions, involve companies from different member states of the eu. cross-border access to business information requires cooperation between business registers. some cooperation between them already exists, but it is limited to certain types of information and does not cover all member states. this proposal will benefit the citizens of the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to ensure technical interoperability between existing national registers. the interoperability of business registers is an important tool to promote further integration of the economic area within the european union and to ensure greater legal clarity for businesses and citizens. currently, commercial registers are managed at national and regional level and there are everywhere factual and legal differences in their legal significance and the reliability of the records. the increasing scale of cross-border economic activities in the eu requires greater legal clarity and transparency and better interaction between business registers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to simplify the exchange of business information at european union level. the exchange of information in business registers is currently regulated by several directives in the european union, but these registers are managed at national and regional level and vary widely in terms of their legal significance and the reliability of the records. as the scale of cross-border economic activities increases, better interaction between business registers is necessary for legal clarity and transparency. it is important to note that this directive will only cover the exchange of information already contained in the national registers and will not create a commercial register with separate data. the aim is to create a platform that will help improve and accelerate communication and access to information for citizens and businesses. such an eu business data platform will provide greater legal clarity for businesses, potential investors and citizens.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because the increasing scale of economic activity across borders and the need for legal clarity and transparency require better interaction between business registers. this would save time and money. the interoperability of registers will make it possible to make effective use of the possibilities of electronic register management. the purpose of this directive is to ensure technical interoperability between existing national registers only and not to harmonise legal implications. the exchange of information contained in the registers is therefore limited and no separate trade repository is established. a platform will be created to improve and accelerate communication and access to information between citizens and businesses. however, the successful interaction of business registers can only be achieved through close cooperation between the commission and the member states. at the same time, this should help to ensure the reliability and accuracy of the information.
in writing. − the system of interoperability of business registers should not create an additional tax and administrative burden for business entities. it is also necessary to ensure that the functioning of such a system should not alter either the content of the company data stored in the national registers or the information on companies transmitted through the system of central, commercial and companies registers. adequate funding is necessary for this interaction of business registers to function effectively. however, member states should not be subject to an additional financial burden in relation to the adaptation of national registers to this system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, whereby the parliament gives its consent to the new protocol of the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the republic of guinea-bissau. while maintaining the provision of financial assistance to guinea-bissau, it renews the terms of the previous protocol and contains an additional clause providing for its suspension should human rights and democratic principles not be respected. i agree with the rapporteur on the need to monitor closely the implementation of the measures set out in the council decision of 18 july 2011 concerning the conclusion of the consultation procedure with the republic of guinea-bissau under article 96 of the cotonou agreement. i strongly support the ep position that article 9 of the cotonou agreement must be respected and its emphasis on the need to monitor the human rights situation in guinea-bissau.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives the european parliament its consent to the conclusion of a new fisheries partnership protocol between the european union and guinea-bissau. this protocol sets out the fishing opportunities and financial compensation for eu countries in the territorial waters of guinea-bissau. the new protocol sets out the allocation of fishing opportunities among the member states concerned, while the fishing conditions remain essentially unchanged. however, the new protocol contains additional provisions on the suspension and review of the payment of financial compensation and on the suspension of the application of the protocol to this agreement in the event of violation by guinea-bissau of fundamental and fundamental principles of human rights and democracy. under the protocol to the fisheries agreement, eur 7,5 million is allocated to a limited number of european union vessels for a one-year fishing licence, part of which is intended to support the policy of guinea-bissau in the fisheries sector and to improve sanitary fishing conditions.
in writing. − i supported the conclusion of the memorandum of understanding as it appeared to be relevant to the needs of guinea-bissau as a key contributor to macroeconomic and budgetary stability and as a driver of the country's fisheries policy, as it provided the financial conditions for the implementation of important measures in the sector to support economic development and sustainability (which, according to the evaluation report, represented on average 7.3% of annual government revenues and about 88% of budgetary expenditure on fisheries). this agreement has had a particular impact in reducing iuu fishing and has improved the sector's compliance with the sanitary requirements for eu trade in fishery products, two important conditions for the development of the country's fisheries sector. the fisheries partnership agreement is an important instrument for maintaining the enlargement agenda in times of economic and budgetary instability. it also assisted the eu and the bissau guinea authorities in continuing the political dialogue to promote responsible fishing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which endorses the conclusion of a new protocol between the european union and guinea-bissau. it should be noted that guinea-bissau has substantial coastal and ocean fish stocks. the protocol will also benefit both parties to the agreement in order to continue the political dialogue to promote responsible fishing. i agree with the new provision in the protocol that financial compensation for violations of fundamental and fundamental principles of human rights and democracy should be suspended. it is also appropriate to suspend the application of the protocol if guinea-bissau does not make efforts to make its fisheries responsible and sustainable.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it aims at establishing an internal market for payment services in euro (single euro payments area or sepa) in which there is no difference of regime between cross-border and national payments. this decision may well bring benefits to the european economy that could amount to eur 100-300 billion in six years time. i believe this proposal will benefit eu citizens as the regulation eliminates the need for consumers to provide a bic code for domestic payments. the consumer only needs to provide the iban code and the bank will automatically establish the bic without extra charge. for cross-border payments, this requirement will be enforced on 1 february 2016. a member state may also allow consumers to use bban instead of iban for two extra years, but the banks need to provide the conversion services for free. i also support the parliament’s proposal that there be no extra charges for payments above eur 50 000.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. secure and efficient payment systems are an essential prerequisite for economic transactions and the proper functioning of the internal market. since 2002, cash payments have been made easier for member states using the euro. however, for a number of reasons, electronic union-wide payment instruments have not yet replaced national payments. this has led to market uncertainty, a difficult economic climate, a lack of legal certainty and high costs for dual payment systems. i agree that it is urgent to create an internal market for euro payments (single euro payments area sepa) with effective competition and no distinction between international and national payment systems, which would save considerable money and benefit the european economy as a whole.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to create a single area for payments in euro throughout europe, otherwise known as sepa. sepa is an area where national and international payments in euro are treated on the same terms as if they were intra-country payments in euro. its objective is to increase competition and encourage new services. the proper implementation of these rules in the member states will therefore make international payments in euro as convenient and fast as local payments in euro. such a single banking system would make a significant contribution to reducing banking charges for both individuals and businesses, and at eu level, according to the european commission, would save around €100-300 billion. the implementation of this initiative will also speed up the timing of international banking transactions in euro. such banking operations are already required to be executed within 1 day as of 1 january this year and in the future it will be aimed to execute such operations in real time.
