in writing. − i voted in favour of this legislative resolution on radio spectrum policy. i support the second reading of the resolution, which contains important amendments such as the 800 mhz frequency band to be made available for broadband wireless internet in all member states by 1 january 2013, the development of a mobile broadband connection with a minimum speed of 30 mbps for all eu citizens by 2020, etc. i agree with the rapporteur that this political agreement will pave the way for developments that will make the eu a world leader in broadband speed, mobility, coverage and capacity. this agreement will also be crucial for the development of a flexible and coherent european spectrum policy.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i agree that in these difficult economic times we need to improve and develop the telecommunications sector, which is one of the sectors that generates the most jobs, thus contributing significantly to economic growth. it is also one of the sectors most likely to adopt innovative technological solutions and to offer the most new services to people. the objective of this document is to establish a common eu-wide radio spectrum management system. indeed, it is a public resource beyond national borders, and its management at european union level would balance the interests of broadcasters and citizens alike and safeguard europe's cultural diversity. the practical expression of this coordinated control will allow the use of radio frequencies, which have been used for analogue television until now, for high-speed wireless internet. this will reduce the load on the current 3g networks, improve broadband services in remote areas and accelerate the deployment of innovative services across europe.
in writing. − i agree that this political agreement will pave the way for a development that will make the eu a world leader in broadband speed, mobility, coverage and capacity. this agreement will be crucial for the development of a flexible and harmonised european spectrum policy, which will allow the exponential growth of mobile data flows to be controlled in the future by the reallocation of spectrum, so that inefficient use of spectrum will be a thing of the past. by supporting the proposal of the parliament and the commission to make the 800 mhz frequency band available for electronic communications services by 1 january 2013, member states will contribute to the development of a european telecommunications market where new services can create new opportunities and ensure the growth of a market of 500 million users. however, the economic crisis and the difficult financial situation may not allow all member states to meet their targets on time, which may not only place additional financial burdens on them. i also believe that member states should have more freedom of action in pursuing the objectives they set themselves, as the technical and financial capacities of the member states differ.
in writing. − as we have seen on many occasions, legislation often lags behind progress in the relationships it regulates. this is particularly true for digital technologies, for example. the european parliament's view expressed in this document is therefore welcome, that at least in the field of digital and radio data transmission we should not follow technological progress but go beyond it and set the course of action at least a decade ahead.
in writing. − i believe that radio spectrum policy must be based on the principles of effective management and use of limited resources, technological neutrality, functional equivalence, proportionality, transparency and non-discrimination. furthermore, the effective implementation of this policy should ensure the minimum necessary regulation in this area, legal certainty in a changing market and due regard for the criteria of economic development, the guarantee of effective competition, the protection of consumer rights, conditions and the objectivity of procedures. given the importance of spectrum policy not only for the eu but also for each member state individually, and the consequences of the past financial crisis, we must avoid making hasty decisions on the allocation of spectrum. it should be noted that not all countries may be adequately prepared and have sufficient resources to implement the technical conditions for the allocation of radio frequencies in the 800 mhz band by 2013. therefore, in order to protect against anti-competitive behaviour and anti-social measures, only a minimum level of regulation should be ensured at eu level, and the decision on the essential issues should be left to the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the european dairy sector is extremely sensitive and economically important to the eu. the milk and milk products sector faced exceptional events between the years 2007-2009 which, combined with the effects of the financial and economic crisis, resulted in farm-gate prices crashing in 2009. europe’s dairy sector will experience a major shift after the expiry of quotas in 2015. the commission identified three key elements: the bargaining power of producers, contractual relations and inter-branch organisations. in its report, the committee on agriculture also highlighted the need for pdos (protected designations of origin) and pgis (protected geographical indications) to be able to manage the volume of their production. i agree with the proposal that, in order to secure a stable future for the sector, the bargaining power of producers needs to be strengthened. however, still further negotiations between the institutions are needed to define the best rates and quotas to maintain competition among farmers, but also to protect consumers and the european market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to increase the bargaining power of farmers in the dairy sector, thereby ensuring fairer milk prices and enabling farmers to meet the milk production quotas set. this regulation was initiated by the european parliament in response to the fall in milk prices in 2008 and 2009 and with a view to stabilising the markets for dairy products. this regulation will allow organisations of dairy farmers to negotiate the conditions for the sale of milk, such as prices, quantities sold, duration of contracts, etc. the commission notes that the milk levy is not a direct or indirect taxation of milk, but a taxation of milk products. this leads to unfair commercial practices, since farmers often do not even know what the price of the milk they deliver will be, since the price is often set much later by the dairies on the basis of value-added criteria that farmers cannot control unless they join cooperatives.
in writing. - i have supported this document because it is clear that there are many differences between the milk production and processing sectors in the member states. in addition, the situation as regards operators and types of operators varies considerably between member states. however, in many cases the concentration of suppliers is low and this leads to a balance of bargaining power between farmers and dairies in the supply chain. this can encourage unfair commercial practices, for example farmers often do not know what the price of their milk will be because the price is often set much later by the dairies on the basis of value-added criteria which farmers cannot control unless they join cooperatives. i believe that the abolition of quotas could help to raise awareness and the responsibility of operators in the milk chain to take account of market signals, to better coordinate prices in the chain, to coordinate supply and demand and to help to avoid unfair commercial practices. in order to ensure a rational development of production and a fair standard of living for dairy farmers, their bargaining power vis-à-vis processing undertakings should be increased in order to ensure a more appropriate distribution of added value in the supply chain. cross-cutting organisations can also be useful for ensuring dialogue between supply chain parties, helping to promote best practice and market transparency. i hope that the european milk sector will be transformed by the end of the quota period in 2015.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is necessary to strengthen the position of milk producers in the milk supply chain. producers must be adequately prepared for changes in market conditions following the abolition of the quota system. in view of the difficult market conditions in this sector, the collapse in prices which has forced many european dairy farmers out of business and the existence of other milk producers is at serious risk, producers need to be confident that they will be offered the right price on the market and will be able to continue their activities and that the sector will remain viable and competitive. it should be noted that contractual relationships, negotiating power of producers, inter-branch organisation and transparency are complementary elements that together ensure the efficient functioning of the supply chain. written contracts between milk producers and processing undertakings will ensure transparency, fairness and legal certainty. strengthening the bargaining power of producers will increase the overall productivity, competitiveness and sustainability of the sector. in addition, producers should be encouraged to join producer organisations and measures to promote transparency should be supported on a continuous basis.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased that the report addresses the problems of price volatility and the imbalance in negotiations between farmers and large dairies. this is very much related to the situation in lithuania. although lithuania is the leading milk producer in the baltic states (about 1.9 million tonnes per year, or 23.4% of total agricultural production), the lithuanian dairy industry is poorly structured. as a result, milk prices are higher than the european average. a recent survey revealed that lithuanian consumers are paying 40 percent more for milk today than they did in 2004. this situation is partly due to the fact that 60% of lithuanian dairy products are exported and at the processing level the current dairy industry consists of only four large companies. the report states that this imbalance can lead to unfair commercial practices. therefore, in order to ensure a fair standard of living for dairy farmers, their bargaining power vis-à-vis processing undertakings should be increased. this would allow for a proper distribution in the supply chain. more stability is needed, especially as the european milk sector faces major changes following the end of quotas in 2015.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution proposing the amendment of rule 48(2) with a view to improving the treatment of own-initiative reports, in particular at the plenary stage, and to examining the question of whether rules 163 and 167 should apply to ini reports. i agree with the rapporteur’s proposal to reduce the necessary quorum for tabling amendments in plenary from one-tenth to 40 members, to extend the application of rule 163 (split voting) and rule 167 (roll-call voting) to ini reports and to amend the last sentence of rule 48(2) to endorse the cop (conference of presidents) recommendation according to which the decision on whether an ini report is ‘strategic’ or not should be carried out by the cop at the authorisation stage. these amendments will make parliament’s work more efficient and dynamic.
in writing. − while acknowledging that own-initiative reports should have a greater strategic relevance, particularly on issues where the ep draws the commission's attention to matters of particular importance, i would like to highlight another aspect. it is often the case that the ep produces reports on its own initiative one after the other on the same issues. unfortunately, even when we express our views on important issues (such as demography or biodiversity conservation), these messages often replicate each other and do not offer anything new, much less a solution to the problem. i would therefore like to draw the attention of the parliament's management to the need to focus more on the relevance and originality of the topics of own-initiative reports rather than on the relevance and originality of the topics of the reports being prepared.
in writing. − it should be noted that the european parliament is the institution representing the citizens of the member states. the elected members of the european parliament act on the basis of the principle of 'free mandate', which is a fundamental law of parliamentary democracy. in this context, the right to make own-initiative reports should not be restricted. furthermore, i do not think it is appropriate to apply the split vote and the roll call vote only to committee proposals for resolutions and their amendments and the roll call vote only once during the final vote on alternative motions for resolutions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which expresses the european parliament's provisional position on the commission's green paper and will be followed by a more detailed resolution or report on the subject. the euro area and its member states must ensure the long-term stability of a currency used by more than 330 million people and many businesses and investors, with implications for the whole world. i agree that stability bonds could be an additional instrument to promote compliance with the stability and growth pact. however, important issues such as budgetary discipline and competitiveness, criteria for lending to member states and the ability to meet debt obligations, measurable and implemented debt reduction programmes, etc. still need to be addressed. the envisaged stability bonds have the potential to enhance the stability of the euro area in the medium term, but the commission should make proposals as soon as possible to effectively address the current sovereign debt crisis.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree that we need to look more closely at the proposed euro bonds idea, looking for ways to ensure stability in the euro area and to make the euro a strong currency again and contribute to the stability of the international monetary system. the idea of a single bond issue is compelled by the fact that the continuing tensions in the euro area bond markets, reflected in the widening of bid and offer spreads over the past two years, are highly volatile and vulnerable to speculative attacks. however, the european parliament draws the attention of the commission and the member states, reiterating once again that the common bond issue is conditional on the establishment of a sustainable fiscal framework aimed at strengthening economic governance and promoting economic growth in the euro area, and that it is essential to establish the appropriate sequence of actions, including the development of a binding action plan.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the possibility of a stability bond could be an additional means of promoting compliance with the stability and growth pact, provided that the issue of non-pecuniary damage and joint liability is addressed. it is one of the possible ways to help resolve the situation today. i agree that the commission should come forward as soon as possible with proposals that would resolutely address the current sovereign debt crisis. the euro area and its member states must ensure the long-term stability of a currency used by more than 330 million people and many businesses and investors, as this affects not only the eu but the whole world. we need to be open to debate, to actively discuss all the issues - both the advantages and the disadvantages - of the possibility of issuing stability bonds, evaluating the various alternative options in order to find the right answer to the current sovereign debt crisis.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it is necessary to create a sustainable fiscal system that will use effective measures to strengthen economic governance and stimulate economic growth in the euro area. in particular, the euro area should have a common liquid and diversified bond market, which would provide an alternative to the us dollar bond market and enhance the role of the euro in the global financial system. the euro will thus become a global safe haven. in addition, the stability bonds will help avoid a recurrence of the debt crisis, stimulate growth in the medium term and increase market efficiency. however, we cannot make hasty decisions in the context of the introduction of stability bonds. better policy coordination is therefore needed to ensure high credit quality and the availability of the stability bonds to all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the annual growth survey, which sets out what the commission believes have to be the main priorities for the coming year in terms of budgetary, economic, employment and social policies and reforms. i agree that the key message should be that more efforts are needed to put europe back on track and sustain growth and jobs. member states should focus on five priorities: pursuing differentiated, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation; restoring normal lending to the economy; promoting growth and competitiveness; tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis; and modernising public administration. together with other members of this parliament, i express a general concern that fiscal consolidation was set as a general priority and that fiscal consolidation measures are a threat to people at risk of poverty and social exclusion. the crisis has had particularly dramatic consequences for the situation of young people trying to seek stable employment but who are now facing an unemployment rate of over 20 %, and of more than 40 % in certain member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. in the eu member states, over 10% of people of working age are unemployed, and this trend is increasing as member states adopt austerity measures that are holding back the economic recovery of both the member states and the eu as a whole. the social consequences of the financial and economic crisis are affecting a growing number of eu citizens and increasing poverty among working people across the eu. i support the calls in the report for member states not to undermine the incentives for growth and employment through austerity measures, and to give priority to spending to stimulate economic growth, such as spending on education, lifelong learning, research and innovation, while ensuring that these spending are effective.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the assessment of the 2012 annual growth survey and i agree that there is indeed cause for concern that the current set of national indicators is not sufficient to achieve the main objectives of the europe 2020 strategy on employment, education and poverty reduction. unfortunately, the guidelines for the fight against unemployment do not correspond to the guidelines for increasing employment, improving the quality of jobs and creating the necessary conditions for more active participation in the labour market. many member states do not offer measures to ensure that workers are paid fairly and have decent working conditions. it is also important to emphasise that, where savings measures are applied, they should not interfere with the respect of social security, health and safety standards. the crisis has had a very negative impact on youth employment on average, one in five young people in europe is unemployed. for many countries, this has become a serious labour market problem, often addressed by seeking work abroad. this phenomenon also undermines the investment made by the state in the skills of people, which cannot be realised. young people try to escape by going on to university, but this only delays the solution of the problem and reduces their motivation to work. and the worst is when the most beautiful dreams and plans of life are destroyed by long-term unemployment. there are currently 7.5 million people in the eu who are neither working nor studying. it is a pity that these people are poor, when their work is so needed by an ageing europe that seeks to ensure a well-being for all based on solidarity between generations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the social consequences of the crisis are severe and have been exacerbated in some countries by austerity measures to combat the sovereign debt crisis, by job losses in both the private and public sectors, by cuts in benefits, by a reduction in the provision of public services and by the deepening of poverty and unemployment across the eu. the current labour market situation for young people, regardless of their level of education, is particularly difficult, as they often face precarious employment contracts and unpaid traineeships. the difficult situation of young people is also due to the fact that the skills they acquire do not correspond to the needs of the market. among those who have also been hit hardest by the crisis are early retirees, the long-term unemployed and low-skilled workers. the growing number of people at risk of low income, the growing risk of child poverty, severe material deprivation and social exclusion require measures to ensure sustainable, progressive, sustainable and inclusive growth, investment and tax reform to support sustainable job creation, to improve the quality of jobs and conditions for greater participation in the labour market, to combat youth unemployment, poverty and social exclusion, and to enhance democratic legitimacy, accountability and responsibility.
in writing. − the economic crisis and the euro area sovereign debt crisis have forced member states to adopt exceptional austerity and budgetary discipline measures. these measures are necessary to manage the crisis, but some of them have other effects, such as increasing social exclusion. even countries that are more successful in controlling the effects of the crisis will remain fiscally constrained, and it is therefore unreasonable to expect an increase in social spending. member states must therefore take well-considered systematic and targeted measures to reduce the negative impact of austerity on the economy and people, and to promote economic growth and job creation. these measures must be based on the eu level, because the failure of one country can mean the loss of all. across the eu, about 23 million people are unemployed, representing about 10% of the working age population. among them are a large number of young people, for example in spain, where 48% of young people are unemployed. the link between business and education systems needs to be strengthened to better match the expectations and opportunities of employers and young people looking for work. more attention needs to be paid to the development of young people's entrepreneurship and their ability to create jobs themselves. with a well-thought-out and targeted approach to limited resources, it is possible not only to stimulate job creation but also to pursue broader objectives such as 'growing the economy' and creating a competitive low-carbon economy.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in particular, capacity for job creation and the promotion of self-employment, including social entrepreneurship and increased labour market participation, must be strengthened. i believe that active labour market policy measures are necessary, with particular attention to incentive initiatives. the eu must be given budgetary freedom and investments in sustainable and good jobs must be encouraged. moreover, increasing the flexibility of employment relationships would facilitate the entry of young people into the labour market. i support the proposal that the council adopt as soon as possible policy guidelines to enable companies that guarantee a fair wage to reduce the burden of non-payment of taxes on employees. the european council must also make continuous efforts to improve the single market and reduce bureaucracy.
in writing. − commissioner, madam president, colleagues, the 2012 annual growth survey presented by the commission does indeed contain a number of good proposals that would help to solve the problems of the current sovereign debt and financial crisis. a considerable effort will be required to regulate the stabilisation of the economies of the eu member states and to restore confidence to investors in the market. it is necessary to take measures as a matter of urgency to create a stable and attractive environment for investors, in particular through the creation of project bonds, which would contribute to the financing of major infrastructure projects and would contribute to the promotion of sustainable growth and employment in the long term. i believe that economic stabilisation will not be achieved without taking into account the medium- and long-term growth and employment objectives. the situation is not satisfactory. unemployment among working age people is increasing and the situation with youth employment is very bad. the 2012 european semester is the first to be implemented on the basis of a legally strengthened economic governance framework (a set of six pieces of legislation), but i believe that in the future it needs to be much more focused on strengthening the social dimension, which in turn would contribute to the sustainable economic recovery and growth of the member states.
in writing. − i voted on this report on participation in the preparation of the 2012 annual growth survey. unfortunately, the annual growth survey does not include the measures needed to restore the confidence of european households and businesses, as well as financial markets, and it does not address the need for urgent action to support short-term activity and employment, which is essential to achieve the europe 2020 objectives. it is recognised that the implementation of the guidelines agreed at european union level has not been sufficiently smooth or uniform across member states, giving the necessary leeway to member states to implement their policies, and that this has prevented the full potential of the agreed guidelines to achieve the europe 2020 strategy objectives from being realised. the european parliament invites the commission to provide a detailed assessment of the implementation of the country-specific recommendations in the member states, which it will publish before the european council in june 2012. in addition, the commission should work more closely with the council to develop a common budget and reporting framework. furthermore, given the importance of the role played by eu-funded programmes in the current economic conditions, the commission is invited to submit a proposal for the financing of europe 2020 actions by transferring unused payment appropriations.
in writing. − i have supported this document because the concrete decisions that all institutions are taking on a daily basis to address the problems of the current sovereign debt and financial crisis should be linked to a particular focus on medium- and long-term growth-enhancing measures and a thorough review of the overall economic framework to ensure greater sustainability, competitiveness and long-term success of the european economy. the annual growth survey does not include measures needed to restore the confidence of european households and businesses as well as financial markets, as it does not address the need for urgent action to support short-term activity and employment, which is essential to achieve the europe 2020 objectives. efforts at national and eu level should focus on five priority areas, namely differentiated, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation to ensure economic recovery and job creation; securing long-term financing of the real economy; promoting sustainable growth through increased competitiveness and investment; tackling unemployment and the social consequences of the crisis; and modernising eu public administration and services of general interest. in deciding on budgetary expenditure and revenue, member states should give priority to pro-growth policies such as education, research, innovation, infrastructure and energy policies and ensure that expenditure and revenue are planned effectively. it is also necessary to reduce unnecessary administrative burdens and to limit bureaucratic procedures.
in writing. − i believe that the annual growth report does not give sufficient attention to actions to support short-term activity and employment. in addition, member states must make greater efforts to achieve the objectives set out in the europe 2020 strategy. thus, at both national and eu level, differentiated, growth-friendly fiscal consolidation must continue, restoring normal conditions for the lending economy. each member state should give priority to growth-friendly policies. to increase the eu's competitiveness and to stimulate economic growth, the eu's financial system needs to be made more resilient. it should be noted that in many countries the quality of public services is poor. in this context, it is necessary to modernise public administration by reducing the administrative and bureaucratic burden.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur rightly points out that the crisis has had a particularly strong impact on the situation of young people trying to find a permanent job. it notes that the number of young unemployed in the eu has increased by 1 million over the last two years. the situation in lithuania is very bad. in three years, youth unemployment rose from 13% to 31%. this is significantly higher than the eu average of 21%. for comparison, in 2008, about 142 000 young people were employed, and now only 93 000 are in employment. according to the latest reports, 49,000 young men are now unemployed in lithuania, which is 1/3 of the lithuanian labour force. it shouldn't be like this. the annual growth review rightly gives priority to the employment of young people, but we must not forget the quality of work and traineeships, which are foreseen in the commission's policy guidelines.

human rights council for freedom of religion or belief, seeking to renew a strong collective response based on human rights standards. finally, last year the council adopted a landmark resolution on of violence against individuals based on their sexual orientation and gender identity. the annual session of the human rights council, which brings together key actors on human rights from states to ngos, can be considered the world’s house of human rights. the eu stands ready to engage and cooperate with countries from all regions to ensure the success of this session. we want this council to have a direct impact on the empowerment of people and to hold accountable those who are responsible for grave human rights violations.

millions of people in europe need books in accessible formats - whether audiobooks, braille books or enlarged versions. unfortunately, books in this format are rarely of interest to publishers, and only about 5 percent of the world's works are published in accessible formats. there are currently no legal provisions providing for an exception to copyright for the international distribution of printed matter in a format suitable for the blind. mr commissioner, do you not think that in order to change this situation, it is necessary to change international copyright laws so that book collections can be shared throughout the european union and beyond without infringing them? i would like to invite the commission and the council to adopt a binding 'books without borders' treaty which would allow the worldwide sharing of books for the blind and visually impaired. the world intellectual property organization is considering the possibility of concluding an international treaty on improving access to books for the blind and other visually impaired, and i ask you, commissioner, to support this treaty. this is also what the blind and partially sighted community in my country, lithuania, is asking for.
in writing. the right of a person to live with family members, as well as the right and duty to care for, educate and live with children, are fundamental rights and obligations not linked to citizenship. these rights must therefore also be respected and guaranteed for third-country nationals coming to live in the european union. i would also like to recall that there are many national and international declarations which take the same position on this issue and recognise the rights and obligations mentioned. the charter of fundamental rights of the european union recognises the right to a family and to family reunification as a fundamental human right. i appreciate that the european commission has started discussions on the revision of the family reunification rules for migrants living in the european union, but the commission should assess very responsibly whether the directive provides for sufficient safeguards on family reunification, whether it is necessary to ensure that discrimination against third-country nationals' families is prevented, as there is still a negative attitude and intolerance towards migrants who have arrived in europe. the commission should also assess all the positive effects of family reunification. the directive states, in particular, that family reunification contributes to social and cultural stability, which creates favourable conditions for integration and allows the promotion of economic and social cohesion, which is beneficial for the local authorities of the host countries. it is also important to recognise that the right to family reunification is a crucial step forward, making a concrete contribution to reducing illegal immigration and dangerous forms of social exclusion.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the creation of a common eu-wide deposit guarantee scheme is particularly relevant and necessary in the context of the ongoing financial crisis. under the rules currently in force in the european union for national deposit guarantee schemes, depositors are to be compensated up to a certain amount in the event of the bankruptcy of a credit institution. it is true that during the financial and economic crisis the level of compensation was increased to eur 100 000 per depositor and the deadline for the payment of compensation was reduced to a maximum of 30 working days. the increased level of protection enhances depositors' confidence and thus helps to prevent a situation where many depositors simultaneously withdraw their money for fear of losing it. these steps towards building depositors' confidence are very welcome, but more can and must be done. it is for this reason that the introduction of an eu-wide mandatory requirement for deposit guarantee schemes to meet common requirements in all eu countries and in all credit institutions is being considered. this would avoid distortions of competition, provide the same protection for depositors in all member states and prevent the transfer of deposits from one credit institution to another with destabilising effects.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the establishment of common requirements for deposit guarantee schemes would allow member states to ensure the maximum degree of flexibility in the establishment of deposit guarantee schemes, while ensuring the same level of protection and stability and avoiding distortions of competition. member states may thus adapt their deposit guarantee schemes to the specificities of national financial markets, subject to provisions on the uniform level of compensation and targeted financial resources and to fixed payment deadlines and conditions for the use of funds. this ensures effective protection of depositors and stability of the financial system. the higher level of compensation is not sufficient to ensure a reliable level of protection for depositors. in order to avoid a 'bank run' and to prevent possible destabilisation of financial markets, deposit guarantee schemes also need to be provided with the necessary financial resources. the financial and economic crisis has shown that the separate national deposit guarantee schemes in europe are underfunded and that the burden of the bankruptcy of a credit institution must be borne by the state and ultimately by the taxpayers. in order to ensure the stabilising effect of deposit guarantee schemes in times of financial stress, it is necessary to ensure sufficient ex ante funding of deposit guarantee schemes across the eu. depositors must be better informed than before about the functioning of deposit guarantee schemes and compensation for depositors in the event of bankruptcy must be paid more quickly. the harmonisation of measures would help to strengthen depositors' confidence and the stability of the european financial system and to achieve the internal market.
in writing. − adequate deposit protection in the event of the insolvency of a credit institution is, as recent events in lithuania have shown, a crucial instrument for ensuring citizens' confidence in both the banking system itself and the state controlling the system. however, i would like to draw attention to a few aspects which have received less attention in this report. the key issue, as correctly noted and confirmed in the document, is the proper supervision of commercial banks by national authorities and the timely response to potential danger signals. second, the need to have an accurate list of criteria for financial instruments falling under the deposit guarantee scheme and to ensure that clients are provided with accurate and comprehensive information on the guarantees applied.
in writing. − i support this resolution because a stable and reliable deposit guarantee scheme will ensure adequate protection for depositors. in particular, common requirements for the comprehensive protection of depositors and uniform requirements for the stability of deposit guarantee schemes will prevent distortions of competition and help to protect cash deposits. moreover, the flexibility of the preventive and support measures will help to avoid the emergence of solvency difficulties of the credit institution and, if they do arise, will allow them to be resolved as quickly as possible. i think it is appropriate to provide a five-working-day grace period for the payment of non-refundable deposits which is favourable to depositors. this will protect depositors from long-term financial difficulties and at the same time preserve their confidence. in addition, the conditions for the rapid return of deposits to depositors will be improved. it is also necessary to strengthen the provisions on information and to allow depositors to transfer a non-guaranteed deposit to another credit institution without penalty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a call by the european parliament for a freeze on the administrative budgets of the eu institutions in the light of the continuing difficult economic circumstances. parliament also recalls that the preparations for croatia's accession will have to be made in 2013 and will have budgetary implications, in particular as regards resources for new members and staffing of the various institutions. however, the european parliament recalls that all institutions must show responsibility and solidarity for the budget and savings in view of the high public debt burden and the need to save now that the member states are continuing to consolidate their national budgets. parliament therefore calls for greater interinstitutional cooperation to share best practice and to seek ways of saving by modernising its human resources, organisational, technology and building policies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the european parliament and all the institutions should show budgetary and savings responsibility in the face of the high public debt burden and the need for austerity now that efforts to consolidate national budgets are continuing. the institutions need to strengthen interinstitutional cooperation to share best practice, seeking ways to save and thus modernise their human resources, organisational, technology and building policies. it is good to note that the structural changes and restructuring of the european parliament have resulted in considerable savings for the 2012 budget. structural and organisational reforms should therefore be pursued and innovations extended to other areas. the secretary-general should submit a comprehensive report to the budget committee, giving a detailed overview of the budget lines under-implemented in 2011 and an objective analysis of the reasons for this under-implementation. at the same time, however, the savings should not jeopardise the ep's legislative work. i believe that all institutions must continue to look for ways to save in order to preserve the budgetary order and to freeze their budgets in the light of legal obligations and new financial challenges.

in writing. − in the current financial situation, the european parliament and all institutions should show responsibility for budgeting and saving. a wise spending policy is therefore essential. i think that the biggest savings would be to have a single seat for parliament and to avoid the monthly travel between brussels and strasbourg. in addition, in order to ensure transparency in the field of buildings policy, a reform of the procedure should be carried out so that the plenary's approval is required for the resolution of these issues.
in writing. − under the implementation plan adopted at the 2002 united nations world summit in johannesburg, the european union has committed itself to maintaining or restoring fish stocks in order to achieve the maximum sustainable yield, with a view to achieving these objectives in respect of depleted stocks without delay and, if possible, by 2015 at the latest. in april 2009, the commission proposed a management plan for the stock, based on the preparatory work of the regional advisory council for pelagic fisheries and the recommendations of the international council for the exploration of the sea and the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries. the objective of this plan is to maintain a sustainable exploitation of the western atlantic common sole, ensuring its biomass, and to provide for the best long-term use of the stock. i voted in favour of this document because long-term management plans for the greatest possible number of stocks are essential to conserve these stocks, as set out in the commission's proposal for a reform of the common fisheries policy. the commission is therefore called upon to take immediate action, as stated and promised on several occasions, to prevent further interinstitutional disruptions in the approval of future long-term management plans, and the council is called upon to present its position on the proposed multiannual plan for the western atlantic bluefin tuna stock, in order to allow parliament to start the second reading and to make progress on this issue.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is essential to ensure that living water resources are used in a sustainable way to ensure economic, environmental and social conditions. it is worth noting that the multiannual plan for the exploitation and fishing of western atlantic hake is an essential conservation measure to ensure the sustainable and long-term exploitation of the stock and to facilitate the better performance of fisheries operators. it should be noted that the fisheries control rules are intended to ensure the management of the stock based on the precautionary principle. the stocks of plaice in union waters, fished by various fleets, are of the highest economic importance. the multiannual plan must therefore provide effective means of ensuring the stability of the fisheries sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the european parliament's assessment of the reform package of the common fisheries policy presented by the european commission last summer. parliament called for this reform to enshrine the sustainable exploitation and conservation of fish stocks as one of the main ideas of the reform of the common fisheries policy. to achieve this, the european parliament proposes a range of measures, including positive discrimination, i.e. providing for better access to eu support funds for those undertakings that engage in sustainable fishing. such practice is already being successfully used in the common agricultural policy. the european parliament also notes that fisheries is a vital sector of the eu industry, providing citizens with high-quality food and creating economic and social added value. therefore, it is of particular importance that the appropriate level of fish stocks is maintained to ensure the long-term viability of fishing activities in traditional areas and communities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the preservation of healthy fish stocks, healthy marine ecosystems and marine biodiversity is an important common asset that must be preserved. a dynamic, well-managed fisheries sector could bring greater benefits to european society and the economy and thus play an important role in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. the fisheries sector is an important eu industrial sector, providing high quality food for eu citizens and creating economic and social added value in the eu, and the reformed cap must therefore ensure the sustainable use and conservation of fish stocks and maintain adequate levels of fish stocks to ensure the long-term viability of fishing activities in traditional zones and communities. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of a european union agency for fundamental rights. the commission, when preparing future policy proposals and decisions, must ensure that the cfp contributes to the achievement of common policy objectives. in this crucial reform process, the cfp must be recognised as a source of development for the european growth project and the necessary conditions must be created for its full potential. in developing and implementing this policy, the commission must take account of the specific characteristics of fisheries and coastal regions.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as there is a strong concern about the way in which democracy and the rule of law are being established, human and social rights are being guaranteed and defended, checks and balances are being implemented, equality and non-discrimination are being ensured in hungary. in the interests of the hungarian citizens and the eu as a whole, the hungarian government is invited to take into account the recommendations, objections and demands of the european commission, the council of europe and the venice commission on the above issues and to amend the relevant legislation accordingly, in line with the fundamental values and norms of the eu. i believe that it is necessary to ensure the full independence of the judiciary, that the regulation of the national bank of hungary must be strictly in line with european legislation, that the independence of data protection and freedom of information institutions must be pursued, that the right of the constitutional court to review any legislation must be fully restored, that freedom of the media and pluralism must be consolidated, that the electoral law must comply with european democratic norms and the principles of political change, that the right to express political opposition in a democratic manner within and outside the institutions must be guaranteed, and that the law on religious communities and confessions must take into account the fundamental principles of freedom of conscience.
in writing. − the adoption by the hungarian parliament of a new constitution and a series of new laws raised doubts about their compatibility with eu law, values and fundamental principles freedom, democracy, human rights and the rule of law. on 17 january 2012, the european commission opened an infringement procedure against hungary for restricting the independence of the national central bank, the courts, the personal data protection agency. citizens of each country acceding to the union must have the same rights and opportunities to defend them as other eu citizens. i therefore support the resolution, which calls in particular for the determination of whether the actions of the hungarian government are contrary to eu law, respectful of democratic principles the separation of powers, pluralism of political parties, and restrictive of the freedom of speech and religion, the right to a fair trial and other rights of hungarian citizens.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the situation in russia. by adopting this resolution parliament clearly shows its position regarding free and fair presidential elections in russia. in a number of mass demonstrations since the duma elections of 4 december 2011, the russian people have expressed their desire for more democracy, including free and fair elections and a comprehensive reform of the electoral system. we, members of the european parliament, call on the russian authorities to uphold fully freedom of assembly and freedom of speech in compliance with the constitution of the russian federation, and to introduce a package of legislative proposals aimed at developing a truly democratic political system. moreover, mikhail khodorkovsky’s continuing incarceration raises serious questions about russia’s commitment to the rule of law, judicial independence and human rights. observers attending his second trial condemned it as failing to meet acceptable standards of due process and independence. the eu must insist on russia meeting its obligations under international law with regard to civil, political and human rights. the kremlin should also act on the recommendations of the presidential commission on human rights, which has been highly critical of the conduct of the khodorkovsky trial.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document, as closer cooperation and good neighbourly relations between the eu and russia are crucial to ensuring the stability, security and prosperity of europe. the development of the strategic partnership between the eu and the russian federation can only be based on shared values. europe remains concerned about developments in the russian federation with regard to respect for and protection of human rights and respect for universally recognised democratic principles, electoral rules and procedures. as a full member of the council of europe and the organisation for security and cooperation in europe, the russian federation is committed to the principles of democracy and respect for human rights. i believe that it is necessary to pursue the development of a genuinely democratic political system, including reforms to provide for easier registration rules for both political parties and presidential candidates, and to address the problem of too strict registration rules in order to facilitate genuinely free and fair elections as soon as possible. it also requires a commitment to tackle the problems of freedom of the media, freedom of assembly and freedom of expression, and to develop the principles of democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law.
in writing. − the eu’s relations with the russian federation are very important for both sides. this country has shown some positive developments, as its recent accession to the wto shows. however, i supported this resolution which raises concerns about the human rights situation in russia. the osce did not consider the latest parliamentary elections in russia free and fair. the post-duma election events – huge demonstrations – testify that civil society in russia is growing stronger. however, there is serious alarm regarding the future presidential elections on 4 march. the russian people have expressed their will for more democracy and a comprehensive reform of the electoral system. the eu should support them and contribute to the establishment of favourable conditions for the exercising of democracy in russia. brussels should do its best to ensure social and democratic consolidation, respect for human rights and the exercising of citizens’ freedoms in russia.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i agree that trade and investment are among the tools used in the eu's neighbourhood policy as drivers of growth, helping to reduce poverty in developing countries, bringing people together, strengthening ties between peoples and contributing to political stability. in view of the political situation in the southern mediterranean countries following the arab spring, i therefore believe that a strong, effective and rapid eu response is needed to maintain a stable situation in this neighbouring eu country with which the union has close trade links. it is worth noting that trade in agricultural and fishery products accounts for about 18% of morocco's exports, and that the number of people employed in the agricultural sector in rural areas amounts to as much as 75% of the total workforce, demonstrating that the stability and development of this sector are of paramount importance for the political stability of the country. further liberalisation of trade in agricultural and fishery products between the eu and morocco is therefore necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document, as the opening up of markets and the gradual integration into the eu internal market can be powerful tools to promote the development of the southern mediterranean countries and help to reduce the widespread poverty and unemployment that are at the root of the region's economic, migration and security problems. this agreement is a constructive step towards promoting political stability and mutual sustainable economic development. however, concerns expressed in certain eu sectors about increased duty-free quotas for sensitive fruit and vegetable imports should be highlighted, and the commission should present an assessment of the impact on european producers, and in particular on farmers' incomes, and keep the european parliament informed.
in writing. − the agricultural and fisheries sectors are highly sensitive and important to the eu as a whole. it should be noted that the increased duty-free quotas threaten sensitive eu fruit and vegetable imports. in this context, the commission must carry out an assessment of the impact on incomes and establish compensation mechanisms for producers and farmers. in order to protect the interests of european economic operators, it is necessary to prevent fraud in the entry price system and to ensure its transparent functioning. in view of these circumstances, i consider it appropriate to continue to regulate the increased tariff quotas under the agreement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco on reciprocal liberalisation measures applicable to agricultural products, processed agricultural products, fish and fishery products.
in writing. − abstained, as the increase in reduced tariff quotas for a large number of fruit (oranges, mandarins, melons, strawberries) and vegetables (tomatoes, eggplants, cucumbers, garlic, cucumbers) would put european producers in a difficult competitive situation and would not support balanced agricultural development in morocco. many producer organisations are very concerned about the circumvention of the entry price system in this sector, especially for fresh tomatoes. this disruption allows operators to pay a lower import duty on fruit and vegetables by taking advantage of the current customs value provisions. the federation of spanish fruit and vegetable producers and exporters (fepex) even approached the ep's committee on petitions on the matter. the effectiveness of tariff protection and the control of the value of imports should be ensured before the new phase of market opening, when additional quotas are introduced. the environmental outlook is also negative and casts doubt on the eu's principle of environmental protection and the expected mitigation of climate change. the european commission has not always assessed the social, economic and environmental impact of this agreement, but has focused on tariff issues. a thorough investigation is necessary to enable parliament to take a decision in full knowledge of the matter.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this very important resolution on the situation in syria. we, members of the european parliament, deplore in the strongest terms the fact that russia and china have exercised their veto in the un security council to block the draft resolution on syria, thus voting against the peaceful transition proposal by the arab league, which was perceived by the assad regime as a licence to intensify the means of repression on the ground, using heavy weapons and indiscriminate force against unarmed civilians. it is regrettable that once again the eu has missed the opportunity for a more coordinated and effective response by the member states. moreover, eu action has not been able to stop the violence or overcome the veto of russia and china in the un. i support the idea that eu governments should increase their pressure on russia and china and regret the fact that this was not possible during the eu-china summit. we cannot remain calm observers in face of a massacre on this scale, tantamount to a crime against humanity.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document as it calls once again on the regime of bashar al-assad to immediately cease the violence against the syrian population, withdraw troops and tanks from the cities and release all detained protesters, political prisoners, human rights defenders, bloggers and journalists, and allow unhindered access to the country for international humanitarian and human rights organisations and international media. an independent and transparent investigation into the widespread, systematic and serious violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms committed by the syrian authorities and military and security forces is urgently needed to ensure that all those responsible for these acts, which may amount to crimes against humanity, are held accountable by the international community. the country must make a peaceful and effective transition to democracy, which is in line with the legitimate expectations of the syrian people and is based on an open dialogue involving all democratic forces and sections of syrian society, with a view to launching a process of deep democratic reforms, taking into account the need to achieve national reconciliation.
in writing. − in exerting their veto right in the un security council, russia and china chose to share responsibility with the al-assad regime for the increasing death toll of civilians and children, for the crimes against humanity and the continuation of violence. (russia and china voted also against un human rights council resolution establishing the mandate of a special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in syria and calling for human rights violations to stop and to be investigated). i do not believe this position gives credits in internal politics; the citizens of russia must be wondering whether tolerance to the deeds of the al-assad regime means such measures against opposition are also an option internally. the eu must utilise its dialogues with both china and russia to persuade them to stand on the side of universal values. (especially since the eu-russia strategic and extensive partnership is declared to be built upon common values). the eu high representative should bring a clear mandate and a united eu position to the meeting of friends of syria. time is scarce, as every day takes the country closer to the vicious circle of violence, revenge, militarisation and humanitarian disaster, threatening the whole region and beyond.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on parliament’s position on the 19th session of the un human rights council. the unhrc is a specific forum dealing with human rights within the un system and is entrusted with the important task of strengthening the promotion, protection and respect of human rights around the globe. we, members of the european parliament, welcome the designation of burma/myanmar, the democratic people’s republic of korea (dprk), syria, libya and iran as key issues, as those issues are also priorities of the eu. we also reiterate once more the call to eu member states to actively oppose any attempt to undermine the concept of universality, indivisibility and interdependence of human rights. we also condemn in the strongest terms the widespread brutal repression and systematic violations of human rights by the syrian regime against its population, including children, and call on the syrian authorities to bring an immediate end to violence and to comply with their obligations under international human rights law in order to allow a peaceful and democratic transition. in this regard, the decision to establish the mandate of special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in syria is highly welcomed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the european parliament's position on the forthcoming session of the united nations human rights council and the issues that it is intended to discuss. the european parliament agreed that priority discussions were to be held on the situation in burma, north korea, syria, libya and iran. parliament also welcomed the fact that public debates were planned on the integration of human rights, freedom of expression on the internet, freedom of religion or belief and conscience, discrimination and violence on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity, the declaration on human rights and hiv/aids, the declaration on the rights of minorities, and that extensive meetings were planned on the rights of the child, torture, human rights and the fight against terrorism, disappearances and arbitrary detention.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because respect for the universality of human rights, their promotion and protection, is part of the eu's ethical and legal acquis and one of the pillars of european unity and integrity. the ongoing review of the eu's human rights policy should contribute to making the eu's external policy a more active, coherent and effective force in the world. the eu and its member states should ensure respect for human rights in their own policies in order to enhance the coherence of internal and external policies and thus enhance the eu's credibility in the unhrc. all international actors must work to eliminate double standards and to prevent selectivity and politicisation in the treatment of human rights issues. the unhrc is a unique body with a special focus on universal human rights and a special forum within the un system for addressing human rights issues. it has the important task of strengthening the promotion, protection and respect of human rights worldwide.
in writing. − i believe that the 19th session of the unsc should pay particular attention to human rights violations in the arab spring countries and to discrimination of all kinds. the session should also include a wide-ranging discussion of the systematic and ongoing violence against christians in egypt and indonesia. it is important to note that in order to maintain a strong eu role in international forums dealing with human rights issues, it is essential that member states ensure respect for human rights in their domestic and foreign policies. this would avoid double standards and would also increase the coherence of internal and external policies and strengthen moral authority in the international arena.
in writing. − with the next un human rights council meeting approaching, it is clear that the eu must ensure respect for human rights in its policies in order to strengthen and make the eu's position credible in the un human rights council. europe's reputation has been badly damaged and will soon be irreparable. this is felt not only within europe but also among the other members of the un human rights council. the annual report of human rights watch, published last month, recalled the need for the eu and its member states to end the era of double standards. the report details how eu governments, including lithuania, have demonstrated a reluctance to tackle human rights violations in their countries. let me quote: 'the sad truth is that eu governments too often push rights at home aside when they seem to be unwelcome, especially for vulnerable minorities, and reject criticism of abuse.' this is the case for lithuania, which was described as a 'flawed democracy' in the 'democracy index' published in january. i hope that the next session of the un human rights council will be a fair and objective assessment of the human rights situation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the world and european organisations representing the blind have put forward a proposal for an internationally binding treaty providing for a targeted copyright exception. the european commission and the council, meanwhile, propose that the european union conclude stakeholder agreements and draw up a non-binding recommendation. the european blind community is not satisfied with this proposal. at present, there is no legal provision for an exception to copyright for the international distribution of printed matter in formats adapted to the disabled. i therefore asked the commission in the course of the debate whether it did not think that, in order to change the situation, it was necessary to amend international copyright laws in such a way as to allow the sharing of book collections throughout the european union and beyond without infringing those laws. i called on the european commission and the council to adopt a binding 'books without borders' treaty, which would allow the worldwide sharing of books in special formats for the blind and visually impaired. we need to be even more decisive in tackling discrimination against people with disabilities and in removing existing barriers to their inclusion. this is also supported by the world intellectual property organisation and the commission and the council should therefore also support this binding treaty.
in writing. − i voted in favour because the access of blind and visually impaired people in the eu to books and other printed material is very limited, as 95% of all published works have never been presented in the appropriate format, such as braille, large print or audio. there is currently no legal framework in the world that could be applied to the targeted exception to copyright rules for the international distribution of printed matter in formats adapted to the disabled. the world intellectual property organization (wipo) is considering the possibility of concluding an international treaty to improve access to books for the blind and other visually impaired. the eu representatives consistently opposed a legally binding text, preferring non-binding recommendations. the european parliament, in its report 'unlocking the potential of the cultural and creative sectors' of 13 april 2011, called for the conclusion of a legally binding ipa. the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, in particular articles 21 and 30 thereof, and the european charter of fundamental rights lay down the principles prohibiting discrimination against persons with disabilities. the council and the commission are therefore invited to support the binding wipo copyright treaty on books and printed matter for the blind and visually impaired.
in writing. − currently, only 5% of books and other printed material in the european union are accessible (in braille, large print or audio) to blind and partially sighted people. the rigid requirements for the protection of intellectual property rights have severely restricted access of persons with disabilities to culture, education and active public life. the publication of tailor-made books is largely dependent on the goodwill of the copyright holders. in lithuania alone, there are about 7,000 people with the most severe visual impairment. the european disability strategy 2010-2020 aims to ensure that people with disabilities can participate in all aspects of daily life throughout the eu, and to develop inclusive and quality education policies. it is therefore necessary to remedy this situation and to seek to provide for appropriate relaxations and exemptions to intellectual property rights that not only do not prevent but also encourage the publication of books for the blind, visually impaired and dyslexic. i believe that the eu, which has set itself ambitious targets in its strategy, should not be satisfied with recommendations alone, but should go further and seek to adopt an agreement within the framework of the world intellectual property organisation, binding both within and outside the eu. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution calling on the council and the commission to speak in favour of a binding treaty within the framework of the cotonou agreement.
in writing. − i support this resolution because the blind and other visually impaired must have unrestricted access to books and the problem of the ability of people who cannot read printed text to read books must finally be solved. it is also necessary to lay down legal rules ensuring adequate protection of the copyright of books and printed matter intended for the blind. only through the implementation of these measures will discrimination against persons with disabilities be prevented and the full and non-discriminatory enjoyment of fundamental human rights and freedoms be ensured for all persons with any disability.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i strongly support the view that blind people deserve better protection and better opportunities. there are about 15,000 blind people in lithuania. many of them are often isolated, unable to find employment or even to shop without help. the situation of deaf and hearing people is even more complex. they represent one of the most socially isolated groups in lithuania and europe. there are at least 150 000 deaf and hard of hearing people in the eu. the exact number of such people in lithuania is not known, since in my country this disability is not officially recognized, nor is there any program to provide the best possible assistance to blind and deaf people. there is also no training for professionals who can assess the needs of deaf and hearing people, or for translators who can help them. in lithuania, blind and deaf people do not have the right to receive the assistance they need for work or to receive daily social care provided by a specialist. it is important that deafness and blindness are recognised as a separate form of disability, as services that are adapted to persons with a hearing or visual impairment are not suitable for blind and deaf people. i also believe that blind and deaf children have the right to receive education, either in a primary school or in a special school, depending on their individual needs.
in writing. − i believe that the application of this convention will overcome the lack of social, commercial and economic integration in the mediterranean region. it will also help the eu to develop and strengthen its trade relations with the arab countries. international trade is a key driver of economic growth and long-term job creation. trade and open markets reduce prices and increase consumer choice. the convention will thus facilitate access to the eu internal market for goods produced and accumulated in the mediterranean region. i believe that a dispute settlement mechanism should be included in the convention in order to deal with the verification of proof of origin in an efficient and expeditious manner.
in writing. − i, as a member of european parliament and a member of the committee on international trade, voted in favour of this resolution as the adoption of the convention is a very relevant step in the creation of a possible free trade area in the mediterranean. the convention integrates all the protocols on rules of origin in force between all the partners indicated; therefore in the end there will a single system on rules of origin in the trades in this area. the practical result of the application of the convention will be a strong boost to and the dynamism of trade exchanges in the area as well as stronger political relations. it also has a political importance especially in the view of recent developments in middle east countries.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it is the european parliament's contribution to the debate currently taking place in the eu institutions on the financing of the european earth observation programme. indeed, there is currently disagreement on the future funding of this european earth observation programme, which raises concerns about the future of this programme. failure to secure adequate funding or to secure long-term and stable funding would result in even higher costs over time, unequal access to relevant information for citizens, the programme being suspended or even suspended and its data being discontinued. this would ultimately mean that the investments made so far have not paid off and that europe would lose its independence in this space infrastructure and halt its technological progress. in its resolution, parliament thus criticised the european commission for failing to act without initiating the necessary legislative action and expressed its disapproval of the system of financing and management of the european earth observation programme proposed by the commission.
in writing. − the european earth observation programme is clearly delivering economic, social and technological benefits. in order to achieve the objectives set for the implementation of this programme, it is necessary to establish the appropriate governance and long-term funding of the gmes programme. otherwise, without the necessary financial support, europe will suffer major losses and lose its independence in the area of space infrastructure. in order to avoid these possible negative consequences and to ensure the proper development of the programme, hasty decisions should be avoided.
