in writing. gender equality is one of the european union's core values and it is therefore essential that this area is given continuous attention. the report rightly emphasises the need to increase women's economic independence. this is particularly important not only in the fight against poverty but also in ensuring better social protection for women of retirement age, as the amount of pensions depends directly on the length of service and earnings. although the employment rate of women is increasing steadily, it is still below that of men by 13%. a welcome exception here would seem to be lithuania, where the female employment rate was almost 2% higher than the male unemployment rate in 2010 and even 7.8% lower than the male unemployment rate. however, the quality of women's employment should be considered here. however, i would explain these figures by the fact that women are willing to work even for low pay. in fact, 31.4% of european women work part-time, mostly for family reasons, compared with only 8.1% of men. in the light of these two facts, it is clear that it is still too difficult for women to achieve economic independence in europe today. in this context, i believe that measures should be taken to help working parents by ensuring that member states have sufficient quality, accessible and affordable childcare services.
the decisions taken by the european council in early march on greece appear to have paid off. at least, it seems so for now. but as we look to the future, we should perhaps remember the words of the italian prime minister, professor monti, who said it right here: democracy and globalisation can and must coexist. indeed, if we want to preserve europe as a union of sovereign states, we must fundamentally change our attitude to responsibility. the governments of the member states must pursue responsible policies and, if such policies are indeed to become the alpha and omega of each country, no fiscal discipline pacts will be necessary. if the member states follow this principle and manage their finances responsibly, and give due attention to the promotion of the single market, innovation and research, then we can be on the road to preserving the european union.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i know that many of the questions have already been answered by our president so, if you will allow me, i will just focus on the issues which have been most frequently mentioned by the honourable members, particularly jobs, growth and where to find investment in order to support policies in both these areas. but first i would like to assure the honourable members of this house that unemployment, and especially youth unemployment, is one of the five key priorities on which we would like the whole european union to focus this year. this was the conclusion of the annual growth survey. this is one of the priorities for the european semester where we, of course, would expect this priority to feature very highly in the national reform programmes of each and every member state because we are fully aware of how painful this is for our citizens and how difficult it is for our economies not to have enough high-quality jobs. what the commission will do further is that already in april we will be putting forward an employment policy package. we are doing our best to help the eu as such and our member states to improve the functioning of the labour market and to create better conditions for the creation of jobs. we would like to focus on the possibilities across the whole economy, but we would also like to be even more concentrated in the areas and sectors where we see a big potential for the new jobs, such as health care, white sector, information, communications technologies and the ict sector as such. we are also going to tackle the problems and the obstacles which still hamper the free movement of labour and labour mobility within the european union. in particular we would like to assist the young people who are witnessing unprecedented pressure on the labour market. we are absolutely convinced that we cannot afford to have 7.5 million young people who are not employed and not in education or in training. we therefore deployed eight action teams from the commission which have already come back from the member states with concrete ideas. we are going to implement them together with the member states and the social partners in these countries. of course we support youth job guarantees. we would like every young european to have a chance to get – within a very short period of time after completing his or her studies – either a job or to have the possibility of continuing their education or, if there is not a particular job available, to work towards requalification or get into retraining so we can use the potential of our young generation in the european union. to do that we are also going to improve the tools which would help young people to seek jobs. we are going to improve and introduce the new scheme, ‘your first eures job’, which should help young people in finding opportunities on the labour market. then of course the question is where to find the investment and where to find the money to be invested in the economy, especially in this time of austerity where budget consolidation is a very clear priority. we would not like to repeat the dramatic events we have gone through in the last two years. with regard to the creation of new jobs and employment, we believe that we still can do much better with the money which is available from eu funds. to date we have eur 22 billion in the european social fund and eur 62 billion in the structural and cohesion funds which have not yet been spent. we want to help the member states to have another look at spending priorities – how they can reprogramme them and use them for the active labour policy so we can create new jobs, for young people in particular, but of course for every european. several ideas have been mentioned as to where we can generate more income and more investments. i think that we have complete agreement on them because the commission is very much in favour of the introduction of a financial transaction tax. it was a proposal which we made and we are working very hard with the member states to convince them because, as you know, we need unanimity on this issue. we are advancing our work on project bonds because our simulations show very promising results. we can actually use eur 230 million from the eu budget and leverage it, together with the eib, to eur 700 million. this would end up, raising the money on the private market, with the sum of eur 3.5 billion. this is money we can spend on infrastructure, on ict and on projects which generate a lot of employment and which improve the overall competitiveness of the european union. you know that we support own resources and we make this point at every single negotiation meeting which takes place with member states. you know – because you are getting the information from your negotiators – that this discussion is difficult but we are truly convinced that, if we want to have a more transparent budget and less drama when we are negotiating multiannual financial frameworks (mff), we need solid own resources for the eu budget. i would say one more thing even. i think that, if we look at investment policy, one of the best investment tools we have in the eu is the eu budget. where in the world would you find a budget where 94% of the budget goes back to the member states with the high value-added proposals supporting in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the speakers that we have had a thorough discussion and concrete agreements in the european council on increasing the social dimension in all eu policies, and in particular in the growth of the member states' economies. i believe that fiscal consolidation, greater coordination of member states' economies and stricter financial discipline are the necessary measures to restore proper balance to our economies and put them in the right direction. however, it is clear from the current state of the eu that fiscal discipline and austerity alone will not achieve the economic growth we are seeking. today, europe is facing a massive increase in unemployment among working age people, a particularly bad situation with youth unemployment, and a difficult time for businesses, especially small and medium-sized businesses, all of which are only delaying the economic recovery of individual member states and, in the process, the eu as a whole. the five key priorities for growth and employment adopted by the 2012 edf will require much greater efforts than before. i think it is very important that member states set out concrete and measurable commitments in their national reform programmes and that the commission monitors implementation of these commitments more closely.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution concerning the mutual legal assistance agreement with norway and iceland, which will improve judicial cooperation in criminal matters between the member states of the eu and iceland and norway by applying certain provisions of the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between member states of the european union and the 2001 protocol to iceland and norway. cooperation will involve the hearing of witnesses, experts and accused persons by telephone or video conference, controlled deliveries, covert investigations and joint investigation teams and requests for information on banking transactions, bank accounts and their monitoring to combat crime in general and organised crime in particular. i believe this will help to combat trans-border crime and enhance cooperation with the two countries and will serve to make the eu safer and more secure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this recommendation. the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states aims to promote and modernise judicial, police and customs cooperation and to better combat cross-border crime. the agreement with iceland and norway aims to improve judicial cooperation in criminal matters between the member states of the european union and iceland and norway. the agreement with these countries was signed six years ago and, in view of its importance, i support the european parliament's recommendation to conclude the agreement without delay.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament recommendation as the agreement between the european union, the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway on mutual assistance by the member states of the european union in criminal matters seeks to improve judicial cooperation between the eu member states, norway and iceland by applying almost all the provisions of the convention on mutual legal assistance between the member states of the european union of 2000 and its 2001 protocol. this agreement includes provisions on the questioning of witnesses, experts and accused persons by telephone or videoconference, on controlled transport, on secret investigations and joint investigation teams, and on the request for information on banking transactions, bank accounts and their monitoring, in order to combat organised crime. the european parliament supports this agreement as it extends the rules on mutual legal assistance already in force and in most cases applied in the member states to norway and iceland. this will certainly help in the fight against cross-border crime. it will also improve cooperation with these two countries, which are already part of the schengen area and are currently negotiating their accession to the european union.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this regulation which aims to remove the obstacles to the free movement of persons who currently face difficulties in asserting their rights in the context of a succession with cross-border implications. at present, citizens have difficulties in foreseeing which country and authority (court, notary, administrator, etc.) have competence in handling the succession and this situation obviously creates legal uncertainty because citizens must be able to organise their succession in advance. this regulation will enable citizens to organise their succession in advance by choosing the law applicable to their wills. this regulation introduces a european certificate of succession which will enable the succession to be settled in a shorter period of time.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. with the increasing mobility of citizens in the eu, civil and commercial legal relationships involving interests in several member states often raise various questions such as which member state's court has jurisdiction to decide the issue in question, which legal system will apply, what the procedure for recognition and enforcement of judgments is, etc. the treaty establishing the european community provides for the progressive establishment of an area of freedom, security and justice, for example by means of judicial cooperation in civil matters. this proposed regulation will aim to address legal issues relating to cross-border succession in order to provide eu citizens with greater legal clarity and simplicity in the exercise of their rights in cross-border succession cases. this regulation also introduces an important innovation, the european certificate of succession, which will enable heirs, administrators of succession or executors of wills to prove their status without any further formalities. this will be a major improvement over the current situation, and will make the process of probate quicker and cheaper.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the creation of a uniform system for dealing with succession matters throughout the european union. i also support the creation of the european certificate of succession, as i believe that this document will avoid a lot of unnecessary administrative procedures for heirs, executors of wills and administrators of assets. this eu legislation will be particularly useful in the future for our citizens, who are increasingly moving abroad to live and work or simply to buy property in foreign countries. however, it is regrettable that, at least for the time being, england and ireland have declared their non-participation to this regulation because of the specific rules in their countries on certain aspects of succession. the accession of these countries to the regulation is of course of great importance, especially for our citizens, and the european parliament has therefore called on the council to continue to seek ways of reaching a compromise with these countries on the question of succession.
in writing. − i abstained in the vote on the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on jurisdiction, applicable law, judicial decisions and authentic instruments in matters of succession, recognition and enforcement and on the taking into use of the european certificate of succession, as england and ireland have declared their non-accession to the regulation due to specific regulations in their countries on certain aspects of succession. the accession of these countries to the regulation is very important, especially for our citizens, who often go to work and live in these countries, so it is necessary to look for additional ways to reach a compromise with these countries on the issue of inheritance so that these countries join this regulation. i am only in favour of creating a uniform system across the european union to deal with succession issues. i also support the creation of a european certificate of succession, as i believe that this document will avoid a lot of unnecessary administrative procedures for heirs, executors of wills and administrators of estates, but both england and ireland must participate in this system to ensure a uniform system without exceptions.
in writing. − the initiative to create a european certificate of succession and to introduce a new right of choice that would increase the autonomy of citizens is welcome. however, given the importance of this issue, no hasty decisions can be taken. in order to ensure that the application of this regulation does not lead to any abuse or circumvention of the provisions of the law, detailed discussions should be held. every person must be guaranteed that the choice of the law applicable to him, when he does not have his habitual residence or wishes to settle in a state other than that of origin, will not create an additional burden for him and that questions of succession will be dealt with in an appropriate and effective manner.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the progress on equality between women and men in the european union in 2011. sensitive issues of today’s society are reflected and incorporated in the report: implementing the principle of equal treatment between persons irrespective of religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation, abortion, the gender pay gap, the role of women in decision-making and the use of quotas in company boards or in politics, and maternity leave. these are still under-solved and unequally treated problems in europe and i believe, with improved support and further actions identified, europe will improve the living environment for its citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the eu is making a major effort to promote greater equality between women and men in all eu policies. i agree that there are still many unresolved issues, in particular the question of the proper assessment of social work, social protection and pensions for people who care for children or elderly people at home. i agree that there is a need to increase investment in accessible high-quality childcare facilities and care facilities for the sick, disabled, elderly or other people in need of care, and to ensure the working age and social protection of those who provide care at home.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report of the european parliament because equality between men and women is a fundamental principle of the european union enshrined in the treaty on european union. despite gradual progress in gender equality, many differences between women and men still persist. although a great many campaigns, targets and measures have been set in recent years to achieve equal pay for equal work or work of equal value, the large gender pay gap has not been reduced. across the european union, women earn on average 17.5% less than men, and the gender pay gap has narrowed very little in the last few years. member states must therefore step up their efforts to reduce this gap by implementing the existing eu provisions. the european parliament calls on the commission to present as soon as possible an eu strategy to end violence against women, including legal criminal law measures to combat gender-based violence, as requested by parliament in several of its resolutions. the european parliament also calls on the commission to declare 2015 the european union year of the end of violence against women.
in writing. − the european union plays an important role in ensuring gender equality and combating discrimination. the aim of increasing women's participation in the labour market and providing them with opportunities for high positions, such as on company boards, must remain a priority. however, despite the positive aspects of this document, i abstained in my vote because i believe that the objective of increasing the representation of women in all types of eu enterprises and introducing mandatory measures that the business sector would have to take is inadequate and would potentially restrict the freedom of enterprise. starting with the public sector, sharing good practice with the business world. the business sector must decide what is best for them, not us setting the mandatory measures. the debate on the economic crisis and its consequences is still ongoing, and we are looking for binding measures to tighten the business sector. on the contrary, we should promote economic growth and entrepreneurship.
in writing. − it is important to note that ensuring equal opportunities for men and women is one of the eu's core values. it is therefore essential that both men and women are provided with the appropriate conditions to achieve a work-life balance. the state should create opportunities and rights, but the people have to decide. in order to meet the needs of european families and the european economy, member states should draw up legislative plans for maternity and paternity leave as a matter of urgency. given the ever-increasing number of people in the world, family planning should be one of the priorities on the political agenda. it is also essential to make further progress in reducing maternal mortality rates and to improve access to quality reproductive health services. in addition, member states should pay greater attention to social work, ensuring that it is properly valued and paid for.
in writing. − i supported this report because equality between women and men is a fundamental principle of the european union and many women still face discrimination, poverty and stereotypes in their everyday lives. as the rapporteur noted, women hold the position of ceo in the eu member states on average only in 12% of the most important listed companies, and only in 3% of the management positions. in addition, women receive 17% and lithuania 19% less pay for equal work done by men. as mentioned in the debates, where member states have established quotas and other legally binding measures, greater progress is being made and equality between women and men is much more assured. action is therefore needed at both national and european level to increase women's participation in decision-making in the public and private sectors, to improve the labour market position of women and to increase their economic independence, in order to reach the eu target of 75% employment of women and men aged 20-64 by 2020. i also support the fight against violence against women and calls for gender equality outside the eu.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, gender equality is far from being achieved in lithuania or in the eu. the report notes that, although legislation has changed, traditional gender stereotypes remain a serious obstacle to fundamental change. in lithuania, there is a clear gender pay gap. the gender pay gap in lithuania is over 21%, one of the highest in the eu, and has increased by 5% over the last six years. in this context, the gender pay gap could reach 25% within a few years unless appropriate measures are taken. the gender pay gap is more pronounced in the private sector, where women are paid less than men for the same work. a report published by the institute for the study of labour argues that the gender pay gap in the eu is not just a glass ceiling problem, but a floor problem. for example, the gender pay gap is higher between the highest and lowest earners in lithuania. improving the situation requires more transparent wage scales in enterprises and stronger measures against enterprises that do not respect the principle of gender equality. in the face of the crisis, more attention needs to be paid to economic equality. lower wages for women inevitably lead not only to lower incomes but also to lower pension benefits.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. reliable, accurate and high-quality statistical data are necessary to provide a fair and objective assessment of the current economic, social, financial and other situations in the member states and to ensure that economic and budgetary policies are effectively formulated at member state and eu level on the basis of these data. at present, all member states are subject to some 350 statistical regulations, there is no standardisation of public sector accounting systems and no general mandatory rules on the compilation and accuracy of statistical data. this raises the risk that member states' data may be inaccurate and may not reflect the real situation in the member states, which may impede the effective implementation of the economic governance package and reduce the ability of member states to revitalise their economies and promote growth and employment. i agree with the need to move towards a common european quality management of statistical data, especially financial data, to establish uniform and mandatory principles for the production of statistical data and to introduce standardised public sector accounting systems in all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report by the european parliament because reliable and accurate statistics are essential for the effective formulation of economic and budgetary policies in the member states at the level of the european union. the users of european statistics should be provided with timely and accurate data collected and compiled by the national agencies, in accordance with the principles of impartiality, objectivity and professional independence. the european parliament therefore supports the commission's intention to propose an amendment to the statistical data regulation to allow for the monitoring and evaluation of public finance data at an early stage, in order to allow for corrective action to be taken as soon as possible, and supports the proposal to establish a legal framework to strengthen the governance framework, in particular as regards the professional independence of the national statistical authorities and eurostat. in addition, member states should be required to formally commit themselves to taking all necessary measures to maintain confidence in statistical data and to facilitate a stronger commitment to the principles of the implementation of the european statistical code of practice. eurostat should explore ways of making its printed publications, especially those available online, more accessible to the general public and non-professionals, in particular with regard to the use of charts. the eurostat website should facilitate access to comprehensive long-term disaggregated data and provide intuitive and comparative charts in order to provide citizens with additional benefits.
in writing. − i have endorsed this report because reliable and accurate statistics are essential for effective economic and budgetary policy-making in the member states at eu level. the emerging sovereign debt crisis in the euro area has exposed the risks of statistical inaccuracy and statistical falsification, which arise both from the quality of the original public sector accounting data and from the shortcomings of the current statistical governance arrangements. i also agree with the view that a partial amendment of the statistical data regulation is necessary to establish a proactive approach to the monitoring and evaluation of public finance data at an early stage, to allow for corrective action as soon as possible, and with the proposal to establish a legal framework to strengthen the governance system, in particular as regards the professional independence of the national statistical authorities and eurostat, and to require member states to formally commit themselves to taking all necessary measures to maintain confidence in statistical data.
in writing. − as recent practice has shown, the lack of transparency in the provision of statistical data, and the disparate approach to their quality in different eu member states, have been one of the reasons for the discrepancies between the declared and the actual economic and financial situation of some countries to be observed so late. i therefore support the provision that common high quality management standards for statistical data should be applied to ensure the independence and transparency of the authorities and officials collecting and processing statistical information. but it is essential that these criteria are applied both within the eu institutions and in all eu member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the management of the quality of statistical data is crucial for effective economic and budgetary policy-making. moreover, these data are an effective tool to monitor and evaluate public finance data at an early stage. to that end, statistical data should be publicly available and easily understandable to policy-makers and citizens. in order to achieve the objectives set, i believe it is appropriate to give eurostat greater powers of investigation and to strengthen the link between this institution and the audit authorities. it is important to note that each member state is responsible for the accuracy and reliability of the statistical data. in this context, it is necessary to use standardised public sector accounting systems and to continuously improve their functioning. in addition, each member state must undertake to take all necessary measures to maintain confidence in its statistics.
in writing. − the report rightly points out that reliable statistical data are essential for effective policy-making at member state and union level. i believe that statistics should be accessible to the public and understandable to both policy-makers and citizens. they must also be honest and impartial. the biggest problem in lithuania today is the gap between what official statistics say about economic activity and how people perceive their living conditions. often, this difference is not due to the poor quality of official statistics but to their misuse. this may lead to biased analysis, misguided policy objectives and may undermine both the credibility of political action and the genuine functioning of lithuanian democracy. for example, while lithuania's leaders and their statistics suggest that the economic situation is recovering and improving, the reality is different. the latest erdf report revealed that over the past year, life satisfaction in lithuania has decreased by 10%. the report also states that young lithuanians' belief in a better future has declined by 20 percent. we need to rebuild trust, and we can only do this if policy action - backed by unbiased statistics - has a tangible impact on people's lives.

i would like to ask a question to commissioner andor. indeed, the free movement of workers is not only an attractive freedom for the european union but also a factor in increasing europe's economic competitiveness. countries that attract skilled workers gain competitive advantages. at the same time, however, countries which leave a large number of skilled workers lose competitiveness. in addition, there are additional pressures on the sustainability of pension and social security systems. my question is: what measures should the european union take, what are the proposals of the european commission, to balance the benefits that free movement of workers can bring to the competitiveness of all the member states? does the european commission envisage any action to compensate for the losses suffered by the countries of high emigration? i have asked the commissioner about this before and perhaps some time has passed and there is some progress. so i would like to know the answers to these questions.
member of the commission. − i agree with the implication of your question: that we need not only to promote free movement in europe, but also to balance the benefits of free movement in the european union. our action to promote free movement takes the form of ensuring that the barriers come down. these barriers are of various kinds; while there are still administrative barriers, and issues related to the single market such as the recognition of diplomas, there are also natural barriers linked, for example, to the existence of many different languages, including the 23 official languages. this is also significant, especially if we compare ourselves to the united states. however, difficulties also arise in connection with the great imbalances – and uneven wage levels – between various countries, which drive movements of workers from one country to another. this occurs, especially, where regions – or sometimes even countries – are in recession, with high unemployment rates, and people move to countries where there are jobs available. i think it is important to ensure that there is freedom of movement and that people who arrive in a country are welcome if they come to work. however, we are also working to achieve a more circular form of free movement whereby, after a certain period in the course of which they gain experience and income, people also return to their home country. we also want to ensure that such movement becomes more demand-driven, and that people do not just leave their homeland but have a greater awareness of the concrete vacancies that exist. that is why we developed the vacancy monitor as part of the agenda for new skills and jobs. that is also why the forthcoming new initiative on the eures programme will help develop eures – which is a great network for advising people who seek work in another member state – to be more robust and more demand-driven. finally, in order to fully counterbalance the trend of population and labour movements inside europe, we obviously have to take cohesion policy very seriously and ensure that more peripheral regions do not remain in stagnation or recession, but regain the potential for economic growth.

in writing. − i have repeatedly stressed that the preparation of the eu budget is, on the one hand, a great opportunity to tackle the real problems facing europe - unemployment, economic recession - and, on the other hand, an opportunity to demonstrate that austerity measures must start from within. i therefore support the view that the eu budget for the coming years must be geared to tackling the crisis, promoting job creation (especially for young people), scientific and technical progress and resource efficiency, but also to making the administrative machinery more efficient and reducing costs.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i believe that the current monetary union system makes it difficult to respond adequately to the current or future economic and social crisis. it should be noted that the budget is not sufficiently flexible. it cannot be increased and made more effective without leading to a weakening of democracy in all member states. the measures to restore sovereignty should therefore be applied in order to restore the economy effectively. europe urgently needs to tackle unemployment and rising poverty. i think it is very important that not only the commission but also the member states give priority to these problems. in particular, it is essential that adequate eu funding continues to be available to support growth efforts. there is a need to identify concrete actions to reduce poverty, promote growth and create jobs, and ways to complement national measures and programmes from the eu budget. in addition, the application of stricter eu funding standards should primarily support companies that do not relocate their operations outside the eu. the budget should include specific actions to support sustainable and long-term industrial policy, competitiveness and smes. eib support for smes and infrastructure should be considered as a top priority.
in writing. - i voted in favour of setting up a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. this temporary committee will analyse and assess the extent and impact of organised crime, corruption and money laundering on the european union and its member states, and make proposals in these areas to make the eu better equipped to prevent and combat these threats more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament decision on the establishment of a special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering to analyse and assess the extent and impact of organised crime, corruption and money laundering on the european union and its member states. the committee will have to propose appropriate measures to enable the european union to prevent and combat these threats at international, european and national levels. the committee will also analyse and assess the current implementation of european union legislation in the areas of organised crime, corruption and money laundering. it will also examine and verify the role and performance of the european union's internal affairs agencies, such as europol, cosi and eurojust, in dealing with organised crime, corruption and money laundering and related areas of security policy. the special committee will be required to organise visits and hearings with the european union institutions and international, european and national institutions, national parliaments and governments of the member states and third countries, representatives of the scientific community, business and civil society, as well as with the general public, victim organisations, officials involved in the daily fight against organised crime, corruption and money laundering, such as law enforcement officers, judges and court officials.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because it establishes a special committee to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the objective of this special committee is to analyse and assess the current implementation of union legislation in the areas of organised crime, corruption and money laundering and related policies, with a view to ensuring that union legislation and policy is evidence-based and based on the best available threat assessment, and to monitor its compatibility with fundamental rights. i believe that we must take all possible measures to prevent these threats, which is why i have voted in favour of the establishment of this special committee.
in writing. − i think it is appropriate to set up a special committee to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering. organized crime is almost always linked to corruption and therefore poses a serious threat not only to the system of governance of a country but also to the political security of the eu as a whole. this is a problem of concern to society and the eu as a whole, and it requires adequate measures to address it. this special committee will help to develop radical measures to prevent crime and corruption at international, national and european levels, which will prevent the spread of threats and allow a complex response to the causes of these phenomena. in addition, the committee will contribute to the development and strengthening of the information, analytical and scientific methodological basis for prevention in the exercise of the functions assigned to it.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, this report is of great importance for lithuania. corruption continues to undermine the lithuanian economy and society. according to the latest corruption perceptions index, lithuania is ranked 19th out of all the eu countries. lithuania scored 4.8 out of 10 (10 points given to a country with high transparency). according to the report, 9 out of 10 lithuanians believe that corruption is the biggest problem facing their country. the head of transparency international, who recently visited lithuania, said that "lithuania's anti-corruption laws and other legislation are welcomed by lawyers and businessmen, but the laws themselves do not work". he's right. i know. we urgently need proper law enforcement. the rapporteur also touches on the problem of organised crime, which unfortunately continues to poison lithuania. earlier this year, europol identified lithuania as one of the five organised crime hotspots in europe with particularly active drug and cigarette smuggling into and out of russia. the situation will worsen if no action is taken in the near future. according to international media, lithuania's shadow economy is likely to account for 20-22 percent of its gross domestic product by 2015.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. in its previous resolutions, the european parliament has already expressed the view that the european area of justice must be based on a common judicial culture of lawyers, judges and prosecutors. discussion fora should be encouraged to discuss the establishment of common principles of professional ethics, the rule of law and the principles of the appointment and selection of judges, avoiding the politicisation of the judiciary and promoting mutual trust. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, in particular the countries of the former soviet union, the former soviet union and the former soviet union. i support the call in the resolution for an annual forum of judges of all categories to express their views on the problems of the existing legal system, to stimulate more in-depth discussions, to contribute to the formulation of concrete proposals and to improve legal education in europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because the current training is far from meeting the european commission's objective of providing such training to half of the legal professions in the eu. the study found that the most common reasons for the low number of people receiving training in eu law (53%, and only one third in the last three years) are language barriers, lack of timely information on available programmes, the fact that programmes are not always tailored to the needs of judges, the high workload of judges and the lack of appropriate funding. the european area of justice must therefore be based on a common judicial culture of lawyers, judges and prosecutors, which is not only based on eu law but also developed on the basis of mutual knowledge and understanding of national judicial systems, through a fundamental rethinking of university curricula, exchanges, study visits and joint training, actively supported by the european law academy, the european judicial training network and the european law institute. the further objective would be to coordinate the training provided by existing judicial training schools and to facilitate and promote dialogue and cooperation between professionals. the european parliament proposes that the commission organise an annual forum where judges from all categories working in the field of law can discuss the latest cases of legal disputes or difficulties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because the european area of justice must be based on a common judicial culture of lawyers, judges and prosecutors, not only based on eu law, but also developed on the basis of mutual knowledge and understanding of national legal systems, through a fundamental re-think of university curricula, exchanges, study visits and joint training, actively supported by the european law academy, the european judicial training network and the european law institute. it is necessary to develop a common judicial culture among judges, drawing on the charter of fundamental rights and the work of the venice commission of the council of europe, in order to promote the core values of the judicial profession, to discuss and disseminate common professional ethics, the rule of law and the principles of the appointment and selection of judges, and to avoid the politicisation of the judicial system, while fostering the mutual trust necessary for the creation of a common area of justice. finally, it is proposed that the commission organise an annual forum where judges of all categories working in areas of law that often involve issues at both domestic and cross-border level could discuss the latest cases of legal disputes or difficulties, in order to stimulate discussion, establish contacts, establish channels of communication and cooperation and build mutual trust and understanding.
in writing. - i support this resolution. it should be noted that the organisation of courses for judges is very complex, given their high level of employment and the need to ensure judicial independence. it is therefore essential that training is properly coordinated and adequately funded. the training aims at developing a european judicial culture. it is also essential that the training be tailored to the specific needs of the judges and address the relevant legal issues. i think it would be very practical and effective to train judges to use the latest technology to save costs and to improve their knowledge. in addition, the training should be provided in different languages, thus enabling judges to participate in training in other member states. this will encourage exchange programmes.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, as the rapporteur points out, reducing the politicisation of the judiciary is necessary for the strength and well-being of lithuania's democracy. unfortunately, this is an area that is very neglected in lithuania. public confidence in the lithuanian judicial system remains very low. according to the latest data from freedom house, public distrust of the judiciary in lithuania increased sharply in 2011 (up to 44 percent). the report emphasises the need for judicial reform. the small and gradual changes that have been achieved are not enough. suspects in custody are not always provided with timely legal assistance and long pre-trial detention remains a problem. freedom house notes that unlawful police actions against detainees, including minors, continue to be reported, and that judges and prosecutors are responding inadequately to such actions. the weaknesses of the lithuanian legal system are an essential part of the larger problem. according to the latest bertelsmann survey, only 50% of lithuanians think they live in a country where all political rights are granted. i agree with the rapporteur and i think we should try to strengthen the core values of the judicial profession and create a judicial culture. this is essential to build mutual trust between the state and its citizens.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. forced child labour and exploitation remain one of the major problems, particularly in the least developed countries. the cocoa sector is characterised by poverty, outdated farming techniques and child labour. the european parliament has repeatedly expressed concern about the exploitation of children in this sector. i agree that the eu must do more to combat this phenomenon, in particular by including provisions against child exploitation in all trade agreements. it is also necessary to ensure that the eu consistently pursues such positions in all areas, in particular trade and development, to ensure the proper implementation of human rights, social and environmental standards and to apply appropriate sanctions where these standards are not respected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because we must condemn in the strongest terms the use of child labour on cocoa plantations. unacceptable child labour in the cultivation of cocoa trees and the harvesting of cocoa beans shall not be tolerated. the international labour organization (ilo) has estimated that more than 215 million children worldwide are engaged in child labor and in activities that should be prohibited. the european parliament calls on all stakeholders involved in the production and processing of cocoa beans and cocoa products, i.e. governments, the global industry, cocoa producers, trade unions, non-governmental organisations and consumers, to fulfil their respective commitments in the fight against all forms of forced child labour and trafficking in children, to share experiences and to cooperate in order to eliminate the use of child labour in the cocoa supply chain. the european commission should ensure that all trade agreements include effective provisions on poverty reduction and the promotion of decent and safe working conditions and that agreements establish legally binding conditions relating to and the implementation of internationally recognised human rights, social and environmental standards, as well as measures to be applied in the event of violations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution as it calls on all stakeholders involved in the production and processing of cocoa beans and derived products, i.e. governments, the global industry, cocoa producers, trade unions, non-governmental organisations and consumers, to fulfil their respective commitments in the fight against all forms of forced child labour and child trafficking, to share experiences and to cooperate in order to make the cocoa supply chain sustainable and to eliminate the use of child labour. a comprehensive and coordinated plan to tackle the root causes of child labour and to be implemented over time by governments, industry, traders, producers and civil society is the only way to achieve substantial change. i agree that the commission must ensure that all trade agreements include effective provisions on poverty reduction and the promotion of decent and safe working conditions and that agreements include legally binding conditions relating to and enforcement of internationally recognised human rights, social and environmental standards, as well as measures to be applied in the event of breaches.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which, in addition to the decision taken on the international cocoa agreement, denounces the problem of child labour in the cocoa sector. the cocoa sector employs thousands of children today, and this is unacceptable. during the debate, one of the main issues raised by members of the european parliament during the examination of this agreement was the use of child labour in cocoa fields. even though a large proportion of child labour is carried out in the family, the situation is worrying. so i think the problem of the worst forms of child labour must be solved urgently. the resolution acknowledges that producers are under heavy pressure to keep labour costs down, but calls on cocoa farmers, eu policy makers and consumers to face up to their responsibilities in the fight against child labour. the european commission is now called upon to coordinate its various policies and to ensure that all its bilateral agreements include a human rights clause.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because child labour poses unacceptable risks and threats to children's health and development. moreover, it is only through joint efforts that we can combat child labour in cocoa plantations, especially in west africa, where child labour in cocoa farms is the most prevalent form of child labour. in this context, a comprehensive and coordinated plan to address the root causes of child labour must be implemented. a sufficiently high level of resources should also be allocated to this objective, taking into account the scale of the problems. i think that all child labor should be classified as child labor that is being eliminated. in addition, the commission should support more actively measures that increase support for fair trade networks in the cocoa sector and rural cooperatives and enable them to obtain a fair price for their production. this would encourage companies to increase their support for initiatives to combat child labour in cocoa plantations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the text of the new 2010 international cocoa agreement, which will replace the international cocoa agreement 2001, as extended. i support the objectives of this agreement. it will lead to the strengthening of the global cocoa sector, supporting its sustainable development and increasing the benefits to all stakeholders, will provide an appropriate framework for discussion on all cocoa matters among governments and, with the private sector, will strive towards obtaining fair prices, will promote a sustainable cocoa economy in economic, social and environmental terms, will promote transparency in the world cocoa economy, and in particular in the cocoa trade, through the collection, analysis and dissemination of relevant statistics and the undertaking of appropriate studies, and will also promote the elimination of trade barriers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this agreement. the cocoa sector is a vital source of livelihood for 50 million people worldwide. africa is the world's largest cocoa-producing region, from which the eu imports about 80% of its cocoa consumption. the eu, as the world's largest chocolate industry, is very much concerned by this agreement and as the world's largest importer of cocoa, it has a certain responsibility to promote the sustainability of the sector. i support the objectives of this agreement, which aim to ensure greater transparency and economic sustainability in the cocoa sector, fair and transparent cocoa prices and revenues for cocoa farmers, with significant benefits for small farmers and communities in cocoa-growing countries. i believe that given the concern about child labour in this sector, the eu must take the initiative and address this issue with the main cocoa producing countries in order to prohibit the exploitation of minors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament recommendation because the new agreement aims to bring more transparency and sustainability to a sector on which the livelihoods of 50 million people worldwide depend. the international cocoa agreement 2010 will replace the current agreement of 2001, to which the european union is a contracting party. the new agreement promotes international cooperation in the global cocoa economy. this agreement should contribute to strengthening the national cocoa economies of the member states, to achieving fair prices that help to ensure fair revenues for cocoa farmers and consumers, and to promoting an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy. the 2010 agreement will improve market transparency by strengthening the role of the international cocoa organisation in the collection, processing and dissemination of data and enhancing its cooperation with industry and ngos. the new agreement will strengthen the mandate of the international cocoa organisation for projects aimed at strengthening the capacity of national cocoa economies to respond to growing demand. the new pact sets clear objectives for a sustainable cocoa economy, recognising the importance of economic viability and social and environmental responsibility at all stages of the value chain.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the report, because it marks an important step towards sustainable, fair, child-labour free cocoa production. the eu is the world’s biggest cocoa consumer, accounting for 40% of global cocoa consumption in 2010, which gives us particular responsibility in this issue. by trading with cocoa producing countries we bear a responsibility for millions of people for whom the industry is their livelihood. we provide them with jobs and allow minimum social standards. in ghana and ivory coast, 90% of the farmers rely on cocoa for their primary income. however, by trading with these countries we are also responsible for child slavery. the situation of children in cocoa-producing countries is horrifying. in the ivory coast alone it is estimated that 100 000 children are put to work in the cocoa industry. the eu has an obligation to ensure child-labour-free cocoa production. i welcome the promotion of fair-trade standards for cocoa, which include no forced labour of any kind, including child labour. i hope countries all over the world – in particular the us, the second biggest cocoa consumer – will take the same approach.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. almost 33 million eu citizens suffer from diabetes and the number of people with the disease is expected to increase significantly over the next decade. in many member states, diabetes already accounts for more than 10% of total healthcare expenditure, with an average of around €2,100 per patient per year. although the growing number of people with diabetes poses a major threat to the healthcare systems of the member states and significantly increases their costs, only fourteen eu member states have national programmes to combat diabetes. i support the call in the resolution for the commission to present an eu diabetes strategy and ensure its implementation in the member states. member states should also take active action in developing national diabetes programmes to promote healthy lifestyles, risk factor reduction, prevention, early diagnosis, diabetes treatment and to provide comprehensive information to the public, especially those at highest risk.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because diabetes is one of the most common non-communicable diseases. it is estimated that more than 32 million eu citizens currently suffer from it, representing almost 10% of the eu population, and another 32 million people complain of impaired glucose tolerance and there is a very high probability that this intolerance will progress to clinical diabetes. diabetes that is not treated properly or is diagnosed too late is a major cause of myocardial infarction, stroke, blindness, limb amputation, and renal failure. unfortunately, the lack of funds and infrastructure to coordinate diabetes research in the european union is undermining the competitiveness of eu diabetes research and depriving people with diabetes in europe of the full benefits of research. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to develop and implement a targeted european union diabetes strategy for the prevention, diagnosis, management, education and research of diabetes. member states should develop, implement and monitor national diabetes programmes aimed at promoting health, reducing risk factors, improving prognosis, prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of diabetes, covering both the general public and high-risk groups, and aimed at reducing inequalities and optimising health resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because almost 75% of all people with diabetes are not in good control of their condition, which increases the risk of complications, reduces productivity and increases the cost to society. as the number of people with diabetes increases, as the population ages and as the incidence of comorbidities increases, these costs will inevitably increase. only 16 out of 27 member states have national schemes or programmes in place to combat diabetes, and there are no clear criteria for what constitutes a good programme or which countries have best practice. there are large differences and inequalities in the quality of diabetes care in the eu. member states are to develop, implement and monitor national diabetes programmes aimed at promoting health, reducing risk factors, improving prognosis, prevention, early diagnosis and treatment of diabetes, covering both the general public and high-risk groups, and aimed at reducing inequalities and optimising health resources in order to achieve the objectives of noncommunicable diseases and to address public health, social and economic challenges, it is important that the eu and the member states focus more on prevention and risk reduction in all relevant legislative and policy areas, in particular environmental, food and consumer policies.
in writing. - i support this resolution, as only joint efforts can effectively combat the diabetes epidemic, which is spreading at a constant and rapid rate. in this context, it is necessary to develop and implement an eu diabetes strategy at eu level. in addition, each member state should develop and implement its national diabetes programmes and effectively implement the prevention of type 2 diabetes and obesity as well as best practice diabetes management guidelines and evidence-based treatment guidelines. with the ever-increasing number of people with diabetes, i believe that the commission should develop common standard criteria and methods for the collection of data on diabetes. it is also essential that it manages comprehensive epidemiological data on diabetes, as well as economic data on the direct or indirect costs of diabetes prevention and management, in constructive cooperation with the member states. it is also essential that adequate funding is allocated to the fight against diabetes.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur reminds us of the seriousness of the diabetes epidemic in europe. diabetes kills 325,000 people in the european union every year, or 2 people every two minutes. studies at vilnius university have shown that the death rate from diabetes in lithuania has been steadily increasing over the past two decades. the report shows that obesity is the most common cause of this disease. the rate of obesity in lithuania is over 20%, the second highest in the european union, and 5% above the union average. according to a report published by the european commission and the organisation for economic cooperation and development, 50.1 percent of europeans are obese - twice as many as 20 years ago. diabetes and obesity are costly not only to human health, but also to the health care system. the european union and the organisation for economic cooperation and development report estimate a 70% increase in healthcare expenditure for the eu member states between 2007 and 2015 due to the spread of diabetes. in lithuania, more than 10% of the healthcare budget is spent on diabetes treatment. these costs are likely to increase unless serious action is taken to tackle the problem of diabetes - as the rapporteur mentioned, the number of people with diabetes in europe is expected to increase to 16.6% by the 2030s.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because the european union remains firmly committed to supporting an independent and united bosnia and herzegovina. one of the key objectives of eu policy is to accelerate the country's progress towards eu membership and thus help improve the quality of life for all citizens. the european parliament endorses the european union's overall strategy on bosnia and herzegovina, which aims to increase the eu's involvement in bosnia and herzegovina and to appoint an eu representative with wider mandates, with a dual role of eusr and head of delegation. the authorities of bosnia and herzegovina should be more effective in investigating and prosecuting corruption cases and should ensure that more offenders are prosecuted. it is worth noting that the authorities of the country are pursuing an action plan to combat corruption in the civil service. in addition, the authorities of bosnia and herzegovina should actively protect and defend the rights of all groups and individuals who should be protected from direct or indirect discrimination and violence. the european parliament calls on the government of bosnia and herzegovina and the neighbouring countries to do everything possible to resolve border disputes with the neighbouring countries through bilateral agreements or other means.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it takes stock of the progress made by bosnia and herzegovina towards eu membership. however, bosnia and herzegovina still has a long way to go in implementing the necessary reforms to become a full eu member. it is necessary for bosnia and herzegovina to ensure an impartial, independent and efficient judicial system, to establish a supreme court, to combat corruption in all its forms more effectively, and to fully pursue the rule of law. it is necessary to combat trafficking in human beings, to prosecute criminals, etc. i believe that the commitments undertaken must be implemented and the shortcomings identified in the report must be fully addressed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of a resolution calling on the new government of bosnia and herzegovina to take immediate concrete steps to ensure that the potential candidate country is firmly on the path of european reforms and demonstrates the necessary progress in the near future. the process of european integration can be an essential stabilizing and consolidating factor, defining the strategic direction of the country's development, helping to avoid a backlog in the implementation of the necessary internal economic and social reforms. the agreement reached by the main political forces suggests that the process of european integration will be intensified. it is noteworthy that truth and justice are essential to reconciliation. a broad and open internal dialogue on recent history, including with other countries in the region, based on facts rather than emotions, is essential for the well-being of society and for friendly relations with neighbours.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i believe that in 2011 bosnia and herzegovina has made little progress in the areas of stabilisation and socioeconomic development. in particular, full eu membership requires constitutional reforms and the harmonisation of four different legal systems. it is important to stress that the border issues with neighbouring countries must be resolved as soon as possible, and that a single, sovereign and united state cannot be a member of the eu.
in writing. − in the past six months, bosnia and herzegovina has managed to form a new government, and has passed important state aid and population census laws. however, i agree with the commission and council representatives who stressed that bosnia and herzegovina must continue to act actively and reform its constitutional framework, its judicial system, agree on fiscal measures, ensure the formation of civil society, respect and implementation of human and social rights, and seek ways to prevent corruption, radicalism and trafficking in human beings. the european parliament encourages the political leaders of bosnia and herzegovina to be resolute and united in pursuing reforms and progress so that the people of the country can live in a politically stable and economically strong state. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the principles and objectives of the european union's policies are in the interests of the people of bosnia and herzegovina and that continued cooperation is necessary to achieve greater progress for this country.
i have been observing the duma and presidential elections in russia at three-month intervals. despite the fact that i witnessed the rigging of the election results in one of the districts of moscow during the duma elections, which was captured on video camera by one of the members of the commission, i returned from russia not too disappointed. the main impression: in moscow and st. petersburg, i saw the great public interest in the elections; the sincere desire of many people, especially the youth, to prevent any falsifications. this was evidenced by the fact that the majority of the members and observers of the committees of the opposition parties and presidential candidates were also present. it is therefore regrettable that the participation of a larger number of parties and candidates for the presidency in both the first and the second elections was artificially prevented. and in the media, the ruling party and the candidate for power had a greenhouse condition, while the opposition had political troublemakers and a cold. but this desire to finally hold an honest and fair election has already permeated not thousands, but hundreds of thousands and millions of russian citizens, as demonstrated by huge demonstrations in moscow, st. petersburg and elsewhere. polls show that 10 years ago, about 20 percent of the country's population would have supported russia's european path, but now 30 percent would have chosen it, and that is more than half of all young people. this trend makes us more optimistic about the future of russia, but it is worth remembering that about 40 percent want a special path for russia, one that could take it further away from democracy and human rights. i therefore strongly support those colleagues who are in favour of intensifying dialogue with russia at all levels and of using the european union's opportunities to encourage russia to take the european path.
mr president, the european union, as russia’s direct neighbour, has followed with particular interest the election process and widespread ongoing protests in russia on both the state duma and presidential elections. we observed the so-called carousel voting on election day, vote fraud, and other irregularities and shortcomings reported by international observers. taking all this into account, as well as the announcement of potentially competitive candidates and tv broadcasting during the election campaign, which was 90% dominated by one candidate, we cannot draw any other conclusion than, firstly, presidential elections were neither free nor fair, consequently the legitimacy of the president-elect is questionable. secondly, the russian people are fighting for free elections and they deserve our support and solidarity. finally, arrests of dozens of peaceful protestors across russia during demonstrations after the disputed victory of vladimir putin deserve our condemnation. all this has to be stated in our resolution.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the competitive low carbon economy in 2050. i believe that our future lies in the development of clean technologies and sustainable rural development. our common european climate change policy strategies and the global race for the efficient use of resources need to be seen as opportunities. in the context of the current economic crisis, the existing targets for 2020 are sufficiently ambitious. therefore, it is important to indicate clear guidelines for the period after 2020 and to encourage investments in sustainable technologies. it will be important to give incentives for the development of low carbon technologies, particularly in the context of the european funding programme for research and innovation, horizon 2020.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european parliament and the european council aim to reduce greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions by 80-95% by 2050. however, it is already clear that this will be difficult to achieve, as no specific targets and measures to reduce emissions have yet been agreed. i support the european parliament's proposal to set intermediate 2030 and 2040 co2 reduction targets covering specific sectors, to set timetables and to propose measures taking into account the specificities, national capacities and potential of individual member states. it is also necessary to maximise energy efficiency, to promote the development of renewable energy and to take decisions on energy storage, energy efficiency and the development of efficient energy transmission infrastructure. the eu must also play a more active role in international fora and negotiations and bring together other countries to reach an ambitious, comprehensive and legally binding agreement on climate change as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament report because it is necessary to assess and seek to eliminate the risk that, on a global scale, if insufficient efforts are made, actions taken within the european union may lead to a shift in market share and the use of less efficient installations in other countries, leading to an increase in global emissions, i.e. carbon leakage. the european parliament therefore calls on the commission to propose, over the next two years, the measures necessary to achieve the 2030 targets, taking into account the specific national capacities and potential as well as international progress in the implementation of climate protection measures. such measures should be implemented in a coherent, cost-effective and efficient manner. the european commission should also provide an economic benefit analysis, examining how the proposed approach is implemented at member state level, taking into account national circumstances resulting from the different technological developments and the necessary investments (and their social acceptability) and the wider variety of possible conditions in the world. it is important to note that the creation of a low-carbon economy would provide many opportunities for creating additional jobs, while ensuring economic growth and providing a competitive advantage to european industry.
in writing. − i abstained in voting in favour of this document because i believe that the adoption of the plan, together with the prospect of reducing emissions and the intermediate stages proposed in the plan for european competitiveness, will create obstacles and will be of little use. the european union currently emits only 11% of the world's carbon dioxide, and our actions alone are not slowing down the warming process. i agree that we need to support technologies that are leading the way and invest in processes that are much more efficient in the use of energy and resources. however, it should be borne in mind that china still accounts for 70% of its electricity supply and there is no guarantee that its targets in the current five-year plan, which prioritises green investment in low-carbon technologies, will be met, although this is envisaged to a much larger scale than in europe. i am convinced that there is a real reason to believe that carbon leakage may occur when companies move from europe to avoid the higher costs of implementing measures to reduce carbon emissions. these changes would not benefit the european economy and would do nothing to reduce global emissions. if these cases can be proven, measures should be taken to protect the industries concerned or compensation should be paid. i therefore believe that the measures must be adequate and logically balanced.
in writing. - i would like to draw attention to a number of aspects of this report. first, i am convinced that we should not set specific co2 reduction targets. the setting of such mandatory targets would both reduce the eu's competitiveness and place a burden on smaller eu member states. secondly, i would like to stress the need to increase energy efficiency and promote renewable energy (alongside the development of smart grids). energy efficiency (as well as other resource efficiency) would not only contribute to reducing carbon dioxide emissions, but would also have positive economic effects by saving on increasingly expensive raw materials.
