in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the 6th world water forum. water is becoming ever more precious and scarce. therefore we need to handle it with more care and to find ways at both european and international levels of how to deal with our water resources sustainably. climate change and population growth amplify the problems. this is why the eu must develop a strategic and long-term water policy in close cooperation with the international community. the health and living conditions of billions of people depend on water. i support the statement in the resolution that water is a shared resource of humankind and, therefore, should not be a source of profit and that access to water should constitute a fundamental and universal right. in this regard the commission and member states have to reinforce their commitment to achieve the united nations millennium development goals in the field of water and sanitation.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. population growth, deforestation, biological and chemical pollution and climate change threaten the security and reliability of water supplies. to date, over 800 million people have access to unsafe drinking water, and poor hygiene kills more than two and a half million children each year in the past, the european parliament has repeatedly called on the commission and the council to take concrete action to ensure access to safe drinking water and sanitation for the most deprived persons, but these repeated calls have not been heeded. i agree with the need to step up international efforts and to adopt an agreement and concrete commitments on global water management at the forthcoming rio de janeiro conference. it is also essential to introduce the latest technologies and to support investment in research and development to ensure the most efficient use of water resources.
in writing. − i voted for this european parliament resolution because technological innovation can increase the efficiency and sustainability of water resources, and in particular can be used for the benefit of developing countries. water is a common resource for all of humanity, and should not be used as a source of profit. access to water should be a fundamental and universal right. the united nations recognises the human right to safe drinking water and sanitation, as enshrined in the right to an adequate standard of living, and it is therefore necessary to make all necessary efforts to ensure that the poorest have access to water by 2015. water use targets should be aligned to meet water demand and ensure access to water and its quality, in particular in developing countries. water is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change, which may lead to a reduction in the quantity and quality of available water, in particular drinking water, and to an increase in the frequency and intensity of floods and droughts. it is therefore essential to develop risk prevention, mitigation and response strategies to prevent water-related extreme events.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution on the 6th world water forum, to be held in marseille from 12 to 17 march 2012, given that almost half of the population in developing countries lack sanitation, more than 800 million people still use unsafe drinking water sources and more than 2.5 million children die each year from lack of access to safe water and sanitation, as well as from poor hygiene. water management has a direct impact on human health, energy production, agriculture and food security, and effective water management is a key element in poverty reduction. technological innovation could increase the efficiency and sustainability of water resources and in particular benefit developing countries. the world water forum, held every three years, provides a unique opportunity for water sector representatives, policy-makers and decision-makers from all regions of the world to meet, discuss and find solutions to water security.
in writing. water is the basis of life, the most abundant natural resource on our planet. sadly, many people on earth still lack a complete supply of safe drinking water. on the other hand, the seas that border the eu (i am thinking in particular of the baltic sea) are also becoming increasingly polluted. i therefore support the provisions that all measures aimed at the conservation and improvement of water resources (of all types) should be given the utmost attention. they should be integrated as widely as possible into other eu policies (in particular agriculture).
in writing. – serbia’s reform progress is to be welcomed and further encouraged, especially in light of the upcoming elections in serbia. much still needs to be done to implement the obligations and agreements undertaken by serbia – especially as regards improving the business environment. the recent experiences of foreign investors in serbia are very discouraging. winners of privatisation tenders invested tens of millions, but were challenged by public institutions and forced to leave. dubious decisions by serbian institutions are now being contested internationally. the commission must monitor very closely the progress committed to in december 2011 and february 2012 and report back at the end of this year. another issue is reconciliation with the communist past. this process is moving forward in many former communist block countries, but not in serbia. serbia was the first country in the region to adopt its lustration law, but later annulled it as infringing the constitution. i cannot see how truth and justice can infringe the constitution of a democratic state? i call on serbia to adopt the necessary legislation and open up its communist-times archives to its citizens as well as to other countries without further delay.
i think the success of the european union depends not only on economic things but also on how we know each other. i'm talking about understanding the historical experience. sixty-three years ago, on march 25-28, the soviet occupiers carried out a carefully planned mass slaughter in lithuania, latvia, and estonia. in a matter of days, some 95,000 people from the three baltic states were sent to siberia in cattle cars. 75% of them are women and children. in 1949, as europe was rebuilding from the wounds of world war ii, another part of europe was experiencing atrocities, mass beatings, persecutions, and imprisonments. this was to destroy those people who were brave enough to fight the system of terror that was the soviet union. i am glad that we have had the opportunity to mention this event in the european parliament today and i think it is very important to maintain the programmes which fund programmes of historical mutual recognition.
for the efd group the rising cost of food and the cost of living are driving more and more people to seek help. the food aid programme for 2012 is allocated eur 113 million. this is lower than the previous allocation of eur 500 million. the implementation of this programme has increased the access to food for the poorest people in the union. an estimated 43 million people in the european union are at risk of food shortages. that means they can't get enough to eat every other day. the importance and special significance of this programme is recognised by many charitable organisations, ngos and organisations across the eu. so we have to find a way to continue this program without cutting funding. i should also point out that social tensions are particularly high in lithuania, as a result of the sharp rise in food and heating prices. the reduction in funding for this programme will further worsen the situation of the population living in poverty and of vulnerable families.
in writing. people in the european union still face obstacles to actively exercising their rights as eu citizens. for example, recent developments in the creation of websites discriminating against workers from central and eastern european countries show that the rights of citizens of the european union are still under threat. we must therefore protect the right of citizens to move and work freely, because the free movement of workers is one of the fundamental values of the european union and all workers must have equal rights and these must be respected in all eu countries. secondly, persons with disabilities in the european union face numerous physical and social barriers on a daily basis which prevent them from enjoying their rights, such as the normal use of public buildings, public services, free movement and access to public transport, infrastructure, information technology and other facilities and services. unfortunately, the biggest obstacle to the integration of disabled people into society is high unemployment, and disabled unemployment is due to insufficient preparation for the labour market. the member states and the commission must therefore, in line with the european disability strategy (2010-2020), take the most active action possible to remove barriers to mobility and accessibility for people with disabilities, which would solve many other problems social exclusion, discrimination, unemployment and others. i also call on the member states to make the most of the 2013 european year of citizens and to make people more aware of the rights that eu citizenship gives them.
in writing the rights of citizens of the european union are of the highest standard in terms of human protection against abuse of power. the principle of justice is strongly emphasised as the basis for the interaction between the state and the citizen. however, there are still countries in the european union which do not respect this principle, and justice has nothing to do with equality before the law. this includes disregard for property rights, in particular land rights in lithuania, where the process of reprivatisation of land seized during the soviet era is underway. very often land is not returned to its rightful owners despite the documents proving the ownership. and the land is going to people who have never owned it before. this leads to financial and corrupt abuses and, above all, violates the sacred right to property. in this way, the state applies laws to its citizens in an unequal and selective way, violating people's rights. another example concerns the high-profile paedophilia scandal in lithuania, which has involved high-ranking judicial officials, including judges. the court, the police and the guardians are doing everything to take away the child's guardian, who is both the victim and the main witness of this incident. it's all happening in an atmosphere of fear and a show of force by the state's institutions. it seems that the purpose of this is to intimidate witnesses, not to disrupt an organized pedophile ring. this is an example of a violation of citizens' rights, which shows that there are equals and peers in such situations. citizens' rights must be equal for everyone, regardless of where a person lives or of his social status.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the continued participation of the european union in the international rubber study group (irg). recently, serious doubts have been raised about the future of the icc as important countries such as the united states, thailand and malaysia have left the organisation. however, the international rubber study group is an intergovernmental organisation whose main function is to provide a forum for discussion on the production, supply and consumption of rubber by all the participating countries. today, it is the only inclusive platform bringing together countries that produce and use rubber, and despite its shortcomings, it is still the most appropriate organisation to increase transparency, and one of the organisation's key objectives is to ensure that rubber is affordable on the global market and can be obtained under fair and predictable conditions. the european union is the second largest consumer of natural rubber in the world, with russia and japan also members of this organisation.
in writing. - i have voted in favour of this document as parliament gives its consent to the draft council decision on the establishment, on behalf of the european union, of the amended statutes and rules of procedure of the international rubber study group. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the goa has been able to achieve the objectives of the guidelines. moreover, despite its shortcomings, the cccme is still the most appropriate organisation to increase the transparency that is lacking in the real market and the organisation that is desperately needed to ensure that rubber is available and affordable on fair, predictable terms worldwide. the revision of the statutes and rules of procedure of the gsc could also be an important step towards the revival of the group as a key forum for various stakeholders. every effort should be made to increase the membership of the group, in particular by including the main rubber producing and consuming countries. a strong membership base remains a prerequisite for the long-term viability and effectiveness of the cwc as an authoritative organisation. this will undoubtedly have an impact on the development of greater industrial sustainability and quality standards, as well as on alternative rubber.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the operation and application of the rights of persons travelling by air. the resolution is a response to the commission's recent communication on a regulation laying down common rules on compensation and assistance to passengers in the event of denied boarding and of cancellation or long-term delay of flights. i agree with the rapporteur that information on passenger rights should be provided in a simple, appropriate and comprehensible manner at all the main stages of the journey. i believe that airports must have qualified staff who can be contacted and who can make immediate decisions on the provision of assistance, the refund of the ticket, the offer of a different route and other matters arising from the cancellation of a flight. in the event of a delay, passengers should be provided with timely information on the reasons for the delay or cancellation of the flight, the expected duration of the delay and, where possible, other travel options and other modes of transport. attention should also be paid to the three options available to the passenger, which are his fundamental rights: to recover the money paid for the ticket, to change the route and to reserve seats on other flights. i think that the european parliament has adopted this resolution at the right time, as the commission intends to review the legislation in this area next year. i urge the commission to take this resolution into account in future reviews of the package travel directive and the airport package.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i am in favour of improving the rights of air passengers. air transport is the main means of transport for people today, and passenger traffic at airports is only increasing. ensuring that the fundamental rights of passengers are properly enforced is therefore of paramount importance in order to prevent possible abuses by airlines. the report adopted today by the european parliament proposes that in future passengers should be fully insured in the event of the bankruptcy or insolvency of an airline and that price transparency should be ensured. it is also proposed that in future passengers will be entitled to have their data changed free of charge if they make a mistake when buying a ticket. finally, the communication calls for passengers to be given access to the passenger data record held by the air carrier and subsequently used by the security services of different countries for counter-terrorism purposes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to increase the legal certainty of the regulations, to clarify them better and to ensure their uniform application throughout the eu. this report takes a broader view of air passengers' rights, including a number of relevant proposals, such as better protecting the rights of air travellers, providing greater clarity and certainty to passengers about their rights and increasing the liability of airlines. i agree with the need to fully insure passengers against the bankruptcy or insolvency of airlines and to effectively implement and enforce the existing legislation on price transparency in order to ensure that the prices published on airlines' websites reflect the final price fairly.
in writing. − we recently endorsed the right of disabled people to travel by bus or waterway. the natural next step is to ensure similar rights for air travel. i therefore welcome the rapporteur's inclusion in his report of provisions indicating the need to ensure adequate travel conditions for disabled persons, in particular with regard to accompanying persons, assistive devices, access to information and airport infrastructure.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the european refugee fund 2008-2013 at second reading. i support the proposal to set up a list of priority refugees (independently of annual priorities with respect to geographic regions and nationalities): children and women, unaccompanied minors, persons with serious medical needs, survivors of violence and torture etc. we, members of the european parliament, endorsed the idea that in order to encourage more member states to take part in resettlement activity, additional financial support should be given to those participating in the resettlement programme for the first time. i support the proposal that the fixed amount for each resettled person shall be eur 6 000 in the first calendar year, eur 5 000 in the second and eur 4 000 in subsequent years – the funding to be invested in the development of a sustainable resettlement programme. i urge the council to continue the process of adoption of this important legal act.
in writing. − i have supported this proposal as the purpose of this document is to ensure that the eu's resettlement actions have a greater impact in terms of providing protection for refugees, as well as to maximise the strategic impact of resettlement by making it more targeted to help those who need it most to move, and to set regular resettlement priorities at eu level. the proposal aims to amend the decision establishing the european refugee fund, taking into account the establishment of an eu general programme for the resettlement of refugees. the commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the detailed rules for the application of this decision. member states will receive additional financial support for each person to be relocated in line with these priorities.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document because these decisions are taken to reduce the risk of dual-use items being used for military purposes and/or distribution programmes. in order to ensure the most effective implementation of such controls, parties to international export control regimes bring together the main suppliers of dual-use items. by agreeing to control trade in specific goods, they effectively seek to reduce the risk of proliferation, while ensuring that no obstacles to legitimate trade are created.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report with its proposal to postpone until 30 april 2014 the deadline for transposition of directive 2004/40/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 29 april 2004 on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents (electromagnetic fields). there are many concerns about implementing the directive, especially that exposure limit values would place disproportionate limitations on the use and development of medical magnetic resonance imaging (mri) applications, considered today to be a vital tool for the diagnosis and treatment of a number of diseases. given the complexity of the matter, the commission proposed extending the deadline for transposition of directive 2004/40/ec. however, i agree with the rapporteur that there should be an extension of 18 months, rather than 24 months as proposed by the commission.
in writing. − the proposal aims to postpone the transposition of directive 2004/40/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 29 april 2004 on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the risks to workers from physical agents (electromagnetic fields) (eighteenth individual directive within the meaning of article 16 (1) of directive 89/391/eec) until 30 april 2014.
in writing. − electromagnetic fields pose a significant risk to workers exposed to these physical agents. however, the medical sector and the procedures used in it, in particular magnetic resonance imaging, require, as practice shows, different legal regulation. the reservations in the medical sector have not yet been agreed, and i therefore agree that the application of the current regulation should be postponed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on regulation (ec) no 2073/2004 laying down a legal framework for administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties. these provisions need to be revised to take into account the introduction of the computerised excise movement and control system (emcs). emcs has been introduced on the basis of decision no 1152/2003/ec of the european parliament and of the council on computerising the movement and surveillance of excisable products. i agree with the rapporteur’s suggestion that the commission establish a new vat and excise duties forum, similar to the joint transfer pricing forum, within which companies can address issues relating to corporate vat and disputes between member states. processing of personal data relating to offences, criminal convictions or security measures is to be carried out in accordance with directive 95/46/ec or regulation (ec) no 45/2001.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation on administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties, as the establishment of a european fiscal union should ensure a comprehensive, rapid, efficient, convenient and, if possible, automatic exchange of information between member states in order to better combat tax evasion. the commission proposes to adopt a new regulation on administrative cooperation in the field of excise duties, which will replace the current regulation. purpose to harmonise legislation in this area with the possibilities offered by the development of the electronic movement control system (emcs) for excisable goods and to provide a more clearly defined legal framework to replace the current manual and semi-automatic procedures. the scope of the regulation will be extended to include administrative cooperation to ensure the enforcement of all excise legislation, not just the proper assessment of excise duties. in addition, the aim is to clarify the rights and obligations of the member states and the commission in this area, both in terms of the scope of the emcs and in a more general manner. the legislation facilitates administrative simplification by providing for common measures that are easy to interpret and apply. public authorities will be able to use common tools and documents within a predefined organisational framework. this package of measures will simplify european cross-border administrative cooperation.
in writing. − we are an eu institution elected by the citizens of the european union. i therefore fully support the view expressed in this report that, as a matter of responsibility to the electorate, we must set an example of thrift in this difficult economic period. although constitutionally we may not be able to avoid the constant travel to strasbourg, which is a drain on us and the eu budget, i agree that other ways of avoiding such travel must be found. at the same time, i welcome the european parliament's understanding of the need to continue the project of the house of european history. while i agree with the need for budgetary discipline, i would nevertheless urge that this project be implemented as soon as possible.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for spain. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional assistance to workers affected by major structural changes in the world trade system. the commission has adopted a new proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf for spain in order to support the reintegration of workers made redundant as a result of the global financial and economic crisis. the spanish application concerns 1 138 redundancies (all of which are covered by the aid) in 513 enterprises active in the construction sector in the valencia region. one of the criteria used by the commission in its assessment was the link between the exemptions and the major structural changes in the world trade system and the financial crisis. in view of this criterion, the spanish authorities argued that the construction sector had been severely affected by the crisis. loans to the construction sector and to individuals have been severely reduced, and the decline in consumer confidence and cash shortages have reduced demand for new homes. according to the spanish authorities, the employment situation in the affected area is particularly vulnerable due to the impact of the crisis on the traditional sectors, i.e. the textile sector or the ceramic and stone grinding, working and finishing sectors related to construction, as these sectors are of vital importance to the region's economy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because after the lisbon treaty parliament and the council have equal powers in the ordinary legislative procedure and in the budget procedure and there is no longer a reason to continue to include council question time in its present form in the agenda. however, i agree with the rapporteur’s position and proposed amendments, that it would be sensible to retain the option of putting questions to the council – during a specific question hour – on matters relating to responsibilities other than those linked to the exercise of its legislative and budgetary functions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the rules of procedure to take account of the changes in the european parliament's relations with the institutions representing national governments following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, since, after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, parliament has become one of the legislators of the european union and, under the ordinary legislative and budgetary procedure, it has the same powers as the council. in view of the new institutional balance, it is considered that the current agenda for the council, i.e. the agenda for each session, should no longer be maintained. on the other hand, it is appropriate, according to the conference of presidents, to maintain the possibility of holding question hours not only for the president of the commission but also for the vice-presidents of the commission and the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy and the president of the eurogroup. the abolition of question time for the council as it has been until now would take account of the change in the institutional balance indicated by the conference of presidents. however, for the reasons set out above, it seems useful to maintain the possibility of putting questions to the council by organising a separate question hour to discuss matters falling within its competence, outside its legislative and budgetary functions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the european parliament's position on turkey's progress towards european union membership. in its report, while stressing the economic and political importance of closer relations between turkey and the eu and its importance for stability, democracy and security in the region, parliament stresses that turkey is making too little progress and has not implemented the provisions of the ec-turkey association agreement and its additional protocol in general over the past six years. the report therefore stresses that turkey needs to make greater efforts to resolve entrenched bilateral issues, including outstanding legal obligations and disputes over land, sea and air borders with its immediate neighbours, including the eu member states, in its own interest and in order to ensure greater stability and to promote good neighbourly relations and constructive political and economic partnership.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the 2011 progress report on turkey, because the european union, its member states and turkey are interdependent. the european union attaches importance to turkey's economic and growth potential and its important role in ensuring regional stability and energy security. this interdependence is complemented by the important potential interaction between the union's and turkey's foreign and security policies and neighbourhood policies, which is beneficial and provides greater leverage for both parties. however, this interdependence can only be successful if it is based on mutual commitment, strategic dialogue and effective cooperation, the success of the reform process and the implementation of these reforms, and good relations between turkey and the neighbouring eu member states. the commission should develop a new positive agenda covering a range of areas of common interest, aiming at a new dynamic in eu-turkey relations, with tangible results and benefits for both parties, and providing for the possibility for the eu to remain the benchmark for further reforms in turkey and to help turkey meet the accession criteria.
in writing. − i am in favor of the eu enlargement policy and the continuation of turkey’s eu accession negotiations. we need to send a positive and encouraging message to turkey, which remains strongly committed to the eu integration process. by delaying the opening of the 15th negotiation chapter ‘energy’ we risk losing the momentum gained in the eu-turkey’s intensified dialogue on energy. we should further strengthen and broaden the eu-turkey’s foreign policy dialogue, encourage closer economic relations, further step up cooperation on migration management and border controls, which could pave the way for visa liberalisation with turkey. a positive agenda initiated by the commission in 2012 could give new impetus and compliment the accession negotiations by creating an additional framework for dialogue at expert level. the implementation of the ankara protocol on the turkish side is a crucial step for the successful continuation of negotiations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out the european parliament's position on montenegro's progress towards eu membership. in its report, parliament welcomes the efforts made by montenegro to implement democratic reforms and welcomes the commission's proposal to open accession negotiations in 2012. the communication notes that the support of the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa) in montenegro is being properly implemented and that the country has achieved good results in the key priorities of preparing for eu membership. however, parliament recommends that more efforts be made to ensure a more transparent legislative process, greater public participation in the preparation of new legislation, a strengthening of parliament's administrative capacity and a more frequent and effective use of the instrument of consultation and control meetings. parliament called for particular attention to be given to investigating alleged threats and physical violence against journalists and to responding to the increasing number of reports of restrictions on media freedom.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the 2011 progress report on montenegro, as eu member states aim to open accession negotiations with montenegro in june 2012. political consensus on eu issues remains important in montenegro and the objective of promoting eu and nato membership is a key foreign policy issue. reforms require strong political will and a fundamental commitment to tackle the challenges ahead of the accession process. montenegro has made significant progress in achieving the seven priority objectives set by the commission in 2010, namely improving the functioning of the parliamentary and electoral system, professionalism of the public administration, independence of the judiciary, fight against corruption, fight against organised crime, guaranteeing media freedom and cooperation with civil society. montenegro has also implemented the trade-related provisions of the stabilisation and association agreement with the eu. however, montenegro needs to continue to pursue reforms by effectively implementing the government's action plan on key priorities, promoting recovery from the economic crisis, while ensuring adequate control of public expenditure and public debt, which, according to 2011 data, is higher than in the previous year. montenegro must also maintain fiscal stability and strengthen and develop the administrative and institutional capacity necessary to assume the obligations of eu membership in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it contains the european parliament's assessment of the commission's green paper on the corporate governance framework. in its report, parliament stresses the need for a more transparent, stable, reliable and accountable business sector in the eu, with better corporate governance embedded in it. regrets, therefore, that the commission does not address in its green paper important corporate governance issues such as board decision-making, directors' liability, directors' independence, conflicts of interest or stakeholder involvement; parliament also stresses that accountability and transparency for its employees, shareholders and, where appropriate, other stakeholders are essential conditions for a well-managed company. i agree with the position expressed by parliament that the business sector should take account of social, ethical and environmental concerns, as well as to achieve better economic performance and to promote job creation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the current european corporate governance framework, as it is important to create a more transparent, stable and accountable corporate sector in the european union, with better corporate governance embedded in it. a review of the eu's corporate governance framework is necessary to avoid excessive bureaucratic burdens and to increase the competitiveness of eu enterprises. the review of the eu corporate governance system needs to take into account the rights and responsibilities of the relevant company management bodies under national law, in particular the differences between the monistic and dualist systems. it is also necessary to carry out an independent audit and to establish rules that take account of the different cultures of the companies. the oecd definition of corporate governance, which is the totality of the relationship between the management, the board, the shareholders and other stakeholders of the company, as defined in 2004, should be further promoted.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the 2010 eib annual report. i support the bank’s approach of placing importance on measuring the results not only in terms of quantity but also in terms of quality and the fact that it is crucial to establish a clear link between inputs and results in order to assess the effectiveness of the system. i welcome the rapporteur’s recommendation to the eib to focus more on granting eu support to eu smes and efforts for transparency and on better accountability for the ‘global loans’ programme. i agree that the eib group should continue reporting annually to parliament on its financing activities. i support the cooperation between the eib and the commission in developing innovative financial instruments to promote the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and climate action needs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which gives a favourable assessment of the 2010 annual report of the european investment bank (eib). the european parliament endorses the bank's approach to supporting eu activities and calls on the eib to continue its activities in support of european economic development, promoting growth and employment and promoting social and territorial cohesion, with a particular focus on projects targeting less developed regions. the bank's capital needs are therefore not limited to the capital needs of the bank, but are also limited to the capital needs of the bank. the eib should make the best use of its resources and instruments to respond to the current financial and economic crisis. the european parliament also welcomes the eib's support to countries in financial difficulty in cooperation with the eu structural funds, including loans to cover part of the national contribution to projects supported by those funds. in addition, cooperation between the eib and the european commission is needed to develop innovative financial instruments to support the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and to implement actions to boost the economy and combat climate change.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the 2010 annual report of the european investment bank (eib) as it welcomes the 2010 annual report and calls on the eib to continue its work in support of european economic development, promoting growth and employment and promoting social and territorial cohesion, with a particular focus on projects targeting less developed regions, and supports the bank's intention to focus on operations where its financing is likely to have the greatest impact on economic growth. in its financing activities in the european union, the eib focuses on six policy priorities: economic and social cohesion and convergence; the implementation of the knowledge economy; the development of european transport and access networks; support for smes; the protection and enhancement of the environment and the promotion of sustainable communities; and the promotion of sustainable, competitive and secure energy. this is of the utmost importance to us at this time, as the eib is one of europe's most important instruments for supporting the real economy and must therefore be encouraged to continue to develop its policies successfully on a european scale.
in writing. − i voted for this report because people in europe still face obstacles to actively exercising their rights as eu citizens. first, member states should remove obstacles to the free movement of eu citizens and take steps to advise mobile workers on employment opportunities and living and working conditions in the european union. it is also necessary to inform citizens about the risks of illegal work as well as the benefits of legal work (tax advantages, social security, right to vocational training, right to citizenship, right to housing, right to family reunification, right of children to access education and vocational training). i would like to remind you that almost 80 million people with disabilities in the european union still face often insurmountable obstacles to the various ways in which they can exercise their right to free movement as eu citizens. it is therefore necessary to encourage the eu institutions and member states to identify and remove the obstacles that prevent people with disabilities from enjoying all the rights of eu citizens. member states also have to combat poverty and exclusion of people with disabilities, as the number of disabled people among the poor is the highest.

in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the eastern partnership is a good instrument for strengthening relations with countries with european aspirations. armenia is a good example of this. with a history that dates back to antiquity, it is one of the most advanced centers of european civilization and culture. the association agreement between the european union and armenia therefore seems to be a natural process that strengthens bilateral relations. the region's complex and often tragic history should not affect the vision of cooperation for the future. instead of criticism often based on misunderstanding of the caucasus' ethno-historical interdependence, the eu should focus on multi-dimensional assistance to armenia so that the country can implement european standards allowing it to associate with the eu in the foreseeable future. the appropriate way to achieve this will be to increase armenia's active participation in multilateral parliamentary cooperation within the euronest assembly. this is a good example of the commitment to european values and principles that is unanimously recognised by the majority of the armenian society. the announcement by the armenian authorities of democratic, transparent and free elections to be held in may this year should be seen as a gesture of goodwill and an expression of the country's european ambitions. the union institutions should be tasked with reinforcing this conviction and making sense of the decisions and challenges that are moving armenia closer to its goal of returning to the european family.
i thank the rapporteurs and support this part of the report which aims to make clarifications to eu legislation in the field of social protection, as they are inevitably changing member states' practices and their legislation. and i certainly particularly support the necessary changes to the content of european union legislation that are necessary to ensure the effective and full implementation of the right to free movement of workers for our citizens. the situation where self-employed workers work in a country where they are entitled to unemployment benefits and lose that right only by moving to another country whose legislation does not provide for such benefits is unacceptable in a european union which promotes the free movement of workers. the european court of justice has also confirmed in its case law that persons who become unemployed in one member state are entitled to receive the unemployment benefit to which they are entitled when they move to another member state to seek employment there. in particular, entitlement to social benefits cannot be restricted where those benefits consist of social security contributions paid by the former self-employed person himself.
king of the hashemite kingdom of jordan. − mr president, distinguished members of the european parliament, thank you all for your warm welcome. the ties between jordan and europe are anchored in rock. it is more than our mutual interest in the prosperity and security of our multi-regional neighbourhood. it is our shared belief in the kind of neighbourhood it should be – the kind of neighbourhood our people deserve, rich in human dignity and freedom, powered by opportunity and progress, and secured by peace. it is to talk about our neighbourhood and future that i join you today. my friends, a long spring is unfolding in the arab world. it will not be over in a season, not even in a year. our societies are facing the challenge of moving from protests to programmes, from criticism to national strategies. different countries will take different paths. in some countries debate and consensus are in the air. elsewhere, we are seeing the winds of division and reaction, bringing instability, violence and a region-wide cost. there are outside actors that seek to take advantage of discord. the risks and uncertainties are real. but i speak for millions when i say the arab world is awake, and positive challenge is on the move. the signs were already there for those who wanted to see them. for a decade or more, people across the region have been raising questions, nurturing aspirations, seeking meaningful reform and empowering civil society, especially women and our digitally-connected, globally-aware youth. events added to the urgency. global crises in finance, food and energy seriously hurt our economies. arab families who sacrificed to educate their children have seen their sons and daughters leave school, prepared for jobs that simply are not there. today, my region faces the highest youth unemployment of any region. some have called it a ‘generation in waiting’. it is 100 million strong, the largest youth cohort in our history. i know that youth concerns are important here in europe as well. our regions have different demographics, but in one statistic they are the same: today’s young people are 100% of our future and we cannot afford to let a single young citizen wait in vain. this reality drives jordan’s approach to the arab spring. we have embraced it as an opportunity to push past road blocks that have slowed reform in the past. and last year we took immediate steps to engage in a national dialogue to build consensus on concrete actions. an early focus has been the constitution, the foundation of our political system. last september, after recommendations by a national committee, one third of the entire document was amended: new constitutional provisions, wider representation, strengthened political parties, protection of civil rights and freedoms, an enhanced separation of powers. other milestones include new laws on political parties and municipal and national elections as well as legislation for the new constitutional court and independent elections commission, and our next tests will be municipal and parliamentary elections. as guarantor of the political reform process, i have urged both government and parliament to keep to the agreed timeline and finalise the remaining legislation as quickly as possible, without sacrificing the inclusive nature of our process. only we, all jordanians, can build jordan’s future, and we must do so in such a way that our country remains a secure, safe haven in spite of a region becoming more turbulent around us, in spite of economic threats, in spite of neighbouring crises. this path demands consensus-based reform, based on structural, comprehensive change – political, legal, economic and social – respecting the rights and freedoms of all our citizens. in the process jordan can set a regional model of peaceful political evolution and democratisation. i am confident that 2012 will be a year of key political reform in jordan. among the most important steps is building the robust political party life that parliamentary government requires. we know that it is not one election but the next and the next and all those that follow which show that a system is working. we greatly value the eu’s recognition of our reform path. just two months ago the new eu-jordan task force met in amman to discuss key programmes which will support our reform priorities: democratic institutions, civil society, job creation, local economic development, human assistance and more. next month marks ten years since our association agreement went into force, opening markets and job opportunities on both sides. i hope these opportunities, now strengthened by our advanced status partnership, will further blossom in the years ahead. jordan has pursued its domestic goals despite regional conflict but, my friends, peace must come if our region is to thrive and be secure. we cannot afford one more generation in waiting for a palestinian state. (applause) ten years ago the arab states spoke in a united voice on behalf of a just peace. we made the decision to look forward, not back; to seek agreement and to offer acceptance. the arab peace initiative has been recognised by every major friend of peace in the world, including the eu and other members of the quartet. we need israel to engage. the arab peace initiative is based on the only possible solution: two states, side by side, in dignity and self-determination – a sovereign, viable and independent palestine on the 1967 borders with east jerusalem as its capital … (applause)and collective peace and security guarantees for israel … (applause)and a final settlement in accordance with un resolutions, and the agreed resolution of all final status issues. this initiative went even beyond offering israel peace and normal relations with all its arab neighbours. the entire muslim world endorsed it. what has been on the table for the past ten years is a 57-state solution. some political elements point to the change in the arab world and tell the israeli people that negotiations can wait. there is no time to wait. the arab spring is rooted in a profound call for human respect. no affront is felt more deeply than the israeli occupation. the longer palestinian suffering endures, the longer settlement-building continues, the greater the frustrations, dangers and unknowns. if we cross the line where the two-state solution is no longer possible, israel will be further than ever from real security and it would take decades, even generations, for peace to regain the initiative. jordan sees an effective peace process as a moral duty and a strategic interest, and we continue to pursue results. this year in amman we succeeded in getting negotiators back to the table several times. we would not have been able to do so without the magnificent work of european diplomacy, energising contacts, mobilising support, keeping up the pressure for peace and, most important, keeping hope alive. indeed over the past two years the european union has been an invaluable friend to those on both sides working for peace in the middle east. the exploratory talks in amman were baby steps, giving the parties an opportunity to resume bilateral contacts. now the process needs a quantum leap forward – and eu partnership is vital. the eu has taken a principled stand for a just, two-state solution, and against the settlement-building that is obstructing progress. you understand the global risks of continued conflict and the global benefits of peace. you have tremendous credibility for your experience in building democratic institutions, security and trust. i hope you can bring all this to bear in the days ahead. my friends, many peoples, one neighbourhood – and one future. this is the challenge for europe and the middle east, and it is our strength. together we face immense issues – economic, political, peace. the solutions are complex and the path forward difficult. but together we have the will and the wisdom to reach the goals we seek. and together we can succeed. (the house accorded the speaker a standing ovation)

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. member states frequently amend national social security legislation, leading to inconsistent references to eu legislation coordinating social security systems and legal uncertainty for stakeholders. i have endorsed the updating of regulations (ec) no 883/2004 and (ec) no 987/2009 on the coordination of social security systems, by incorporating amendments to national legislation and the latest case law of the court of justice of the european union (cjeu).
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it aims to make adjustments to eu legislation in the field of social protection, i.e. to harmonise and refine concepts and definitions. this should bring more clarity and certainty. i also agree with the provision that persons who become unemployed in one member state are entitled to continue to receive the unemployment benefit to which they are entitled when they move to another member state.
in writing. by voting in favour of this resolution, i support the importance of ensuring adequate coordination at european union level of national social security systems. it reflects developments in the legal situation at national level and in cross-border mobility. i also think that this resolution is important because it also regulates the rights of selfemployed persons who have been insured in the member state in which they last worked, and the rights of seafarers, by recognising the 'head office' as the 'base of employment'.
in writing. − one of the eu's operating principles is the free movement of persons. this right is also inseparable from the social guarantees linked to the employment relationship or arising from the termination of that relationship. therefore, while supporting this report, which provides for social security in cases involving more than one member state, i would also like to point out that in the future we will inevitably have to face the need to fundamentally revise the current social security model as a result of the ageing of the eu.
in writing. − i support this resolution as it will ensure that there is adequate coordination of national social protection systems at eu level. it should be noted that the envisaged common rules will only regulate those aspects of national legislation which may have a negative impact on persons who have exercised their right to free movement of workers and who are confronted with differences in the social security systems of several member states. cooperation and, where appropriate, joint action by member states would help to solve common problems more effectively. it will also make eu law more effective, facilitate the coordination of social protection systems in the member states and contribute to the protection of eu citizens who migrate.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the harmonisation of the social protection systems of the different eu countries is essential to achieve one of the eu's main objectives: the free movement of workers. until now, it has been the case that selfemployed workers in one country pay taxes and gain entitlement to unemployment benefits, but lose this right if they leave to look for work in another eu country. this practice reveals shortcomings in the legislation of individual eu countries that should be addressed as soon as possible. i therefore support the wish expressed by the rapporteur, the european commission and the council to reach an agreement on the regulation at the first reading. the necessary legal provisions would then be put into effect in the near future.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur that we urgently need common rules to guarantee access to social benefits without harming european workers who enjoy the right of free movement. this issue is of great importance to most lithuanians. for example, i believe that self-employed lithuanians who are entitled to unemployment benefits in the country where they work could receive them when they return to lithuania. this is essential to encourage young and talented lithuanians to return home. the report also touches on a wider problem that is currently plaguing lithuania. the board of the state social insurance fund of lithuania (sodra) needs to be completely restructured immediately. as with most of the lithuanian public institutions, sodr was weakened by loss-making expenditure. this is a very serious problem, as last year sodra accounted for almost 70% of lithuania's national budget. according to media reports, 9 out of 10 sodros branches in lithuania are formally bankrupt. the analysis of the regional chapters revealed that 90% of the regions have more pensioners than workers. in lithuania's poorest regions, income is less than 40% of the amount that is due for pensions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to examine how the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth can be achieved in the outermost regions of the european union. the outermost regions of the european union are those regions which, by reason of their specific characteristics relating to physical and structural conditions resulting from their remoteness, isolation and the difficult topographical and climatic conditions, constitute a specific group of regions recognised by the treaty of lisbon. the outermost regions of the european union are currently madeira, the azores and the canary islands, martinique, guadeloupe, réunion, french guiana and saint-martin. those regions enjoy a special status under the treaty, which allows for derogations from the provisions of the treaty and their assimilation to the outermost regions, taking into account their specific characteristics and conditions. i supported the proposals in the report to take due account of the specificities of these regions and to give particular attention to cohesion policy, which is the main pillar of small farms in these regions, to coordinate eu policies in the outermost regions in order to better achieve the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion in these regions, to contribute to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and to further integrate these regions into the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because cohesion policy must be integrated into the europe 2020 strategy and the outermost regions intend to cooperate in the implementation of the five objectives in the fields of employment, innovation, education, social inclusion, climate and energy, which must be achieved by 2020. the outermost regions have a justified special status enshrined in the treaty, as they face specific difficulties linked to their physical and structural circumstances, mainly due to their remoteness, isolation and difficult topographical and climatic conditions. the initial conditions for achieving the cohesion objectives in remote regions are therefore more difficult than in certain regions, and it is also necessary to exploit their potential and promote the growth of efficient sectors in order to ensure the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. cohesion policy must remain one of the main instruments of european union action to reduce disparities between all european regions, in particular the outermost regions, with regard to the internal market and to achieve the europe 2020 objectives, as the european funds are a key instrument for achieving the objectives. it is not only aid but also compensation for the region's shortcomings. however, it should be borne in mind that this eu policy alone cannot overcome all the challenges faced by the outermost regions.
in writing. − cohesion policy is one of the main instruments of eu action to reduce disparities between all european regions, especially the outermost regions, with the aim of integrating these regions into the internal market and strengthening them in the relevant geographical area, promoting their economic development and convergence with the eu mainland, and pursuing the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, as the european funds are a very important instrument, but i believe that this eu policy alone cannot overcome all the difficulties faced by the outermost regions. i therefore abstained in my vote on the european parliament resolution on the role of cohesion policy in the outermost regions of the european union in the context of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. −cohesion policy must be coordinated with the europe 2020 strategy in order to achieve the objectives of the strategy properly and effectively. the outermost regions, although geographically remote from the eu member states, are of great economic importance. the eu's cohesion policy aims to promote the economic development of these regions and their convergence with the eu mainland. i believe that eu rules and programmes should be implemented in the same way throughout the eu. clear criteria must be established to ensure that support is given to those who really need it. it is also essential that aid be granted in accordance with the gdp indicator and the level of development of each region.
in writing. − the eu respects two principles: harmony and specificity. european cohesion policy promotes prosperity of all the regions by taking advantage of their strengths. in the context of eu 2020 the outermost regions of the eu need a specific approach to help them to reach the objectives. i voted in favour of this report, because the european policy towards the outermost regions needs a strategic approach. on the one hand, the outermost regions have to be managed in a specific way, based on their particularities. on the other hand, these regions cannot be excluded from transverse european policies. in view of success already achieved, specific measures should be developed in different sectors, promoting the growth and cohesion of these regions. a very important measure to ensure their cohesion is the promotion of partnership relations with both neighbouring regions and more remote territories.
