in writing. - i voted for this document. the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) aims to remove some of the main tax obstacles to growth in the single market. in the absence of common corporate tax rules, differences in national tax systems often lead to over- and double taxation, and companies face a high administrative burden and compliance costs. this situation is not conducive to investment in the eu and therefore hinders the implementation of the priorities set out in the europe 2020 strategy. although the commission proposal does not make it mandatory for ucits, in order for the scheme to have a real impact on businesses, to increase fiscal transparency, and to improve the fairness and efficiency of the tax system, it needs to be made mandatory for all businesses operating in the eu. i therefore support the european parliament's proposal to establish a timetable for the transition to the mandatory application of the ccctb in the long term.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) is a necessary instrument for the creation of the european internal market and for ensuring the european economic integration necessary for the stability of the euro area. the tax bases of the member states of the european union are different and partly constitute barriers to trade which hamper growth and employment. the european union's system of stss comprises a comprehensive set of rules governing how the separate tax for each undertaking or branch is calculated, how those results (profits and losses) are consolidated and how that consolidated tax base, when positive, is allocated proportionally to all the member states concerned. the important point is that each member state will apply its own tariff to its part of the tax base. only the calculation and allocation of the tax base will be coordinated. member states will be able to set their own rates of taxation. nor will national financial reporting rules be harmonised. with regard to the ccctb, the objective will be to reduce the cost of tax compliance for companies in the internal market by establishing a common corporate tax base system so that groups of companies can deal with only one tax administration. however, to ensure that the calculation of the tax base does not take account of fraudulent transactions whose main purpose is to avoid taxation, it is necessary to consider stricter anti-abuse rules.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the ccctb directive sets out common rules for the calculation of the tax base applicable to companies operating in the eu. this eu tax system comprises a comprehensive set of rules on how to calculate the individual tax for each company or branch, how to consolidate those results (profits and losses) taking into account the other members of the group and how to distribute that consolidated tax base, where it is positive, proportionately to all the member states concerned. only the calculation and allocation of the tax base will be coordinated. member states will be able to set their own rates of taxation. the national financial reporting rules shall also not apply. the escb is a necessary instrument for the creation of the european internal market and for the economic integration of europe. the various distortions of the internal market can only be eliminated by adopting a common set of rules, applying common administrative procedures and the 'one-stop-shop' principle. the main benefits of using the ccctb are: greater fiscal transparency; lower implementation costs and less red tape, thus improving the growth potential of cross-border businesses, making the eu more attractive to foreign investors; the likelihood that decisions on allocation in the internal market will be taken in a more tax-neutral socioeconomic context than is currently the case; reduction of two types of tax problems (tax avoidance and evasion, and double taxation).
in writing. − establishing a common eu-wide consolidated corporate tax base an attractive proposition, providing convenience for companies operating in more than one member state, providing clarity in the calculation of corporate tax. on the other hand, the harmonisation of the base must not lead to the harmonisation of the tariff, since this could have a negative impact on the economy of some member states and on investment in them.
in writing. − i support this resolution on the council directive on a common consolidated corporate tax base. i believe that it is necessary to enable all taxpayers in the european union to calculate the tax base on the basis of uniform rules for the calculation of taxable profits. this will benefit companies operating across borders. i think it is appropriate that the system for calculating the corporation tax should be optional rather than mandatory. in particular, greater fiscal transparency, lower implementation costs and less red tape will be ensured. i do not support the proposal to set a minimum european rate of corporation tax. the proposed minimum corporate tax rate of 25% would not be objectively justified and appropriate for many companies. i think that the member states should set the level of corporate tax themselves.
in writing. - i abstained on this important question. the commission's proposal on energy products and electricity taxes is indeed a major contribution to the reduction of greenhouse gases set out in the eu's 2020 strategy. the commission proposes to split energy taxation into co2 taxation and energy value taxation. this means that a single minimum rate of co2 emissions (eur 20/t co2) will be set for all sectors not covered by the eu emissions trading system. therefore, these sectors, in particular households, transport, small businesses and agriculture, will be subject to a co2 price. in addition, each energy product will be taxed according to the amount of energy that can be extracted from it. while the introduction of a co2-related tax of eur 20 per tonne is projected to generate eur 20 billion in tax revenues from all eu member states as early as 2020, it is necessary to assess in detail the impact of this proposal on eu industry and its economic growth. the adoption of this proposal would lead to a significant increase in diesel prices in many member states, which would have a negative impact on europe's competitiveness in the development of diesel engine technologies and on the european automotive industry, which is already facing serious competition from third countries. i think it is necessary to review and evaluate the implications of this proposal in depth.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it is a major contribution to the implementation of the european union's strategy europe 2020 on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. the main objective of the current energy taxation directive, adopted in 2003, is to prevent distortions of competition in the energy sector of the internal market. with this proposal to amend the directive, the european commission aims to bring together four themes: climate change, energy efficiency, the internal market and the promotion of growth and employment. it is important to adapt the energy tax structure in order to contribute to the objective of transitioning to a low-carbon, energy-efficient economy and to avoid problems in the internal market. the commission proposes to tax energy on two bases: the amount of co2 emitted and the energy value. this communication, which includes a co2-related element in energy taxation, aims to bring energy taxation into line with the eu's commitments to combat climate change. the aim is also to respect the proportionality of the different minimum levels set by the member states in the european union. the key is therefore to find the right balance between the objectives in order to provide the right impetus at european union level.
in writing. − i would vote against, because although energy price increases encourage more efficient use of energy, the negative consequences of energy price increases ultimately outweigh the positive effect. moreover, recent scientific developments in europe show that the use of diesel engines can be partly used to reduce co2 emissions. the european commission is surprisingly inconsistent in wanting to end automatic wage indexation where it still applies, but, on the same grounds, it proposes to introduce it in the area of energy taxation. the negative impact on households and businesses would be significantly greater than the expected positive impact. the collection of revenues through energy taxes reduces people's incomes.
in writing. − when we consider the issue of energy products and electricity taxes, we are not only talking about eu energy policy, but also about eu environmental policy. in the debates in this chamber, it is often the lament of members that we have too few concrete measures to combat climate change. i therefore welcome the proposal put forward by mr algirdo šemetė, member of the european commission, in particular because it ensures fairness and uniform rules for the taxation of different energy sources by means of a uniform calculation methodology. on the other hand, i agree that the proposal may seem too revolutionary for industry, especially in the light of long-established practices and trends. i agree with the general provisions on the need to change the energy taxation system to promote energy efficiency and the use of less polluting fuels. if we are to achieve our climate change and energy efficiency goals, we will have to take this step. however, i also support a longer transitional period to allow the energy and automotive industries to adapt to the new requirements and the requirement that the ec carry out an impact assessment analysis and only then take appropriate action.
in writing. - i do not support this resolution. the proposed taxation of energy products and electricity will have a significant negative impact on the autonomy of member states' energy tax regimes and on companies operating in the energy market. the automatic indexation of the thresholds would deprive the state of its right to control the thresholds. i believe that member states should choose the most appropriate measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. it should be noted that energy prices have increased recently and are high. however, the application of this directive would lead to an increase in those costs. the final consumer would thus be placed under an unreasonable and disproportionate burden. in addition, the difficulties and problems faced by eu consumers and industry would increase. in view of this, i think that more attention should be paid to industrial policy. this directive should not apply to energy-intensive industry.
in writing. - i supported this report because i agree with its main idea: the rules on energy taxation must be adapted to today's realities and the eu's aspirations. a double taxation system, whereby part of the tax is determined by the co2 emissions of the fuel and part by the energy value of the fuel, will create a level playing field for all fuels. the commission will also consider whether the measures are compatible with the internal market. this will encourage the development of new, more environmentally friendly technologies. new tax rules are particularly important if europe is serious about meeting its climate change commitments by 2020. the commission proposal will only set a minimum tax base. eu countries will have a lot of freedom to set minimum or higher levels of taxation. importantly, the proposal allows eu countries to exempt fuel used for heating residential buildings from taxation. i would think that the transition period until 2023 would give the eu industry, transport and other sectors enough time to adapt to the changes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the problem of tax evasion is becoming more and more acute in the member states of the european union. it has been found that tax evasion and tax avoidance have resulted in the loss of huge amounts of revenue to the budget of the governments of the member states of the european union. this encourages deficits and debts in the member states. the funds for public investment, growth and employment are also declining. the commission has also identified a number of problems with tax evasion and avoidance, which undermine citizens' confidence in the fairness and legality of tax collection. countries participating in aid programmes that have improved tax collection and abolished concessions under european union proposals have experienced their large enterprises leaving them to take advantage of tax breaks offered by other countries. publicly available information on tax evasion and avoidance in each member state should therefore be substantially improved. eu member states should review their tax systems to make them more efficient and effective, to eliminate unjustified exceptions, to broaden the tax base, to reduce the taxation of labour, to improve the efficiency of tax collection and to tackle tax evasion. it is also important to adopt european union rules to prevent forms of tax competition which impede the implementation of recovery strategies by the countries concerned. this can contribute to the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, including those involving third parties.
in writing. − i have endorsed this document as it calls on the commission to address as soon as possible the issues raised by the revision of the eu savings tax directive and to reach an agreement with switzerland and the member states concerned as a matter of urgency. the strengthening of the regulation and transparency of company registers and trust fund registers is an important prerequisite for combating tax avoidance. the commission should identify areas where improvements in eu legislation and administrative cooperation between member states can be made to reduce tax fraud. member states should ensure smooth cooperation and coordination of their tax systems in order to prevent inadvertent tax avoidance, tax evasion and tax fraud. member states must also allocate adequate resources to the national services responsible for combating tax fraud. it is important to implement new and advanced strategies to combat vat fraud across the eu. member states should review existing bilateral agreements between member states and bilateral agreements between member states and third countries to determine the extent to which they contribute to tax avoidance and to the extent to which they impede effective taxation in the country of source in certain member states. there is a need for greater transparency and stricter controls to prevent the use of tax havens belonging to non-cooperative foreign jurisdictions that have no or minimal taxes, do not share information with foreign tax authorities and whose legal, regulatory or administrative provisions are not sufficiently transparent.
in writing. − i support this resolution, which calls for concrete action to combat tax evasion and tax avoidance. in the context of today's european economy and economic downturn, the issues of tax collection and tax policy in general are of particular importance. tax evasion and fraud are a major factor that threatens the revenue of every country and cost billions. this is not a problem that can be solved only at the national level. only an effective and targeted fight against tax evasion and avoidance is the key to securing the resources needed to increase public investment in europe's international competitiveness and growth opportunities. the effectiveness of this fight should not be achieved by policing, but by creating conditions in which tax evasion is both useless and unprofitable. the council should develop eu quantitative targets for reducing tax avoidance by 2020 and complete the reform of the savings tax directive as soon as possible. this would enhance the automatic exchange of information and ensure fair and appropriate taxation of savings income across the eu.
in writing. indeed, the delay in the european union's accession to the european convention on human rights is both worrying and surprising. in particular, all parties, including the two member states opposed to eu accession to the convention, supported and signed the treaty of lisbon in 2007, which provides for the accession of the european union to the convention. a particularly worrying aspect of this issue is that it is precisely these states, which do not support or seek to delay eu accession to the european convention on human rights, that are also seeking reform of the european court of human rights, which would limit the ability of citizens to directly address the court and reduce the court's competence and power. the european parliament already receives letters from concerned citizens for whom the possibility of appealing directly to the court of human rights and the binding nature of its decisions on member states, even in our democratic 21st century european states, is often the last chance to restore justice to them. of course, reforms that would speed up the settlement of cases before the court of human rights are welcome.
i thank the rapporteurs for their work. there is a lack of understanding of the relationship between gender and climate change, and perhaps that is why mr griffin has not understood the problem well enough, and that is what he said today. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new rules and to monitor the implementation of the new rules. while climate change affects all humanity, the recurrence of natural disasters has shown that women and children are still the most affected and the most affected by natural disasters. the poorest women in developing countries are the most vulnerable to climate change, because they do the hard physical work of running the household, working in agriculture, which is really detrimental to their health. unfortunately, women often lack access to health services, and climate change will require even more physical and mental strength from women now and in the future. data are still lacking and statistics are not available by gender. unfortunately, this also hinders a better understanding and appreciation of the gender dimension of climate change. the future will be marked by increasing climate change impacts, and the fight against climate change must be a priority for the european union.
in writing. – i supported the report on the impact of climate change on women because it raises a very specific aspect of environmental policies. climate change is not only about nature and natural resources. human rights and human well-being are challenged by climate change as well. and our efforts in this domain could improve life conditions for millions of people on the earth. the report clearly shows how the environmental policies can promote equality between women and men if they are adjusted to meet the specific needs of women. the issue is particularly important since women play a much more significant role in climate-change-related activities than men. we have to provide women equal opportunities, promote their rights to work, to an equal salary, to necessary health conditions. we also have to improve communication in order to learn their demands and to encourage them to use existing opportunities. therefore i support the rapporteur’s call to the european institutions and national governments to make more efforts to make their environmental policies more gender sensitive.
in writing. today we are discussing the future guidelines for eu environmental policy. this is a relatively new and fast-developing policy area, and it is not surprising that with each environmental action programme adopted new regulatory areas emerge and that existing regulation is often tightened during the programme's lifetime. new scientific data and technical possibilities, as well as accidents with an impact on the environment, mean that the concept of a 'high level of environmental protection' must be constantly reviewed, raising the bar higher and higher. one of the aspects to which we should pay attention in the forthcoming seventh environment action programme is the improvement of the environmental impact assessment process, ensuring its independence. the process that started as a voluntary assessment of planned activities has now become an integral part of the planning process. however, the current arrangements do not ensure that this process is objective and independent of the client. the eu is aware of a number of cases where there were reasonable doubts as to whether the ppp process was indeed transparent. i therefore call for the independence and objectivity of the eia process to be established as one of the environmental policy priorities and for discussions on possible mechanisms to start now, without waiting for the eia directive to be revised.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the draft amending budget for 2012 which aims to allocate eur 650 million in commitment appropriations to the european joint undertaking for iter. this project has been running since 1988 and aims to demonstrate that fusion energy could be a highly useful source of energy in the eu, with the long-term reliability of energy supply and the diversity of energy sources. this international project involves the european union, japan, the united states of america, the people's republic of china, south korea and the russian federation. the price adjustments have increased the eu contribution, which led to the agreement of the european parliament and the council in december 2011 to allocate an additional eur 1 300 million to the iter project in 2012-13.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the europe 2020 strategy envisages that by 2020, 40% of people aged 30-34 in europe should have completed tertiary education or equivalent. it is estimated that 35% of all jobs will require highly qualified workers by 2020, but only 26% of the workforce currently has such qualifications. member states therefore face a major challenge in reforming and modernising their national education systems and adapting them more closely to labour market needs. in this difficult economic and financial period, it is important for all member states to maintain adequate funding for education and to ensure that higher education is accessible to all. given the increasing mobility of eu citizens and its importance, it is necessary to ensure the mutual recognition of diplomas and qualifications in all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report because the situation of youth employment is very bad today in most member states of the european union, including lithuania, and it is only getting worse. unemployment affects all groups of young people, regardless of their level of education and training. however, young people with lower levels of education and training or with no work experience are at greater risk of not finding a job. in addition, many young people are at risk of becoming long-term unemployed. so we need to talk not only about what we will do in the future, but we need to decide what we are going to do now with the young people who are already out of work and who are already at risk of long-term unemployment. it is essential to ensure that future generations of young people entering the labour market have a high level of education and training that meets current and future needs. this means reducing the number of people who are out of school and ensuring that more young people are in vocational education. in addition, barriers between the education sector and the labour market need to be removed and the partnership between enterprises and the education sector strengthened. in the current crisis and budget cuts, young people do not need pretty words and promises, but effective and targeted investments. we must invest in people, in education, in vocational training, in lifelong learning, in jobs, because only then can we give young people the opportunity to find jobs that match their education and qualifications.
in writing. − the report emphasises the importance of eu countries in increasing the number of people with a degree. this is not the most important thing for lithuania, as my country has one of the highest university graduation rates in the eu. lithuania also exceeds the eu average in terms of the number of students per thousand inhabitants compared to the total population (lithuania 73.21; eu 52.8). the priority should be to improve the quality and application of what is taught in our universities. i strongly support the rapporteur's view that university study programmes should respond to the real needs of the labour market and enable graduates to find employment in their field of expertise. according to a january media survey, 32% of lithuanian employers do not agree that people with higher education qualifications have the necessary skills for work. financing of high quality education is a problem in lithuania. although almost 10% of the eu structural funds allocated to lithuania are allocated to higher education, research and innovation, the funding per student in lithuania is one of the lowest in the eu the funding per student in lithuania is about half the eu average. educational reforms are necessary, and it is also important that both students and academics are actively involved in the process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the creation of a digital single market is one of the key objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. a competitive digital single market would remove all remaining barriers to cross-border e-services, contribute to employment, sustainable economic growth, in particular in the area of smes, and allow for the modernisation of public administration and the reduction of the cost of public services. the ict sector directly generates about 5% of the eu's gdp, worth over €660 billion a year, but its potential is not fully exploited. citizens have so far made little use of cross-border electronic commerce, as they do not feel safe due to the legislation in force in different countries, especially in cases of compensation. there are also a number of administrative barriers to business which lead to additional costs, such as the different status of e-accounts, the requirements in different member states and the difficulties arising from the different regulation of e-signatures. i support the commission's 2011-2015 european egovernment plan, the successful implementation of which in the member states would allow for the modernisation and cost reduction of european and national public administrations, and therefore the implementation of this plan in the member states should be closely monitored and assessed annually by the commission, with the objectives of the digital agenda and annual reports to the european parliament.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it would be in the interests of the citizens of the european union to remove all obstacles to the provision of crossborder e-services and to avoid distortions of competition in a competitive digital single market. e-government covers the tools and systems provided by information and communication technologies to deliver better public services to citizens and businesses. the information and communication technologies (ict) sector plays a major role in supporting the balance between eu industrial policy, innovation, growth, competitiveness and trade. the contribution of ict to overall productivity growth is very high. ict can therefore play a major role in the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, in particular in the areas of employment, sustainable economic and productivity growth, empowerment of citizens in research and technological development, energy, innovation and environmental protection, and in addressing major societal challenges. furthermore, remote computing resources services are an economic and ecological measure aimed at improving the performance of public and private companies' computing activities and reducing the costs of data processing and storage. however, the rules for the issue of electronic invoices are not uniform and the benefits of these rules are still not widely exploited. competitive digital single market measures are therefore necessary to ensure the successful deployment of ultra-fast broadband and telecommunications networks in all eu regions and to eliminate disparities in the level of infrastructure deployment within and between member states in order to ensure the demographic sustainability of sparsely populated regions.
in writing. − with the increasing use of broadband internet and the rise of e-commerce and other digital network services, the public sector cannot be left behind. the european commission's initiative to simplify the use of electronic signatures for eu citizens with links to several member states is essential. on the other hand, member states themselves have a long way to go to make electronic services accessible and efficient not only to citizens of other countries but also, and above all, to their own citizens.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the use of electronic services (electronic public administration services) in lithuania is 23%, which is significantly lower than the eu average of 41%. the same applies to internet use in lithuania, which is 54%, compared to the eu-27 average of 70%. in recent years, a large amount of money has been allocated to the development and improvement of electronic services in lithuania from the eu structural funds and the national budget. as the report notes, an important objective of the digital agenda for europe is to promote transparent and sustainable e-government. this is a sensitive objective and i believe that lithuania is interested in promoting digital technologies. the modernisation of the public administration sector in lithuania is essential. however, we should have clear priorities: it is not possible to successfully develop e-government structures until the real power is transparent and sustainable. good management of day-to-day decisions is one of the conditions for effective electronic services. the report rightly notes that electronic services for business are more advanced than those for citizens. however, the problem of the high technological gap between urban and rural areas is not mentioned. this should be reflected in an effective digital agenda for europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because security, stability and development in the whole sahel region are of paramount importance to the european union. the sahel is actively engaged in the fight against terrorism through policies of development, social justice, strengthening the rule of law and integration. however, a coup d'état on the night of 21-22 march 2012 overthrew malian president amadou toumani touré and ended a long democratic process that had begun more than two decades earlier. the proliferation of weapons from libya, the drug trade, high unemployment and poverty are contributing to the destabilisation of the entire region. the country is also facing renewed fighting between government forces and rebels in the north, which has displaced more than 200,000 people since january this year. others have fled to neighboring countries, where severe drought has caused food shortages in recent years. moreover, child soldiers are being recruited into battle. the sahel region is thus facing the worst humanitarian crisis in the last 20 years. the malian people have been subject to numerous human rights violations, particularly in the rebel-held northern regions. millions of people are severely malnourished and over 175 000 children suffer from severe malnutrition. we need to offer local people economic opportunities, alternatives to the criminal economy. a framework agreement should be signed, providing for actions capable of restoring constitutional order.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the changes taking place in burma present important opportunities for improving relations between the european union and burma (myanmar). on 1 april 2012, burma held by-elections for 40 seats in the pyithu hluttaw, the lower house of parliament, and these by-elections, which were considered free and fair by the international community, are an indication that burma (myanmar) is moving towards democratic change. the invitation and participation of foreign observers and journalists, including the representative of the european parliament, in the elections demonstrates the determination of the government of burma (myanmar) to continue the reform process, which should be sustainable and irreversible. in addition, in its first year of office, the government of president thein sein made more progress towards democracy than in any of its previous decades. finally, the government has taken action to address concerns about projects that may be environmentally and socially harmful, and has taken steps to increase civil liberties in the country by granting greater freedom of information and expression. the developments in burma are thus welcomed by the member states of the european union. however, policy decisions at the highest level still do not match the limited institutional and technical capabilities on the ground. the changes are slowly affecting the lives of most burmese citizens as they continue to face problems related to high poverty, high debt, lack of employment and lack of social services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. back in 2000, at the united nations millennium summit, 189 nations around the world adopted the millennium development goals, which they committed to achieving by 2015. these goals include halving global poverty by 2015, reducing by two thirds the under-5 mortality rate, reducing by three quarters the maternal mortality rate, halting the spread of hiv/aids and other communicable diseases, ensuring sustainable economic and environmental development, and so on. the european external action service established by the treaty of lisbon should contribute effectively to the achievement of these objectives, and therefore, with three years to go until the ipa deadline, there is a need to strengthen the coordination of action by the eu, the member states and the partner countries and to combine development action with its effectiveness and efficiency. i agree that the eu external action service needs to be strengthened and that its mandate and competence in the field of development cooperation should be clearly defined.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the reform of the european union's external aid should help to show how aid helps to improve the lives of people living in poverty. the main objective of the delegation of power and the further reform of the commission's external aid management is to speed up and make more robust the financial management procedures and to improve the quality of assistance to partner countries. in addition, the delegation of power should be tailored to the system of providing all relevant information at member state level on where the agencies intend to spend their budgetary resources, thereby improving the targeting of the assistance and allowing the identification of resource gaps and funding opportunities for individual member states. the commission should complement the criteria and improve the procedures for assessing the quality of the projects financed, in order to improve the quality of the aid granted and to minimise the implementation of non-productive projects. the commission should also take all necessary measures to address the shortcomings in the supervisory and control systems, in particular at delegation level. in addition, the commission and the member states should make greater efforts to strengthen the links between the european union delegations and bilateral agencies, government partners and other development actors such as expert groups, universities, foundations, non-governmental organisations and regional institutions, as closer links would help to increase the transferability of mandates and the comparative advantages of different actors at national level.
in writing. − i voted for this report on women and climate change because there is still a lot of work to be done in this area, as the gender dimension in climate policy is still not integrated. in some regions, nearly 70% of all working women are engaged in agriculture and produce up to 90% of the harvest of some crops, but they are hardly represented in budgetary considerations and climate change action. in addition, drought and water shortages caused by climate change are forcing women to work harder to secure water, food and energy, and young people are often leaving school to help their mothers with these tasks. it should be recognised that climate change is exacerbating gender discrimination, among other catastrophic consequences. stopping dangerous climate change must therefore be the top priority of the european union's internal and external policies. unfortunately, there is still a lack of data and gender-based statistics that could be used for research in transport, energy and agricultural policy. more data on climate change could help to better understand and assess the gender dimension of climate change. the commission should therefore step up its efforts in this area and aim to integrate gender equality into the european union's climate change policy as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because biodiversity is essential for the survival of human life and for the well-being of societies because of the ecosystem functions it provides, and payment for ecosystem functions is a promising innovative financial instrument for biodiversity conservation. the european union has not achieved its 2010 biodiversity target of preventing biodiversity loss. at present, the loss of this species is reducing global gdp by 3 percent each year. almost 65% of habitat types and 52% of species listed in the annexes to the habitats directive have an unsatisfactory conservation status. climate change is also a threat to habitats and species. moreover, more than 11 000 alien species have already entered the european union, of which at least 15% are invasive and destroy biodiversity. measures are therefore needed to preserve nature and ecosystem functions for future generations, with a higher political priority for biodiversity. the main objective of the european union's europe 2020 strategy in the field of biodiversity and the global biodiversity commitments should also be achieved. it is also important that other multiannual financial programmes provide for adequate funding and the value of biodiversity and ecosystem functions in the economy. the conservation of biological diversity is a shared challenge that, with sufficient financial resources and political will, must be met with the participation and commitment of a wide range of stakeholders.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because a healthy environment and a high level of environmental protection are essential to ensure a quality of life and to preserve the stability of ecosystems. the current sixth environment action programme, the first adopted under the legislative co-decision procedure, will expire on 22 july 2012. over the decade, the sixth environmental action programme has provided a comprehensive framework for environmental policy planning, consolidated and substantially supplemented environmental legislation and reinforced its legitimacy, and contributed to increased accountability. however, progress towards the objectives set out in the sixth environment action programme has been uneven. the eu member states and the commission have not always acted in accordance with this programme there are still wide differences between member states in the quality of the environment and public health. in addition, there were a number of inaccuracies in the programme that needed to be corrected. the remaining major environmental problems can therefore have significant consequences if they are not addressed. urgent action is therefore needed to help make the transition to a sustainable future. the seventh environment action programme should be adopted, which should be a comprehensive framework to address persistent and emerging environmental and sustainability challenges, taking into account measures already implemented and planned. it is important to focus on the implementation and strengthening of environmental legislation, the integration of environmental objectives into all sectoral policies and the international environmental dimension.

mr president, i would like to touch on a question regarding the report on the european institute for gender equality. paragraph 3 proposes the merger of the european institute for gender equality and the european union agency for fundamental rights. gender equality is a founding value of the european union and has implications broader than simply those of human rights. i have to say that these two bodies have completely different objectives. the institute for gender equality was planned over more than 10 years. the initiative for it came from this parliament, and after long preparations it started work in 2010. i have not heard anything to suggest that its work has been inefficient. the main argument is that of saving resources. in this house we often speak about greater integration in the european union, in order to bring it closer to our citizens. agencies, institutes, other eu bodies and the member states all help us to deliver the message of the european union. to have more europe in every member state is our goal. these bodies contribute a great deal to both eu and national policies. if we are concerned with saving resources, we need to talk about reform in a broader sense, systematically, and not only merely in terms of merging some of the eu institutions or agencies. when we talk about savings, we can talk about strasbourg and about other things, but money is not always what is at issue. there are certain things that we deliver to our citizens, and i think that having this kind of agency in member states is crucial. i call on you to vote today not to merge these institutions.
in writing. i would like to ask my colleague to vote in favour of the report adopted by the committee on budgetary control on the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european institute for gender equality (eige) for 2010. i would also like to ask my colleagues to support the amendment tabled on behalf of the socialist group, which proposes that the proposal to merge the european institute for gender equality and the european agency for fundamental rights be deleted from the resolution annexed to parliament's decision. in view of the importance of this institute in promoting the implementation of the gender equality dimension in the policies of the european union and its member states, as well as the efforts to ensure the implementation of gender equality in the labour markets of the member states and the awareness raising of citizens on this issue, we cannot vote for the abolition of this institute in the future. gender equality is one of the european union's fundamental values, reaffirmed in the europe 2020 strategy and in all its implementing documents. progressive thinking should prevent us from even considering such a possibility. the eige's mandate is unique compared to that of the european agency for fundamental rights in that it concerns the control of de facto equality between women and men, which means the practical equality between women and men in all areas of life enshrined in eu policies. the fundamental rights agency's mandate, on the other hand, is related to legal equality.
in writing. i would like to express my disagreement with the proposal to merge the european institute for gender equality with the european union agency for fundamental rights, which is included in the 2010 discharge. this proposal is based on the need to save money and avoid duplication of work. i would like to draw the attention of my colleagues to the fact that the objectives of the two institutions differ. the institute was created precisely because some of the gender equality tasks were not being fulfilled by the institutions in place at the time. the european institute for gender equality has a unique mission: coordinating research data and information, centralising and disseminating information, networking, raising the profile of equality between women and men, etc. the institute was only established in 2007 and the recruitment of staff has also recently ended. so when the institute is finally able to perform its functions effectively, i think it is irrational and unjustified to reform it.

in writing. − the european union as member of wto respects its commitments to wto agreements. we regret that european legislation was not conforming to them and welcome the modifications. this case is particularly important concerning china which is a huge trade partner for eu, but unfortunately is not completely governed on market-economy principles. current european rules impose strict duties on individual chinese exporters, who are already disadvantaged in their own country by market regulation. i support modifications brought to the european legislation on this topic, because i consider the efforts that european union should make to support non-state economical actors in non-market economies, such as china is important.
in writing. - i support the proposal to repeal regulation (ec) no 1342/2007. in view of the accession of the russian federation to the wto, the regulation and the quotas for imports into the eu of steel originating in russia should be abolished. i am pleased that the eu can expect to gain greater access to the russian market once russia joins the wto and adheres to the rules-based multilateral trading system. any obstacles to bilateral trade in steel products should be kept to a minimum and applied only in accordance with wto rules governing tariffs, trade defence measures, technical standards, special customs and customs clearance procedures, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing council regulation (ec) no 1342/2007 on the administration of certain restrictions on imports of certain steel products from the russian federation. the russian federation became a wto member on 16 december 2011 and as of the date of russia's accession to the wto, the eu is not entitled to continue to apply steel import quotas. the eu can be expected to gain greater access to the russian market once russia adheres to the rules-based multilateral trading system of the wto. the european commission estimates that the value of additional exports in the iron and steel sector will be around eur 107 million per year. it also envisages that the export duties on ferrous scrap, which will be reduced from 15% currently to 5% five years after the date of accession, and the gas prices adapted to local industrial customers in russia will increase the competitiveness of the eu steel sector.
in writing. − the eu welcomes very much the fact russian federation has joined wto. it is big step forward which means significant progress in russia's move towards market economy and worldwide trade without barriers. wto rules forbid protectionism and unfair trade practices (such as dumping, etc.) what makes the economy more open, liberal and competitive. i voted in favor of this report, because russia's membership has even greater importance, since this country is finally moving a big and long awaited step towards liberal evolution. russia's membership in wto has big importance for the eu as russian federation is the largest eu trade partner in many sectors. eu respects its wto free trade commitments and welcomes removal of existing import quotas for several steel products from russian federation. as far as steel sector represents important part not only in eu import, but also export, we envisage bilateral benefits for eu-russia trade system, significant growth and increase of competitiveness.
in writing. - i support the draft regulation. the publication of the electronic version of the official journal on an equal footing with the current publication of the official journal is a welcome reform that will increase access to eu legislation for citizens, increase legal certainty and reduce the cost of access for consumers and businesses. at present, almost all eu legislation is available only in electronic form, and the fact that electronic versions are not legally binding is unacceptable and creates uncertainty about the exact content of eu legislation in the eur-lex database.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft council regulation on the publication of the electronic version of the official journal of the european union. as you know, the commission presented its proposal on 4 april 2011 with the aim of strengthening legal certainty by broadening access to eu law and enabling everyone to rely on the electronic edition of the official journal of the european union (oj) as the official, authentic, up-to-date and complete version. the proposal therefore provides for the publication of the electronic version to be equivalent to the publication of the official journal in force. however, in exceptional and short-term cases of unforeseen disruption to the publication of the electronic version, the printed version would have legal effect.
in writing. − i support the proposal to emphasise the importance of regional airports and their contribution to the eu transport network, thus promoting the creation of a strong, competitive and economically viable eu aviation area. the movement of people and goods across regions and the smoother functioning of the eu's single market are key drivers of economic growth in the eu. airports play an important role in enhancing territorial, economic and social cohesion in the member states by connecting regions. the commission notes that the airport services agreement with ryanair was signed on the same day as the airport services agreement with ryanair. the commission notes that the airport services agreement between ryanair and ams was signed on the same day as the agreement between ryanair and ams. one of the main recommendations i see is to encourage the sector to develop a diversified transport offering through the sale of continuous travel tickets for use in both the rail and air transport sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the future of regional airports and air connectivity in the european union, as regional airports and air connectivity are of vital importance not only because they are vital transport hubs for the movement of people and goods between regions and the smooth functioning of the eu single market, but also because they are in themselves the most important driver of economic growth. together, they push the boundaries of traditional trade routes and make a significant contribution to the prosperity of the cities and regions they serve. these infrastructures and services are important for people living outside the core urban areas and for the eu as a whole. the european commission tends to focus on the major major airports when proposing legislation in the field of aviation. this report seeks to restore balance and to highlight the often unintentional but disproportionate impact of certain eu legislation on regional airports and air services. in addition, ways should be sought to improve the operational and economic efficiency of regional airports and air connectivity services, as well as to ensure a better experience for passengers using these infrastructures and services.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the discharge. the commission is responsible for the implementation of the eu budget and the management of programmes, and it is therefore essential that, in this difficult economic and financial crisis, the commission sets an example of good public governance. good governance is a key factor in maintaining citizens' trust in the european union. the ongoing financial and budgetary crisis in the member states also poses risks to the union budget, in particular financial risks linked to loans to member states. i support the european parliament's calls for the commission to present an action plan for priority actions such as closely monitoring financial engineering instruments, improving and strengthening accountability, reconsidering the use of pre-financing more frequently and creating an effective sanction mechanism in cohesion policy.
in writing. − as a reminder, by granting discharge, the ep recognises that the institution or agency has implemented its budget properly. it is clear that europe is facing a serious budgetary and financial crisis which may undermine confidence in the european union and it is essential that the union and the european commission, as the executors of the union budget, set an example in ensuring good public governance. more than 90% of all errors were identified not by the commission but by the member states' authorities and final beneficiaries. i voted in favour of the discharge for the european commission's budget, which represents more than 80% of all eu expenditure. however, i believe that the european union, in the current situation, needs a rigorous, independent and effective external audit more than ever. there are many problematic questions to which citizens of the european union must have answers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i welcome all the special reports from the court of auditors which show the positive aspects of the commission's work, but also the problems the commission faces in implementing the eu budget and managing eu programmes. i agree with the conclusions and recommendations of the court of auditors contained in these reports and with the calls on the commission and the member states to take full account of these recommendations. as a member of the s&d group responsible for the consultation of the olaf committee on budgetary control, i would like to draw particular attention to the court of auditors' special report no 2/2011 further measures in the light of special report no 1/2005 on european anti-fraud management. the court is very concerned to note that the average duration of olaf's case management is more than two years, which indicates that problems remain with olaf's management system and the allocation of tasks. olaf and eurojust signed a cooperation agreement in 2008 to combat fraud more effectively, but the number of cases olaf has transferred to eurojust (five in 2008 and one in 2009) shows that cooperation between the two services is not effective. i agree that it is necessary to improve olaf's governance structure and to reduce the time it takes to deal with cases, so that financial crime and fraud can be tackled more effectively across the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the court's special reports in the context of the commission's discharge procedure for the implementation of the 2010 budget, since, in accordance with article 17 (1) of the treaty on european union, the commission implements the budget and manages the programmes in accordance with the provisions of article 317 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, in cooperation with the member states under its own responsibility and in accordance with the principle of sound financial management. the court's special reports provide information on key issues relating to the use of funds, which is therefore important for parliament's role as discharge authority. parliament's comments on the court of auditors' special reports form an integral part of the abovementioned decision of 10 may 2012 on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section iii commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the discharge for the european parliament. i welcome the rather positive evaluations of the court and agree with all its conclusions and recommendations. it is important that parliament takes due account of the court's recommendations, in particular by improving procurement procedures, reviewing procurement controls to ensure the most competitive prices for the services and goods offered and the most efficient use of eu taxpayers' money. as i did last year, i am in favour of parliament having only one seat in the same place as the other institutions of the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2010, section i european parliament, as the court's audit found that the supervisory and control systems required by the financial regulation were satisfactorily applied by all the institutions in the management of administrative expenditure in 2010 and that 93 per cent of the 58 audited payments were free from material error. on 16 june 2011, the secretary-general stated that he had reasonable assurance that parliament's budget had been implemented in accordance with the principles of sound financial management and that the control procedures in place had adequately ensured the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the discharge for the 8th, 9th and 10th european development funds. the court found that the final annual accounts of the eighth, ninth and tenth edfs presented the financial position of the edfs for 2010 correctly in all material respects and that there were no material errors in the accounts for revenue and liabilities. the problem of the shortage of workers is a concern. i welcome the fact that a financial management toolkit has been distributed to give project implementing organisations more knowledge about financial management and compliance. as regards the court of auditors' special report no 11/2010, i agree with the audit findings and the useful recommendations contained therein. i believe that the gsp is a very valuable aid instrument that can increase the autonomy and accountability of the governments of the beneficiary countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution with observations forming an integral part of the decision on discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2010. the court of auditors considers that coding errors are still frequent. it is noted that the court concluded that, although these errors did not have a significant impact on the 2010 annual accounts, they could affect the reliability of the financial management data of the europeaid directorate-general. the court found that there were no significant errors in the accounts for revenue and liabilities, but was very concerned that there were too many non-quantifiable errors affecting the obligations to comply with the tendering rules and the legal deadlines for the conclusion of contracts. it is worrying that there was an increase in projects with unsatisfactory results in 2010 (12,6% compared to 11% in 2009) and that commitments errors are still very common in projects under decentralised management.

in writing. − since 2008, the problem of piracy at sea has been growing steadily the number of attacks has increased every year, the technological level of the weapons used by pirates has improved, the coordination of attacks has improved, the ransom demand has increased. it is worth noting that without the efforts of the international community and the eu atalanta mission, this problem would probably have become even more widespread and out of control. examples of ships carrying military equipment falling into the hands of pirates are particularly worrying. piracy complicates international trade, endangers the transport of strategic and environmentally dangerous cargoes, increases costs (the cost of insuring a single ship has increased tenfold), can lead to ecological disasters (e.g. oil spills from ships), deepens the destabilisation of countries and regions, hinders development and, above all, constantly claims innocent lives. piracy cannot be justified on any grounds, it is an international crime and could be equated with terrorist activity. i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that the fight against piracy at sea must be further strengthened.

in writing. − i am pleased that my fellow meps have endorsed my report on the fight against fraud in the european union. the commission estimates that fraud costs the eu over €120 billion a year, but the true extent of fraud in the eu is not known because of the lack of reliable data. it is safe to say that, since 1989, when the commission started to submit annual reports to the european parliament and the council, neither the commission nor the anti-fraud authority olaf has reliable data from the member states on the actual extent of fraud. this is recognised by the commission itself, which states in its annual report that the data it provides in its annual report should be treated with caution. i think that this situation needs to be changed fundamentally. the report adopted by parliament states that one of the main provisions is that the commission must take full responsibility for the recovery of eu funds illegally paid and for the collection of accurate, relevant and comparable data from the member states, which would allow us in the future to have accurate and correct data that would allow us to objectively assess the extent of fraud in the member states and to combat the misuse of eu funds more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as a large proportion of eu funds continue to be misused, and the commission is called upon to take decisive action to recover more funds wrongly paid, to ensure that member states take greater responsibility for losses related to irregularities still to be recovered, to improve the prevention and detection of irregularities and fraud, and to suspend payments immediately and apply effective sanctions in the event of misuse of eu funds. i also agree with the provision that olaf's independence, efficiency and effectiveness must be further strengthened and that the commission must take full responsibility for the recovery of funds wrongly paid.
in writing. − the european union functions on principles of cooperation and consensus. our common welfare depends on good coordination of 27 member states. it is extremely complicated task which necessitates fair contributions of all participants of the process. the whole world is witness of difficult situation in which eu was put because of frauds of some governments of the member states. this situation gives us even more responsibility: we have not only to overcome our difficulties, but to improve our cooperation processes. good reporting is one of integral part of this task. commission's annual report 2010 on the protection of the european union's financial interests argues that not all member states honor their reporting obligations. i support the rapporteur in his call to the commission to demand all necessary data from the member states. i voted in favor of this report because i agree that the eu governments should promote effective use of reporting tools in order to improve commission's eu development monitoring and facilitate european decision-making.
in writing. - i agree with this report. the low use of roaming services in the eu does not meet the needs of the european economy and is incompatible with the idea of a digital european single market. in order to reduce the often high roaming data prices, it is essential to promote competition between operators and thus encourage them to offer more attractive prices to customers. it is essential to reduce the current ceilings for wholesale and retail prices for calling and sms services and to set a ceiling for retail prices. the current regulation on roaming on public mobile telephone networks in the community will expire in june, and i therefore support the new version and the proposals contained therein. i agree with the lower prices proposed by parliament, respectively: • 24 euro cents per minute for a consumer call, • 10 euro cents per call received, • 10 euro cents for a text message, • 50 euro cents per megabyte for downloading data and browsing abroad.
in writing. − i voted for roaming on public mobile networks in the european union, as most europeans turn off their mobile services abroad for fear of having to pay huge bills when they return, as is often the case when using mobile services abroad. only 19% (a minority) of mobile users who use a mobile phone network abroad consider roaming data prices to be acceptable. according to the commission, the average price per megabyte is currently more than eur 2 and in extreme cases it reaches eur 12. this weakness is primarily due to the fact that the roaming market remains under-competitive. excessively high roaming charges, combined with an under-utilisation of roaming services in the eu, do not meet the needs of european consumers or the european economy. this trend is incompatible with the basic idea of a digital european single market. the present proposal for a regulation therefore seeks to rectify this situation. as early as 2010 in the digital agenda for europe, the commission set the objective of achieving broad harmonisation of roaming and domestic mobile tariffs by 2015. in addition to the structural measures envisaged, greater efforts are needed to ensure transparency. first, clear information is needed on the new opportunities and tariffs that the unbundling measure will bring to customers. in the future, roaming contracts would be drawn up and written in a clear and uncomplicated manner.
in writing. by voting in favour of this report, i am affirming that europe is at the service of its citizens. until now, roaming charges have been much higher than national charges for no good reason. the new eu regulation puts an end to this unfair pricing by imposing caps and allowing consumers to choose a different operator than their national operator for roaming services. this regulation is a welcome step forward for european citizens who will now have more control over their mobile phone bill.
in writing. − travel is an integral part of european life. it is therefore natural that we want to receive the same services abroad and on the same terms as we receive them in our own country, and not feel discriminated against by the inhabitants of the country we are travelling to. one area where further reductions in separate charges for roaming and data transmission are needed. this decision not only helps europeans on the move, but is also one of the examples of how the european parliament is making a real contribution to the building of a united europe.
in writing. - i agree with this report. i welcome the new wording of the regulation drawn up by the commission. it is important to clarify some definitions and to align the regulation with the new legislation and to involve echa in the implementation of the regulation. it would be logical to have a european chemicals agency which could take over a large part of the responsibility for the implementation of this regulation. i would not agree to a change in the rules of procedure of the ips. the ips procedure applies to chemicals, including pesticides and industrial chemicals, which are banned or severely restricted due to their effects on health or the environment. the eu should exercise extreme caution when exporting these chemicals to third countries, so that this is not done against the will of these countries. i do not think that the eu's interest in ensuring the profits of producers of dangerous chemicals who have difficulty selling them within the eu should take precedence over the eu's commitment to protecting human health and the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union is implementing the rotterdam convention, which aims to promote the exchange of information on chemicals traded between the parties to the convention and also to implement the prior informed consent (pic) procedure when a party to the convention exports a chemical covered by the convention to another party to the convention. the ips procedure helps to ensure that the exporting countries obtain the approval of the official importing countries for the substances before export. the european union is taking a step further than the rotterdam convention in the new version of the regulation adopted today, as it includes more substances than the rotterdam convention. the new wording of the ips regulation is necessary to clarify and align it with recently adopted legislation in the field of chemicals, to change the provisions relating to representation outside the union, to facilitate export and import conditions and to apply stricter measures for the incorrect implementation of those conditions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the export and import of dangerous substances, as regulation no 689/2008/ec (the ips regulation) implements the rotterdam convention in the european union. the purpose of the rotterdam convention is to promote the exchange of information on chemicals traded between parties to the convention and to implement the informed consent procedure (ips) when a party exports a scheduled chemical to another party to the convention. this is a measure to ensure that the exporting countries of chemicals obtain the approval of the official importing countries before export. this procedure applies to chemicals listed in annex iii to the rotterdam convention, which covers pesticides and industrial chemicals that are banned or severely restricted by the parties for reasons of health or environmental impact and are notified to the parties for the purpose of applying the ips procedure to these substances. in line with regulation (ec) no 689/2008, the eu is going beyond the scope of the rotterdam convention, as this regulation covers more substances than the rotterdam convention. furthermore, the ips procedure is applicable to all countries importing listed chemicals from the eu, not just the parties to the convention.
in writing. − the european union is now a world leader in environmental protection. i hope we can maintain these positions for the foreseeable future. i therefore support the rapporteur's call for administrative procedures to be simplified for the transport of chemicals and for them to be brought into line with international agreements, but i would stress that this must be done in a way that does not have the slightest impact on the environment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree with the amendments to the european commission's proposal for a regulation on the export and import of dangerous substances put forward by the rapporteur. dangerous chemicals should not be exported to other countries without the consent of the host country. experience has shown that the receiving countries do not respond to the request because they do not see the need to respond to requests for chemicals that are covered only by eu legislation but not by the rotterdam convention. i voted in favour of the report because i agree with the rapporteur and i do not support the export facilitations for dangerous chemicals proposed by the european commission. i call for no changes to the rotterdam convention's regulations, whose primary objective is to protect human health and the environment.

mr president, colleagues, recently we all witnessed the doubtful management and misconduct of our parliamentary work when a document duly adopted by plenary was later partly cancelled in a discussion of the conference of presidents. this happened with the resolution on eu-azerbaijan negotiations. no parliamentary rule states that, once adopted, a document can afterwards be changed in substance by another member of parliament. deletion of the relevant part of the text was announced as having been made allegedly in accordance with rule 216, which refers to something different, namely to possible corrigenda to literal or linguistic errata when discovered in a text after the vote. as this was not the case, the corrigendum – as distributed in a breach of due procedure – looks unlawful when the resolution in the form in which parliament voted on it was lawful and legitimate.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in addition to ordinary circulation euro coins, the member states of the european union may issue, in accordance with the rules, special circulation euro coins to commemorate certain events. however, in order to ensure that such coins represent only a small proportion of the total number of euro coins in circulation, a certain limit should be set for the number of circulation commemorative coins. the reduction in the number of commemorative coins in circulation will simplify administrative procedures, such as those for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting. credit institutions and other payment service providers, taking into account the scope of their payment service activities, as well as any other institutions involved in the handling and distribution of banknotes and coins, are obliged to ensure that the euro banknotes and coins they receive and intend to re-circulate are checked for authenticity and recognised as counterfeit. the reduction in the number of commemorative coins in circulation will enable member states to carry out more effective and efficient authentication checks on euro coins throughout the euro area.
