in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. parliament is a full institutional actor in security policy issues and it is therefore necessary to ensure its involvement in defining the specificities, priorities and evaluation of the eu internal security strategy (iss). the objectives of the iss are not exhaustive and should be better defined, and i therefore support the proposals in the report for strengthening the eu's security policy. a policy cycle assessment should be carried out to coordinate national and european action to combat organised crime, as well as an analysis of the threats to be addressed. a parliamentary review of the stockholm programme must be carried out and close cooperation with third countries on security issues ensured.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, even after the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, neither the member states nor the commission had envisaged any role for parliament in this process. the treaty of lisbon created an area of freedom, security and justice in the european union, respecting fundamental rights, the different legal systems and traditions of the member states. the european union's security policy is closely linked to the concrete rule of law principle of the european union and must therefore be strengthened on the basis of democratic values, citizens' rights and fundamental freedoms. the main threats identified in the common strategy for internal security organised crime, terrorism and radicalism, cybercrime, corruption and border management problems have a link between external and internal aspects. the stockholm programme stresses that the internal security strategy of the european union should be developed with a view to further enhancing security throughout the union and to combating organised crime, terrorism and other threats effectively, while respecting fundamental rights, international protection and the rule of law. coordinated and consistent action in both areas is needed to ensure the effectiveness of any response.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution because the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon created an area of freedom, security and justice in the eu, respecting fundamental rights, the different legal systems and traditions of the member states. this policy is a shared competence of the eu and the member states. the commission communication on an internal security strategy 2010-2014 identifies five priority areas where the eu can add value: the fight against and prevention of serious and organised crime, the fight against terrorism and cybercrime, strengthening the management of external borders and increasing resilience to natural and man-made disasters. the ep welcomes the work on the internal security strategy and the main principles underpinning the european security model, in particular the stronger link between security, freedom and privacy and cooperation and solidarity between member states. eu security measures and cooperation must be consistent with the eu's commitments on fundamental rights and must focus more on targeted law enforcement and intelligence-led activities that can reduce crime and prevent terrorist attacks. it is important to ensure coherence and complementarity between the internal and external security aspects and it is also necessary to ensure that the measures and actions implementing the internal security strategy are consistent with the eu's commitments on fundamental rights, as well as with external policy objectives and international human rights and humanitarian law.
in writing. − the need to develop an eu internal security strategy to respond in a coordinated, solidarity-based and effective manner to the diversity of internal security challenges is clear. i agree that freedom, security and justice are objectives to be pursued simultaneously and that the implementation of the eu charter of fundamental rights must be one of the essential elements of the strategy. however, it is regrettable that at a time when we are working to strengthen the european judicial culture, to ensure coordination of the external border management of the countries, and to establish a system for the use and coordination of eu and national measures, there are very painful cases where, in application of the provisions of eu legislation, a third-country national detained in one eu country on suspicion of war crimes and crimes against humanity has been released without being transferred to the judicial authorities of the eu member state that brought the charges against him. this lack of cooperation and solidarity goes against the very essence of the eu's security strategy under development, undermining the member states' ability to pursue justice. i therefore hope that the forthcoming mid-term review of the stockholm programme and other related assessments will take account of such cases so that similar situations do not recur.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the rapporteur mentions organised crime, terrorism and cybercrime as the main themes of the eu's internal security strategy. the problem of organised crime in lithuania is a matter of great concern. eu statistics show that the crime rate in lithuania has risen sharply as the economic situation has deteriorated. in the last few years, drug-related crime has increased by 19%. the economist intelligence unit predicts that this increase in crime will continue to increase in the coming years. in its latest report on crime in europe, the international law enforcement agency europol drew attention to organized crime in lithuania. the report, entitled 'organized crime threat assessment 2011', mentions lithuania 24 times, mostly in the context of organised crime. for comparison, estonia is mentioned 3 times in the report, while latvia is mentioned only once. according to the europol report, lithuanian organised crime groups have established drug trafficking infrastructure, extended supply routes and supplier networks in almost all regions of lithuania. given that lithuania is a member of the eu, this problem is not only a problem for lithuania but for europe as a whole. since 2008, the number of criminal offences in the eu has increased by 7% each year.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the eu is committed to providing its citizens with an area of freedom, security and justice without internal borders, with measures to prevent and combat crime. it is necessary to ensure the consistency and high quality of the eu criminal law, as it is inconsistent today and there is still no body responsible for coordinating all proposals containing criminal law provisions. i support the proposal for an interinstitutional agreement laying down the principles and working methods for the regulation of eu criminal law provisions and the call for the commission to be given clear responsibility for coordinating all proposals containing criminal law provisions. it is also important that the legal provisions are fully clear and in line with the national systems in force.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union has so far often developed criminal law provisions on an ad hoc basis and there is therefore a need for greater consistency. there was no separate area for criminal law. the treaty on european union commits the eu to provide its citizens with an area of freedom, security and justice without internal borders, in which the free movement of persons is ensured by the application of appropriate measures, inter alia, to prevent and combat crime. criminal law provisions can thus be found in the justice and home affairs instruments, as well as in many other eu policies. in order to ensure a more coherent and efficient criminal justice system of the highest quality, parliament needs to improve its procedures in conjunction with the other legislature. the lower crime rate in the eu may not be determined by the criminal law itself the investigation of criminal offences and the enforcement of penalties for them are equally, if not more important. the harmonisation of criminal law in the european union should contribute to the development of a common eu legal culture against crime, complementing but not replacing national legal traditions and having a positive impact on mutual trust between member states in their legal systems.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the eu approach to criminal law because the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has opened up more possibilities for regulating this area at eu level, and therefore aims to harmonise the concept of substantive law, to make it clearer and more understandable. however, proposals for substantive eu criminal law provisions must fully respect the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, and criminal law must fully respect the fundamental rights of suspects, accused persons or convicted persons.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, we must create a genuine common area of justice in the eu. citizens must have confidence that their rights will be protected, regardless of where they are in the 27 member states. the european commission recently acknowledged that the eu has been working for a long time to create a european area of criminal justice with one hand tied behind its back. i think there have been many occasions when the eu's other hand has also covered its eyes. the rapporteur argues that the growing distrust is a prerequisite for the eu-wide recognition of judgments given in other member states. in order to enhance that trust, common minimum standards should be established in relation to the right to a fair trial and the rights of victims of crime. in lithuania, this is a problem. according to many reports published by the european council on foreign relations, judges in lithuania are part of the problem, as they choose a more complex system that they can manipulate to their advantage, such as the 'fee' for changing the date of a court hearing. lithuanians have little confidence in the courts, according to a eurobarometer survey earlier this year. only 22% of lithuanians trust the courts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. eu consumer protection legislation aims to provide overall consumer protection against unfair commercial practices, false advertising and unfair contract terms, but vulnerable consumers must be given special protection and a separate strategy. i agree with the calls on the commission and the member states to analyse carefully consumer behaviour and the circumstances in which certain groups may be vulnerable in order to ensure protection for all consumers, regardless of their abilities. most consumers become vulnerable because of their lack of perseverance in defending their interests, their lack of understanding of the information or opportunities available to them, and their lack of familiarity with current complaint systems and procedures. i therefore support the european parliament's proposals to focus more on consumer information and education campaigns, to simplify complaint procedures, to tighten advertising standards, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the promotion and protection of consumer rights are core values for developing eu policies in the relevant areas, in particular to strengthen the single market and to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. all consumers may become vulnerable at some stage in their lives due to external factors and their interaction with the market or because they are unable to obtain or understand information of importance to consumers and therefore require special protection. the widely used concept of vulnerable consumers covers a heterogeneous group of certain categories of persons considered vulnerable on account of mental, physical or psychological disability, age, infirmity or gender. this concept should also cover consumers who are temporarily placed in a position of powerlessness caused by a gap between their individual status and characteristics or by their external environment, taking into account criteria such as education, social and financial status or access to the internet. the objective of eu consumer protection policy should be to ensure a high level of empowerment and protection for each consumer. in developing a strategy to strengthen the rights of the most vulnerable consumers, it is necessary to seek to enable them to participate in the single market, to contribute not only to their social inclusion and to the creation of a fairer and more tolerant society, but also to the functioning of a more dynamic, secure and competitive internal market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on a strategy to strengthen the rights of vulnerable consumers, because the diversity of cases of vulnerability, both when consumers are legally protected and when they are vulnerable in a particular sector or over a certain period of time, makes it difficult to apply a single appropriate approach and adopt a comprehensive legal instrument. in accordance with current legislation and policy, the issue of vulnerability is therefore addressed on a case-by-case basis. the problem of consumer vulnerability needs to be addressed by eu legislation at a horizontal level, taking into account different consumer needs, capacities and circumstances. the rapporteur specifically addresses the following sectors: finance, food, transport, internet, liberalised markets, access to justice. the vulnerability of older consumers is also highlighted, in particular due to the digitalisation of services and the additional costs incurred in administering services in traditional shops and branches, which in many cases result in older consumers paying more for the same products.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i agree with the rapporteur's main argument that strengthening the rights of the most vulnerable consumers not only contributes to their social inclusion and a fairer society, but also to a more competitive internal market. the rapporteur rightly points out that better consumer information is important to reduce consumer vulnerability. but information alone is not enough. the eurobarometer survey revealed that lithuanian consumers need a stronger consumer protection system. the survey showed that only 37% of lithuanian consumers believe that existing consumer protection measures are sufficiently protected, compared to 59% in the eu. lithuanian consumers reluctantly trust governmental organisations to protect their interests. only 37% of lithuanians believe that the authorities will protect their interests (compared to 54% of the eu average). slightly more lithuanians would trust consumer associations providing help 42% of lithuanians trust independent consumer organisations that defend their consumer rights. the problem, as the world bank report revealed, is that consumer organizations receive limited funding from the government, which is inadequate. ideally, funding from the government would be complemented by funding from european agencies or by their cooperation with existing european consumer associations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i agree with the proposals put forward by the european parliament that the european commission should carry out an analysis of the possible impact of the issue of the 1 and 2 euro banknotes and present a report outlining the positive and negative aspects of the issue of the 1 and 2 euro banknotes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the question of optimising the euro is relevant now that the euro has established itself as an important international currency, increasing investment demand and promoting trade. the single currency and monetary policy of the euro area countries have led to closer trade and financial links between the countries. this growing economic integration has led to more closely coordinated economic policy strategies. although this report relates to the issue of euro coins, one possibility for the future of the euro that the european central bank and the european commission could also consider is the issue of 1 and 2 euro banknotes. while the issuance of 1 and 2 euro banknotes would reduce the circulation of 1 and 2 euro coins, the use of 1 and 2 euro banknotes would at the same time have advantages for the member states: increased currency governance and favourable treatment and a positive impact on european tourism without affecting the value of euro coins. the issuance of the 1 and 2 euro banknotes would increase the value of collectible euro coins. reducing the number of commemorative coins in circulation would help to simplify administrative procedures and their increased rarity would also further increase the value of each commemorative coin.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the single market scoreboard pursues one very important objective: to improve the functioning of the internal market. the importance of a functioning internal market was underlined at the first common market forum in krakow in 2011, in particular in the krakow declaration. this is also reflected in the european parliament's resolution on the outcome of the single market forum, which describes the single market as the most powerful instrument for putting europe back on the path to sustainable growth and jobs. the internal market cannot function properly until the directives relating to the functioning of the internal market are properly transposed into national law and enforced. the average rate of non-transfer is currently 1.2%, above the 1% target agreed by heads of state or government in 2007. the number of directives that have been incorrectly transposed into national law is also high. the internal market scoreboard provides objective and substantive data on the transposition and implementation of eu legislation in the member states on an ongoing basis. this scoreboard is one of the main tools to encourage member states to improve the quality of transposition of internal market directives.
in writing. − i abstained because it is not clear why and why member states are delaying the transposition of eu directives into national law, even though i agree that the single market should be the most powerful instrument to put europe back on the path to sustainable growth and jobs. the internal market cannot function properly unless the directives relating to the functioning of the internal market are properly transposed, applied and enforced. it is necessary for member states to transpose internal market legislation into national law not only in a timely manner but also in an appropriate manner, and the failure of one member state to comply with it is detrimental not only to the economic interests of that member state but also to those of the union as a whole. it is also not enough to transpose eu directives into national law in a timely and proper manner. however, i think the eu should pay more attention to the cause and effect assessment of why some member states are able to implement the provisions in time while others are lagging far behind. knowing the real reasons might even help us to improve our results in this area.

in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i have always supported all initiatives such as the eu citizens' initiative which aim to strengthen the direct link between citizens and the institutions by ensuring that the eu institutions are presented with issues which citizens feel are being ignored. the european citizens' initiative can help eu citizens to participate actively in the eu decision-making process. unfortunately, lithuania lacks serious citizens' initiatives. a recent study published by the london school of economics (lse) revealed that, despite the existence of direct democratic legislative instruments, the political influence of these institutions remains highly questionable. the lse report indicates that this is mainly due to the high level of distrust of lithuanians towards politicians and political institutions, as well as to the skepticism towards citizens' ability to influence politicians. the lack of formation, weakness and passivity of civil society in lithuania also gives me great concern. the problem is partly due to the strict procedural requirements for citizens' initiatives in lithuania. in lithuania, organisers of citizens' initiatives have to collect 300 000 signatures (11.4% of the total population) within three months. this is proportionally several times higher than in most eu countries, further reducing the number of citizens' initiatives.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. china, with its economic potential, has become one of the european union's most important trading partners. trade between the union and china has shown a steady upward trend over the past three decades, giving both partners a high share of world trade. there is, however, one aspect of trade relations to which we should pay particular attention. for almost 15 years, there has been an imbalance in bilateral trade. it's only good for one side of china. this is why the trade deficit is around eur 170 billion to the detriment of the union. the european parliament should draw the commission's attention to the application of the principle of reciprocity in the common commercial policy in relations with china. only in this way will we minimize the lack of fully fair competition resulting from the fact that the chinese economy does not meet the criteria of a market economy. in addition, the union should oblige china to adopt international standards for products and services, which will promote transparency in trade and contribute to the safety of chinese-made products for european consumers. the deepening trade imbalance with china is a warning to the union that without reciprocity in our relations, europe will become a mere market for the chinese economy, rather than a partner for the dynamically developing chinese economy. this is why it is so important to heal the trade relationship between the eu and china.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because in november 2010 in paris, the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icact) amended its multiannual recovery plan for eastern bluefin tuna. as a contracting party to the iccat, the european union is obliged to implement those amendments into eu law. stocks of bluefin tuna have been severely depleted and urgent action is needed to protect them. in this context, icao has adopted a new recommendation. the amendments include a reduction in the tac and a tightening of control measures, in particular those relating to movements and caging operations, to implement the recovery plan. this is of great concern to the european union, as despite the significant investment in eu fisheries management measures, many problems related to the traditional overfishing persist. since the icao recommendation has already been adopted at international level, the possibilities for amending the transposable text are limited. however, a few amendments may be made to improve the proposal. the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna shall take into account the commitments set out in the marine strategy framework directive.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the tac for bluefin tuna has been amended and strengthened many times. this communication contains amendments drawn up in november 2010 and relates to: the reduction of the tac from 13 500 tonnes to 12 900 tonnes (although the tac is not included in this regulation); the strengthening of various aspects of control, in particular as regards the transfer of tuna from nets to traps; the requirement for more detailed data to be included in member states' fishing plans, capacity management plans and inspection plans; the strengthening of measures relating to capacity reductions; the extension of the prohibition period for fishing with beam traps in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean; the prohibition of fishing operations in conjunction with non-eu flagged vessels; the various provisions aimed at increasing inspection and surveillance capacity and the corresponding amendments to the annexes. the eu has no choice but to accept these amendments, as they have been agreed by an international organisation and the eu has not objected to them. the rapporteur therefore confirms them as they stand.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the question of the introduction of double hull or equivalent design requirements for single hull oil tankers is of great importance. oil spills caused by oil tanker accidents such as the 1999 erika and the prestige are major ecological disasters and tragedies for marine fauna and flora. in the interest of the environment and in order to learn from past mistakes, this regulation aims to accelerate the application of the double-bodied requirements in order to reduce the risks of accidental hydrocarbon pollution in european waters. this proposal does not change the substance of the regulation but introduces certain updates. in the light of the power conferred on the commission by the treaty of lisbon to adopt delegated acts, i support the commission's proposal to recast the regulation as it stands at present.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the issue of the early introduction of safety requirements for single hull oil tankers is of great importance for the european union. oil spills caused by oil tanker accidents are a major ecological disaster and a tragedy for marine life. in the interest of the environment, this regulation aims to reduce the risks of accidental pollution in european waters by establishing double-blind requirements. the requirement for tankers to have a double hull would protect cargo tanks from accidents and reduce the risk of pollution. in the cargo tanks of single hull ships, oil is separated from seawater only by the hull plates of the bottom and wall. if these hull plates were damaged by collision or by being washed ashore, there would be a risk that the contents of the cargo tanks could leak into the sea and cause large-scale pollution. an effective way to avoid this danger is to cover the cargo tank with a second layer of sheets of the inner shell, at a sufficient distance from the outer shell.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the accelerated introduction of double hull or equivalent design requirements for single hull oil tankers (recast), as the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission considered that the proposal does not contain any substantive amendments other than the amendments indicated and that, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of the earlier acts and the amendments indicated, the proposal seeks only to codify the existing texts without changing their substance. in the interest of the environment and in order to learn from past mistakes, this regulation aims to reduce the risks of accidental hydrocarbon pollution in european waters by accelerating the application of the double-bodied requirements. in the cargo tanks of single hull ships, oil is separated from seawater only by the hull plates of the bottom and wall. if these hull plates were damaged by collision or by being washed ashore, there would be a risk that the contents of the cargo tanks could leak into the sea and cause large-scale pollution. an effective way to avoid this danger is to cover the cargo tank with a second layer of sheets of the inner shell, at a sufficient distance from the outer shell. this double-hull design protects the cargo tanks from accidents and reduces the risk of pollution.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the light of the economic difficulties, this commission proposal for a financial transaction tax (ftt) is an important response to repeated calls throughout the european union to require the financial sector to contribute to the costs of the current crisis. the fsm is essentially linked to the common market. the creation of a european legal framework for ftt pursues a dual objective: equity, since financial transactions remain largely exempt from taxation, and harmonisation, since a uniform european approach to the taxation of financial transactions must be respected, with tax rates that are at least similar, if not uniform across the eu, and set at the common minimum rate. the emff is also closely linked to the objective of fully exploiting the potential of the single market to revive economic growth in europe and thus enable the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. investment in the single market is necessary and should be provided by a european source of funding. the fms, whose revenue supplements the general budget of the european union, would therefore help to raise the money europe needs by investing consistently in its economic progress. however, the fsm must ensure sufficient revenues to fulfil its role as a policy tool to overcome the crisis and not to shy away from such investment instruments, which are needed in the eu to ensure economic growth and adequate income for pensioners.
in writing. − i voted in favour because the 2008 global financial crisis spread rapidly and with significant effects to the real economy, causing a major global economic downturn and a significant boost to employment. the need for public funds to finance rescue schemes for oversized financial institutions has led to a significant deterioration in the state of public finances and to a further intensification of the global and european economic downturn. the discussions on the financial transaction tax (ftt) were driven by the desire to ensure that the financial sector contributes to the costs of the crisis and that the taxation of the financial sector is uniform with respect to other sectors in the future. it is necessary to create barriers to the excessive risk-taking of financial institutions. this will complement regulatory measures aimed at preventing future crises and generating additional revenue for general budgets, including for fiscal consolidation purposes to promote growth and job creation or to finance specific policy areas such as development aid and climate change. but we must tax the financial sector, not the citizens! the objectives of the fsm can only be achieved if it is set at global level, and the union should lead the efforts to reach agreement on the fsm at global level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i support the european commission's proposal to introduce a financial transaction tax. the socialist and democratic group has for several years urged the european commission and the european member states to cut the profits of financial speculators. the economic crisis has made the need for this tax even clearer, and has finally led the european commission to propose legislation. the financial transaction tax will reduce the risk of speculation, and will make the financial sector more stable. investors will think about long-term investments rather than short-term overnight gains. the estimated €100 billion in annual revenues will allow crisis-hit countries to invest in job creation, innovation and the advancement of the green economy. of course, it would make sense to introduce such a tax globally, or at least at eu level. the reluctance of a few countries to regulate speculative machinery should not be seen as a guarantee for all eu member states. however, if no consensus is reached, individual eu countries or groups of them, as proposed in the communication, could decide to introduce a financial transaction tax on transactions within their countries.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament's proposal for a regulation of the european parliament on the detailed provisions governing the exercise of the right of inquiry by the parliament and repealing decision 95/167/ec, euratom, ecsc of the european parliament, the council and the commission, as this regulation lays down the detailed provisions governing the exercise of the right of inquiry by the european parliament, in the performance of its duties, in respect of suspected irregularities and maladministration in the implementation of union law. the treaty of lisbon has created a renewed and strengthened institutional balance in the union, enabling the union institutions to operate more effectively, more openly and more democratically. in these circumstances, the european parliament's political control functions have been strengthened and extended. in accordance with the practice of national parliaments and in accordance with the requirements of the treaty on european union, the treaty on the functioning of the european union and the treaty establishing the european atomic energy community (hereinafter referred to as the 'treaties'), the committees of inquiry of the european parliament should therefore be strengthened and given specific, concrete and clearly defined powers which better reflect the political importance and powers of the european parliament, while respecting the principle of proportionality enshrined in article 5 of the treaty on european union. the powers conferred on committees of inquiry, which are the exclusive instruments of political control, should be without prejudice to the responsibilities of other institutions. it should be noted that the doctrine of separation of powers should be respected, which provides that the legislative (parliament), executive (government) and judicial (courts) powers should be separated in order to prevent abuse of power.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. macro-financial assistance (mfa) was launched in 1990 to provide financial assistance to third countries experiencing short-term balance of payments difficulties. a total of 55 mff decisions have been approved so far for 23 countries, with a total commitment of eur 7.2 billion in grants and loans. it is important to provide for a formal legal instrument for mtfs to third parties and to provide for a faster and more efficient decision-making process for individual mtf actions. i agree with the proposal to update and clarify certain rules, in particular those relating to the geographical coverage of the mfp. as for the political conditions, i agree that the eu does not take them very much into account when providing mff. i therefore support the european parliament's proposals to give sufficient weight to the eu's democratic interests and to the respect of political conditions in the regulation, and in cases where these conditions are not respected to reduce or terminate aid. i also agree that the ep should approve every decision on mff and maintain effective oversight of the funding allocated.
in writing. − i voted in favour because the eu's macro-financial assistance (mfa) was launched in 1990 to provide financial assistance to third countries experiencing short-term balance of payments difficulties. a total of 55 mff decisions have been approved so far for 23 countries, with a total commitment of eur 7.2 billion in grants and loans or a combination of both. eligible countries include candidate countries, potential candidate countries, countries participating in the enp and, in exceptional circumstances, other third countries close to the eu politically, economically and geographically. the regulation, drawn up in accordance with the geneva criteria, stipulates that mfa is granted on the condition that the country has effective democratic mechanisms, including multi-party parliamentary systems, respects the rule of law and respects human rights. the mfi criterion is based on the political, economic and geographical proximity of the countries to the european union and on the imf's system and financial discipline. the main objectives of the commission's proposal are to provide a formal legal instrument for mff to third countries, to provide for a faster, more efficient and more rational decision-making process for individual mff actions, to agree on the rules and conditions applicable to eu institutions (the ep should be involved in the development of these rules), to update and clarify some rules, in particular those relating to the geographical coverage of mff, and to align the decision-making on mff with other external financial assistance instruments.
in writing. − eu macro-financial assistance is a significant instrument that allows the eu to help third countries and territories meet the needs arising from sudden economic crises in an operational and add-on way, while strengthening commitments to the union's recognised common values of democracy, the rule of law, good governance, respect for human rights, combating forced child labour, sustainable development assistance, poverty reduction, the fight against corruption, and the principles of open, rules-based and fair trade. it is not a long-term measure, normally for three years, and may be revised if the need for funding decreases. it is important to set clear eligibility criteria for third countries and territories, to give additional powers to the commission, while ensuring democratic control through adequate and timely information to the european parliament and the presentation of an evaluation of implementation every four years.

kalfin on his important and – by the way – timely report. that needs to be underlined, for it is timely and it also opens the floor for a debate. i appreciate highly all that has been said here by members of this parliament for this is not only an issue that is heavy with facts and figures, but it is also a kind of trust and security for people who use the internet. as we say that every european should be connected and should be digital, then it is our responsibility – of parliament, the council and the commission – to provide trust and security, so to speak. as rightly acknowledged in this report, every day, the internet and the digital ecosystem boost productivity, drive innovation, and stimulate growth and high-quality jobs. at the same time, threats are growing and so is the vulnerability of our networks. since 2001, the commission has adopted a number of policy initiatives on network and information security to boost cooperation at eu level, with the involvement of member states and relevant stakeholders and with the support of enisa. this includes the action plan on critical information infrastructure protection (ciip) adopted by the commission in 2009 and revised in 2011. as you may know, the commission is aware that capabilities and preparedness across the eu vary considerably. i have been constantly monitoring the state of progress in the member states on the adoption of national cyber-security strategies and cyber-incident contingency plans, the organisation of national cyber exercises and the establishment of well functioning national/governmental certs, which as you are aware stands for ‘computer emergency response teams’. all those points are addressed in the report and, once again, great work has been done. this stocktaking exercise has demonstrated that, despite the efforts undertaken so far, we need to do more. we need to act strategically and give attention to cyber-security at the highest political level. parliament and relevant stakeholders have long called for the commission to adopt a strategic and comprehensive vision. your support will be crucial in the adoption and implementation of such a vision. in the coming months, i will present, together with high representative catherine ashton and my colleague commissioner cecilia malmström, a comprehensive european strategy for cyber-security. that cyber-security strategy will provide for both policy and regulatory measures. reaching a high level of network and information security across the eu is vital to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market. the measures that we will propose will aim at raising levels of security nationally as well as at eu level, by establishing appropriate mechanisms for cross-border cooperation as well as for public-private cooperation and information exchange. we need to make sure that there are no weak links across the eu. from the policy side, the vision should hinge on the need to improve the overall resilience of network and information systems, stepping up the fight against cybercrime, and developing an external eu cyber-security policy. we will ensure continuity with our policies and make steps forward on key areas such as fighting botnets, cyber-security of industrial control systems, smart grids and security standards, as well as on research and development, awareness-raising and international cooperation. the strategy will include actions to stimulate the competitiveness of the european ict industry and stimulate user demand to provide security functionalities in ict products and services. horizon 2020 will support the goals of the strategy. overall, the strategy will help europe put its own house in order. that will strongly contribute to better positioning the eu at international level also. i hope that you will agree that the strategy adequately responds to the recommendations provided in parliament’s ciip report.

member of the commission. − mr president, a year ago there was a lot of anxiety about schengen. there was fear of unilateral actions on unclear grounds. there was uncertainty over how to act in cases of real persistent problems at borders and under what conditions borders could temporarily be reinstalled. the european council asked the commission to bring forward proposals to strengthen schengen and to enable it to deal with future crises. it asked for a european-based mechanism. in september last year, the commission brought forward such a proposal. it brought forward a proposal on a european-based evaluation to enable the commission, together with member state experts and their agencies, to detect problems early at our borders in order to be able to identify what could be done, to propose remedies, to activate all our tools and to present an action plan that would be compulsory and that the commission would monitor. this would replace the peer-to-peer review that we have today and which has proven to be quite useless. the legal basis for this would be article 77, because only then would there be a robust evaluation with binding impact and an increase in political legitimacy, as the european parliament would be a co-legislator. this is not just a legal proposal; it is also a political ambition. (applause) the other proposal was on the schengen border code, which is also a european mechanism for the reintroduction of borders as a last resort and is linked to the evaluation mechanism. such a situation might arise when everything else has been tried. member states are masters of their borders, but schengen is a joint european achievement and very much cherished by our citizens. new borders will affect citizens, business, trade, jobs and growth, and that is why any decision to reinstall borders cannot be taken unilaterally. it must be a european decision. on the commission side, there is clear disappointment at the decision by the council. it adds very little to current rules; we are creating a system where there is no real enforcement decision that can be followed up at eu level and it does not equip us to fight abuse or populist movements arising from domestic pressure. i appreciate the european parliament’s support for this and am convinced that the last has not been said on this matter. we also took note of the vote yesterday in the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe). the commission will work on this file together with parliament, and i count on parliament’s support to work towards a stronger schengen to the benefit of our citizens, where we defend security but also freedom of movement for citizens, business, jobs and growth so that we have clear and transparent european rules for evaluation and decision-making. (applause)

border controls which the honourable members have raised are covered by the ordinary legislative procedure. it is therefore a great misunderstanding that parliament has no influence on these matters. the substance which the council was able to agree to. the council's discussions on the substance of the proposal made it very clear that the necessary majority could not be obtained for a proposal which could be kept within article 77. there can be no doubt that the council fully recognises that the council and parliament have an equal interest in ensuring a good and well-functioning schengen system. i would therefore like to acknowledge and thank parliament for the continuing drive it has shown in developing schengen cooperation. the european parliament has in many cases been a decisive factor in the continuous adaptation and development of cooperation, and it is therefore also to its credit that the schengen system has been equipped to meet the challenges that have constantly arisen. mr coelho has been the embodiment of this drive for many years, and it is my clear hope that we will also benefit from mr coelho's insight and commitment in the future. despite the differences compromise agreed by the council. i believe that the presidency has been very successful in this respect and therefore the presidency also very much hopes that the final result for all parts of the schengen governance package will be satisfactory to both the council and parliament. the ball is now in parliament's court. as regards the frontier code, parliament will have to play its usual role as co-legislator. in relation to the schengen evaluation mechanism, parliament will be involved in the outcome of the council's negotiations. but as i stressed in my opening remarks, the council is open to take the utmost account of the views expressed by parliament in the course of the consultation. let me be very clear: the council has the greatest possible desire and the strongest possible will to enter into a close dialogue with parliament on this matter. let no one doubt the council's best intentions! the reality is that only if the council and parliament join forces can we achieve the results that are absolutely necessary and that are also expected of us. i look forward to further cooperation on this matter and to entering into a close and constructive dialogue with parliament. i know that this also applies to the next presidency. i now look very much forward to parliament making a formal offer on how you see the matter. i would like to take back to the council the many statements that have come here today and then i would like to thank you again for the opportunity to be here today to explain in detail the council's deliberations on this matter.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report of the european parliament because the commission proposes to grant financial assistance to italy from the european union solidarity fund under point 26 of the interinstitutional agreement of 17 may 2006. the interinstitutional agreement (ia) provides for the possibility of mobilising the fund within the annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. this is the first call for funds in 2012. at the same time as this proposal to mobilise the solidarity fund for italy, the commission also presented a draft amending budget to include the corresponding commitment and payment appropriations in the 2012 budget. italy submitted an application for assistance from the fund following the floods that devastated the regions of liguria and tuscany in october 2011, causing significant damage to residential, commercial and agricultural buildings and destroying key transport links and key public infrastructure networks. the disaster is classified as a natural disaster and falls within the scope of the european union solidarity fund. the commission confirmed that this proposal met the eligibility criteria and proposed to use the funds for commitment and payment appropriations from the eu solidarity fund.

in writing. - i voted for this document. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established in 2006 to provide additional assistance to workers made redundant as a result of structural changes in the world trade system. during the economic and financial crisis, financial support from the fund could also be granted to people made redundant as a result of the crisis. the egf regulation provides for the possibility to allocate each year 0,3% of the annual maximum amount of the egf to technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. in the light of this provision, i have approved the allocation of eur 1,12 million from the egf to ensure the proper implementation of the egf regulation. however, the commission must also take into account the requests of the european parliament, in particular in terms of saving money in the areas of administrative and technical assistance, the creation of a knowledge base and ensuring effective monitoring. i am disappointed by the council's decision not to extend the authorisation of the crisis derogation, which allowed for additional financial assistance to staff made redundant as a result of the current economic and financial crisis, and to increase the level of eu funding to 65% of the cost of the programme. i consider that, in view of the continuing difficult economic situation and the high level of unemployment in the member states, it is necessary to extend the validity of this exceptional provision.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. one of the eu's foreign policy objectives is to develop relations and build partnerships with third countries to promote the economic, social and environmental sustainability of developing countries. the lisbon treaty provides for the common objective of development cooperation to be to eradicate poverty and promote sustainable economic and social development and to achieve the millennium development goals (mdgs) by 2015. i agree with the call made by the european parliament for the need to explore new ways of developing cooperation between the eu and the latin american region in the negotiations on the next financial instrument for development cooperation for 2014-2020. i agree with the need to help latin american countries to pursue fairer fiscal policies, to strengthen tax capacity and to fight fraud and tax evasion, to allocate 20% of eu funds to education and health programmes and to expand the various programmes aimed at strengthening eu-latin american dialogue and cooperation. i believe that the new financial instrument for development cooperation should focus on the fight against poverty and the implementation of the objectives of the imp, in particular by supporting regional, fiscal and tax policies and by promoting social services, science and innovation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because latin america and the eu are pursuing a strategic partnership between the two regions based on shared values and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the eu cannot fail to consider latin america as a priority, and this is reflected in the eu-latin america interregional relations, which have made considerable progress in developing in recent years. the lisbon treaty also provides for a common objective for development cooperation: eradicating poverty and promoting sustainable economic and social development, as well as achieving the millennium development goals (mdgs) by 2015. the latin american region is among the middle-income countries that have made significant progress in reducing poverty and inequality through economic growth and political and social reforms, but despite this, one in three latin american people still live below the poverty line and ten of the region's countries remain among the 15 most unequal countries in the world. the eu must cooperate with all latin american countries, taking the lead in south-south cooperation and the fight against poverty. social cohesion has been the main objective of the strategic partnership since its inception.
in writing. − i supported the document as the eu's development cooperation policy should be defined in close consultation with latin america in order to form a sustainable, fair and well-coordinated development policy for the region. in order to align latin american and eu development policies, latin america must make a special effort to promote the political, economic and trade integration of its region. the lisbon treaty sets the common objective of development cooperation as 'the eradication of poverty and the promotion of sustainable economic and social development, and the achievement of the millennium development goals (mdgs) by 2015'. latin america and the eu are pursuing a strategic partnership between the two regions based on shared values and respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. two of the eu's nine strategic partners in the world are in latin america (brazil and mexico), and the eu is its largest investor and second largest trading partner, as well as its main provider of development aid. most of the world's poor live in these middle-income countries. these countries often face glaring inequalities and weak governance that threaten the sustainability of their own development process. middle-income countries play a key role in global politics, security and trade, and in the production and protection of shared global public goods. after periods of economic prosperity, they are still vulnerable to global economic, environmental or security threats. support for these middle-income countries is important for achieving the mdgs.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european year of volunteering 2011 was launched to raise public awareness of this important area and to encourage volunteering, especially among young people and older people. the number of people engaged in volunteering varies significantly between member states, and some of them do not have a clear and voluntary legal framework to encourage the growth of volunteering and the recognition of volunteers' rights. volunteering is essential to promote social change and solidarity between generations, to help older people make the transition from work to retirement easier, to reduce social exclusion and to promote greater inclusion of young people in society and social processes. however, in order to fully exploit the benefits of volunteering, it is necessary to remove existing barriers, especially for young people, to engage in volunteering both within their own member states and to promote volunteering across borders, and to ensure the recognition of skills and competences through non-formal education and work experience. i therefore fully support the call for the commission to take immediate action to ensure that the european skills passport is introduced as soon as possible, which will provide greater social security, especially for young people, and encourage them to take part more actively in voluntary activities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the initiatives for the voluntary year for active citizenship (2011) have been successfully implemented at european, national and regional levels and there is therefore a need to highlight the value of volunteering clearly and unambiguously. the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations 2012 will be another important occasion to assess the importance of volunteering in everyday life and to enable older people to contribute to the development of a community of solidarity. volunteering non-formal learning experiences for people of all ages. its benefits relate to personal development, the strengthening of democracy, civic values, social solidarity, more active participation in democratic activities, knowledge of other cultures and the acquisition of social and professional skills. moreover, these activities contribute to the eu's policy ambitions in the fields of social inclusion and anti-discrimination, employment, education, culture, skills and citizenship. this is an important factor in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour as the commission is called upon to implement the european skills passport as soon as possible, as the skills acquired through volunteering are also very important in professional life and provide added value to the cv, and it is clear that volunteering can help young people to choose their career path. the creation of a european skills passport will ensure the recognition of professional qualifications at cross-border level and will help individuals to document the competences and skills acquired through their participation in voluntary activities. the passport will be based on the europass model (a european standard cv to be completed online) and will allow skills to be recorded in a transparent and comparable way: volunteering needs to be more recognised by society as a useful experience for young people to acquire skills that they can use in areas such as education and employment. volunteering is an important factor in generating social capital, promoting development and economic and social cohesion, taking into account non-formal learning opportunities, in order to help volunteers acquire skills that will increase their employability and thus contribute to the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. − volunteering is growing both in europe and worldwide. young people choose volunteering for a variety of reasons, from helping those in need to broadening their horizons and improving their skills, to improving their chances of entering the labour market for the first time or re-entering it in the future. unfortunately, bureaucratic or other constraints do not always allow volunteers to make the most of their opportunities. it is therefore essential to reduce the bureaucratic obstacles that hinder volunteering outside the home member state. the full inclusion of voluntary work in the total length of service would also be a crucial step.
in writing. − european action on volunteering is necessary, we have to support this comprehensive instrument which promotes european values, intercultural exchanges, learning of languages, young employment, active ageing. i consider harmonization of cross-border volunteering in the eu as important as erasmus program for higher education. in order to promote cross-border volunteering member states should apply the same approach. volunteers need european recognition of their experience, of their new skills, respect to their work. i support measures proposed by rapporteur to create “skills passport” and to include acquired skills in the ects. support for volunteering organizations is necessary as well and i welcome measures proposed in this document.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, the percentage of lithuanians engaged in voluntary activities is much lower than in other eu countries. according to a report by the european commission, less than 10% of lithuanians volunteer periodically, compared with 40% of austrians, swedes and britons. most lithuanians who volunteer are usually between 15 and 19 years old, and this is also the case in relation to school activities. lithuania's rate is also well below the eu average (23%). in some cases, the difference is very large - more than 15% of irish and finns volunteer in sport. in lithuania, the figure is only 0.1%. why is the rate of voluntary activity so low in lithuania? this is partly due to the poorly developed voluntary sector in lithuania. a survey by vilnius university revealed that 26% of lithuanians do not know where and how to participate in volunteering programmes. lithuanians lack guidance and structure from state leaders who have abandoned civil society. i believe that volunteering opportunities are important for lithuanian society as an expression of citizens' activity in all areas of social life. volunteering is important for the development of democratic values, human dignity and equality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. today, the internet and computer technologies are becoming an integral part of economic, political and social development, making cybersecurity a major political priority in the eu and globally. the europe 2020 strategy includes the eu digital agenda, which sets the eu's technological development goals. the development, use and deployment of technologies depend on their safety and reliability, which must be improved. to this end, i support the proposals to establish effective national certs (networks of computer incident investigation services), develop national cybersecurity strategies, ensure effective coordination between national and eu relevant services through the european network and information security agency (enisa) and implement the already adopted eu programmes to enhance cybersecurity.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the role of technology has increased significantly in all areas of our daily lives: from communications to finance and banking, from transport to energy, from culture and entertainment to health. the full potential of information and communication technologies (ict) can only be realised if consumers have confidence and trust in their security and resilience and if effective enforcement of existing legislation on data privacy and intellectual property rights is ensured.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because, in an age of increasing use of the internet and computer technology, internet security is becoming a top political priority for the eu and the world. the increasing use and deployment of innovative technologies such as high-speed and ultra-high-speed fixed and mobile internet and core networks, smart electricity networks, as well as internet services such as remote computing services and the internet of things, depend on one simple but very important aspect: security, resilience and reliability. it is clear that the internet is a critical infrastructure and that disruptions to its operation can lead to significant losses and security risks, which would affect a very large number of european citizens and businesses. furthermore, rapid technological developments require the prevention of cyber-attacks and remedial action and the resilience of the global network should be based on a comprehensive, responsive, flexible, innovative and long-term system. it is necessary to ensure effective cooperation between governments, businesses, individuals and all other stakeholders through this system. equally important, the resilience of the internet can only be enhanced through an effective framework of international cooperation and international norms.
in writing. − as the events in estonia a few years ago and the constant hacking of websites and databases of important public and private institutions have shown, we are entering a new phase in life where threats to our security are no longer physical but virtual. i therefore support the report's call for greater attention to be paid to this, for a joint eu force to be built up and for crossborder cooperation to be promoted, ensuring that critical infrastructure is protected not only physically but also in computer networks. at the same time, i would like to recall that this protection must be proportionate to the other values recognised and protected in the european union, in particular the protection of personal data and privacy.
in writing. − cyber-security more and more becomes a concern for members states and for ordinary citizens. the eu tries to achieve a better connectivity among the eu states and its citizens, so naturally it has to take necessary measures to protect them as well. it is a inclusive issue balancing between the respect for human rights and need to intervene. i voted in favor of this report, because i consider particularly important the cooperation and information sharing among eu member states regarding the fight against cyber crimes. information technologies make people in europe and all over the world closer. challenges do not respect borders, and we have to harmonize international cyber-security environment. i support the proposal to advance the legislation on cyber crimes. in order to assure due level of protection and security the eu has to manage risks, not just to respond to challenges.
in writing. − cybercrime is a major problem for lithuania not only for our public institutions, but also for ordinary citizens. the cyberattack on the bank of lithuania a few months ago showed that lithuania had failed to learn from previous attacks on our institutions four years ago, which temporarily paralysed the government and industry. more than 55% of lithuanians use online banking, shop or plan holidays online. with the increase in the use of the internet in everyday life, organised crime in lithuania is also increasing, and these crimes are reflected in the entire lithuanian society. according to a study by yahoo!, lithuania has one of the highest rates of online fraud in the world, alongside nigeria, colombia and romania. another new report revealed that organised crime groups sell credit card data for €1 and bank account data for €60. this is not just a problem in lithuania. about one million eu citizens are victims of cybercrime every day. norton, the maker of antivirus software, estimates that cybercrime costs nearly $388 billion a year. as the rapporteur notes, cybercriminals are invisible and often go unpunished. only coordinated action will stop the perpetrators and reduce the risks of cyberspace.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. it is essential to ensure that the european union fully develops its crossborder energy infrastructure and that energy policy is an integral part of the eu's foreign policy. the eu is one of the largest energy buyers in the global energy market and, in order to give it a strong role in international energy relations, it is important to create a well-functioning internal market that creates more competition with external partners. i am in favour of closer cooperation with supplier countries and international organisations and the development of the european energy network and of links with neighbouring countries (the western balkans, the eastern neighbourhood, the caspian countries, north africa and the middle east) by creating new links. i agree that the eu should concentrate its efforts on research, technological development and innovation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in order to address the common global energy challenges and to achieve the eu's ambitious energy and climate change objectives, the european union needs to take joint, effective and equitable action at international level, in particular by strengthening the external dimension of its energy policy and by taking a united position to increase the diversification of energy sources, enhance security of supply and support sustainable production and consumption. the eu can and should continue to foster existing priority areas through cooperation in the field of external energy policy. only a fully integrated european energy market, based on the principle of solidarity, can adequately address the challenges to energy security arising from the different structure and share of energy imports in the various member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour because energy has become a powerful foreign policy weapon today. given the importance of energy in our daily lives, it should be considered a commodity for consumption rather than a tool for foreign policy. the eu must take into account all aspects of our energy security. europe is one of the largest energy buyers on the global energy market. this status could be seen as a weakness, but it could also be one of our strengths: we are the largest importers and if we took advantage of this by coordinating our actions at eu level and maintaining a firm common position in negotiations with third countries, we would always have a good negotiating position and could use our strength as a strong market player. in shaping european energy policy, we should seek a common approach, extending our sphere of influence beyond europe, especially in the case of energy market rules. it is necessary to create a well-functioning internal market that creates more competition for our external partners. we should promote regulatory convergence with our neighbours. ensuring reliable, competitive access to global energy resources is necessary to promote european competitiveness and security in line with the eu policy objectives set out in the 2020 package and the long-term commitment to achieve the lowest carbon economy by 2050. a coherent and coordinated approach by the member states, the commission and the council will allow the eu's external energy objectives to be effectively achieved and will contribute to a better negotiating position vis-à-vis third countries.
in writing. − in today's world, energy is becoming global we import both energy sources and energy itself from third countries. however, energy is closely linked to environmental protection, as natural resources are used and other environmental impacts are generated in the extraction, production and transmission of energy. this impact is also felt in eu countries. it is therefore important to cooperate with third countries to ensure that they comply with relevant environmental standards. first of all, i am talking about nuclear energy, whose environmental impact could be catastrophic in the event of an accident. therefore, one of the key issues in eu cooperation with foreign energy partners is to ensure a high level of nuclear safety, in line with eu standards, for the construction, refurbishment and direct operation of existing power plants in third countries. this should be a basic condition for importing electricity into the european union from nuclear power plants in third countries.
in writing. − given the union's high dependence on energy imports increased diversification of supply sources and transit routes and the development of eu sources of renewable energy is an urgent and essential element supporting the union's external energy security policy. energy policy must become an integrated and prominent part of the common foreign policy and should be elaborated and implemented in synergy with other policies that have an external dimension. i voted in favour of this report, because i agree that external energy policy cooperation must contribute to the promotion of the core values of the union including responsible use of natural resources, fight against climate change, and comprehensive protection of the environment, promote establishing peace and be coherent with the union's foreign policies. i support the rapporteur that the commission should monitor and enforce the highest international safety standards of nuclear power plants in countries neighbouring eu using all available instruments and treaties. eu should again call the neighbouring states to perform comprehensive eu nuclear safety and risk stress tests.
on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, the appointment of an eu special representative on human rights has long been a strategic objective of parliament. that is why we are delighted that the appointment of such a representative is imminent. we look forward to frequent exchanges with the appointee. it is our hope that such a position will help to ensure that human rights feature even more prominently in our external action, and will help further consolidate our credibility in this field. the eu special representative (sr) will have to find his or her place in a complex institutional setting. moreover, the challenges in the field of human rights are many and varied, so the appointee will have to hit the ground running. despite the plethora of competing issues, i hope that the case of tibet will feature prominently among the priority issues to be tackled. also, in anticipation of this afternoon’s debate, i must emphasise that the human rights situation in tibet deserves particular attention. freedom of conscience and belief is very close to my group’s heart. we therefore hope that the eu sr will pay particular attention to the plight and self-immolations of the monks who are subject to the restrictive policies of the chinese authorities. we are worried about the lack of progress and, indeed, worsening repression, and believe that we will perhaps eventually have to consider the appointment of a specific eu sr on tibet. from an institutional perspective, the recommendation that there should be an eu special representative on human rights is obviously only one part of the ongoing review of the eu’s overall human rights strategy, where we are mobilising our potential and political will and increasing interinstitutional preparations to become even more effective on the world stage. meps from a wide spectrum of political groups desire to work towards some form of joint interinstitutional document, an ambitious and united declaration, much like the european consensus on development, which defines the framework of common principles within which the eu and its member states implement their development policies. we need to strive towards a european consensus on human rights which will set out our common vision on the promotion of human rights in the world, with concrete steps on how to achieve our goals. only as ethical partners in the field of human rights will we ever be truly effective as a union. i look forward to working with the different institutions on this in the future.
for the alde group the annual human rights report is always a unique opportunity for the european union, its politicians and human rights defenders to articulate a world vision for which liberal democracies are willing to wage ideological battles that bring us closer to a reality in which cooperation and partnership between states are based not only on economic capacity, rich natural resources, security interests and wise compromises between historical and modern exceptions, but above all on the universal recognition that the value of human life, dignity and rights are essential and fundamental criteria for the civility and credibility of the state, that human rights are not and cannot be the object of negotiation or economic collateral. we had a historic opportunity to see that the quest for freedom and dignity is not just an invention of the modern western world, that it is a universal human quest, spontaneous and momentary, even without any sophisticated politics and philosophy, that unites humanity around the world. this is the arab spring, with its great force of freedom and democracy, which can rightly be compared with such great events in our recent history as the freedom struggles of the peoples of eastern europe and the great human rights movements from andrei sakharov and his comrades in russia to solidarity in poland. as a future rapporteur, i will have the difficult task of trying to assess the lessons learned in europe from the arab spring and to analyse the implications of these lessons for the future of the european union's overall human rights policy. both the arab spring and other events of the past year have increasingly revealed the power of information technology and the importance of the word, media and social media for democratic revolutions and the advancement of democracy. i cannot therefore fail to mention in my report the important events of the past year in belarus and the very bad human rights situation in tibet, which is of concern to my group and, i think, to the whole of parliament and which must be addressed at european union level. mr president, madam president-in-office, the annual report on human rights and the european parliament's cooperation with you must be an opportunity to look boldly ahead to the future of europe and the world, because, let us be frank and not hide this, the retrospective speech in the report on the state of the world in 2011 will be nothing but a speech on the future of the world and strategies for humanity.
in writing. europe is now ready to change course and to take the difficult but necessary decisions that have been taken too slowly and hesitantly. with investors losing confidence in the markets and new member states queuing up for financial assistance, there are still doubts about the necessity of solutions such as the debt-reduction fund or eurobonds. i commend the commission for its proposals on the banking union and its determination to strike a balance between budgetary discipline and long-term growth and job creation. however, i am missing an essential commitment to fight fraud more actively in the member states. the situation is unjustified, since the commission is not aware of the real fraudulent intent, since the member states do not provide the necessary data. the fight against fraud must be strengthened and the commission must take responsibility for the misuse of funds and their recovery in the eu budget. when we talk about economic recovery, we must not forget the need to protect our markets from excessive influence from third countries. the openness of the eu market benefits operators in third countries, and our operators in those countries operate under more difficult conditions than those of the local operators. we have thus reduced our competitiveness and narrowed the labour and business market to our own citizens. i believe that the fight against fraud and the protection of the market must be one of the cornerstones of future initiatives and strategies that will ensure a more stable and faster economic recovery in the long term.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report of the european parliament because the proposal to appoint mr ivanov as a member of the court of auditors was welcomed by the committee on budgetary control of the ep. the committee assessed the qualifications of the proposed candidate, in particular in the light of the requirements laid down in article 286 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. iliana ivanova has 12 years of work and policy experience in the public and private sectors related to governance, audit and accountability. after focusing on financial management and accountability issues, she developed her professional experience in major banking and financial institutions. in 2009, iliana ivanova became a member of the european parliament and a full member and vice-chair of the committee on budgetary control. it is also rapporteur for a number of committee on budgetary control documents, such as the 2010 annual report of the eib, the regulation on the 'hercule iii' programme to promote the protection of the financial interests of the european union, the regulation on the financing, management and monitoring of the common agricultural policy, the opinion on innovative financial instruments under the next multiannual programme, and others.
