in writing. − i support the report containing detailed recommendations for improvement of the global governance helping to promote eu values, preserve our world and improve quality of life for millions of people. the european union is one of the world's biggest democracy, peace, human rights promoter and development supporter. we have to use opportunities offered by the un at the global level to strengthen our foreign policy and achieve its goals more effectively. on the other hand, the eu can increase the effectiveness of the un. the eu should take advantage of its experience, take leading role in strengthening cooperation between different un organs and other stakeholders and put this common potential into action. the joint global action is needed in many fields in many places in the world.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the current system of preferential common customs tariffs was established back in 2008 and i believe that it should be improved and adapted to today's needs. the aim of this trade facility is to enable developing countries to participate more actively in international trade and to obtain additional export revenues. a number of important changes to the system should be made in order to ensure that import preferences are granted to those countries which really need them. i agree that the preferences for countries that use alternative preferential instruments and for countries that the world bank classifies as high-income countries should be abolished. i also believe that certain products should not be covered by the gsp if they become highly competitive on the eu market. as regards the poorer countries, i agree that the benefits should be increased and the product coverage extended. as regards gsp+, i agree with the new criteria set by the commission, it is important that more countries are included in gsp+.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament report because the common preferential tariff (cft) is one of the eu's trade instruments for promoting sustainable development in developing countries, poverty reduction and respect for human rights. since 1971, the european union has applied unilateral trade preferences under the gsp in the form of reduced tariffs to goods from developing countries entering the european market. the gsp forms part of its common commercial policy. this important trade instrument aims to enable developing countries to participate more actively in international trade and to obtain additional export revenues, as well as to support income growth and the implementation of their own sustainable development and poverty reduction policies. the last system was established in 2008 and therefore needs to be revised. the new legislative proposal maintains the general structure mentioned above, but provides for some changes to the system of imports from developing countries in order to give import preferences to those countries which really need them. in practice, this means that the benefits are withdrawn for some countries and extended to those countries that remain under the scheme.
in writing. − ladies and gentlemen, i wholeheartedly support the rapporteur's proposal to encourage aid to the poorest countries and at the same time to strengthen the safeguards to protect the eu textile and clothing industry against the import of goods from third countries. the rapporteur notes that this is a very late step, the first time that the european parliament has used its power under the lisbon treaty to legislate on the common tariff preferences. the lithuanian textile industry, which employs 25 000 people, remains one of the cheapest producers in the eu. the changes proposed in the communication would help the lithuanian textile industry to increase its competitiveness. lithuanian textile producers play an important role in our economy, exporting more than 80% of their production. however, in recent years they have not reached their full potential. lithuania's tradition of high-quality industrial production is linked to its strategic transport and logistics infrastructure, which means that the lithuanian sector can do better. i strongly support my colleagues in the alde group in the need to update the tariff system to reflect the latest developments in the world economy, for example by removing the preferences for eu imports from countries on the world bank's list of countries with per capita income (including brazil, kuwait, saudi arabia and qatar).
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. excessive national debt can have serious consequences for those countries and for other eu member states. in order to avoid severe economic and social consequences and to ensure financial stability and economic growth in the euro area, serious measures are needed, and i therefore agree with the adoption of the two pieces of legislation under discussion in the six-pack. i believe that member states should consult the commission in advance on important economic or fiscal policy reforms in order to assess their potential impact on the euro area as a whole. it is important to coordinate the preparation of national budgets by establishing a common timetable for all countries, which should ensure that budgetary countries take timely account of european recommendations and national reform programmes. in addition, a euro area member state in severe economic difficulties would be required to submit a detailed borrowing plan to the commission.
in writing. − i voted for this document because excessive national debt can have serious consequences for the member states themselves and for other eu member states. the reputation of the euro area is more at stake than its very survival. the commission proposal complements the six-pack of eu economic governance legislation adopted by the ep and the council in 2011. the substance of the proposed regulation a member state whose currency is the euro should be subject to enhanced surveillance if it is experiencing or is at risk of experiencing serious financial difficulties. a rapid return to normalcy should be ensured and other euro area member states protected from possible adverse spill-over effects.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i agree that it is necessary to provide for additional eu measures to coordinate and monitor the budgetary and economic policies of the member states. i agree that member states need to comply with the stability and growth pact (sgp) and improve the coordination of their fiscal policies. member states should exercise caution during periods of fiscal upswing and should build up sufficient reserves for periods of downturn.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because each of the member states whose currency is the euro should consult the commission and the other member states whose currency is the euro before adopting any major plans for fiscal policy reforms that may have side effects, in order to assess their possible impact on the euro area as a whole. they should regard their budgetary plans as being of common interest and submit them to the commission in advance for monitoring purposes before they become binding. the commission should be able to deliver, where appropriate, its opinion on the draft budgetary plan, which the member state and, in particular, the budgetary authority are invited to take into account when adopting the budgetary law. member states whose currency is the euro and which are subject to an excessive deficit procedure should be monitored more closely to ensure that the excessive deficit situation is corrected in a complete and timely manner. closer monitoring should ensure early correction of any deviation from the council recommendations to correct the excessive deficit situation.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the arab spring in the southern and eastern mediterranean countries and their hopes for a transition to a well-functioning democracy must be addressed. i support the geographical extension of the european bank for reconstruction and development to these countries. i believe that the projects financed by the erdf in these countries will provide a solid foundation for an open market-oriented economy. as the mediterranean countries are very different from the eastern bloc countries where the ebrd has traditionally been active, i believe that the ebrd should carry out a rigorous technical assessment of each country before starting operations. i agree that, pending the entry into force of the amendment to the agreement establishing the escb to include the mediterranean countries, article 18 of the agreement establishing the escb should be amended to allow the escb to carry out operations financed from the special-purpose funds.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. without adequate funding from the eu budget, it will not be possible to achieve the overall eu policy objectives and the europe 2020 strategy to help europe recover from the crisis and create jobs. it is very important to ensure a proper balance between the real own resources and expenditure of the eu budget, and i believe that the ep is not prepared to give its consent to the regulation on the next mff until a political agreement on the reform of the own resources system has been reached. i support the proposals to increase budgetary flexibility by shifting expenditure from one category to another and from one mff financial year to another, thus ensuring the appropriate alignment of budgetary resources with changing circumstances and eu priorities. i think that the ep and the council should negotiate their political positions before formally submitting their proposals to the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution because, in accordance with article 311 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union must provide itself with the means necessary to attain its objectives and implement its policies, and its entire budget must be financed from own resources. the european parliament has consistently called for the creation of new genuine own resources. therefore, in accordance with article 312 (2) tfeu, the council, acting unanimously after obtaining the consent of the european parliament, is to adopt a regulation establishing a multiannual financial framework (mff). the european union budget is dedicated to promoting economic growth and job creation, and the eu's role in the world. however, it must be stressed that the budget of the european union is an investment budget with a strong leverage effect. the eu budget, while limited in size, also serves as a catalyst for budgetary resources and provides the economies of scale and cross-border impact needed to achieve the commonly agreed eu policy objectives. moreover, the eu budget is a very powerful instrument for increasing strategic investments with european added value, and for stabilising the european economy, promoting growth and employment, while at the same time achieving economic and social cohesion throughout the union.
in writing. − the structure of the european union budget is currently very complex. i therefore fully support its being as simplified as possible. it is also essential to abandon the exceptions arising from historical reasons, which are essentially obsolete as a result of changes in both the size of the eu and the degree of integration. it is important that the measures introduced are universal, for example, the financial transaction tax will only achieve its objectives if it is applied throughout the european union. on the other hand, any reservations should be based on objective criteria, for example, the higher costs of customs administration in member states with external borders to the eu should be taken into account when determining the cost of own resources collection.

in writing. - i voted for this resolution. to date, there is no legally binding international treaty regulating the transfer of conventional arms. insufficient regulation and control and lack of transparency in the arms trade facilitate the irresponsible arms trade, as well as the unnecessary suffering of people, fostering armed conflict, instability, terrorist attacks and corruption, and damaging peace processes, social and economic development, the overthrow of democratically elected governments and the disregard for the rule of law, human rights and international humanitarian law. the united nations general assembly has proposed the adoption of an international and legally binding treaty on the arms trade, setting international standards for the import, export and transfer of conventional arms. this would allow states to ensure that they have national systems and internal controls of the highest standards in place to prevent conventional weapons from entering the illicit market from the legal market, where they could be used for terrorist acts, organised crime and other criminal activities. i support the european parliament's call for a historic step forward in the negotiations for a legally binding international arms trade treaty in july 2012 and for greater transparency and accountability by setting the highest international standards and criteria against which conventional arms transfers, imports and exports are judged.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this european parliament resolution as un general assembly resolution 64/48 calls on un member states to develop an effective and legally binding instrument for the transfer of conventional arms, in accordance with the highest common international standards, and to conclude a strong and effective treaty. the overall treaty on the transfer of conventional arms is not yet in place. there are no binding commitments in the area of arms transfers that explicitly protect international human rights and international humanitarian law. the un general assembly defines the att as a legally binding treaty that sets international standards for the import, export and transfer of conventional arms. they would be designed to oblige member states to set up national systems and internal controls operating to the highest standards. this would prevent conventional weapons from entering the illicit market from the legal market, where they could be used for terrorist acts, organised crime and other criminal activities. a common, coherent and consistent eu approach to this issue is essential for the ratification and effective implementation of the att at the global level, and the long-term success of the att depends on the adoption of a set of high, rigorous and clear standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the value of global exports has continued to increase despite the economic and financial crisis and because eu member states' exports consistently account for around 30% of total exports and are among the world's leading arms producers and exporters, and the eu has a responsibility and an interest in developing and contributing to a regulated, transparent and controlled arms trade on a global scale. while it is regrettable to acknowledge the contribution of the arms industry to job creation and economic growth, i believe that the poorly regulated, unregulated and non-transparent arms trade creates the conditions for irresponsible arms trade, as well as unnecessary human suffering, fosters armed conflict, instability, terrorist attacks and corruption, and undermines peace processes, social and economic development, encourages the overthrow of democratically elected governments and disregards the rule of law. it is necessary to take a historic step in the negotiations for a legally binding international arms trade treaty in july 2012 and to ensure greater transparency and accountability by setting the highest international standards and criteria against which conventional arms transfers, imports and exports are judged. i agree with the need to adopt the un comprehensive and universal arms trade treaty without delay and to facilitate its entry into force. transparency and accountability are the cornerstones of an effective att.
in writing. − the arms trade has a major impact on fuelling conflict, poverty and human rights abuses worldwide, but remains an opaque, weak and ineffectively regulated area of global trade. the arms trade is growing steadily, unabated even by the global economic recession. it is therefore necessary to reach agreement as soon as possible on a global arms trade treaty that is binding on all actors involved in the arms trade, and to establish an effective system for monitoring and supervising its implementation. at the same time, the fight against illicit arms trafficking and corruption must be strengthened. one of the key criteria to be enshrined in the treaty should be the level of democracy, stability and respect for human rights. the treaty should ensure that in painful situations such as the one currently in syria, the supply of weapons is stopped immediately, knowing that they are being used to kill civilians.
in writing. - i voted for this resolution. on 28 november 2011, the democratic republic of the congo (drc) held its second general elections since the entry into force of the constitution in 2006, which are a key factor in the consolidation of democratization and the stabilisation process in the drc. in the context of the elections, 33 people were killed and at least 83 injured between 26 november and 25 december 2011, and at least 265 civilians were detained by members of the defence and security forces during this period. the european union electoral observation mission in the democratic republic of the congo concluded in its final report that the electoral process was characterised by a lack of transparency and integrity, due to the high number of irregularities and fraud detected. the country has also seen a rise in the repression of human rights defenders and journalists, who are unjustly detained and threatened. i support the european parliament's recommendations that the drc investigate these violations and engage in a dialogue with all parties, including the opposition and civil society, which will pave the way for genuine democracy and political reform in the country.

a lot has been said today about the single market, and i see it as clear that it is the foundation for rebuilding our european union economy, creating additional jobs. it has been rightly said that the current situation in the single market is very advantageous for some countries because of certain restrictions, and very detrimental for some countries. i really support and welcome the idea you have expressed that common rules should be established as soon as possible in the single market. secondly, the introduction of public procurement: i would suggest that we introduce public procurement as soon as possible in order to strengthen the conditions of competition in our internal single market and to make more efficient use of european union funds. the second point is that we must start thinking about protecting the single market from third countries, especially those which do not allow our individual companies to compete on equal terms in their countries and states, because we are reducing jobs and reducing people's incomes in our own countries.
unfortunately, the development of environmental policy is often such that new environmental requirements are usually adopted when a major disaster occurs. environmental legislation should aim not only at response but above all at prevention in order to prevent such accidents. in the future, we must go further and apply what is known as the precautionary principle. the directive under discussion today is designed to bring legal requirements into line with technological progress. unfortunately, we have only to regret that we are not ambitious enough and are still only facing reality. for example, offshore exploration and production of hydrocarbons and transport activities are not yet covered by the directive. it probably makes little difference whether the tanker is carrying oil or gas or, say, ammonia. in the event of an accident, the damage is, in any case, considerable. but i am very pleased that the provisions of the aarhus convention have been incorporated into this document. i believe that citizens have the right to information, to participate in decision-making and to have recourse to the courts. i believe that all this will ensure a high level of environmental protection. it is important that citizens are informed about the actions to be taken in the event of a possible accident, in order to be informed about the date of the inspection of the objects. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr aderi, who i believe has done a great job and wish him success in his presidency of hungary.
in writing. it is good that the subject of food for infants and young children and food for special medical purposes is being considered in such detail in the european parliament. the protection and safety of children and the sick, their welfare, must be the goal of our action. therefore, it is unacceptable that the possibility of pesticide residues in infant formulae or formulae for children under three years of age should be allowed under the community legislation currently in force. exposing children to toxic products, especially at such an early stage of development, can have irreversible harmful effects. pesticides for which maximum residue levels were approved in the 2006 directives and which do not meet the safety conditions should necessarily be withdrawn from the market and should not be used in the production of food covered by this regulation. it is also urgent to apply the principle of prohibition of pesticides in products of animal origin such as milk and to require strict controls on production, especially for foods for young children. there is one other important issue concerning food for special medical purposes which is not clarified in the proposed regulation, and that concerns the 32 million europeans suffering from diabetes. unfortunately, the regulation does not provide an appropriate legal framework for foods for diabetics. the main aim is to introduce a uniform eu-wide requirement for the labelling of foodstuffs, describing their composition in terms of safety for diabetics.

in writing. − i support the communication updating another food safety legislation. at the same time, i would like to draw the attention of my colleagues to the fact that there are many such laws in the field of food safety, and their updating is the constant work of the environment committee. what they all have in common is that we want to protect the consumer by providing him with as much information as possible about the products he consumes. however, the fact that the provisions are scattered across the different pieces of legislation creates some confusion. i would therefore urge the commission to consider the possibility of codifying all food safety legislation as soon as possible and to present a draft single food safety code covering all existing eu legislation governing the safety of various food products.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the french authorities' examination of the physical integrity of a sample of silicone breast implants from the french company pip revealed defects in the pip casing that are not found in other commercially available implants, posing a serious risk to women's health. clinical and epidemiological data on the potential risks associated with pip breast implants are still lacking. 10 to 15% of third-generation implants are ruptured within ten years of insertion. the need to ensure rapid access to medical devices for patients should never override the need to ensure patient safety. the application of the existing legislation therefore requires closer cooperation, in particular in the areas of market surveillance and inspections, and a strengthening of controls in order to provide greater guarantees of safety for patients.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the poor quality of breast implants produced by pip. although the company has been out of business since 2010, there are still thousands of patients in europe and beyond who are wearing substandard silicone-filled breast implants. i have identified the following problematic aspects: the absence of an implant registry, the failure of a control mechanism, the lack of information and market monitoring. i agree with the idea of a passport for every implant holder and a common independent register of implants in the eu member states. this would not only help to trace the implant holder of a particular manufacturer, but would also speed up the exchange of information between member states, especially in the case of low-quality implants. this fraud case, which affected the health of many patients, revealed a dysfunctional legislative process at national and eu level. it is necessary to emphasise the need for stronger sanctions and controls at european level, rather than leaving it to the member states alone. patients should be provided with not only guarantees of the safety of the implant, but also with adequate information on the quality, risk factors, and the possibility of replacing the implant. this requires effective and goodwill cooperation between all the chains: manufacturers, healthcare providers and patients. as regards market control and monitoring of manufacturers, i call for a coordinated operation of inspectors in the member states, for the inspection of randomly selected implants, for the audit of manufacturers. the checks must be carried out before the introduction on the market or the granting of marketing authorisations to undertakings, thus creating a preventive system to prevent the recurrence of the french company's case of industrial silicone for breast implants spilling into patient tissues.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the single european railway area. this proposal for a directive establishing a single european rail area is a merger of three directives in force and contains provisions regarding the adequate financing of and charging for rail infrastructures, the conditions of competition on the railway market, and the organisational reforms needed to ensure appropriate supervision of the market. i support an adequate, transparent and sustainable funding of the infrastructure, better predictability of the infrastructure development and access conditions, as well as the improvement of the competitiveness of rail operators vis-à-vis other transport modes. it is important that a strong and independent national regulatory body would be established which would exchange information within a network with other national regulatory bodies. finally, for the successful liberalisation of the railway market, it is necessary to introduce transparent rules for the calculation of track access charges and promote technical harmonisation.

in writing. − the official position is that the amendments to the directive proposed by the european commission are designed to develop the railway system and create a common transport market. however, some of the proposed provisions raise concerns that they may have very negative consequences or be disastrous for the lithuanian railway system. the situation in lithuania, as in the other baltic states, is specific in the railway sector, with railway tracks not meeting european standards, which remain largely integrated into the cis market. the draft under consideration presents more favourable, compromise options for lithuania. the requirement to separate rail infrastructure from passenger and freight transport activities was not the most dissatisfying. however, other requirements concerning the independence of freight terminals, stations, refuelling, distribution lines, etc. remained, which were of no less concern to lithuanian railways. this may cause major problems in the future, as it will be virtually impossible to ensure the independence of these divisions within a single company and the ec may then start to require their separation. the proposal to allow the application of a higher infrastructure charge to third country freight transport is also highly questionable. it is not clear how this provision would be implemented in practice, but it is certain that the commission would require a reduction in taxes and the difference to be covered by the state budget. the european parliament will return to the railway directive in the autumn of this year. i hope that we will be able to find convincing arguments that will allow the directive to be formulated in a way that is favourable to lithuania and ensures the continued functioning of its railway system.
in writing. − the creation of a single railway area is an important step towards further eu integration, which will not only improve rail transport in general in the future, but is also likely to lead to lower freight and passenger charges. unfortunately, it is regrettable that the second reading did not take account of the member states which, in all areas of infrastructure - electricity, gas transmission, railway - are still part of the former soviet union. the adopted document does not take into account the important provisions for lithuania, latvia, estonia and finland, which use the broad gauge railway, that they need additional resources to become full members of the single railway area.
in writing. − the implementation of this directive will cause a number of serious problems not only for lithuania but also for the other baltic states. i think that the implementation of the provisions on infrastructure separation and infrastructure charge will cause a particular amount of confusion. in particular, this directive does not lay down specific requirements for the separation of infrastructure. in order to ensure increased competition, continuous investment and economic efficiency of the services provided, i believe that the management of infrastructure and the provision of transport services should be carried out by different departments or entities within the same undertaking. it should be noted that the provision in the directive on the possibility of applying a higher charge to the carriage of goods from third countries is questionable and difficult to implement in practice. in order to establish a common method of calculating the amount of the levies, the commission must as soon as possible draw up a comparative analysis of the methods of determining the amount of the levies applied by the member states.
in writing. − this communication is another important step towards a common eu rail system. the document sets out the responsibilities and financial obligations of the transport system operators of the eu and its member states. i voted in favour of this report because it facilitates the creation of greater competition in this sector, encourages more investment in environmental rail transport programmes and creates a more transparent financial accounting regime for the sector. there is a need for more detailed discussion on the need to separate infrastructure managers from operators. this would also allow third-country railway companies to gain a foothold on the eu rail market, whose interests would not necessarily coincide with the objectives of eu transport policy. in some eu countries, this would pose a security threat. in addition, the consideration of the single european railway area should continue to effectively seek to reduce the specificities of the railway system in certain eu countries. for example, the railway carriage of the baltic states is not in line with the standard used in many eu countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on recording equipment in road transport. i believe that professional drivers will enjoy safer working conditions with the introduction of more efficient recording equipment in road transport as endorsed by the european parliament today. we have given our backing to a review of the tachograph regulation, which dates back to 1985. the revision aims to combat fraud, enforce better working conditions for professional drivers and save european transport companies up to €515 million per year by reducing administrative burdens. the european commission has found that up to 45,000 vehicles were in breach of eu tachograph rules at least once. breaches include not adhering to minimum rest periods or maximum driving times, resulting in fatigued drivers and increased road safety risks. with this latest proposal, the parliament is seeking to support the transport industry by easing the burden on companies and clarifying tachograph laws. however, road safety is of paramount importance, and transport companies operating in europe and their drivers must obey the safety rules.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the use of the latest technologies, in particular tachographs, is essential to improve road safety and drivers' working conditions, and to ensure fair competition between transport companies. the data recorded by the tachograph on driving, working and resting time will help transport companies to comply with social rules, i.e. minimum breaks, rest periods and maximum driving time. it is particularly important that eu member states comply with the tachograph regulation and the social rules applicable to transport undertakings, as companies that do not comply with the legislation will gain a significant competitive advantage by reducing prices, as the costs of staff represent up to 50% of the total operating costs of a transport undertaking.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union's main objective in the field of transport is to improve road safety, improve the working conditions of drivers and ensure fair competition between transport companies. however, the provisions of the social legislation adopted by the european union concerning road transport, which in practice is based on the control of data recorded by the tachograph (on driving, working and resting time), are not sufficiently implemented. two main problems are identified: the social rules are still often violated and the tachograph system is not sufficiently effective. according to the data provided by the commission, about 9% of the vehicles checked are in breach of social rules. approximately one quarter of these vehicles were found to be particularly non-compliant with the provisions of the tachograph regulation. moreover, the tachograph system was designed and operated primarily as a tool for maintaining order, rather than as a labour-saving tool. therefore, in order to achieve better application of social rules and to reduce administrative burden by making full use of new technologies and introducing certain new regulatory measures, it is necessary to review existing social legislation. however, none of the objectives of the proposal will be achieved if the member states do not commit themselves to improving the implementation of this regulation.
in writing. - i abstained in voting in favour of this document because i think there should not be an additional financial burden for the verification of carriers etc. (as was tried with gps, i.e. carriers will have to pay). i also believe that the tachograph system should not only monitor the driver but also help him - to warn him of the end of working hours, of the necessary rest, and so on. i also think that the information from the tachograph should go to the company and not to other third-party sources.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to make the control system in the field of road transport more efficient and reliable and thus to improve road safety. the tachograph is a fundamental tool in the fight against road safety, as it ensures that the rules on driving time and rest periods for road drivers are respected, and it also ensures fair competition between operators. i can only support this proposal which will improve the safety of the system and the productivity of control, in particular by introducing the latest technological innovations and by addressing the training of police services.
in writing. − given the complexity of the situation of carriers, no additional financial burden should be imposed on them. the hasty and incorrect implementation of the provisions of this regulation may have very serious negative consequences for the sector. in view of this, i consider that the mandatory installation of smart tachographs should be limited to vehicles registered for the first time after the date of entry into force of this regulation. the new tachograph system should not only control the driver but also help them to improve their working conditions by providing the necessary and detailed information. it is also essential to ensure that the information provided by the tachographs is only transmitted to the undertaking and not to unrelated third parties.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on customs enforcement of intellectual property rights. intellectual property rights (ipr) are fundamental to innovation, which is a key priority of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. given the increase of ipr infringements and international trade in infringing goods, large parts of economic growth and jobs in the eu depend on the effective enforcement of ipr. it is estimated that piracy and counterfeiting cost european businesses eur 250 billion each year. the customs authorities are in a comparatively good position to enforce iprs effectively at the eu's external borders, before the goods enter the internal market. once the goods spread across different member states, it becomes much more difficult and costly to trace them and to initiate proceedings. i support the position of the rapporteur that the proposed regulation should only lay down the procedures enabling the customs authorities to prevent the movement of goods which are suspected of infringing ipr.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. intellectual property is one of the factors of eu competitiveness and therefore its protection is of particular importance. infringements of intellectual property rights and trade in counterfeit goods have a negative impact on the health and safety of eu industry and consumers. at eu borders, customs is the first institution to fight against counterfeiting and the illegal entry of goods into the eu, and i therefore support the proposal to review the current regulation on the implementation of border controls in order to protect the iuu and to simplify customs procedures. i agree that procedures should be established for customs authorities to prevent goods infringing the int. the principle that counterfeit goods infringe the trips should also be recognised when they are intended for personal use. i believe that the simplified investigation procedure should apply not only to counterfeit and pirated goods but also to all infringements of the int. i agree that right holders should be given access to information on goods being destroyed and that they should be given the right to claim compensation from the recipients of the goods.
in writing. − i abstained in voting in favour of this document because such practices can cause serious economic damage to rights holders. however, this regulation should help to ensure that customs authorities act effectively and swiftly to reduce the risks of disturbance to legitimate trade. economic operators who are regularly involved in customs formalities have a good knowledge of customs procedures. therefore, burdensome administrative procedures that would prevent the competent customs authorities from acting effectively and quickly should not be introduced. the final consumer, who is not familiar with customs formalities, should be better protected.
in writing. − customs have a special role to play in the fight against the illicit entry of goods and counterfeit products into the common market in order to ensure the proper protection of intellectual property rights. in this context, every effort should be made to strengthen customs procedures for the enforcement of intellectual property rights, to ensure the proper implementation of the protection of traders' interests and to prevent abuse and piracy. it is essential that measures to combat infringements of intellectual property rights at the eu's external borders are combined with targeted action in the country of origin. similar provisions on intellectual property rights should be included in trade agreements. i believe that, in order to ensure adequate protection of intellectual property rights, this regulation should also apply to goods in transit through the customs territory of the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of eu water legislation. europe as a whole extracts only around 13 per cent of its total available water, but the geographic distribution of resources is very uneven and many european countries and regions are subject to heavy water stress. there can be no ‘one size fits all’ solution: the regional and local dimension should be strengthened, local stakeholders and communities should be involved in a participatory process at all stages of policy design and implementation, and the commission should foster capacity building and design clear guidelines for implementation. i support the position of the rapporteur that regional water consumption data must be considered when setting new rules. the biggest water consumers by far are the energy production and agriculture sectors. here we can find a huge potential to increase the efficiency of the water consumption. it is important to stress that all existing rules need to be fully implemented in the eu member states.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on ecall: a new 112 service for citizens. i support the introduction of a mandatory electronic system of emergency – ecall – in all new car models. the satellite-based electronic notification system shall be programmed to send automatically a signal to the nearest emergency call centre when a serious accident happens. it will transmit data, such as the exact location, vehicle id and the time of the accident. ecall should be activated via the existing pan-european emergency number 112. this has two advantages: first, in case of accidents, the severely injured would be given priority, and second, abuse can be prevented by the automatic recall of the rescue coordination centre. i also fully support the opinion that the mandatory deployment of a public ecall should be a public emergency call service, free of charge, for the benefit of any driver in europe, independently of his car brand.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the introduction of an emergency call service in all vehicles across the eu is one of the eu's key road safety priorities. this system is essential to increase the efficiency of emergency services, to improve road safety in europe and to help reduce the number of people killed and injured in road accidents. i agree that member states should modernise their emergency services infrastructure by 2015 to enable them to install the appropriate equipment to accept calls from the emergency call system. i agree that the system should be free of charge and that the public distress call service could be provided in conjunction with a private distress call service. however, it is also important to ensure that data relating to drivers is properly protected and that only those data elements are used that are necessary and relevant in the specific case.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the introduction of a european union-wide emergency call service, operating in all vehicles and in all countries, has been one of the union's main road safety priorities since 2002. the main benefit of the emergency call is the reduction in the number of road casualties and the less severe consequences of injuries due to the faster arrival of emergency services at the scene of an accident. according to official statistics on the emergency call service, the introduction of this system in all cars in the member states of the european union would save 2 500 lives a year and reduce the severity of injuries by 10-15%. however, the mandatory deployment of a public distress call service should not be based on or dependent on the existing positive experience of providing an independent distress call service in line with business principles. the benefits of the scheme to society at large should also be taken into account. the emergency call should be a public service to call for assistance, free of charge and available to any driver in europe, regardless of the make of the vehicle. the mandatory public call service could be a catalyst for the launch of many other commercial services that are already ready for the market but cannot be successfully delivered until the main application is in place. the distress call system could therefore encourage the development of other public or private telematic services that would provide even greater security and economic benefits.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution as the purpose of the in-vehicle emergency call system is to ensure that emergency services are automatically informed in the event of a serious accident, in order to reduce the number of people killed in road accidents and to alleviate the consequences of injuries suffered by them by the early arrival of qualified and properly equipped emergency workers (the so-called 'golden hour' rule). according to 2004 figures, road accidents kill more than 40 000 people and disable 150 000 people in the european union every year. in contrast, the emergency call system does not prevent accidents but would increase the efficiency of the emergency services. immediately informed emergency services, with knowledge of where the accident occurred, could arrive quickly at the scene and reduce the risk of death and the severity of the consequences of injuries. it should be noted that the results of many studies and projects based on scientific methods have confirmed the positive safety effects of emergency systems. the emergency call service should be free of charge and should be mandatory for all new vehicles. the public emergency call service should be simple, accessible, operational and accessible to all in the eu, regardless of the vehicle in which it is installed and the location where it is located.
in writing. - i voted yes. i am in favour of having the emergency call system installed in all new car and light vehicle models from 2015 and fully operational throughout the eu, and in other european countries that wish to do so. in lithuania alone, more than 6,000 car accidents occur each year, injuring more than 8,000 people and killing nearly 700. by 2015, the introduction of ecall in all cars in the eu member states would save 2,500 lives a year and reduce the severity of injuries by 10-15%. the cost of installing the 'ecall' system in a new car would be less than eur 100, but the consumer should not be subject to a financial burden and the emergency call service should be free of charge. the system shall not send any signals and shall be completely inactive until the sensors detect that a serious accident has occurred and automatically transmit the signal even if the driver or passenger involved in the accident is unconscious. the system can also be activated by a person who has, for example, witnessed an accident. studies show that this technology makes rescuers arrive 40% faster in urban areas and 50% faster in rural areas. it is regrettable that more than five years of voluntary system implementation have produced no results.
in writing. - i support this resolution. the ecall system is a vital system. the emergency call system should be continuously expanded and improved in order to improve the living conditions of citizens and even to save their lives. the full implementation of this system could save thousands of lives every year. it is very important that the system is used in heavy-duty, agricultural and industrial vehicles. these vehicles are used in remote and isolated areas, which sometimes leaves drivers with no access to emergency services in the event of an accident.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report in order to strengthen the protection of european citizens. the eu does so much for free movement within the member states, and we have to make this movement safe. i regret that many member states have not joined yet the ecall system. it is a joint project and all european citizens have the right to the same level of protection regardless their nationality. the improvement of the european emergency service will permit up to 2500 lives to be saved annually and to reduce the severity of injuries by 10-15%. therefore i support the rapporteur who calls on the commission to make legally binding decisions on that issue. i join the colleagues who are concerned about respect for the privacy of the people who have the ecall system installed. the system should not be allowed to track the movement of cars. only information on the exact place of the accident is necessary for intervention in case of emergency.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as council regulation (ec) no 73/2009 laying down the rules applicable to the current system of direct payments to farmers should be replaced by proposals for the reform of the cap 2014-2020, which should apply from 1 january 2014. while council regulation (ec) no 73/2009 will continue to apply in 2013, some financial provisions will only be valid until 2012. the calendar year 2013 also corresponds to the financial year 2014, which means that the new financial framework for 2014-2020 will already apply this year. this proposal was drawn up to provide for financial provisions for the transitional period of 2013. it is therefore necessary to fix the net ceilings for direct payments for calendar year 2013 by establishing a modulation-like adjustment mechanism to ensure continuity of the level of payments, taking also into account the gradual increase of payments for the new member states and the voluntary discontinuation of modulation. in order to ensure continuity of support to farmers in 2013, this act should enter into force before 1 january 2013. it should also be borne in mind that this commission proposal was drawn up on the basis of the assumption that the proposal for the harmonisation of the communication (com (2010) 539) would be adopted first. therefore, at the time of the approval of the notification in question, the ongoing procedure should be taken into account and possibly additional amendments should be submitted.
