in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to align council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 on the common organisation of agricultural markets with the new separation of powers between the commission and the member states under articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). for the sake of completeness, this proposal incorporates the proposals for amendments to council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 which the commission has already submitted separately to the european parliament and to the council. it is proposed to align regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 with the new requirements based on the division of the existing commission powers into delegated and implementing powers under regulation (ec) no 1234/2007. this was done in the light of implementing measures adopted by the commission under its existing mandate. in order to ensure a balance between the effective and rational functioning of the commission and the legislative powers conferred on parliament and the council by the treaty of lisbon, it is necessary to adopt the new regulation as soon as possible. in this way, the substantial future reform of the single common market organisation (in the context of the overall reform of the cap) would not unduly complicate the still pending negotiations on the commission's proposed harmonisation, which is still under consideration.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal as the commission's proposal aims to reconcile council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 on the common organisation of the markets with the new separation of powers conferred on the commission and implementing powers laid down in articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in addition, for the sake of completeness, this proposal incorporates the proposals for amendments to council regulation (ec) no 1234/2007 which the commission has already submitted separately to the european parliament and to the council. this proposal empowers the legislator to lay down the framework for the common organisation of the markets. for example, the legislator sets the objectives of market intervention measures, production restriction schemes and aid schemes. the legislator also lays down the principle for the establishment of a system of import and export licences, the essential aspects of the rules relating to trade and production and the principle for the application of penalties, reductions in payments and their abolition. in addition, the legislator provides for specific provisions for individual sectors. the principle to be followed is that an effective and rational balance must be struck between the commission's activities and the legislative powers conferred on parliament and the council by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to adapt the council regulation to the new treaty provisions on the commission's implementing powers. the proposal will increase legal clarity and certainty, thereby bringing the lisbon treaty into effect, and will make the common organisation of the single market more accessible to all stakeholders.
in writing. − it is essential that the legislation relating to the single organisation of agricultural markets is simplified, transparent and as clear as possible to citizens. in addition, in each case, the decision to adopt delegated acts should be taken with caution and only in specific and limited cases. any abuse of this right must be prevented. i believe that the commission should consult experts from the member states on a regular basis and take their views into due account in order to ensure the necessary quality of delegated acts and their feasibility.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as, in accordance with the general agreement on procedures for the application of delegated acts in practice, approved by the conference of presidents on 3 march 2011, and regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules, mechanisms and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers, a number of amendments should be made to the conditions for delegation (period of delegation, period for lodging objections to a delegated act, extension of this period, committee procedure, etc.). under the treaty of lisbon, the alignment of regulation (ec) no 1290/2005 with the new rules of the treaty is based on that regulation, by applying the classification of provisions adopted by the commission into delegated and implementing powers. the amendments relating to expenditure financed by the eagf and to the recovery procedure aim at simplification by repealing two council regulations and reducing the administrative burden on the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal, since, under the lisbon treaty, the alignment of regulation (ec) no 1290/2005 with the new treaty rules is based on the application of the classification of provisions adopted by the commission into delegated and implementing powers under that regulation. the committee examined the commission proposal in detail and identified areas where the conditions for delegated acts were met. the conditions for implementing acts were subsequently verified. the rapporteur proposed a number of amendments concerning the conditions for delegation (period of delegation, period for objections to a delegated act, extension of this period, committee procedure, etc.), based on the framework agreement on procedures for the application of practical reciprocal acts, approved by the conference of presidents on 3 march 2011, and on regulation (eu) no 182/2011 of the european parliament and of the council laying down the rules, mechanisms and general principles concerning mechanisms for control by member states of the commission's exercise of implementing powers. the amendments relating to expenditure financed by the eagf and to the recovery procedure aim at simplification by repealing two council regulations and reducing the administrative burden on the member states.
in writing. − i support this resolution, but it is of the utmost importance to ensure that legislation on the financing of the cap is clear and understandable to citizens. the principle of legal clarity and certainty must therefore be properly applied and legitimate expectations must be taken into account at all times. moreover, the implementation of the legislation should not impose additional administrative burdens on member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report regarding organic production and labelling of organic products. we, members of the european parliament, encouraged the commission to adopt specific rules, measures and conditions necessary for the application of this regulation in order to better take account of the expectations of consumers regarding the quality of organic products and to ensure the adequate application of rules by the authorities, bodies and operators concerned and the proper functioning of the single market and trade. it is very important that all member states adopt all measures of national law necessary to implement the regulation and to ensure high quality of organic products.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation (ec) no 834/2007 on the harmonisation of organic production and labelling of organic products. harmonisation is proposed in order to take better account of consumer expectations as regards the quality of organic products and to ensure the correct application of the rules by the authorities and operators concerned, as well as the proper functioning of the single market and the smooth functioning of trade. it is necessary to reduce the unnecessary bureaucratic burden on organic farmers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as, in order to better take into account consumer expectations regarding the quality of organic products and to ensure that the rules are properly applied by the relevant institutions, bodies and operators, as well as to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the smooth functioning of trade, it is necessary to adopt by means of delegated acts the specific rules, measures and conditions applicable to this regulation (for example, on the authorisation of products and materials for use in organic production, their inclusion in the restricted list or their removal from it for the purposes laid down in articles 16 and 21, on the processing methods used for food processing, on the prohibition of the use of gmos and products produced from or with gmos, on the conditions of application for labelling rules and other aspects). the proposal for a partial amendment of regulation (ec) no 834/2007 on organic production and labelling of organic products does not propose any amendments concerning the classification of delegated and implementing acts. in accordance with the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the current regulation (ec) no 834/2007 is to be harmonised on the basis of the principle of separation between implementing and delegated measures. this proposal is one of several commission proposals for legislative approximation to adapt agricultural legislation to the new provisions provided for in the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because, under the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the current regulation (ec) no 834/2007 must be harmonised on the basis of the principle of separation between implementing and delegated measures. article 290 tfeu allows the legislator to 'delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-general legislative acts supplementing or amending non-essential elements of a legislative act'. the treaty refers to the acts adopted by the commission in this way as delegated acts (article 290 (3)). in order to better take into account consumer expectations as regards the quality of organic products and to ensure the proper application of the rules by the institutions, bodies and operators concerned, as well as to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the smooth functioning of trade, the commission shall adopt by means of delegated acts the specific rules, measures and conditions necessary for the application of this regulation (for example, on the authorisation of products and materials for use in organic production, their inclusion in the restricted list or their deletion for the purposes laid down in articles 16 and 21; on processing methods used for processed food; on the conditions of application of the ban on the use of gmos and products produced from or using gmos). the labelling rules, requirements and specific criteria for the presentation, content, size and design of the organic production logo of the european union, as well as the conditions and rights for its use under title iv, etc.).
in writing. - i support this resolution. for reasons of legal clarity and certainty, the regulation currently in force should be aligned with the principle of separation between implementing and delegated measures. this will better reflect consumer expectations for the quality of organic products it will also enable the authorities concerned and other relevant actors to apply the rules more effectively and create favourable conditions for the smooth functioning of the common market and trade. i consider it appropriate to entrust the commission with the task of adopting, by means of delegated acts, the specific rules, measures and conditions necessary for the application of this regulation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is one of several commission proposals for legislative approximation to adapt agricultural legislation to the new provisions of the treaty of lisbon. the harmonisation procedure is related to articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu). in order to update the existing provisions in the light of legal reality, it is necessary to check the provisions of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 485/2008 on the component of the financing system of the european agricultural guarantee fund for transactions carried out by member states. the commission proposal has been analysed in detail on the basis of the criteria applicable to each type of legislation and the areas where the conditions for delegated acts have been met have been identified. the conditions for implementing acts were subsequently verified. no inconsistencies were observed. the use of the provisions of delegated and implementing acts in these articles is appropriate. however, the wording of the parts of the articles relating to the delegation of power do not correspond to the standard wording of those articles agreed in the draft framework agreement or to the wording endorsed by the institutions when adopting regulation no 438/2010, and therefore their replacement is necessary.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the proposal as it amends regulation no 485/2008 by including one provision on delegated acts (article 1 (2) which sets out the list of measures to which the regulation does not apply). the first sentence of article 1 (2) of regulation no 485/2008 refers to regulation no 1782/2003 (1), which is no longer in force and has been replaced by regulation no 73/2009 (2), and this provision has not been amended by the proposal and therefore needs to be amended. the treaty of lisbon abolishes the old comitology system, which was based on the classical comitology procedures (consultative, administrative, regulatory) and the regulatory procedure with scrutiny. this system is replaced by a two-tier system, consisting of delegated and implementing acts (in the former case parliament has a veto) and conferring implementing and enforcement powers on the commission. in this way, the existing legal rules must be adapted to this new legal reality. one of the first proposals is to harmonise this proposal for a regulation amending council regulation (ec) no 485/2008 on the verification of transactions carried out by member states in the framework of the financing of the european agricultural guarantee fund. the proposal is limited to changes that are made for the purpose of harmonisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-russia agreement on the preservation of commitments on trade in services. this eu-russia agreement contained in the current eu-russia partnership and cooperation agreement must be viewed in the light of the new legal framework arising from russia’s recent accession to the world trade organisation. as a result of that accession, russia will become a country that is relatively open to foreign services. although russia has agreed to lower its barriers to trade and investment and to grant more favourable treatment than it did previously to foreign service providers in 11 sectors covering professional services, it services, construction, postal services, telecommunications, media, transport, distribution, tourism and travel, and financial services, we, members of the ep, urge the russian government to make major adjustments in the russian law, in particular trade and competition law and customs regulations, in order to be able to implement those concessions. the ep and all european community expect that the commitments made by russia would not only provide new business opportunities for eu firms; they would also improve the business environment – not least as regards non-discrimination and free competition – for eu exporters and investors already working with russia.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a new bilateral eu-russia partnership and cooperation agreement on trade in services, replacing the 1994 partnership and cooperation agreement. russia's accession to the world trade organisation and compliance with the general agreement on trade in services (gats) will liberalise trade in services and provide much greater market access for foreign service providers. it is important that the eu and russia renew the terms of bilateral commitments that are almost 20 years old, in order to give the eu additional concessions compared to the multilateral regime and to maintain russia's current commitments on market access for european service providers in the maritime trade and temporary labour mobility sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conclusion of an agreement, as the eu must conclude a bilateral agreement with russia in order to obtain additional concessions compared to a multilateral regime. the russian commitments to liberalise the trade regime provide for more rights in many service sectors than under the regime hitherto applied to european companies under the partnership and cooperation agreement signed in 1994 and implemented since 1997. the european union would continue to benefit from a more favourable regime and greater benefits compared to the multilateral framework. this bilateral agreement defines these commitments to grant exclusive privileges to the european union only. it does not impose any new obligations on the european union. the agreement should also strengthen the rights of european service providers to establish themselves in the territory of russia.
in writing. − i agree with this agreement on the continuation of the obligations on trade in services, which will continue to apply a more favourable treatment to the european union. the liberalisation of trade arrangements will give more rights to many service sectors. i think it is appropriate and necessary for the eu to conclude a bilateral agreement with russia, as it will already provide more additional concessions than a multilateral regime. it is of particular importance that the current commitments by russia on market access for european service providers in the maritime trade and temporary labour mobility in the service sectors are maintained.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-russia agreement on trade in parts and components of motor vehicles. the eu has negotiated this bilateral agreement to have a compensation mechanism for the eu car components producers if the risk of falling eu exports of such products to russia materialises as a result of the application of russia's automobile investment programme until 2018. the eu must adopt this agreement because it is tied to its wto commitments. to ensure that the scheme benefits its producers immediately, it must do so before the russian federation joins wto. i support the position of the rapporteur that the survival of trade-distorting measures in russia after its wto accession is regretful, but it is important to stress that the eu producers of automobile components will benefit from a compensation scheme in case their exports to russia fall significantly. we, members of the ep, call for a close monitoring of the evolution of the trade relation in vehicles and their components between the eu and russia and, if necessary, for renegotiating the terms of the compensation scheme.
in writing. − with the recent accession of the russian federation to the world trade organisation, it is necessary for the eu and russia to conclude bilateral agreements in order to secure for the european union additional bilateral trade concessions that complement the existing system. a bilateral agreement would be beneficial to both parties in promoting beneficial trade and investment. however, it is of concern that the russian accession package tolerates certain trade-distorting measures, such as the russian automotive package, which imposes an obligation on car manufacturers to have a place of business in russia, which means that imported car parts and components are subject to discriminatory conditions and restrictions on imports. it is necessary to ensure that such measures are removed in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conclusion of the agreement because the eu negotiated this bilateral agreement with the aim of establishing a mechanism for compensation to eu car parts manufacturers in the event of a risk of a decline in eu exports of these products to russia due to the application of the russian investment programme in the automotive sector until 2018. the eu is obliged to ratify this agreement as it is linked to its wto obligations. to ensure that this regime immediately benefits its producers, the eu must do so before russia joins the wto. the aim of this agreement is to take into account the assumption that there is a risk that eu exports of automotive parts to russia will decrease. however, the european commission argues that russia's accession to the wto will generate significantly more business opportunities in the eu automotive sector in russia. the establishment of such a backstop is paradoxical: stakeholders, including eu negotiators, are not clearly aware of the future trends in bilateral trade in cars and their related details.
in writing. − i believe that it is appropriate and useful for the eu to conclude an agreement with russia on trade in parts and components for motor vehicles. first, it is an eu commitment to the wto. the compensation mechanism provided for therein will also ensure that the investment regime in the automotive sector does not reduce imports of parts and components for motor vehicles from the union into the russian federation. the application of the agreement will therefore bring clear benefits to their producers and will provide significantly more business opportunities in russia.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-russia agreement on the introduction or increase by the russian federation of export duties on raw materials. the agreement is an important step in stabilising the trade relationship between the eu and russia, which might serve as a substantial improvement in trade relations. russia exports numerous raw materials for which there is a high demand in the eu. in the context of russia's accession to the world trade organisation (wto), the country has committed itself to gradually reducing or eliminating its existing export duties. however, not all the essential goods are covered by russia's commitments in the wto accession. for this reason, the eu has negotiated a separate agreement to ensure that no additional export duties are applied on raw materials important for the eu. i support the rapporteur that despite this step forward, the agreement has several important shortcomings and has to be considered as a temporary solution until it is replaced by an adequately strong treaty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the eu-russia agreement on the introduction or increase of export duties on raw materials by the russian federation. the eu is a major importer of these raw materials, which could potentially disrupt global supply. as the eu is russia's largest trading partner and investor, it is necessary to reach an agreement on further trade aspects, applying the principle of reciprocity and the commitments that russia has undertaken at the time of its accession to the wto. it is important to ensure that a partnership and cooperation agreement, setting out strict and binding principles for bilateral trade, is secured in the longer term.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conclusion of the agreement, as this bilateral agreement commits the russian government to make every effort not to impose or increase export duties on raw materials listed in the agreement. in order to apply export duties to these products, russia will have to consult the european commission at least two months before their application in order to reach a mutually acceptable solution. the eu is russia's largest trading partner and investor. it is therefore expected that the commitments to the urgent reforms required by wto accession will be given with the appropriate gravity, respecting the principle of reciprocity and commitments in the negotiation of a new agreement of mutual benefit, in particular in the areas of energy, trade and investment. the agreement should therefore be seen as a temporary measure to be replaced by a sufficiently stringent eu-russian federation agreement on trade in raw materials, which is likely to be an integral part of the new agreement currently under negotiation.
in writing. − i agree to the conclusion of this agreement on the export duties on raw materials levied or increased by the russian federation. it should be noted that the agreement contains a comprehensive list of raw materials of major import importance to the eu. it is therefore essential that russia, the eu's largest trading partner and investor, does not apply or increase export duties on these raw materials, which pose a threat to global supply due to the supply disruption. however, given certain shortcomings of the agreement, i believe that it should be seen and applied only as a temporary measure, soon to be replaced by a strict, comprehensive and clear eu-russia agreement on trade in raw materials.
in writing. − i supported the proposal to postpone the vote until the european court of justice gives its legal assessment, requested by the commission. i regret that majority of the ep rejected acta. rejecting acta without trying to address concrete concerns, after years of negotiations, does nothing to handle serious threats to european jobs and enterprises acta intended to solve. large-scale infringements of intellectual property rights cost europeans hundreds of thousands of jobs and many millions in lost revenues. vote against acta also diminished possibilities to fight counterfeit medicines which pose serious threats to the health of european patients. european union does not have many natural resources which could bring substantial revenues. our main resource is our people and intellectual products created by them, which must be protected. with regard to our citizens, acta was an instrument to protect their intellectual property rights and i regret that the european parliament rejected it.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, which sought to reject the conclusion of the acta agreement on behalf of the european union. acta is an important trade agreement that addresses the problems of counterfeiting and piracy on the internet for commercial purposes by coordinating the enforcement of existing copyright infringement laws at the global level. however, the text of the acta is not sufficiently precise as regards the measures envisaged against individuals, the definition of the concept of 'commercial purposes', the role of internet service providers and the possible disruption of the transit of generic medicines. the future benefits of this international agreement are thus far outweighed by the potential risks to civil liberties.
in writing. − i voted against this agreement because the adverse effects of acta are of great concern. the benefits of this international agreement far outweigh any threat to civil liberties. given the uncertainty and doubts about the interpretation of some aspects of the text of the document, the european parliament will not be able to ensure adequate protection of citizens' rights in the future on the basis of acta. therefore, i am against the conclusion of acta. it should also be noted that this agreement was opposed not only by the main international trade committee but also by the four other parliamentary committees which prepared an opinion on the matter.
in writing. − i voted against this treaty because the fight against piracy, copyright and the proposed document which aims to legitimize total citizens' spying, with reference to individual rights and freedoms, are two different things and have nothing in common. if such an agreement comes into force, it will restrict the freedom of the internet, the personal rights of citizens, the interference in their private lives, and i am sure that their fears have a very real basis. the fact that there is no court ruling and no legal guarantee that acta does not violate any treaty or fundamental human rights is another strong argument for not voting for such a treaty.
in writing. − i voted against acta, which was designed to protect intellectual property against counterfeiting and illegal distribution, because it could restrict freedom on the internet. my decision was also influenced by the thousands of emails that came to my inbox urging me to vote against acta. i think the decision on acta is a political issue. i therefore support my socialist colleagues who opposed the proposal by the ppe members to postpone the vote until the conclusion of the court of justice of the eu assessing the consequences of the acta treaty. i agree with the rapporteur, mr martin, who pointed out that some of the provisions of acta are contrary to the eu charter of fundamental rights, as they do not fully guarantee the right to privacy and the protection of personal information. while it is important to combat counterfeiting and piracy, isps should not play the role of policeman. we need to protect artists and their work, but we cannot allow the freedom of the internet to be violated. this rejection should not mark the end but the beginning of a global debate on how to protect intellectual property in the european union.
in writing. − i voted against this document because i do not agree with the reduction in the amount of direct payments to be granted to a farmer in calendar year 2013 in general.
in writing. - i do not support this resolution. i think that the setting of net ceilings for direct payments will have negative consequences. first, farmers will receive lower payments. the current economic crisis and its negative impact will pose serious risks to farmers. their competitiveness, productivity and operational efficiency will be reduced. this is likely to have a negative impact on end-users.
in writing. − this communication is of particular importance to farmers in the new eu member states, including lithuania, as it sets out the conditions for direct payments for the transitional period of 2013. the new eu member states are given the opportunity to join the system of additional direct payments, which could give their farmers up to 20% more payments. this will encourage greater eu integration, as the current level of direct payments to farmers varies several times between countries. this is not correct, given that farming costs are similar in the eu. i voted in favour of this report because it is a good example of a compromise reached in difficult negotiations. this gives hope that in the next difficult negotiations on the 2014-2020 agricultural financial perspective, greater fairness in direct payments for all farmers in the eu will be achieved. this is particularly relevant for farmers in the three baltic states, who currently receive the lowest payments in the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on 2013 budget - mandate for trilogue. the commission and the eu council must ensure that inter-institutional cooperation is fruitful because, without a common starting base, it will not be possible to have a joint vision on the real needs. the european parliament must lead the fight for payments because funds are needed for commitments made over the last years and no one can ignore that today, with a level of outstanding commitments amounting to eur 207 billion, there are still many bills to be paid. in particular, the need for payments focuses on those sections that are more related to development and economic growth and this is why it is important to conduct this battle. it is important to stress that the eu budget for the year 2013 is the last one of the current financial framework. for this reason, an increase in the level of due payments at the end of the programming period is expected. that is why it will be even more important to avoid a dangerous shift of payments from 2012 to 2013.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. it is important to focus investments on the priority areas identified in europe 2020 in the light of the complex economic circumstances and the burden on national budgets. i support the proposal to increase payments by 6.8% to stimulate growth and job creation in the eu and the proposal to increase commitments by 2% at current inflation levels. i am in favour of increasing payments to the research framework programme, the competitiveness and innovation programme, the structural funds and the cohesion fund and the lifelong learning programme. i believe that resources should be allocated to areas where the eu budget delivers additional benefits and reduced in areas where delays occur and little money is spent. i support calls on the commission to present its draft amending budget for the corresponding additional appropriations as soon as all member states have ratified the act of accession of croatia.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because europe is experiencing a serious economic, financial and budgetary crisis and because it is necessary to take all measures to ensure that the budget of the european union is used as efficiently as possible to restore the economy. in the current difficult environment, one of the most demanding tasks is to promote growth and create jobs, especially for young people. similarly, the collection of vat and customs duties has a direct impact on the economies of the member states and on the budget of the european union. financial responsibility is therefore particularly important in times of crisis. furthermore, to enable the european union to play an active role in global markets, sufficient funds must be allocated from the budget of the european union. the union budget should therefore take into account the priorities set by the common commercial policy as part of the europe 2020 strategy. the european union and the member states must pay close attention to their partnership with developing countries. it is necessary to examine the issue of unspent appropriations carefully in the preparation of the 2013 budget and in the negotiations on the next multiannual financial framework in order to ensure that the budget is implemented as efficiently and effectively as possible. similarly, different types of revenue have different negative effects and the possibility of covering the costs of revenue collection from other sources of revenue should be considered.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as the eu budget is a common and effective instrument for investment and solidarity, which is needed especially at this time to stimulate economic growth, competitiveness and job creation in the 27 member states. despite its small size, representing less than 2% of total union public expenditure, the eu budget has had a real economic impact and has thus successfully complemented member states' economic recovery policies. it is therefore necessary to support an appropriate level of resources in the budget for the following year, as defined in the draft budget, and to oppose all efforts to reduce resources, in particular policy measures that promote growth and employment. in times of crisis, the financial responsibility and resources that are crucial must be allocated to areas where the eu budget can provide additional benefits and could be reduced in sectors where unjustified delays occur and where little is used to save queues that have caused problems of execution.
in writing. − it is essential that the 2013 budget is realistic and that resources are allocated to areas that can deliver additional benefits. it is also essential that the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy are implemented in a cost-effective manner. the green economy is a crucial factor for the eu's future competitiveness and resilience and more resources must be devoted to its promotion. even in difficult economic conditions, the eu cannot freeze its budget, as this would cause enormous damage not only to individual member states but also to the european union as a whole. this is not an acceptable and justifiable strategy. in view of the strict austerity policies being implemented by the member states, i believe that the eu must act more responsibly and take decisive action, in particular by determining the location of the european parliament's headquarters.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for a new animal welfare strategy for 2012-15, the implementation of which would be based on experience, understandable legislation and easy control. a high level of animal welfare is integral to sustainable development and it is therefore important not only to achieve the objectives of the new strategy but also to complete the objectives of the 2006-2010 strategy with additional funding. i believe that the new strategy should harmonise animal welfare at eu level and contribute to improving animal and public health. it is important that animal welfare issues are given due consideration in trade policy and in bilateral and international trade agreements. i believe that the implementation of the objectives of the new animal welfare strategy would help to ensure the productivity and competitiveness of the european livestock sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the commission communication on a strategy for animal welfare 2012-2015 is very necessary, especially as it addresses many of the issues addressed in parliament's resolution of 5 may 2010. the health status of wild animals is deteriorating and their population is increasing in most member states. this may not only lead to an increase in the number of pet-borne infectious diseases but also to a deterioration in public health. the complexity and different interpretation of eu and national animal welfare rules creates legal uncertainty. this may put producers in some member states at a much more competitive disadvantage than others. similarly, the implementation of eu legislation, in the absence of the requirements laid down, the harmonised standards and the intermediate objectives approved by the legislation, distorts competition and fails to ensure a level playing field for all market participants. animal health standards are crucial for the development of livestock farming in europe and increasingly affect the competitiveness of farms. similarly, rules on animal welfare must not be contrary to the principles of the eu's single market. if we make good use of this communication on the animal welfare strategy 2012-2015, we will be able to achieve a clear and uniform level of animal welfare throughout the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal as the commission's communication on a strategy for animal welfare 2012-2015 is very much needed. there are a myriad of different national legal requirements currently in force. there is no universal definition of terms and complex rules and requirements make it difficult for keepers or owners to understand good animal husbandry practice or good practice. as a result, animal welfare conditions currently vary widely across the eu member states. if we make good use of this communication, we can achieve a clear and uniform level of animal welfare throughout the eu. maintaining a high level of animal welfare, which is integral to sustainable development, is important to protect animal and public health and to ensure the productivity and competitiveness of the european livestock sector. the commission also included in its communication the parliament's proposal for a european animal welfare framework law. the basic principles of such a law would be transparency, simplification and practical application of scientific principles. the complexity and lack of information on current european and national animal welfare rules has led to legal uncertainty and distortions of competition due to non-compliance and lack of legal means. this is why we need a new approach to animal welfare: it should be based on science and recognised experience of recent years, legislation should be easy to understand and easy to control.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it is necessary to ensure a high level of animal welfare at eu level. a uniform, comprehensive and systematic approach to animal protection needs to be established. it is very important to remember that animal welfare is linked to the welfare of producers. in this context, it is essential that the commission and the member states, through joint efforts, seek to invest in projects that explore and find ways to promote the welfare of producers and reduce administrative burdens. it is also essential that animal welfare rules are compatible with the principles of the eu's single market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because there is still no european union legislation to protect pets and stray animals, despite the estimated number of over 100 million pets in the european union. not all member states have yet signed the european convention for the protection of animals kept as pets, and pets and stray animals are often the victims of mistreatment and cruelty in many member states. in accordance with article 13 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), the union and the member states are to take full account of animal welfare requirements. it is therefore necessary for the european union and the member states to ratify the european convention for the protection of pet animals and to transpose its provisions into national law. the main steps in the european union's animal welfare system can be: strengthening the link between animal health and public health, full compliance and enforcement of legislation, implementation of the european animal welfare system, establishment of equivalent welfare standards for all imported animals and products, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because animals are sentient beings and the union and the member states must take full account of animal welfare requirements. to date, no eu legislation has been developed to protect pets and stray animals. nor have all member states signed the european convention for the protection of pet animals. pets and stray animals are victims of maltreatment and cruelty in many member states. the european union and the member states are therefore invited to ratify the european convention for the protection of pet animals as soon as possible and to transpose its provisions into national law. the commission, in turn, is invited to propose eu legislation to ensure the protection of pet and stray animals, including: rules on the identification and registration of animals; strategies for the management of stray animals, including vaccination and sterilisation programmes; measures to encourage the responsibility of animal owners; the prohibition of illegal breeding and shelters; the prohibition of killing stray animals without health information; animal welfare information and education programmes in schools; and strict penalties for non-compliance by the member state.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it is necessary to establish legal regulation at european union level to ensure the full implementation of animal welfare requirements in ethical, social and economic terms. effective measures are necessary to prevent illegal activities related to the breeding, slaughter, killing or other cruel treatment of animals.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the court of justice of the european union has proposed a number of amendments to its statute which relate in one way or another to all three courts which currently constitute the court of justice of the european union: the court of justice, the general court and the civil service tribunal. the court considers it desirable to create the post of vice-president of the court of justice and to amend the rules relating to the composition of the grand chamber. the court of justice states that the workload of the president has increased considerably over time and that it would be appropriate to appoint a deputy who could replace him or assist him in the performance of his duties in the future. the proposals for changes in content also concern staff replacement and increase. the court of justice observes that the gap between the number of cases examined by the general court and the number of new cases has been widening for many years and that the number of cases pending before the court is constantly increasing. the increase in the number of judges will ensure the necessary efficiency, speed, flexibility and consistency of the court's case-law.
in writing. − the court of justice (cjeu) proposed a number of amendments to its statute and the adoption of a regulation on ad interim judges of the civil service tribunal. the proposed amendments relate in one way or another to all three courts which currently make up the eu's general court: the general court (cj), the civil service tribunal and the european court of justice. in addition to the changes in content, the two proposals concern staff replacement and increase, which require more resources and are therefore directly related to the eu budget. tt argues that the workload of the chairman has increased considerably over time and that it would be appropriate to appoint a deputy to replace him or to assist him in his duties in the future. the president of the court of justice has many duties, the performance of which is essential to the smooth functioning of the court. there have been cases where decisions on certain appeals against decisions of bt to impose provisional safeguard measures were taken more than a year later. the introduction of the post of vice-president should improve the situation in this area. tt also argues that for many years the gap between the number of cases examined by bt and the number of new cases has been widening, with a steady increase in the number of cases not examined. the court considers that the number of cases will continue to increase each year. in view of this, the court has, after careful deliberation, decided to propose an increase in the number of judges, since only in this way will the necessary efficiency, speed, flexibility and consistency of the tc practice be ensured. that is why i voted in favour of this document.
in writing. - i support this resolution. in view of the heavy workload of the presidents of the chambers, it is necessary to increase the number of judges in the grand chamber. in order to ensure greater consistency in the practice of the court, i am in favour of the introduction of a new post of vice-president, which would allow the vice-president to be present at the hearing of each case before the grand chamber and would assist the president in the performance of his duties. in view of the number of pending cases before the general court, it is necessary to implement the structural changes to that court as a matter of urgency. the number of judges should therefore be increased in order to increase the efficiency of the general court.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as, in order to ensure that the european union civil service tribunal does not find itself in a situation which prevents it from exercising its judicial functions, article 62c of the statute of the court of justice should be amended to provide for the appointment of ad interim judges to specialised courts. the court of justice has proposed a regulation to allow the appointment of ad interim judges to the european union civil service tribunal. the civil service tribunal shall consist of seven judges. the court of justice shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the appeal against decisions of the general court. the main features of the proposal are as follows: the council of the european union, on a proposal from the president of the court of justice, draws up a list and adds to it three persons who may be appointed ad interim judges. the judges-advocates shall be chosen from among former members of the court of justice of the european union who are eligible to sit as judges of the civil service tribunal. the proposal is a rational solution to a practical problem which could seriously impede the work of the european civil service tribunal. the amendments proposed by the commission are of a purely technical nature and have already been submitted by the commission in its opinion.
in writing. − i have endorsed the proposal from the court of justice for a regulation allowing the appointment of ad interim judges to the european union civil service tribunal. the civil service tribunal shall consist of seven judges. the court of justice shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine the appeal proceedings before the general court. in order to ensure that the european union civil service tribunal does not find itself in a situation which prevents it from exercising its judicial functions, it is proposed to amend the statute of the court of justice and, in part, annex i to the statute, and to provide in general for the appointment of ad interim judges to specialised courts. in such circumstances, the president of the tribunal may have recourse to the services of an ad interim judge. these ad interim judges will exercise their judicial prerogatives only in the cases assigned to them. in other words, ad interim judges will be able to exercise only strictly judicial functions and will not be able to participate in the administrative activities of the tribunal or in the election of the president of the tribunal or the presidents of the chambers.

member of the commission. - our european energy community is an offer to the countries of the former yugoslavia, to all the countries of the western balkans. you're a member there. the european union has a duty to help the countries of central and eastern europe. this means that the largest country in the western balkans leads the energy community. there we are making good progress in bringing the european internal energy market beyond the eu-27 to neighbouring countries, to the benefit of all citizens inside and outside the european union. we are only supporting from the european budget infrastructure which benefits more than one member state. why would you do that? the basic idea of subsidiarity is that where a distribution network a smart grid serves the local citizen but only in one member state, this is a matter for the member state and the regional market. what we do is standardize. together with our partners in the european energy and electricity industries, we are in the process of achieving uniform european standards for smart grids and smart meters. this is in the interests of the internal market and in the interests of consumers, with higher volumes and a possible reduction in costs. our budget has not yet provided for funding for distribution networks in the region.
member of the commission. - i am not aware of any such agreement. but even if it did, it wouldn't be relevant. the european internal market law in the field of energy is governed by european rules and not by bilateral agreements between a member state and a third country. i mean, i can't confirm your guess, but even if i could, it wouldn't be relevant to me. in the field of gas pipelines, we always determine where the entry point to the european market is. nord stream, for example. when does the single market come into force? and the access to the sub-markets of europe will then be subject to the european internal market law you decide. there may be exceptions, but as a general rule, there is third party access: access to any pipeline for anyone, and there is unbundling, i.e. the independence of the gas network operator from gas producers and gas users so that they play a high, objective part in this energy business.
member of the commission. - i have no intention of denying it to parliament. of course, the russian partners have different interests than we do. you understand our internal market rules very well. they don't really accept it. the russian partners have a different culture than us. in all our discussions with our russian partners, we attach great importance to the full application of our internal market rules. you can expect the commission to respect the law applicable to any third country - whether russia, norway or algeria - and to insist that the third country does so.
member of the commission. − nord stream is a two-pipeline project, the second of which will be inaugurated in a few weeks. then up to 55 billion cubic metres of gas from russian sources will come to europe via nord stream, which is about 10% of our total eu gas consumption per year. from greifswald-lubmin, a german town on the baltic sea where the nord stream pipeline ends, supply lines go to the central european markets. they are subject to internal market law. we're in sensitive negotiations with our russian partners about the extent of third-party access. the key is that gas from anywhere benefits every european citizen. this means that we need a functioning, reverse flow, intra-european gas network with the ability to transport from each sub-market to each other. the north-south link from the baltic sea to croatia, for example, a project which we are currently planning, is an important contribution to this. interconnectors between member states are a second contribution. the combination of internal market rules and infrastructure means that in the medium term we will also have equal rights for consumers and comparable gas prices throughout europe, and there will be no great disparity in gas prices between lithuania/latvia on the one hand and france/germany on the other.
member of the commission. - these pipelines are in the european interest. that's why we support them. whether financial support is needed depends on two factors. firstly, what are the costs and are they reasonable for the gas consumer? can they be financed on the market by transport charges or does the european union need to co-finance them? secondly, it is possible if parliament adopts the seven-year financial framework in the coming weeks and supports the connecting europe facility in the energy sector with 9 billion euros. i am then able to act and willing to talk to the respective energy ministers and the transmission system operators of entso-g.
member of the commission. - the energy customer, in the case of the electricity customer, is satisfied if, firstly, there are no or very few power cuts. it can be said that in europe the issue of power cuts is far less important and that stability, security of supply, is far more likely to be maintained than, for example, in many countries in asia or even in the united states. we have more security of electricity than the americans in detroit or los angeles. secondly, the customer is satisfied if the price is reasonable. we have evidence that, thanks to the opening up of the market, competition and the rules of the internal market, prices have risen less in recent years than if there were monopolies where the consumer could not change his supplier. transparency, i.e. knowledge of electricity suppliers and their prices and contractual conditions, is one of these. thirdly, many citizens - not all - are also interested in other issues such as environmental protection, sustainability and climate change, as electricity consumers. we are also working towards this, and we believe that the internal market and our european energy and climate policy have therefore helped the consumer and that further improvement will help him further.
vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i wanted to complete my colleague günther oettinger's answer very briefly because, thinking of electricity users and, in particular, citizens and families, obviously from the point of view of my responsibilities as commissioner for competition, i have instructed my services to monitor very closely and continuously the situation on the electricity market and other energy sources. if you recall, ladies and gentlemen, there was a sector survey a few years ago, when neelie kroes was the commissioner for competition, and since then a whole series of actions have been carried out in the light of what we analysed as a result of that survey. in the french case in particular, there have been decisions which contribute to a better functioning of the market, although the concentration of that market is obvious, with an extraordinarily powerful main operator, and i can tell the honourable member that at the moment we are following in particular some of the actions of that operator on the market. i cannot reveal which ones, or how far our investigations have gone, but rest assured that we do not forget the users and, in particular, the citizens who use electricity, neither in the former member states, in respect of which the commission has already adopted competition decisions in relation to some of its most important operators, following that sectoral survey, nor lately in the member states which acceded to the union in 2004 and 2007, in which we have also opened investigations and are working on several cases.
the commission's vice-president − it is true that several authorities are responsible for ensuring that european standards to regulate both the electricity sector and competition are applied as we have intended, so as to have a positive effect on the market. the french energy authority, of course, and the french competition authority, exercise these responsibilities on the french market. the commission, through my colleague mr oettinger in particular, is responsible for enforcing the directive. for example, several procedures were initiated when it became apparent to the commission that the directive - in particular the third package - was not being applied by the member states. wherever necessary, investigations will be opened and decisions taken on the basis of articles 101 and 102 of the treaty on competition, whenever it is considered that the rules of the treaty are not being applied or that operators are not applying them in this market. how do we work in the competition sector? we sometimes open investigations on our own initiative. we receive a number of extremely useful information from users - citizens or businesses. therefore, if you have information which you believe should be known by the competition authorities, the dg competition or myself, because it may lead to the initiation of proceedings in the area for which i am responsible, i would be grateful if you would share it with me.
today, we have just recently been informed by the honourable commissioner almunia that the timeliness and accuracy of the data or information is of the utmost importance. our main objective is the implementation of the third energy package. however, tomorrow we will vote for another document, called 'the mechanism for the exchange of information on intergovernmental energy agreements between member states and third countries', which leaves the member states and companies free to provide information on mutual agreements. my question is: will not the implementation of the third energy package be weakened by this option and will not the internal market within the european union be distorted on this basis?
member of the commission. − we believe that the external energy policy to be discussed tomorrow will not have a negative impact on the development of the internal market. we believe that we need a common european strategy on third countries, particularly supplier countries, and that is why we attach importance to the disclosure of state contracts, i.e. contracts between third countries and member states. what we do not want, and do not demand, is the disclosure of specific private contracts - prices, quantities, conditions - unless they are contrary to internal market law. but then and only then are examinations necessary, as mr almunia pointed out half an hour ago. but we do not think that general disclosure of private sector contracts is appropriate.
thank you very much for your answer. my next question is: our main objective is to reduce our dependence on third countries, and this depends on the energy balance. what is your view today on the development of nuclear energy, so that this type of energy could be the most rapid and efficient way of addressing the question of the positive side of the energy balance in relation to third countries, especially russia?

in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal for the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund in accordance with the danish application egf/2011/008 dk/odense steel shipyard. in accordance with article 6 of the regulation on the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf), the egf should support the reintegration into the labour market of individual workers made redundant. in addition, only active labour market measures that ensure long-term employment can be co-financed by the egf. the egf shall not replace actions for which undertakings are responsible, as defined by national law or collective agreements, or measures for the restructuring of undertakings or sectors. as the industrial structure of the local economy is characterised by a high number of jobs in the manufacturing industry, particularly in the metallurgical sector. many jobs in this sector have already been lost or moved to other countries where wages are lower. the dismissed shipyard workers have a wealth of technical knowledge that is difficult to apply in other industries in funen or even in denmark as a whole. most of them had worked in the shipyards all their lives, as had perhaps their parents. i therefore also welcomed the decision of the danish authorities to apply measures to provide emergency assistance to workers before the final decision to grant egf support under the proposed harmonised package.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this energy efficiency proposal. the eu spends around €400 billion a year on energy imports. it is therefore necessary to take all measures that can promote efficient and sustainable energy consumption and contribute to energy security and to reducing energy dependence on third countries. i support the mandatory targets set out in this directive at eu and national level to achieve a 20% energy efficiency target by 2020, which will not only improve the union's energy security but also contribute to the eu's economic recovery. i support the creation of energy saving schemes in the member states to reduce energy consumption and the obligation for public organisations to purchase energy-efficient buildings. the provisions on the deployment of smart meters in this directive will help to better protect eu consumers from unjustified increases in energy prices and increase consumer awareness of real energy consumption and energy prices.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the main objective of eu environmental policy is to reduce emissions of dangerous and harmful gases and other pollutants. the best way to do this is to promote energy efficiency. energy efficiency can help to reduce the costs of efficient products and services and increase business opportunities in the related industrial sectors. the 2007 heads of state decision set a target of 20% energy efficiency improvements and is a key element of the roadmap to a low-carbon economy by 2050. in order to achieve this objective, member states should draw up national action plans that are robust and specific, and the commission must have the right to assess and amend them. a european methodology based on a model allowing the assessment of the different situations of the member states should also be established. a correction factor related to the economic situation of the country should also be applied, in order to avoid that the model becomes difficult to implement for some countries and insufficiently robust for others. it is worth noting that the pursuit of energy efficiency is inseparable not only from the regulation of the activities of each citizen and smes, but also from the provision of incentives, such as support for the establishment of an energy saving system. however, in order to avoid national incentives being considered unlawful state aid, they need to be clearly defined.

in writing. − the energy efficiency report is one of the most important pieces of work in this parliament's term. it is a very important piece of legislation for eu citizens and businesses, helping to fight the economic crisis and unemployment. the eu has no direct means of reducing global oil and gas prices, but it can help reduce energy consumption. this directive will also create 2 million jobs for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly in the construction sector. this is also true for young people. in addition to saving money, energy efficiency also helps the environment by reducing emissions. i voted in favour of this report because it is of particular importance to eu citizens in difficult times. the increase in energy prices is particularly damaging to the eu countries, which are still in a difficult economic situation, and to the weakest sections of society. it is important that this directive is not understood as a mere document promoting energy efficiency. saving energy is also important in everyday life.
