in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the commission's 2013 work programme. the commission should use its powers to take action to overcome the consequences of the economic crisis, to achieve financial stability, economic recovery and a more competitive eu. i support the proposals set out in the report on the establishment of a banking union, greater powers and accountability for the european central bank in overseeing the eu banking sector, a more comprehensive agenda for economic growth and changes to eu tax law to combat tax evasion. other important priorities in the commission's work programme are the urgent adoption of the multiannual financial framework, the implementation of the reform of the own resources system and the improvement of the governance of the single market. the commission should also focus more on the implementation of the european resource efficiency action plan and the creation of a fully integrated and interconnected single energy market. the coordination of the cap and the europe 2020 strategy to promote innovation in farming and the provision of a wide-ranging reform of the common fisheries policy are also important.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it is the european parliament's annual expression of its position on the commission's proposed work programme. this year's debate on the european parliament's evaluation was particularly important, as the decisions taken by the eu institutions together will now have a decisive impact on the future of the european union. the progressive alliance of socialists and democrats (s&d) has called on the commission to devote particular attention to job creation, to a more active implementation of the citizens' agenda in the areas of justice and home affairs and to the union's foreign policy next year. of course, one of the key and overarching priorities of the european parliament at the moment is the management of financial and economic policy in order to recover from the impact of the crisis in europe.
in writing. − the prolonged euro area crisis continues to threaten all the member states of the european union. the european union is also facing a deep competitive crisis, as most other regions of the world are growing faster than they are in terms of productivity and innovation, and the european union will lag behind if decisive action is not taken. the commission should therefore focus its energy and resources on supporting member states to overcome the crisis effectively and quickly, while reducing red tape and centralisation. i therefore believe that the 2013 work programme for the last full year of the current commission's mandate should give priority to more targeted and concrete initiatives that would boost real growth and improve competitiveness. that is why i abstained in voting in favour of this document.
in writing. − we are now in the fourth year of this commission. the commission's main task is to deal with the economic crisis that has affected a large part of the eu. while much has been done in the area of economic promotion, it would be desirable for the commission's environmental action to be rational rather than based on ambition alone. often, draft legislation proposed by the commission, while moving in the right direction towards a greener eu, becomes an insurmountable burden on member states, both because of the implementation measures and because of overly strict deadlines. on the other hand, i would urge the commission to stick to its long-term programme and to present a draft of the new wording of the eia directive in 2013.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the evaluation of the 2nd voluntary unpaid tissue and cell donation report. while healthcare is largely a member state competence, the recommendations aim to develop areas such as cross-border donation. it is essential that member states organise and define compensation for donation carefully, setting strict conditions under which financial compensation may be granted and that compensation is strictly limited to the reimbursement of the costs incurred in the context of organ donation. it is essential to ensure that the human body is not a source of financial gain. i agree that it is important to regulate the online purchase of germ cells to avoid the emergence of a possible online black market and to increase the number of blood stem cell collection centres to increase the chances of finding a donor.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because donation should be voluntary, which means that no material benefit is sought. the health sector is largely managed at national level, and the guidelines therefore aim to complement existing practice by developing certain areas such as cross-border donation. in the case of donation, the emphasis is on altruism in the donation of tissues and cells. the compensation of the member state for the donation should therefore be well organised and should cover only the costs incurred as a result of the donation (e.g. travel costs). effective international cooperation is essential to ensure sound controls in order to ensure the greatest possible transparency and security in the donation system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on voluntary unpaid tissue and cell donation, as voluntary unpaid tissue and cell donation helps to ensure high standards of tissue and cell safety and therefore the protection of human health. healthcare is largely a member state competence and the recommendations aim to complement existing practice in the member states and develop areas such as cross-border donation. member states are encouraged to increase public information and awareness campaigns on tissue and cell donation and to ensure the provision of clear, accurate, scientifically sound and convincing information and data enabling the public to make informed decisions. it is also emphasised that donors should be fully informed about the procedures involved in this process and the moral, psychological, medical and social implications associated with them.
in writing. − i agree with this document tissue and cell donation must be voluntary, without any profit or financial gain. i fully agree with the condition that tissues and cells intended for recipients may only be taken in two cases: for medical or scientific and therapeutic purposes, and that tissues and cells must be taken free of charge. any unethical practices for the purpose of removing tissues or cells should be avoided and should be carried out only by professionals in their field. i think there are a few things that can be singled out to avoid a vague donation. first, public information information campaigns ensuring clear and scientifically based information is provided to donors and recipients, from consent to donation to the consequences of transplantation. secondly, traceability from donor to patient must be ensured, while maintaining anonymity and applying the highest standards of quality for transplanted tissues and cells, in particular in the case of third countries. the european commission also has a special role in overseeing the morally sensitive donation system, which is based on the principles of anonymity and voluntariness. and to act as quickly as possible when possible irregularities are detected in member states, especially in the case of financial compensation.
in writing. − addressing the shortage of tissue and cells available for medical purposes is a growing challenge for all eu member states. this report focuses on three main objectives: increased harvesting of umbilical-cord blood, further expansion of stem-cell donation, and financial compensation for potential tissue donors. umbilical-cord blood contains 10 times as many stem cells as bone marrow, but in many member states it is wasted. i voted in favour of this report, because it encourages the introduction of appropriate, transparent, and regularly audited financial compensation for potential donors. by attracting donors, this will ensure a steady supply of vital stem cells. the compensation will cover only the cost incurred in donation, protecting the health of the donor while upholding the ethical argument that the human body must not become a priced commodity. i agree with my colleagues that this initiative will allow eu citizens greater access to life-saving and tissue-regenerating stem cells while increasing the transparency and traceability of donations. this will ensure the safety of stem-cell use and provide for a plentiful donated supply of quality tissue and cells.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the essence of a green, or sustainable, economy is to preserve the productive functions of ecosystems while creating a society that meets people's basic needs. therefore, the creation of a green economy requires respect for nature and the fair distribution of resources, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, ethnic origin, disability or beliefs. gender equality in political and economic decision-making is essential, as democracy is based on the elected representatives of all the population. parties should take all measures to achieve gender balance and to ensure that women's interests are taken into account on an equal footing with men's. it must be borne in mind that natural resources are limited. also, the production and consumption of food products emits pollutants that enter the ecosystem. therefore, the economical use of natural resources is important to avoid negative ecological impacts. this means that we need to move to a green economy scenario. gender equality is part of a green and sustainable economic system. it is very important to make the role of women visible, and women should be allowed to participate in the development of society.
in writing. − the current trends in society are leading to a relentless consumption of resources and a deepening of social exclusion. the starting point for changing this is to promote activities in environmentally-oriented areas. this report makes a significant contribution to the creation of a green economy, where social equity and human well-being are created by reducing the negative impact on the environment. the report highlights the need to integrate women into agriculture, science and eco-innovation. since women have a harder time adapting to a changing labour market than men, their integration should be one of the eu's top priorities in building a green economy. i voted in favour of this report because its implementation would not only improve women's well-being, but also encourage changes towards a more sustainable economy.
in writing. − i voted for this report because 83.1% of women of working age are employed in the service sector. unfortunately, there are certain stereotypes in society that determine the division of work between the sexes. it is believed that there are female and male jobs, with the female being predominantly domestic. stereotypes also exist regarding flexibility, and it is still considered that women's primary responsibility is to take care of the home and family, and therefore it should be acceptable for them to work on a flexible schedule, in temporary or part-time jobs. women, on the other hand, are very concerned about reconciling work and family life. equal pay is also a key issue, as women in the eu now earn 17.1% less than men. the current legislative initiatives call for equal pay, but it still varies and progress is very slow. in its report 'equality between women and men 2010', the european commission highlighted the persistence of employment inequalities and expressed concern that the economic crisis was contributing to the deterioration of the situation by reducing or eliminating equality measures.
in writing. − eu statistics show that women are the majority of workers in the service sector. i voted in favour of this document because i agree that there is still a gap between men's and women's work in specific sectors. although the service sector generates the majority of jobs and income, it is still the lowest paid sector. in assessing the responsibilities of women in the household, the possibility of terminating work because of pregnancy the possible discriminatory lower remuneration. also, one of the biggest threats in this sector is illegal employment and wages. therefore, particular attention should be paid to the exploitation of workers, in particular third-country emigrants, by employers in the service sector in the member states who employ women on a part-time basis and pay inadequate remuneration for their work. investment in training, gender pay equity, flexible work schedules, taking into account the roles of women key measures to improve the position and working conditions of women in the service sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is another step towards reducing social exclusion and improving the position of women in the labour market. the service sector provides about 70% of all jobs in the eu, and women account for about 83% of all workers in this sector. statistics show that women earn 19% less than men for the same job. this encourages discriminatory treatment of certain professions and affects social security at retirement age. the eu must therefore take decisive action to promote the deeper integration of women into the labour market, to protect their rights and to improve their working conditions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the priorities for the 'education and training 2020' programme for 2012-14. it is important to promote cooperation in this area in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, which requires more advanced investment and policy reform. i agree that the main priorities of the programme should be to reduce the number of out-of-school children, to promote lifelong learning and to promote international mobility. i support the suggestions that more attention should be paid to the development of the pre-school child, that lifelong learning should be facilitated for the disabled, and that small grants should be made available for students from poorer backgrounds who are not yet in university. it is also necessary for universities in the eu member states to develop learning opportunities, update curricula and adapt them to changing market needs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because language skills and, in general, multilingualism are important for finding a job in another eu country. both the eu contribution and the resources allocated at national level are important. another area of concern is the labour market outlook for older people. now that pension age is rising in many eu countries, it is important to achieve lifelong learning not only in theory but also in practice. in general, it is important to emphasise that in education, priority is given to assessment from the pupil's perspective and interests. the development of pre-school children should also be considered, as this stage is the basis for further education and training. unfortunately, economic hardship often leaves this area in the background, and it is important to stress that this is not a luxury that can be relinquished without harm. investments in this area can have excellent social benefits in the future, such as lower crime rates.
in writing. − i voted in favour because 'education and training 2020' (et 2020) is a strategic programme for european cooperation in education and training, based on the previous work programme on education and training for 2010 (et 2010). every two years, the ministers of education and the european commission publish a report on the overall state of education and training across the eu, assessing progress towards the common objectives. the report summarises the actions and developments of the first phase of implementation of et 2020 in 2009-2011 and proposes priority areas for european policy cooperation for the next phase in 2012-2014. in particular, it focuses on how cooperation in education and training can contribute to achieving the europe 2020 objectives. europe needs strong investment and policy reforms, and more efforts are needed to achieve the europe 2020 headline target of reducing the number of out-of-school children. it is worth noting that international mobility provides an opportunity to acquire new skills.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it highlights the eu's main political priorities in education. in the face of the current economic crisis, we cannot reduce funding for education, as this will have negative consequences for the future economy and increase social exclusion. only five of the 27 eu countries have managed to implement the european commission's proposal to allocate 1% of gdp to education. i therefore support the proposals in the report to increase funding for programmes in pre-primary education, multilingualism and lifelong learning, as we cannot achieve the objectives of europe 2014-2020 without a responsible approach to the development of education programmes.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a legal framework to facilitate the crossborder distribution of audiovisual works in the digital single market. the cultural and creative sectors in the eu generate 2.5% of eu gdp, the same as the automotive industry, and the eu should therefore promote this sector and create an environment conducive to legitimate supply, innovation and creativity. i support the proposals to improve the conditions for acquiring original works online, to develop alternative innovative systems for small payments for works, such as sms payments. i support calls for the permanent application of an international system for the identification and numbering of audiovisual works, which would give each work a permanent, unique number and thus facilitate the movement of works. i agree that in the future vat should be reduced on cultural works and services distributed in digital format in order to address the inequality between online and face-to-face services.
in writing. − the audiovisual and cinema sectors are vital components of the eu’s cultural and creative industries, which collectively contribute added value to the economy to the tune of 2.5% of total gdp – as much as the automotive industry. i supported this report because it calls for a public environment that fosters the creation and accessibility of legal audiovisual content. legal certainty and regulation of authors’ rights and copyright laws must exist in the european online environment in order to establish such beneficial conditions. the distribution and promotion of original european audiovisual content is vital to the development of european education and culture in today’s digital age.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. the report on minimum legal standards and support for victims of crime is an important and long-awaited vote by the european parliament. the aim of the directive is to strengthen the rights of victims in the eu and the mutual recognition of protection measures in judicial proceedings. all victims of crime, irrespective of their legal status, should be afforded the widest possible protection throughout the union. for this reason, we should establish minimum protection standards across the community that grant rights to all victims of crime, regardless of their nationality or the place where the crime was committed. the right of the injured party (understood as the victim of a crime) to information, interpretation and translation, access to legal aid and victim support services and the right to be heard should therefore be guaranteed. the provision of the directive protecting the victim from unwanted contact with the offender deserves support. victims, but also, and importantly, their family members, and in particular children, should be offered free support, including psychological support, from the moment they are harmed. to make these changes, a uniform definition of 'victim' is needed, the same for all legal systems in the eu member states, whereby 'victim' will mean not only the person harmed by the perpetrator, but also the members and close family members. the union should establish as soon as possible a transparent justice system which will include the above proposals.
president of the commission. − mr president, i will give very concrete answers to very concrete questions. first of all, to mr martin – because he was accusing me of giving too much attention to other members of the parliament – we are currently discussing in the commission what we can do in terms of this issue of the risks inherent in different kinds of activities between banks. as you know, commissioner barnier has asked mr liikanen to put forward a report. based on that report we will take decisions about what we can do to prevent risks associated with big banks, namely the possibility of addressing the issue of different activities they may pursue. regarding other concrete issues, such as romania and bulgaria, we have already said that we believe that romania and bulgaria meet the necessary conditions to become members of the schengen area. i want to reiterate that here today. that, of course, does not mean that we do not have the right to act when we believe decisions taken by any of our member states may call into question some of the principles of the rule of law that all member states accepted. some of you insisted on the issue of social cohesion. indeed it is a very important matter. the reality is that we are doing what we can at european level, but there are differences here between the instruments available at national and european level. as you may be aware, one of the concerns we now have in terms of the discussion for the next mff is the opposition that some of our governments are signalling, not only about the reinforcement of the social fund, but also the globalisation adjustment fund, which is so important for workers who may feel the impact and be considered redundant because of some structural transformations in europe, and even the solidarity fund, because there are some governments that are simply proposing the elimination of this fund. i would also like to thank those of you who have referred to the european programme of aid for deprived persons. i would like to confirm that the commission will put forward a proposal for a new programme to help poor people in europe because there is now rising poverty in europe. so that is why we have to be absolutely sincere and frank. yes, i say those words once again. you cannot withdraw from the european institutions the instruments for showing solidarity and afterwards criticise europe because europe does not have enough solidarity. we also need to act at european level in the social area. this is critically important, not only because it is just, but because we need a social dimension at european level so that we can keep support for our social market economy and for our european project. when we speak about more europe, it is not just more europe for the sake of europe or for the european institutions. the crisis in the euro area has shown that the credibility of the euro as a single currency is also dependent on the coherence and integration of the decisions taken for the euro area. when people ask me why we need more europe, we need more europe if we want to keep and sustain a common currency. we need more integration of the institutions, but also more harmonisation of norms to avoid behaviours that are against the common norms and also we need more coherence of policies. this is indispensable for a common currency. of course, we want to make those proposals not just for the euro area but for the european union because we want this to be united and open for all. if some members do not want to join us, of course they have that right, but they should not have the right to prevent those who want to have a stronger union from building that stronger union, not only for the currency but also for our common goals of a united europe. finally, let me thank you for this debate. i believe in democracy. i believe in national democracy, but also in european democracy. i want to reiterate that today, in the 21st century, with national democracy alone our citizens will not be able to control their future and their countries will become irrelevant. we are living in fundamentally new times. that is why we need to complete our national democracies with a strong european democracy. this parliament is the basis for that future stronger european democracy. [applause]
in writing. in the european union, as the financial, economic and social crisis continues, it is necessary to find the political will to take unpopular and difficult decisions that are essential for the eu's survival. today, the creation of a european banking union was mentioned, which will allow for more effective supervision of this sector in the future. i support this decision, but i regret that the union has not yet taken the steps that, if they had been taken in time, would have enabled the union and its member states to deal more successfully with the crisis. i am talking about the creation of a european credit rating agency, which would allow a fairer and more objective assessment of the economies of the member states. i also recall the call for the establishment of a gas purchasing group at eu level to ensure fair and competitive gas prices for all member states, which in turn would increase the competitiveness of our industry and reduce consumer bills. for a long time, we were convinced that the crisis was over and that the only way out of it was to adopt the most austere austerity measures. we now see that these austerity measures have reduced consumption and revenue collection, have led to a sharp increase in unemployment and have halted economic growth in the member states for a long time. most economists acknowledge that austerity measures have not delivered the benefits they were hoping for and have only made the eu's economic and social recovery more difficult.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the directive on the rights, support and protection of victims of crime. this directive aims to protect the rights of victims, to provide assistance and protection to victims and their family members, and to ensure the protection of the rights of victims in criminal proceedings by providing them with information in clear and understandable language on the progress of the proceedings and the decisions taken. harmonising these minimum standards would boost the confidence of eu citizens in their own and other member states' judicial systems. i support the proposal to adopt a comprehensive european legal framework giving victims, regardless of their nationality or the place of the crime, the right to information, to interpretation and translation, to access victim support services, to avoid contact between the victim and the offender, to protection during interrogation during criminal proceedings, etc. i agree that a uniform definition of victimhood should be established, which would extend the victim status not only to the victims of crime but also to their immediate family members.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, with the entry into force of the 2009 treaty of lisbon and the guidelines set out in the stockholm programme, the protection of victims of crime in the eu has become one of the most important issues on the eu agenda. closer cooperation between member states and better coordination of action with regard to victims would help to reduce the negative impact of crime and the risk of secondary and repeat victimisation and stigmatisation. all victims, regardless of their origin or the nature of the harm suffered, should receive free assistance, be treated with respect and be communicated in a language they understand. the victim concept should also include the provision of assistance to the children and family members of victims. it is essential that the privacy and family life of victims be protected by all possible means during and after criminal proceedings. particular attention should be paid to the media, which often makes victims feel vulnerable and disoriented, and it is therefore necessary to ensure that the media take self-regulatory measures. in order to avoid indirect discrimination, persons with disabilities, women or children who are victims of sexual violence, victims of terrorism and victims of organised crime should be defined not as 'vulnerable victims' but as 'victims with special needs' and be guaranteed specific protection measures: asylum, medical assistance, legal and psychological counselling.
in writing. − the creation of a single area of justice requires that the rights of participants in judicial or administrative proceedings are also guaranteed in the same way throughout the eu. it is therefore very important that we have today voted in favour of a directive which harmonises the rights of the most vulnerable parties to the proceedings, i.e. victims, at eu level. this directive will have particular relevance in the case of transnational crime. i also urge the council to adopt the text adopted by parliament as soon as possible.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to align the part of the legislation governing eu trade policy with the provisions of articles 290 and 291 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the amendments should cover the appropriate involvement of the european parliament in the preparation and implementation of delegated acts, the extension of the period for the possible objection to a draft delegated act, the delegation of power by reason of a deferral of time and the modification of the procedure for the application of the written procedure. references to the committee procedure in relation to the regulation on the common organisation of agricultural markets should also be deleted and incorporated into this regulation in order to reflect any changes resulting from the application of the written procedure. this would also ensure that the european parliament's committee on international trade does not lose its right to scrutinise implementing acts necessary for the administration of the quota system.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i want consistency in the legislation governing trade. to achieve this, the necessary amendments to the two general trade regulations, namely new recitals on the implementation of the acts, should be inserted in the basic acts, the european parliament should be involved in the preparation of delegated acts, the period of delegation of power to the commission should be limited, the period for opposing the draft delegated act should be extended, together with the extension of the examination period, and the conditions for the application of the written procedure should be changed. in order to ensure the effective application of the written procedure, a reference to committee procedures should be inserted in each amended regulation. under the new regulation, the international trade committee of the european parliament will have the right to examine such implementing acts, thus ensuring a fair follow-up to the implementation of the legislation in the field of the common commercial policy (based on article 207 tfeu).

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on improving and simplifying the functioning of the mutual recognition agreement (mra) with australia. the aim of this agreement is to remove technical barriers to trade and to protect the health, safety and environmental objectives of both parties to the agreement. to this end, each party to the agreement is empowered to verify and certify on its territory, prior to export, that the products meet the regulatory requirements of the other party. i agree with the proposed improvements to the agreement, including the removal of the restriction on rules of origin for industrial products, so that the gsp applies to all products covered by the agreement, irrespective of their origin. i agree that in order to simplify the operation of the cmp, it is necessary to provide for a simpler procedure for the designation and suspension of conformity assessment bodies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it offers the possibility of improving the mutual recognition agreement (mra) with australia, which entered into force on 1 january 1999. the amendments will make the structure of the sectoral annexes more flexible, remove trade restrictions between the parties, reduce the administrative burden associated with the gsp and clarify the gsp. the restriction relating to the rules of origin for industrial products should be removed, as this is the only way to ensure that the gsp applies to all products covered by it. as the joint committee is co-chaired by the parties, all references to the chair of the joint committee should be deleted. it is important to emphasise that the joint committee may amend the sectoral annexes when taking into account technical progress and other actions. in order to simplify the operation of the ce marking, the procedures for the designation, withdrawal of designation and suspension of conformity assessment bodies should be facilitated.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the draft agreement amending the agreement between the european community and australia on the mutual recognition of conformity assessment, certificates and markings. these are agreements on mutual recognition of conformity assessment of regulated products. the gpa gives both parties the power to verify and certify on their territory, before export, that products meet the regulatory requirements of the other party. the aim of the saa is therefore to remove technical barriers to trade and to protect the health, safety and environmental objectives of both parties to the agreement. the gpa with australia provides in its main part for rules governing the establishment of conformity assessment bodies and specific rules applicable to the various sectors concerned.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it offers the possibility of improving the mutual recognition agreement (mra) with new zealand, which entered into force on 1 january 1999. the amendments will make the structure of the sectoral annexes more flexible, remove restrictions on trade between the parties, reduce the administrative burden associated with the gsp, simplify and clarify the gsp. in order to apply the gsp to all products covered by it, irrespective of their origin, an unnecessary restriction on the rules of origin for industrial products should be removed. it is worth noting that the joint committee is co-chaired by the parties, so all references to the chair of the joint committee must be deleted. it is important to emphasise that the joint committee may amend the sectoral annexes when taking into account technical progress and other actions. it is also necessary to facilitate the procedure for the designation, withdrawal of designation and suspension of conformity assessment bodies, as this will simplify the operation of the cab.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the application of measures to states which allow illegal fishing. the continuing violations of the un convention on the law of the sea and the agreement on fisheries, as well as the actions taken in breach of the established requirements for cooperation between states in the management of migratory fish stocks, require the adoption of a legal instrument allowing the eu to take action against non-cooperative states. in order to reduce the negative impact on fish stocks, it is necessary to impose appropriate sanctions on member states, and i therefore support the proposals set out in this report on the introduction of quantitative restrictions on imports of fishery products into the eu by countries that allow illegal fishing. the export of fishing vessels and fishing gear to such states should also be prohibited, as should the conclusion of private trade agreements with other states by nationals of such states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to adopt a legal instrument enabling the eu to take effective action to deter illegal fishing against states that do not want to cooperate in the adoption and implementation of agreed management measures, that repeatedly violate the un convention on the law of the sea and the un agreement on fisheries, and that take unilateral action without regard to the requirements laid down. strict action is required in the event of any infringement, otherwise the negative impact on eu fisheries will not be stopped and fish stocks will be depleted. a clear political position, including a clear concept and effective measures, is therefore essential.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of measures relating to states which allow illegal fishing for the purpose of conserving fish stocks. the purpose of the document is to impose restrictions on the access to union ports by fishing vessels flying the flag of states authorising illegal fishing, except in cases of force majeure or accidents requiring the provision of services directly related to the remediation of those situations. the new regulation thus contributes to the promotion and implementation of sustainable and responsible fishing at international level and is also closely linked to the regulation on illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products. in view of the objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy and in order to promote sustainable production activities, the mandate of the organisation should be reviewed. i support the proposals to involve producer organisations more in fisheries management, to strengthen their economic viability and to encourage the creation of international producer organisations. another very important issue in this report concerns the labelling of fishery products. it is essential to ensure and increase consumer awareness of fishery products. the obligation for consumers to receive more detailed information on the fishery product purchased should therefore include the date of landing and the eu ecolabel for products caught in a straight line.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document on the common organisation of the markets in fishery and aquaculture products. whereas the common organisation of the market in fishery and aquaculture products must also have a positive impact on the dynamic development of the eu's agricultural sector in the future, so that the depletion of natural fish stocks can better meet the growing demand for fish in europe; aquaculture producer organisations should also have access to a set of tools to implement promotion and communication actions at national and international level and to provide added value for their members.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the common foreign and security policy. it is an important document, and i fully support its provisions. i am glad that it has a place to mark the eu-taiwan relations. this is very important to me, especially in the context of today, when the long-running dispute between japan and china over the island chain has recently become an open confrontation. it should be noted that taiwan's presence and its peaceful, non-confrontational policy is not only important for maintaining stability in the east china sea region, but also acts as a stabilising factor in general. the eu welcomes the good relations with taiwan, which must be further developed. in this context, i support the provision in the resolution that it is imperative to urge the commission and the council to take concrete action to further strengthen eu-taiwan economic relations and facilitate the negotiation of an eu-taiwan economic cooperation agreement. the eu should also strongly support taiwan's meaningful participation in relevant international organisations and activities, including the world health organisation. i am pleased that the eu visa waiver programme for taiwanese citizens, which entered into force in january 2011, has proved to be mutually beneficial.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the eu's common foreign and security policy. the eu's foreign and security policy must, in particular, ensure the protection and defence of the eu's values and interests in the world, and contribute to peace, human security, the strengthening of solidarity, conflict prevention, the promotion of the rule of law and democracy, the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, poverty reduction and the defence of other values in the international arena. the eu has acquired a new dimension in european external action with the treaty of lisbon, which means that eu external policy must be coherent, consistent and effective, and based on long-term strategies. i agree with the criticism in the resolution that the council's annual report on foreign and security policy does not set out clear priorities for the medium and long term and the means to ensure their consistency. i believe that the eu's external policy must be based on clearly defined and measurable criteria and guidelines, which allow progress to be monitored and ensure consistency in eu policy in this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the development of a new strategic approach is a major contribution to the european union's foreign policy. the 2010 council report under-emphasises several important aspects of the objectives of the lisbon treaty. examples include the failure to translate cfsp priorities or strategic guidelines, the avoidance of issues that ensure that the union's resources are aligned with its foreign affairs priorities. in particular, the eu is strongly encouraged to pursue greater synergies based on the tripartite mandate and the support of the eeas.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i believe that the eu should continue to develop its foreign policy ambitions, to promote values and to defend its interests worldwide, in line with the common objective of contributing to peace, human security, strengthening solidarity, conflict prevention, promotion of the rule of law and democracy, protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms, gender equality, respect for international law and support for international institutions, effective multilateralism and mutual respect between peoples, sustainable development, transparent and accountable governance, free and fair trade and poverty reduction. to achieve these objectives, the eu should be able to engage and develop strategic partnerships with countries that share common values and are committed to common policies and mutually agreed actions. the eu's ability to influence the international order depends not only on the coherence of its policies, actors and institutions, but also on the existing strategic concept of eu foreign policy, which must unite and coordinate all member states and convince them to follow the same priorities and objectives, so that they can show solidarity and have a united and balanced voice in the international arena. the eu's foreign policy must provide the means for the union to operate effectively and consistently on the world stage.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. it is intended to avoid over-intensive fishing and the depletion of fish stocks, while ensuring the livelihood of eu fishermen. i support the proposals for long-term management plans for all eu fishing regions, taking into account the specificities of the seas, and for a separate regime for small-scale coastal fishing. long-term management plans should have a clear objective and be based on an ecosystem-based approach to managing mixed fisheries. i agree that a mechanism should be set up to compensate fishermen who have experienced financial difficulties. it is necessary to establish an effective no-discharge policy, a mechanism for sanctions against member states that do not comply with the rules and to give the european fisheries control agency greater powers to ensure the functioning of the sanctions system.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the efforts of eu member states to strengthen conservation, restore fish stocks and reduce the capacity of the fishing fleet have been insufficient. the recovery plans must be established for all eu and geographical fishing regions, taking into account the different characteristics of the seas, with a separate approach for small-scale coastal fishing. the current situation is that short-term national issues obscure the long-term governance aspect, which hinders the pursuit of the common objective. it is essential to develop a decision-making framework for management plans and decisions on tacs and quotas, which would be applicable in the absence of data, as there is now a clear lack of reliable and available data. as the current cfp provisions are not sufficient to tackle overfishing, the cfp needs to be reviewed, with clear deadlines for fleet reduction and speed, and a sanction mechanism for member states that do not comply. financial support should also be provided for fishermen who suffer from the consequences of the overfishing of the identified fishery resources. fleet capacity regulation is another very important aspect that could be ensured by the remuneration received for sustainable fishing. in addition, organic fishing vessels should be allowed to benefit from preferential fishing rights.
in writing. − i supported the proposal as it calls for the conservation of living resources and long-term environmental sustainability, the increase of fish productivity and the conservation of living aquatic resources and marine ecosystems. the commission's report confirms once again that the current common fisheries policy (cfp) is falling short of its objectives for the protection and sustainable exploitation of eu fisheries and the adaptation of existing fishing capacity to the available fish stocks. more than 60% of fish stocks in european waters are caught in excess of the maximum sustainable yield. it is recognised that the tac and quota system alone have not been effective in the sustainable management of some fish stocks over the last decade. a very large number of jobs in the european fisheries industry have been lost due to the poor state of the resources, the increase in production costs, the fall in prices.
in writing. − the ep resolution on the reform of the common fisheries policy is important for lithuanian fishermen and the entire fishing industry. i supported two amendments to this document, which proposed to allocate subsidies from the eu budget to the refurbishment of fishing vessels (these subsidies were suspended in 2002, i.e. before lithuania joined the eu). the second amendment proposed an increase in fishing quotas. the first amendment was rejected and the second adopted by the ep plenary vote. the reform of the fisheries policy, adopted in 2002 and still in force, has left all the new eu member states without subsidies for fleet renewal, placing them in a very difficult situation. most of the ships that needed repair were cut up. such reforms excluded potential competitors from the markets of the old eu member states, forgetting that fisheries are not only jobs and income for the people of the new eu member states, but also a tradition and a way of life. the lithuanian fishermen have suffered a considerable loss, which has a monetary impact. unfortunately, the amendments to the eu member states' subsidies for the renewal of their fishing fleets were not supported by a majority of meps. i therefore voted against this document, expressing my opposition to the proposed reform of the eu's common fisheries policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the reform of the eu's common fisheries policy. the aim of the reform is to avoid over-fishing and depletion of fish stocks, while ensuring the livelihoods of eu fishermen. it is necessary to ensure that by 2015 all fish stocks are fished below sustainable levels and that long-term management plans are established. in order to make the measures chosen more appropriate to regional and local needs, the most appropriate safeguard measures should be chosen by the member states themselves. i agree that it is necessary to prohibit the discarding of unwanted fish and to ensure that consumers are provided with all the necessary information on the quality and sustainability of the products they buy. financial support should be limited to environmentally friendly initiatives and a strict control system should be established to ensure that illegal activities are not financed. finally, it is important that the eu promotes the same principles of good maritime governance around the world.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the reform of the common fisheries policy, as the fishing industry is of strategic importance for the supply of fish products to society and for the stability of food supplies in the various member states and in the european union itself, and as it makes a significant contribution to the social and economic well-being of coastal communities, to development at local level, to employment, economic activity and to the preservation and creation of jobs in the production and consumption sectors, as well as to the preservation of local cultural traditions. it is vital that the implementation of the cfp in the fisheries sector is guided by an approach that takes into account the biological, ecological as well as the economic and social aspects (the three pillars of the cfp reform) in order to always find a compromise between the situation of existing resources in the different marine zones and the social and economic structure of coastal communities that depend on coastal fishing for jobs and prosperity. it is also important to bear in mind that the main objective of any fisheries policy is to ensure the supply of fish to the public and the development of coastal communities by promoting employment and improving the working conditions of fisheries professionals, while ensuring the long-term viability of the resources, thus enabling them to be properly conserved.
in writing. this decision is a very important and welcome step towards the formulation of a single external energy policy for the eu by ensuring that third-country entities operating in the eu's single internal energy market under construction are subject to the same rules as eu entities. while the solution could be more ambitious, if member states cooperate in good faith and share information, we will soon be able to see the benefits of this for the development of the eu's energy sector, common infrastructure and the creation of the internal market. i welcome the commission's declaration to participate actively, to continue monitoring and to make further legislative proposals if necessary.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of an interinstitutional agreement on the transmission to the european parliament and the handling in the european parliament of classified information held by the council on matters not covered by the common foreign and security policy. whereas transparency and access to all necessary documents and information are the foundations of democracy and its indispensable precondition; this is particularly important for the european parliament to be able to do its job. furthermore, the agreement on the transmission to and handling by the european parliament of classified information held by the council which is not related to the common foreign and security policy is a necessary instrument for the full exercise of parliament's powers and functions. it is therefore necessary to lay down the rules for cooperation between the council and parliament to achieve these objectives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the smart regulatory agenda is a step forward towards better regulation, simplification of eu law and reduction of administrative and regulatory burdens. the idea was to transform the lisbon strategy into a 'europe 2020' strategy, with a focus on competitiveness and reducing administrative burdens through smart regulation, to ensure that markets serve people. the key now is to ensure that more active action is taken. it is important to update the 2003 interinstitutional agreement in the light of the legal circumstances arising from the ratification of the treaty of lisbon. the need for action in the areas of subsidiarity checks by national parliaments and impact assessments by parliament and the council should also be emphasised. finally, the functioning of the existing legislation should be examined.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the need for a euro-atlantic policy strategy is clear. a strategy will be launched in 2014 with european union as well as national and regional funding. it is also very important to emphasise that the atlantic private and public partners will be involved in the process of preparing the action plan in 2012 and 2013. the atlantic region has specific problems which are not only national in scope and therefore solutions should be taken at the level of the atlantic coastal region as appropriate. the strategy aims to promote the conservation of atlantic resources, to control human activities in an appropriate way in order to maintain the ecological balance. the strategy also aims to improve connectivity with the atlantic regions, to promote the competitiveness of industrial sectors, and to improve the response to certain emergencies and other emergencies.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the atlantic region has several characteristics which make the problems broader than national and require political solutions at the level of the atlantic coastal countries. it is desirable that the atlantic strategy be a macro-regional strategy in order to promote the interaction of the various measures and actions at different levels of spatial planning policy. the macro-regional approach will also ensure that local actors (private sector, regional and local authorities, civil society organisations) are involved in the definition and implementation of the strategy's objectives. the strategy is encouraged to be based on two themes: maritime and land-based spatial planning and improving land-sea links and promoting the economy of the atlantic regions through an industrial policy adapted to their specific characteristics.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it provides for the conclusion of economic partnership agreements between the african, caribbean and pacific states and the eu together with the member states, and council regulation (ec) no 1528/2007 clearly sets out the detailed arrangements applicable to the production from these countries. this regulation provides for duty-free access to the eu market. unfortunately, some countries have not taken all the necessary steps to ratify the epas and have not concluded the regional negotiations, and the european commission has therefore proposed (as of 1 january 2014) to remove these countries from the list of countries covered by this provision. seventeen countries have not yet begun the ratification process, which the european commission considers to be inconsistent with wto rules. in principle, measures are proposed to give impetus to the negotiations, but agreements of this type are complex, difficult to implement within a strict time limit, and the proposed deadline (until 2014) is too short. the amendments incorporated in the proposal also aim to bring the decision-making procedures into line with the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. − i voted in favour of removing certain countries from the list of regions or countries which have withdrawn from the negotiations, as the current situation was not in line with wto rules and raised a question of fairness both with regard to countries which have fulfilled their commitments and ratified agreements and with regard to developing countries which are not acp partners. the amendments proposed are designed to intensify the ongoing negotiations on the epa and thus to conclude comprehensive regional agreements. in general, the main reason for this proposal is probably to increase pressure and thus to give impetus to the negotiations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because a reliable energy supply is essential to fostering a predictable economic environment for eu citizens and for the eu industry as a whole. a stable internal energy market is the best way to ensure energy supply. however, given that eu countries still import over 60% of their gas and over 80% of their oil, many eu member states are vulnerable in this respect. the 2009 gas supply crisis has demonstrated the weaknesses and vulnerabilities of the eu gas supply system. the adoption of regulation (eu) no 994/2010 has provided the union with certain measures to combat future gas supply shortages, but the challenge of providing gas at competitive prices remains.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the decision establishing a mechanism for the exchange of information on intergovernmental energy agreements between member states and third countries. the eu is highly dependent on energy imports, and its energy security is therefore vulnerable to disruptions in supply from outside the eu. moreover, energy imports account for a large proportion of total eu imports - a high cost and risk to the eu economy. the eu and the member states should have an interest in the regulation of external relations in the field of energy through intergovernmental agreements and in strengthening the negotiating capacity of the member states through the exchange of information and best practices between the member states and the commission. intergovernmental agreements, especially if they are properly coordinated by the member states, should therefore help to increase the eu's competitiveness. intergovernmental agreements can support the eu's objective of increasing the diversity of energy supply routes and sources. moreover, a sustainable and reliable energy supply is crucial to fostering a predictable economic environment for citizens and the eu industry. the best way to ensure energy supply is through an internal energy market. i therefore supported the objective of this proposal to increase the transparency of intergovernmental agreements in the field of energy between member states and to ensure that member states are informed of the conformity of the agreement with the internal market rules or of any infringement thereof. the commission will therefore have to develop standard provisions which member states will be encouraged to use. this will ensure that the intergovernmental agreement does not infringe eu law.
in writing. − with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty in 2009, energy became an eu policy area. the document adopted today is one of the first steps towards achieving the eu's energy policy objectives. the single energy market in the european union cannot exist unless member states coordinate their actions and share information on planned or existing agreements with third countries in the energy sector. i hope that this is not the last document to help the european union and the energy sector speak the same language.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because consumers are very concerned about the quality of food, which stimulates demand for high-quality products both in the domestic and international markets. the eu has its own food quality policy instruments: labels and quality schemes that focus on the valuable qualities of products and the regional specificity of products. new proposals are currently being made for the application of national and private certification schemes for quality and marketing standards relating to quality assurance. one of the priorities is to try to simplify and develop existing schemes, as well as to introduce new quality terms. the main objective of all the amendments submitted is to ensure consistency with other amendments that promote a move beyond processed foods.
in writing. − i voted in favour, as the quality and diversity of the european union's agricultural, fisheries and aquaculture production is an important asset, a source of competitive advantage for eu producers to succeed and an important part of the european union's living cultural and gastronomic heritage. this is due to the skills and determination of eu farmers and producers who have managed not only to maintain traditions but also to take account of the development of new production methods and materials. european agriculture produces a wide range of food products using a methodology that protects the environment and takes account of the needs of rural communities. this document aims to help producers of agricultural and food products to inform buyers and consumers about the characteristics and the characteristics of those products derived from the farming method, thus improving the conditions of fair competition between farmers and producers offering agricultural and food products with value-added characteristics and characteristics, the availability to consumers of reliable information on such products and the respect of intellectual property rights and the integrity of the internal market.
in writing. − during this parliamentary term, we have discussed legislation on several occasions to improve consumer information on the origin and composition of the food they consume. this regulation on agricultural product quality schemes is therefore another step towards better information. i hope that the council's approval of the text will make it easier for consumers to understand information on both the production methods of agricultural products and geographical indications or designations of origin.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is essential to create a european sector focused on investing in legal persons engaged in non-profit-making activities, with a wide range of social objectives. certain types of investment funds may be granted the status of 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and the corresponding passports, provided that they meet the criteria set out in this proposal. two directives already apply which are linked to investment funds: directive 2011/61/ec of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2009/65/ec of the european parliament and of the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to create a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises. in order to qualify as a 'european venture capital fund', investment funds must meet the requirements set by the managers of the venture capital fund. investment restrictions will also apply, which will be determined by the use of the fund's assets. two directives already apply: directive 2011/61/ec of the european parliament and of the council and directive 2009/65/ec of the european parliament and of the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as the european union trade agreement with colombia and peru was signed on 26 june 2012 providing for the reduction and elimination of customs duties, as well as a safeguard clause which provides that preferential tariffs may be suspended or eliminated if increased imports due to trade liberalisation would worsen the situation of european industry and also threaten employment in the eu. the provisions of the bilateral safeguard measure in the peru-colombia trade agreement submitted by the european commission are similar to the provisions of the bilateral safeguard clauses in the eu-republic of korea epa, except for two key differences: the stabilisation measure for bananas and the special regime for the outermost and vulnerable regions of the european union. finally, it is essential to include certain aspects such as reporting and monitoring of provisions. in principle, it is necessary to ensure that the agreement is implemented in accordance with international labour and environmental conventions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the amended proposal because this agreement has a significant impact on the agricultural sector, in particular the corresponding impact on banana exports to the european market. the provisions of the agreements mean that the eu market will be more open to imports, in particular of bananas, sugar and beef, and that the eu will have more scope to export other agricultural products to these countries, such as dairy products, cereals, pigmeat and spirits. both the agreement with colombia and peru and the agreement signed with the six central american countries contain a chapter on the mutual recognition of geographical indications, which will allow the european union to protect some 200 geographical indications. bananas are the main agricultural product exported to the european union from these countries, in particular colombia and costa rica, and to a lesser extent from panama, honduras, peru and guatemala. the agreements provide for even lower customs duties for the european union on imports of bananas from these countries, thus making the contractual conditions for latin american exports to the european market even more favourable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because on 22 march 2011 the european union signed an agreement with six central american countries, which established preferential, liberalised trade in certain agricultural products. this has resulted in a greater openness of the eu to imports, which will increase the eu's ability to export certain products to central american countries. the agreement also includes a stabilisation measure for imports of bananas, which allows the suspension of the preferential rate of duty if a certain import ceiling is reached (foreseen until 2020). it is essential to ensure the effectiveness of both the stabilisation mechanism for banana imports and the safeguard clause.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the rational dissemination of information in virtual space is beneficial for the internal market and the digitisation of cultural works should therefore continue to be supported. the european parliament supports the idea of a legislative solution to help solve the problems of unregistered copyright works. the creation of a european database to facilitate access to information is also welcomed, but it should not be forgotten that the copyright management system itself needs to be improved. there is a proposal to allow certain institutions (education, as well as libraries, museums, archives) to publish works without copyright. access to such works should be free for all. the commission also provides for exemptions and licences to facilitate the digitisation of unregistered copyright works. it is important to emphasise that, in principle, copyright is an essential basis for innovation, investment and production in the creative industries, and it is therefore essential that rightholders have the possibility to revoke the status of unencumbered copyrighted works.
in writing. − i abstained from voting on this document as the question remains whether the harmonised definitions of the beneficiaries mentioned in the commission proposal should be applied and how the member states intend to proceed in cases where one member state has to carry out a thorough search but the information available in another member state is more accurate, up-to-date and therefore more suitable for the necessary search. more attention should also be paid to the spectrum of authorised uses, as the proposal allows for a broad interpretation not only of the definition but also of any use in different member states.
in writing. − this report proposes ways of regulating the use of works by unidentified authors more fairly. according to statistics, about 45% of all works in the european union fall into this category. under the current regime, in order to protect the rights of works not identified by the author, such works cannot be publicly displayed and are not accessible to the public. this prohibition shall remain in force until the authors are identified. the report argues that the current system is an obstacle to the dissemination of european culture. i voted in favour of this report because it calls for the demonstration of works which are not subject to copyright and for all the funds to be used to find the creators of these works. i support the rapporteur's joint proposal to help public libraries, museums, archives and broadcasters to contribute to the revival of europe's cultural heritage by all possible means.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it seeks to adopt a regulation establishing aid measures for pakistan, which has recently been hit by floods. the main objective of this regulation is to extend the autonomous trade preferences for 75 products. despite the fact that humanitarian aid is already being provided, trade preferences would further contribute to combating the long-term negative economic consequences of the floods. the recovery of the state of pakistan is important not only for its citizens but also for the overall stability of the region. it is important that the commission carries out a full assessment before setting an exact time limit for the extension of the autonomous trade preferences. the overall impact of the measures on eu trade and production, their effectiveness for the pakistani population and fiscal resources, as well as pakistan's commitments to improve the efficiency of the tax system should be assessed. it is essential that the rules of origin of the products concerned are strictly respected and that the trade preferences benefit only those to whom they are intended, and it is essential that this serves the recovery of the pakistani economy. it is also important to underline that the deterioration of the human rights situation in pakistan may affect the suspension of trade preferences in the future.
in writing. - i abstained on the emergency autonomous trade preferences for pakistan. as the autonomous trade preferences for pakistan have also been extended for a period of three years, the commission did not carry out a full assessment of the proposed measures before adopting the proposal for a regulation. it should also be noted that the commission proposal does not impose any obligations on pakistan in the field of human and social rights. furthermore, it can be assumed that similar initiatives may be taken in the future following the decision to grant autonomous trade preferences to flood-affected pakistan. there is therefore a risk that the adoption of autonomous trade preferences, without any human rights conditions attached, would in fact undermine the current eu preference system based on respect for fundamental rights and values.

in writing. today we are voting on the european parliament's position on the 2013 budget of the european union. while there is a lively debate on what the eu budget should be for next year, it should nevertheless be remembered that, despite differing opinions, we all have the common interest in the well-being of the member states of the european union and their citizens. i therefore urge you to take note of the positions proposed by the european parliament, which are truly balanced and relevant, ensuring the implementation of the eu's key priorities. first and foremost, we must ensure the continuity of eu-funded projects, and we must not allow the european union to put a stop to what it itself is promoting through its priorities. i am pleased that the budget for the coming year focuses heavily on economic growth, promoting competitiveness, and employing young people. it is essential that the eu supports long-term investment in research, development and innovation (rdi), and no less necessary is coordinated funding to boost member states' recovery. i understand the member states' desire to cut spending, to reduce their budget deficits as much as possible, but we cannot forget that the eu budget is investing in the future of our own countries. economic growth is based on the development of energy, innovation, research and education, and it is therefore necessary to ensure not only the continuity of existing programmes but also the development and financing of new policy areas, clearly defined in the priorities of the european union.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank you and my colleagues for the opportunity to say a few words regarding the agreement on conformity assessment and acceptance, the so-called acaa between israel and the eu, which is a fiercely debated issue. let me start by recalling what an acaa is about. its objective is to eliminate barriers to trade, by allowing products covered by the agreement to enter the markets of the parties without additional conformity assessment procedures. so we are basically talking about mutual recognition of conformity assessment and inspection, results which will reduce costs and time for economic operators. acaa is a protocol to the eu-israel association agreement and its scope of application is therefore the same as set out in article 83 of the association agreement. as follows from the international obligations of the eu and as confirmed by the european court of justice in the brita case, the eu does not recognise israeli jurisdiction over the territories placed under israeli administration after 1967. rest assured that the commission will observe this position in the implementation of the acaa. as you know, when the agreement enters into force, the commission will have to acknowledge under article 9 of the acaa the responsible israeli authority which will have to deliver conformity certificates. this acknowledgement will not entail any recognition of israeli jurisdiction over territories placed under israeli administration after 1967. you can also rest assured that, upon receipt of the israeli notification of its responsible authority, the commission will expressly state that acknowledgement is granted only on the basis that the territory covered by the responsible authority does not include the territories brought under israeli administration in 1967. in the light of this, palestinian products cannot be discriminated against in the certification process in israel because israel will have to apply the eu acquis. like any eu member state, israel must carry out inspections irrespective of the origin of the product, when a request is received. if there were to be cases of discrimination, the palestinian manufacturer could lodge a complaint with the israeli judicial authorities. of course, the commission could also use existing means under the association agreement to ensure that israel implements the acaa. there could be a link between the certification process and the origin of the products in a situation where the israeli responsible authority goes into the occupied territories in order to certify products made in the settlements. and we need to be aware of this. i would also like to react to recent concerns about parliament’s role in the context of procedures to amend this acaa, including by adding annexes for other industrial products in future. the matter seems to be in line with the lisbon treaty. moreover, the commission will also abide by its obligations under the framework agreement to keep parliament fully informed before approving modifications to an agreement under article 218(7) of the lisbon treaty. lastly, we have other acaas in the pipeline with other countries where we would expect to face similar, though not identical, concerns. our experience with the present consent procedure will serve as a useful guide.
on behalf of the ppe group. – madam president, the ppe group is in favour of the acaa and we look forward to the vote in order to give our consent to this important agreement between the eu and israel. after a deliberation of more than two and a half years, we are finally having this discussion in the plenary session on acaa. i am happy that there has been enough common sense among our colleagues in the inta committee to vote in favour of this agreement, which is good for both the eu and israel and is part of the eu association agreement. israel is the first country in the mediterranean region to achieve the basic conditions that enable it to reach an acaa with the eu. the acaa, together with the additional protocol on pharmaceutical products, aims at facilitating market access by eliminating technical barriers to trade in industrial products. in order to make the framework of the acaa operational, it has to be implemented into specific sectors, practices and regulations. as we know, once adopted, the acaa would cover mutual recognition of regulatory and verification procedures for pharmaceutical products in the eu and israel. such mutual recognition would certainly benefit european consumers and they would get quicker access to israeli pharmaceutical products, as there would no longer be a need for a second testing in the eu – something that normally takes from one to three years. colleagues, it should be mentioned that it took israel more than six years to adopt the necessary standards in the field of good manufacturing practice for pharmaceutical products. in other words, in order to conclude this agreement, and the additional protocol, israel had to substantially approximate its regulatory framework on pharmaceutical products to that of the eu. so we are spreading our acquis communautaire to israel, with a spill-over effect to other areas as well. in other words, it is in the eu’s interest to get israel’s legislation and standards closer to the eu’s. i would, therefore, like to encourage my colleagues to give our consent to the acaa later today. (the speaker agreed to take a blue-card question under rule 149(8))
blue-card answer. – human rights are universal and we should not have double standards – one for palestinians and another for israelis. human rights are very important, but this agreement we are discussing today is purely technical in nature. it is part of the eu-israel association agreement. once we have concluded the association agreement, we should take the necessary steps in order to implement it. of course it is always our duty also to address human rights, whether we are speaking about israel or palestine.
