in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, in which the european parliament supports the commission's proposal to declare 2013 the european year of citizens. the european year of citizens must build a bridge between brussels and the eu member states, which will encourage eu citizens to take an active part in elections and ensure that their voices are heard in the eu institutions. the year 2013 will be a pivotal year in promoting and strengthening a common european identity based on the fundamental values of the european union. i believe that in the midst of the ongoing economic crisis, the european year of citizens will encourage eu citizens to seize their rights and opportunities offered by freedom. statistics show that one third of eu citizens would like to exercise their rights, but they still face obstacles in the labour market, such as administrative difficulties when moving to another country. the european year of citizens is being celebrated to mark the 20th anniversary of eu citizenship as enshrined in the maastricht treaty. all initiatives and awareness-raising campaigns will highlight the real value of eu citizenship - active participation in the democratic life of the european union, and in particular in the 2014 european parliament elections.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because the overall objective of the european year is to increase awareness of the rights attached to citizenship of the union so that citizens can fully exercise their right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states. unfortunately, there is a lack of visibility and awareness of the specific benefits of union citizenship for eu citizens, students, workers, consumers and businesses, as well as suppliers of goods and services. the proposal therefore aims to give a new impetus to the debate on citizenship of the union and to put a strong emphasis on the informed and effective implementation of this right on the political agenda. i therefore believe that it should be of the utmost importance to strengthen citizenship of the union at all levels and at every stage of the democratic process, to ensure that citizenship becomes a highly relevant aspect of eu policy and a key priority for union action in all areas. to encourage citizens to participate in the democratic life of the union, citizens need to be informed about the real benefits of eu law and policy for them and how to make use of them everywhere in the societies of the eu member states. i am convinced that by providing more information about citizenship of the union and its concrete benefits to individuals, we are increasing awareness of the value of european integration.
in writing. − i support the proposal to declare 2013 the european year of citizens. this must be an efficient and rational use of time and resources, as the eu works to increase the level of information available to its citizens, so that they are better aware of their rights and unprecedented privileges, which are not available to citizens of any other member state of an international organisation. every citizen of the union enjoys the right to move and reside freely within the territory of the member states, the right to vote and stand as a candidate in elections to the european parliament and to local government in the member state in which he or she lives, the right to protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any member state in a third country, the right to petition the european parliament, the right to apply to the european ombudsman and the right to have recourse to the institutions of the union, as well as a host of other rights in areas as diverse as the free movement of goods and services, consumer protection and public health, equal opportunities and treatment, employment opportunities and social protection. the 20 years of development of the concept of citizenship of the union have brought many good results, but there are still many cases where eu citizens are prevented from exercising their rights because of practical obstacles and because they are not sufficiently aware of their rights and obligations. we will therefore await the 2013 european citizenship report, which should set out proposals to remove the remaining obstacles. it is also desirable that the impact of the information and communication campaign on european citizens be analysed by means of quantitative studies at the end of 2013 to see whether the campaign has been effective and whether the objectives set have been achieved.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because this commission communication lists the rights of passengers in all modes of transport, which as a whole in the eu ensure the necessary protection of passengers. the eu rules are formulated to ensure the proportionality and differentiation necessary due to the differences in transport modes and their markets, i.e. in terms of type of journey. however, together they form a common framework of passenger rights: non-discrimination means that passengers and tour operators cannot be discriminated against on the basis of their place of residence or nationality; information on travel conditions; transparency, including price transparency; assistance in the event of disruption of travel by offering alternative transport or a full refund of the ticket price if the route is cancelled or delayed for a long period; compensation (except in exceptional circumstances); care of passengers (meals or, depending on the circumstances, hotel accommodation). also, the provision of assistance and accessibility to disabled persons or persons with reduced mobility.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the document, as the potential of european entrepreneurs will be strengthened and the eu economy will grow again only if the eu succeeds in improving the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and at the same time adopts measures to reduce the administrative burden on smes. the role of industry is crucial to the european economy. manufacturing accounts for 25% of private sector jobs in the eu and 80% of private sector research and technological development. all agree that the eu should improve the competitiveness of eu enterprises of all sizes in order to recover from the crisis. this requires an environment conducive to new ideas and new business ventures. such a business-friendly environment in europe is not well developed, also because of the wide variation in industrial policies between member states. however, the reality is that it is essential and necessary to achieve sustainable growth and economic recovery, as called for in the europe 2020 strategy, by pursuing a coherent and coordinated industrial policy by member states and implementing fundamental structural changes in the eu industrial system.

in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on trade and economic relations with the united states. the usa and the eu are very important trade partners: the two economies together account for about half of the global economic output and nearly a third of world trade flows, making this relationship the largest economic relationship in the world. although the economic ties between the eu and the us are among the most open in the world, there is a general consensus that the potential of the transatlantic relationship is far from being fully exploited. therefore it is important to foster the ongoing joint discussion between the eu and the us on how to work collectively to increase growth potential and financial stability. i support the rapporteur’s view that, in order to ensure long-term prosperity and employment, a joint commitment and effort is needed to create new opportunities for businesses both large and small, to promote entrepreneurship and to capitalise on the advantages offered by the uniquely integrated transatlantic market. in this regard, we, members of the ep, emphasise that there are many areas where progress would be greatly beneficial, such as the removal of trade barriers and better market access.
in writing. - i voted yes. in the context of the continuing economic and financial crisis in the european union and the united states, it is important to remove existing barriers to bilateral trade. this would bring mutual benefits to the budget revenues of both countries, help mitigate the effects of the crisis, boost growth in both economies and in people, reduce unemployment, promote entrepreneurship, and open up new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises. the economies of these two trading partners account for more than half of the world economy, almost a third of global trade flows and the largest economic relationship in the world, but the potential exists to expect even greater mutual benefits and positive impacts on the global economy. i therefore hope that the current eu-us dialogue will be productive and that concrete and far-reaching proposals will be forthcoming in the near future.
in writing. the creation of the single market should be one of the eu's major achievements, and eu citizens and businesses should already be benefiting from it. however, to date, particularly economically strong member states have been engaged in protectionism on their markets, which has prevented genuine competition in the internal market. the successful functioning of this market is directly dependent on the proper implementation of other eu policies. as regards agriculture, farmers in some countries, including the baltic states, have not yet been able to benefit from the benefits of the single market because they are not given equal opportunities to compete in agriculture because of the very low level of direct payments. in the field of research and innovation, different rules apply to researchers from different countries participating in european projects, in particular because of lower remuneration for the same work. a transparent and uniform public procurement system has not yet been established. the access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises is not facilitated. i believe that in the current difficult economic climate, every opportunity must be taken to strengthen the eu's single market and to exploit its full potential for growth and employment. i would therefore urge the commission to take concrete action and to put forward the necessary proposals to remove the existing obstacles and to make the single market work in practice.
in writing. in the european union, there are still many obstacles that make it difficult to reap the full benefits of the single market and to exercise the right to free movement. several issues require the european commission's particular attention. companies continue to face problems in accessing public procurement in other member states. this applies to both contractors and subcontractors. this is due to the excessive diversity of national practices and the complex administrative requirements in individual countries, including the lingüistic barriers that still exist in the offices, which are contrary to the promotion of linguistic diversity by the union. another thing that would facilitate access to the community labour market is to simplify and speed up procedures for reimbursing medical treatment abroad and to ensure that the necessary measures are taken within the health and social insurance systems to ensure that mobile citizens are adequately protected. greater mobility of skilled workers can make the european economy more competitive. this requires the adoption of a modern model for the recognition of professional qualifications. it should be stressed that the movement of workers between member states must be voluntary and must be accompanied by full respect for workers' rights. any discrimination based on the origin or nationality of workers in any member state shall be unacceptable. removing these barriers will allow europeans to enjoy the positive aspects of membership of the european union.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources. it is important to me that the european parliament unanimously approved the commission's proposal to extend the 12-mile zone regime until the new common fisheries policy (cfp) is agreed. if we had not voted for this resolution, the 12-mile zone regime would have ended by the end of this year. i agree with the rapporteur that this would be totally unacceptable and unjustifiable. the important point is that member states have managed coastal fisheries quite successfully compared to the common fisheries policy, which is not feasible in practice due to over-centralized and ineffective controls from brussels. i agree with the rapporteur that the overall effectiveness of controls by member states in the 12 nautical mile zones clearly shows that management is most effective in the light of local circumstances.
in writing. - i agreed to this. since 2003, member states have been allowed to restrict fishing by certain vessels within the 12 nautical mile zone of member states (territorial waters). the purpose of this derogation is to enable member states to protect biologically vulnerable regions, ensure the sustainable management of fish stocks and preserve traditional fisheries. this derogation expires on 31 december 2012 and i therefore agree to extend it until 31 december 2014 in order to ensure the continued application of this derogation until the adoption of the new eu fisheries policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the commission's proposal aims to extend the existing regime for the exploitation of waters and resources in the 12-mile zone. under the current legislation on the common fisheries policy (cfp), article 17 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002 provides for a derogation from the principle of equal access to the fishery resources of the member states in the 12-mile zone. this exemption shall apply from 1 january 2003 until 31 december 2012. the current proposal aims to extend the validity period until 31 december 2014. the current 12 nautical mile zones are functioning well, but if the current proposal is not accepted, they will expire on 31 december this year. those zones provide a degree of protection for vulnerable coastal communities, which would be incomprehensible to those fishing communities if the interinstitutional access bottleneck were removed.
in writing. − i have agreed to this proposal as it aims to extend the existing regime for the use of waters and resources in the 12 nautical mile zone. in addition, it remains to be expected that the reformed cap will be set up in a highly decentralised manner in general, and that member states will be allowed to take real management decisions through cooperation at regional level.
in writing. − the current situation of the common fisheries policy is unfortunately not conducive to sustainable exploitation of fish stocks. therefore, while the future of the cfp and the wider use of fisheries resources based on scientific evidence are being discussed, it is appropriate to use individual instruments which, as practice has shown, can be used effectively and ensure the conservation and sustainable use of fisheries resources. for this reason, i support the extension of the scope of the regulation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of an eu-moldova agreement on the mutual protection of geographical indications for agricultural and food products. the aim of this agreement is to promote bilateral trade by providing for the extension of the system of geographical indications to protect the names of certain regional foodstuffs against plagiarism and to prevent possible misuse of eu indications. the republic of moldova shall undertake to ensure the protection of all listed eu geographical indications, while protecting its current geographical indications within the eu. i support the proposed agreement, which will contribute to closer eu-moldova trade relations, improving the quality of the food chain and promoting sustainable rural development.
in writing. − adequate information on agricultural and food products a prerequisite for ensuring safe food for consumers. one of the elements of such information is the appropriate protection of geographical indications. it is important that the same rules apply to products originating in the eu as to those imported from third countries. i therefore support the decision approving the agreement with moldova on the protection of such geographical indications.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the food aid convention on behalf of the european union. this convention is in line with the eu's efforts to contribute to the reduction of poverty and the eradication of hunger worldwide in the context of the millennium development goals. i agree with the need to establish an international legally binding framework which also defines the obligations and measures relating to the provision of food aid to developing countries. i support the proposals made to promote, in the implementation of this convention, a method of grant-based food aid, which would increase agricultural productivity and improve the livelihoods of rural areas. it is also important to monitor closely the impact of food aid on local food production and markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in accordance with the provisions of article 5 of this convention, the european parliament calls on the eu to make an ambitious minimum annual commitment for 2013 and to properly implement its annual commitments on food aid to developing countries. the visibility of the european union as a humanitarian actor is regrettable, as there is no common minimum annual eu commitment covering both eu and member state contributions. the european parliament, by common accord, therefore requests the commission to keep the eu and the member states that are parties to the convention fully informed of the implementation of the convention, inter alia, by transmitting their annual reports and by briefing the development committee on the implementation of the convention and the work of the committee on a regular basis. compliance with and further development of this convention will allow the most effective and efficient food aid policy to be pursued, consistently meeting the food and nutrition needs of the most vulnerable populations through objectively defined commitments.
in writing. − the european union's own practice shows that food aid is an important part of social policy and support for the eu's most deprived citizens. food aid to third countries is also an important part of the eu's development policy, which pursues essentially the same objectives. i therefore support the conclusion on behalf of the union of the renewed convention simplifying the procedure for the provision of food aid. the entry into force of these amendments will allow us to provide more effective assistance to the population of third countries suffering from food shortages.
in writing. − today, global food security and hunger represent a serious challenge. in 2010, approximately 925 million people (13.6% of the world’s population) did not have enough food to eat. despite advances made in reducing income poverty around the world, 98% of undernourished people live in developing countries. child malnutrition runs rampant as well, affecting millions of children worldwide every year. the eu is committed to fighting poverty and eradicating hunger on a global scale. the food aid convention 2012 will greatly aid in the construction of an international, legally binding framework to define and provide the necessary instruments for the delivery of food aid to developing countries. i voted in favour of this recommendation, because i believe that fac 2012 will streamline and improve food aid policy and ensure that the food and nutrition needs of the most critical populations will be met effectively. fac 2012 will increase transparency of food assistance and humanitarian programmes and provide for more effective donor coordination. we in the eu have a responsibility to assist our less fortunate counterparts in developing countries – fac 2012 will go a long way towards helping us to achieve that goal.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on consular protection of union citizens abroad. the new directive aims to replace the 1995 regulation on diplomatic and consular missions. according to article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, every citizen of the union is entitled, when in a third country in which his member state is not represented, to protection by the diplomatic or consular authorities of any other member state on the same conditions as nationals of that state. this principle is also enshrined in article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights. the proposed directive covers not only everyday situations, such as losing identity documents, being arrested or imprisoned, but also critical situations where eu citizens may need help. i agree with the view that in a crisis, the european union delegation would be responsible for the preparation of the crisis and for the coordination and delivery of support during the crisis. in order to avoid imposing an unbearable burden on either the eu presidency or the other member state represented in the area, the eu delegation should be responsible for the coordination of all cooperation and, in exceptional cases, for the coordination of the plans and actions of the eu member states' missions, the coordination of evacuation. i agree with the rapporteurs that this proposal is a great example of how 'more europe' does not mean more bureaucracy or more brussels. 'more europe' means more help for eu citizens, even when they do not have their own embassies in certain territories where they are in dangerous, critical situations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on strengthening consular protection for citizens of the european union abroad. the major crises of recent years, both those following the uprisings in libya and egypt and those following the earthquake in japan, which affected some 150 000 eu citizens, have shown the importance of consular protection in third countries. it is necessary to ensure that every eu citizen in a third country where his member state is not represented is entitled to protection by the consular authorities of any other member state under the same conditions as nationals of that state. i support the proposals made for the establishment of a clear framework for the coordination of cooperation and support between member states and for the establishment of common concepts of consular protection. i agree that member states should consider setting up a consular protection trust fund from which the embassy of the assisting member state could advance the costs of its assistance to the non-represented citizen and into which other member states should reimburse the funds paid.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to define more clearly the means of coordination and cooperation necessary to ensure the consular protection of eu citizens who are not represented on a daily basis. consular protection is a fundamental right conferred by eu citizenship within the meaning of article 20 (2) (c) and article 23 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) and article 46 of the charter of fundamental rights of the eu. in particular, in order to distinguish between two levels of consular protection, namely consular protection at local level, which applies in everyday life, and consular protection in crisis, member states should consider establishing a consular protection trust fund from which the embassy or consulate of the assisting member state could advance the costs of its assistance to the non-represented citizen and into which the other member states should reimburse the advance payments, in order to avoid financial burdens on the parties and to ensure that contingency plans take account of all eu citizens, including non-represented citizens. that council directive should allow for a wider network of eu delegations to play a greater role in ensuring consular protection.
in writing. − i supported this proposal because i believe that a new legislative instrument is needed to ensure that eu citizens can exercise their rights, including the right to protection in third countries. the right of citizens whose member state is not represented to request the assistance of the consular services of other member states which are represented is one of the rights conferred on citizens of the union. however, experience has shown that citizens cannot fully exercise their rights of consular protection. one of the main problems is that citizens are not aware that they have the right to receive assistance from the consulate of another member state when in a third country where their member state is not represented. this new directive aims to address this problem. this directive also aims at a harmonised approach to the issue of assistance to unrepresented union citizens. without prejudice to the right of unrepresented citizens to seek assistance from any member state's institutions, this directive will establish a framework under eu law whereby member states may agree that in certain countries or regions one member state will act as the lead state and coordinate consular activities. such agreements will be published, i.e. citizens travelling to certain areas will know which consulate they can contact first. in the long term, this could save money, as the need for other member states to have their own representations in the area concerned would be reduced by the appointment of a lead country by agreement between member states.
in writing. - i voted yes. once this decision has been taken, a national of a member state who is in difficulty in a third country where there is no diplomatic representation of his country will be able to apply for and receive equivalent consular assistance at the representation of another eu member state. this decision is a true expression of solidarity between eu member states, helping to better safeguard the rights of eu citizens in third countries and to provide them with the appropriate assistance. at the same time, it will allow the rationalisation of consular services, which is particularly relevant for smaller eu member states that do not have a wide network of diplomatic missions and do not have many bilateral consular agreements. it is important that this right is properly publicised and that eu citizens travelling abroad are aware of and use it.
in writing. − when eu citizens travel abroad in any third country in which their home state does not have representation, they should be entitled to protection by the consular or diplomatic authorities of any eu member state. for example, if a lithuanian citizen needed access to consular services in a third country and could not reach a lithuanian embassy or consulate, then that citizen should have a right to go to any eu member state consulate that is available. in crisis situations (such as national instability or rioting), the eu delegation present in the country should coordinate all cooperation between member consulates. i voted in favour of this report, because this document intends to make this goal a reality.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. this year marks the 20th anniversary of the creation of the single market. indeed, progress has been made in many areas and eu consumers and businesses still face serious obstacles to taking full advantage of the opportunities offered by the single market. a well-functioning single market is a key prerequisite for the successful implementation of the europe 2020 strategy and a key eu instrument to promote the recovery and future growth of the member states' economies. many obstacles remain today because of the inadequate or untimely implementation of particularly important legislation in the member states. there is also a lack of political will, especially in the council, to agree on meaningful measures such as e-signature authentication, clear protection of intellectual property and copyright, consumer redress, and this is causing mistrust in the single market among eu citizens and businesses. i therefore expect the european commission to play a much more significant and responsible role in this area, particularly in monitoring the way in which member states transpose and implement the single market legislation and ensuring the smooth functioning of the single market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the economic and social well-being of eu citizens requires the creation of an internal market and a concrete plan of action and proposals to help address these citizens' concerns. i believe that the eu needs to do more in this period to remove the barriers to the functioning of the single market, particularly in sectors that can accelerate sustainable economic growth, such as cross-border business and entrepreneurship, the provision of services, access to finance and financial literacy. i would also urge the european commission to encourage smes to recruit young people and to strengthen youth mobility programmes so that young people can further develop their skills and have more opportunities to be employed and to be better integrated into the labour market. it is particularly important to develop a holistic approach to the single market, focusing on enabling citizens to benefit from the benefits of the single market and thus contribute to the territorial, economic and social cohesion of the european union.
in writing. − i voted for this document because the objective of the single market, which was completed in 1992, is to strengthen the links between citizens and member states, an area in which persons, goods, services and capital can move freely. the single market is a key factor in achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and its objective of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. in this respect, it is essential to promote and enhance the efficiency of this single market, which has more than 500 million consumers and over eur 11 000 000 million of economic activity, in order to enable europe to boost economic growth and employment and to build the confidence of its citizens. unfortunately, as we mark the 20th anniversary of the single market this year, we find that expectations about the single market still do not correspond to reality. specific european citizens and businesses are still facing obstacles to the exercise of their rights under the single market acquis.
in writing. − i have endorsed this communication, which seeks to amend the regulation on protection against dumped imports from countries not members of the european community, in the light of the judgment of the court of justice of the european union in the case of duties on certain footwear with leather uppers imported from the people's republic of china and vietnam.
in writing. − protection against dumped imports is an important means of protecting the eu's internal market and must therefore be as effective as possible and in line with the provisions of eu primary law. i agree that we should update the legislation governing this protection in the light of the observations made by the court of justice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the eu-japan negotiations on a free trade agreement. i am pleased that the european parliament adopted this resolution by a large majority, demonstrating the importance of developing eu-japan trade, the potential of which is still not fully exploited for the benefit of eu businesses, workers and consumers. the most obvious reason is the imposition by japan of non-tariff barriers which adversely affect the access of european businesses to the market. the successful implementation of the fta would create some 420 000 new jobs in the european union and increase eu exports to japan by 30%. this is particularly important in the light of the economic crisis, the high unemployment rate and the weak growth prospects for the eu economy. i agree with the rapporteur that in the formal negotiations for an eu-japan fta, japan needs to reaffirm the commitments it has made, in particular on the removal of non-tariff barriers to trade (ntbs). it is also important to ensure that if japan does not show sufficient willingness to take account of eu priority requirements such as the elimination of npas during the negotiations, the commission, after consulting the european parliament and the council, should suspend the negotiations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of opening negotiations on a free trade agreement with japan. it is vital that the eu strengthens its economic and trade links with this country, one of the most economically influential in the world. this cooperation is particularly important in the light of the current economic crisis in the eu, the high unemployment rate and the weak growth forecasts for the eu economy. the eu's bilateral trade with japan is significantly lower than that with other partners such as the us, china and russia. a free trade agreement would allow for trade, and the removal of tariffs and other barriers could increase eu exports to japan by about 70%. in order to exploit the significant potential of eu-japan trade relations, it is essential that the japanese government commits to removing non-tariff barriers to trade; i also support the proposals put forward for the introduction of concessions on public procurement to ensure access for eu companies to japan's strategic sectors. i agree that an effective dispute settlement mechanism should be established to combat the emergence of new non-tariff barriers to trade and barriers to entry in the procurement market in japan.
in writing. - i supported this proposal because the eu and japan together generate more than a third of global gdp and account for more than 20% of world trade. the importance of japan as a political ally with an eu-like approach to the new challenges of a globalised world should therefore be taken into account. it is essential that the eu fully enhances its economic and trade links with the world's economically most powerful countries, such as japan, in order to maximise the employment and growth opportunities offered by the europe 2020 strategy. this is particularly important in the context of the current economic crisis, the high unemployment rate and the weak growth prospects for the eu economy.
in writing. − i supported the european parliament resolution calling on the council to allow the commission to open negotiations on a free trade agreement with japan, based on the scope of cooperation and clear objectives. the existing bilateral trade potential needs to be exploited to the mutual benefit of the eu and japanese economies, which are currently experiencing a difficult year. preliminary estimates alone suggest that by reducing tariffs and non-tariff barriers as much as possible, eu exports to japan could increase by 71% and japanese exports to the eu by 61%. the future negotiations on a free trade agreement will of course have to take account of the problematic aspects outlined in the european parliament's resolution, including environmental protection.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. global demand for energy and water is projected to increase by about 40% and food by 50% by 2030. the continuing increase in population and the growth of the middle class, especially in developing countries, will significantly increase the use of natural resources. development policy at eu and global level must therefore be geared to the needs of developing countries. i agree that the eu's trade agreements with third countries must reflect adequately the provisions on social standards that will contribute to the sustainable development of these countries in the future.
in writing. − i voted for this report because i support the adaptation of the eu's trade and investment policy to the countries most in need, and the commitments to support small producers and promote fair, natural and ethical trade initiatives. it is also important to draw attention to the eu action plan on gender equality and the empowerment of women in development and to the promotion of monitoring and implementation of gender mainstreaming in eu-funded projects.
after long negotiations, russia finally became a member of the world trade organization. this should boost russia's gdp growth, accelerate the common modernisation programme with the european union, maintain and create jobs both in russia and in the eu countries, and implement higher environmental standards. the accession removed a major obstacle in the negotiations between the eu and russia for a new partnership and cooperation agreement. however, russia would have to implement its commitments consistently, further liberalise its trade regime and create a transparent and predictable environment for trade and foreign investment. membership of the wto does not allow for the deterioration of international trade conditions for political reasons or in the interests of lobby groups. it is important that the russian government, by reducing import tariffs, does not artificially introduce new, additional duties. eu-russia trade cooperation should also encourage closer integration of neighbouring belarus into world trade following russia's accession to the world trade organisation. the european union, together with russia, could help belarus to accelerate the adoption of wto standards that are compatible with trade regulations.
madam president, we welcome russia’s accession to the wto, but let us not forget that today is the ninth anniversary of mikhail khodorkovsky’s arrest. the yukos case, in which khodorkovsky’s oil company was essentially confiscated by the russian government, continues to cast a shadow over russia’s efforts to reassure its new partners in the wto. the yukos case is one of many examples of russia’s political use of justice, and that is why russia still needs to show that it can be trusted as a commercial partner. since khodorkovsky’s arrest in 2003, there have been many other signs of russia’s selective approach to the rule of law, especially in the commercial field. russia is also prone to using its gas resources as a diplomatic weapon, and a current eu price-fixing inquiry aimed at gazprom suggests that the kremlin will continue to put its own interests above its international obligations. so, russia is an important commercial partner for the eu, but it remains potentially unreliable.
we have not received any changes or innovations from belarus, a neighbour of the european union, for almost 20 years. the pyramid of power there is monumentally stable. the elections were again held without a choice, and were considered by the osce and other international organisations to be undemocratic and unfair. however, i fully agree with commissioner fühle that in this situation too, we must continue the critical dialogue with minsk and not isolate the belarusian people. the electronic archives show that over 18 years, as many as 116 european parliament resolutions covering belarus were adopted, mostly in response to specific events in the country. i think it is time for a broader report, which at parliamentary level would try to propose ways of breaking the deadlock in eu-belarus relations and modernising belarus.
for the efd group i am glad that i had the opportunity to observe the elections in georgia. i would like to thank you for the opportunity and also to emphasise that georgia has passed the democratic test by electing a new parliament. georgia has shown a very high level of confidence in europe and has shown that it has learned its lessons well. i would like to thank in particular the office for democratic institutions and human rights of the organisation for security and cooperation in europe for the great work it has done. i think that this election was peaceful, it was well organized. i hope that the new government will continue to cooperate with the european union and nato, and i hope that the european union's relations with georgia will remain strong in the future. a good example for emerging democracies: in georgia, both sides - the position and the opposition - wanted the elections to be transparent, and this has produced good results, but unfortunately this is not always the case.
author. − mr president, today we are discussing the case of malala yousafzai, a 14-year-old girl from the swat valley in pakistan who, on 9 october, on her way to school, was shot in the head and neck and severely wounded. of course we, the european parliament, stand firmly behind malala and her family. that is clearly expressed in our resolution. tehrik-i-taliban have claimed responsibility for the attack. furthermore, they have issued a statement to the effect that they would attempt to kill malala yousafzai again if she recovers from her injuries. women and girls continue to become victims of domestic violence, trafficking and forced marriages and are being traded in the settlement of disputes. the perpetrators of violence against women and girls in pakistan remain unprosecuted. my belief is that, wherever children become a target of military attacks and this is tolerated by the leadership of the country, that regime and that nation do not have a future. children should go to school. children should be better educated than their parents, and if their fathers, uncles or older brothers prevent children from enjoying even their very basic rights, such as the right to education, it is lamentable.
i voted for this resolution. parliamentary elections in georgia have shown that georgia has passed the democratic test. the elections were indeed well organised, transparent, and did not focus on minor irregularities. president saakashvili has shown that he is a politician who values democracy and the will of the people. it was very important at a time of great stress. the former opposition will have to learn to respect the opponent, i am talking about when the opposition leader b. ivanishvili after the elections immediately offered the resignation of the president of georgia. the most important thing is that the european union continues to pay close attention to georgia and that its new government maintains the reform momentum. the eu-georgia relationship could now be the time for the 'for more' principle. i was part of the close monitoring of this election and i saw the heated atmosphere. certain threats from the opposition to people who were going to vote for someone other than their political force did indeed raise a certain amount of mistrust. i hope that these cases are solved and that the european union should also take note of this.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this agreement, which will promote energy efficiency in stationery. energy star is a program developed by the u.s. environmental protection agency to improve the energy efficiency of stationary equipment. in 2000, the eu and the us signed an agreement on the harmonisation of energy labelling programmes for stationery. the agreement, which was renewed for a second five-year period in 2006, provides for the creation of the energy star programme in the european union, which will allow for closer eu-us cooperation in the development of product specifications. therefore, this agreement seeks to extend the energy star program for an additional period of five years. i believe that in the next five years, negotiations with the united states should be held to ensure that the principle of mutual recognition of the energy performance of products is applied in the future.
in writing. − i voted for this report because in 2000 the eu and the us signed an agreement on the harmonisation of energy labelling programmes for stationery. this agreement, which was aimed at improving the energy efficiency of stationery, was renewed in 2006 and expired in 2011. the council authorised the commission to negotiate a new agreement to extend the energy star programme for a third additional five-year period. these negotiations were concluded in november 2011 and were recognised by both parties as effective and successful in promoting energy efficiency. in view of this, the conclusion of the agreement is expected to be in favourable circumstances.
in writing. − in order to use resources (in this case energy) efficiently and effectively, it is important that consumers are properly informed about the energy performance of the installations concerned. the energy star labelling used in the usa is sufficiently well known in the european union and it is therefore appropriate to continue to use it. i support the position that an agreement should be reached on the further recognition of this marking.
in writing. − i have endorsed this report, which aims to assess the innovative financial instruments and their use in the financial perspective for 2014-2020. although the eu institutions have developed a number of innovative financial instruments since the early 2000s, combining funding from the union budget with public and/or private funding to increase investment in the union's strategic objectives, public investment in the eu has been steadily declining over the last decade, a trend that was further intensified by the onset of the 2008 financial crisis. the eu will need a huge investment in this decade to achieve the europe 2020 goals, and the potential of these innovative financial instruments must be properly exploited to attract private sector funds. i agree that the wider use of innovative financial instruments should not lead to a reduction in the eu budget, but should help to optimise its use.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that practical experience and technical capacity in the use and management of financial instruments should be strengthened at the level of the managing authorities, financial intermediaries and banks. i agree with the view that the objective of innovative financial instruments is that in the event of market failures or investment shortfalls, they should act as a catalyst. it is important to note that in the field of the union's internal policies, innovative financial instruments are implemented at european level (they are managed by the commission itself or by an institution delegated by it) or at national level in the context of regional and cohesion policy (shared management with the member states). i think it is very important to note that implementing innovative financial instruments requires time, a high level of investment skills, well-designed projects and a thorough knowledge of market mechanisms. these financial instruments can only improve governance if there is an adequate balance between the financial and human resources of the parties.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the provisions of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provide for the possibility for eu citizens to refer to the european ombudsman when eu institutions or bodies fail to comply with rules or principles binding on them and infringe the principles of good administration. in 2011, the european ombudsman assisted more than 22 000 citizens. there is also a tendency for the number of complaints received to decrease each year. i believe that the effective functioning of the ombudsman and the ability of eu citizens to defend their legitimate claims is one of the main ways of promoting citizens' trust in the european civil service and the eu institutions. i agree that despite the progress made, it is necessary to increase the awareness of eu citizens about the possibilities of defending their rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because in 2011 the european ombudsman assisted more than 22 000 citizens, of whom 2 510 lodged complaints, 1284 requested information and 18 274 received advice using the interactive guide of the european ombudsman's website. i think the ombudsman's work is commendable and successful, considering that the european network of ombudsmen comprises more than 90 offices in 32 european countries and that more and more citizens of the european union are starting to use this service. i believe that cooperation should continue to be encouraged, which is geared to the principles of improving the way the eu operates and which seeks to strengthen the european citizens' initiative, allowing people to participate directly in the process of drafting, promoting and enforcing legislation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the annual report on the activities of the european ombudsman for 2011. as i support the work of the european ombudsman, a brief outline of the core values that eu civil servants should reflect in their behaviour can be an effective way of promoting citizens' trust in the european civil service and the eu institutions it supports. i also agree with the european ombudsman that an institution with a good service culture does not see complaints as a threat but as an opportunity to communicate better and, if a mistake is made, to correct the situation and not to make the same mistakes in the future.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this directive, which aims to make financial markets more efficient, resilient and transparent and to better protect investors. the markets in financial instruments directive, which has been in force since november 2007, regulates how banks and investment firms are to provide investment services in financial instruments (brokerage, advisory, transaction, portfolio management, guarantee, etc.) and how traditional exchanges and alternative trading venues (so-called multilateral trading facilities) are to operate. although the implementation of the rdp has encouraged competition for these services and has provided investors with greater choice and lower prices, the financial crisis has revealed certain shortcomings. at the 2009 pittsburgh summit, the g20 agreed on the need to increase transparency and oversight of less regulated markets, including derivatives markets, and to address excessive price volatility in commodity derivatives markets. i agree with the need to create stronger and more efficient market structures, to increase the powers and control of these markets and to ensure better protection of investors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the position set out below, taking into account the recommendations of the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, does not contain the amendments and other substantive changes referred to and because, as regards the unchanged provisions of the earlier acts and the necessary codification of those amendments, the proposal seeks only to codify the existing texts without substantially altering them.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal as the financial crisis has revealed shortcomings in the functioning and transparency of financial markets. the development of financial markets has revealed the need to strengthen the regulatory framework for markets in financial instruments, including trading on over-the-counter markets, by increasing its transparency, by better protecting investors, by enhancing confidence, by taking the unregulated areas into account, by ensuring that supervisory authorities have sufficient powers to carry out their tasks.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the amendment of the regulation on markets in financial instruments and on european market infrastructures. the financial crisis in the eu has exposed the lack of transparency in financial markets. in order to enhance transparency and the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, it is necessary to establish uniform transparency requirements for transactions in markets in financial instruments. detailed rules should also be laid down for the different financial instruments. both proposed documents should provide a legal framework governing the requirements applicable to investment firms, regulated markets and non-eu firms providing investment services or performing investment activities in the union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as enhancing transparency is one of the general principles that must be implemented in order to strengthen the financial system, as confirmed in the declaration adopted at the g20 meeting in london on 2 april 2009. in order to enhance transparency and the functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, a new framework is necessary to establish uniform transparency requirements for transactions in markets in financial instruments. this framework should lay down detailed rules applicable to the various financial instruments. the adoption of a regulation ensuring the direct application of the requirements is the most appropriate means of achieving those regulatory objectives and of ensuring a level playing field, thus avoiding the divergent national requirements which may arise from the transposition of a directive. this system should complement the requirements for share-based orders and transactions laid down in directive 2004/39/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 21 april 2004 on markets in financial instruments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this change because i agree that the recent financial crisis has exposed the lack of transparency in financial markets, which can contribute to negative social and economic impacts. i therefore consider that, in order to achieve greater transparency and a better functioning of the internal market in financial instruments, a new framework is necessary to establish uniform transparency requirements for transactions in financial instruments markets.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. the european semester is a six-month period each year during which member states' budgetary and structural policies are reviewed to identify discrepancies and imbalances. during this period, the commission provides governments with policy guidance and recommendations before finalising national budgets. this helps member states to better coordinate their economic policies, taking advantage of the eu's common economic agenda while adapting policies to their national circumstances. i support the proposals put forward to democratize the european semester by involving national parliaments, the social partners and civil society more closely in the process. i welcome the proposed measures to ensure sustainable public finances, reduce macroeconomic imbalances and enhance competitiveness, which will lead to faster growth and more employment. i support calls on the commission to prepare an annual growth review for 2013, based on sound economic data and reflecting the real macroeconomic situation in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the economic, social, financial and sovereign debt crisis is not yet over. the current economic situation has shown the need for better coordination of member states' macroeconomic and budgetary policies with a view to achieving a more integrated and better balanced economic union. i support the proposal that the commission should, on the basis of the european semester for the coordination of economic policies (codified in regulation (ec) no 1466/97), present a framework regulation setting out the tasks (and deadlines) for the member states and the eu institutions in the various stages of the european semester. the european council is committed to bringing together all the levers, instruments and policies to promote smart, sustainable, resource-efficient and job-creating growth by adopting a comprehensive agreement on growth and jobs.
in writing. improving economic governance must be a priority for the european union, which is why i supported this report. the economic dialogue between the member states and the eu institutions needs to be strengthened. in this context, wage increases must be commensurate with productivity. in addition, funds must be reallocated to research and innovation with a view to a europe at the forefront of these fields. finally, it is necessary to ensure the coherence of european economic policy in order to generate sustainable growth for future generations.
in writing. − it is regrettable that even in the face of the crisis, member states have not paid sufficient attention to an economic policy element such as promoting efficient and effective use of resources. unfortunately, once again, a lot of money is lost through inefficient use of available resources. i therefore urge the commission and the member states to pay greater attention to this element in the coordination and monitoring of economic policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-russia trade relations following russia’s accession to the wto even though russia remains a potentially unreliable partner for the eu. the european parliament today welcomed russia’s accession to the world trade organisation, but also underlined that, in order to benefit from this strong potential, it is of the utmost importance that russia fully lives up to the obligations and rules of the wto. as we see already now, russia has not been duly fulfilling all its duties as a member of the organisation since it joined the wto in august this year. even though the accession of russia to the wto is an important step, a comprehensive and binding partnership and cooperation agreement should be the objective for both the eu and russia. the agreement must be based on common values of democracy, human rights and rule of law. in this regard, it is appropriate that on the ninth anniversary of mikhail khodorkovsky’s arrest we raise concerns about russia’s trustworthiness as a trading partner. one way for the kremlin to restore investor confidence in russia would be to commission an independent and impartial inquiry into the yukos case and the subsequent politically-motivated prosecution of mikhail khodorkovsky.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. russia is the eu's third largest trading partner. in 2011, exports to russia accounted for 7% of total eu exports, while imports accounted for 12% of total eu exports. russia's accession to the world trade organisation will facilitate trade between the eu and russia and boost economic growth and job creation in both countries. i believe that the signing of the new partnership and cooperation agreement would be an important next step in contributing to stronger economic ties between the two countries. i support the proposals set out above for the russian federation to fully comply with its wto obligations, to lift unjustified trade bans, temporary tariff increases, protectionist measures and barriers to open and fair trade. i agree that in the eu's negotiations with the russian federation, particular attention should be paid to the openness and transparency of the eu-russia energy market, the reform of the country's customs procedures in the light of international conventions and the abolition of russian double pricing for goods and clarification of the conditions for the establishment of service companies. the commission should ensure that fair rules and procedures for the award of public contracts apply to both parties.
in writing. - i supported the european parliament resolution expressing concern that russia is not complying with its wto commitments as soon as it joins. russia and the eu are important trading partners for each other and, after 18 years of negotiations, the eu welcomed russia's accession to the wto as a new stimulus to strengthen and expand the country's economy. unfortunately, there are examples of unrealistic expectations. one of those exporters of used cars who had a reasonable expectation of higher trade volumes at lower prices, but whose car exports were made even more difficult by russia's introduction of a so-called recycling tax from 1 september than before wto membership energy resources account for the majority of russian exports to the eu, while the eu exports a wide range of products to russia. the european commission has identified 300 products subject to import duties that do not comply with wto obligations. the experience with, for example, the energy charter treaty shows that russia does not avoid selective compliance. in addition, russia has lost a major case involving yukos due to its failure to comply with its obligations in international arbitration. i believe that the european parliament's signal to russia is necessary and timely.
in writing. - after 19 years of negotiations, russia joined the world trade organisation in august. the european union is a strategic trading partner of russia, leading in import and export indicators. russia, meanwhile, has become the eu's second largest importer of goods and the fourth largest exporter of goods to the eu. i voted in favour of this resolution, which applauds russia's membership of the wto. in the medium to long term, this will further boost trade flows between the eu and russia, stimulating economic growth and job creation in both the eu and russia. i also agree with the important provision in the resolution that the implementation of a 'joint action to achieve visa-free travel' is one of the key conditions for more favourable eu-russia trade and investment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on elections in belarus. i deeply regret that that the conduct of parliamentary elections in belarus once again failed to meet many of the basic standards set by the osce, resulting – notwithstanding some minor improvements in the elections’ legal framework – in unfair, non-free, non-transparent and unbalanced consultations, so-called ‘elections’. therefore, the parliament elected in belarus cannot be considered as having a democratic legitimacy. i fully support the position to continue its policy of not recognising the so-called belarusian parliament. it is important to stress that parliamentary elections in belarus were conducted in an atmosphere of persecution of journalists, constant pressure on media and civil society. we condemn the detention of journalists, a tactic obviously aimed at controlling the free flow of information by not allowing journalists to exercise their regular duties, thus violating such basic freedoms as freedom of speech and freedom of thought. belarusian authorities and citizens should know that the european union is ready to renew its relationship with belarus and its people as soon as the belarusian leadership proves its respect for democratic values and basic rights of the belarusian people.
in writing. - it is regrettable that the situation in belarus is not changing. in its resolution, the european parliament notes that the parliamentary elections in belarus have once again failed to meet many of the osce's basic standards and have therefore been unfair, unfree and unclear. since the new parliament of belarus does not rely on democratic legitimacy, the european parliament will continue its policy of non-recognition towards it. at the same time, it is necessary to further strengthen civil society in belarus, including by continuing and strengthening funding for the european humanities university (ehu) in vilnius. this year, the belarusian university celebrates its 20th anniversary, seven of which have been hosted and successfully run in lithuania in order to avoid the persecution of the lukashenka regime. the ehu is one of the most efficient and successful eu-funded projects and, in the absence of any possibility of relocating ehu activities back to minsk, the eu should continue to provide funding for the activities of the university in the new financial perspective.
in writing. − observers from the osce and other international organisations have not recognised any elections held in belarus since 1995 as meeting international standards. the country continues to violate human rights, civil liberties and persecute political opponents. no opposition representative was elected in the september parliamentary elections. the new parliament will be composed of five members from political parties representing the regime only. the opposition forces were unable to unite and develop a common electoral strategy. independent observers reported a high number of infringements. i voted in favour of this resolution because it expresses concern at the continuing deterioration of the situation of fundamental human rights and freedoms in belarus. the european parliament has also called for the immediate release of all political prisoners and for the abolition of the death penalty. we call on eu countries to continue to support the civil society of belarus in its efforts to create a movement for political, economic and social change in their country.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on elections in georgia. i congratulate the georgian people on the significant step they have taken towards the consolidation of democracy in their country. moreover, i welcome the fact that the elections were free and fair and in line with internationally-recognised standards. georgians freely expressed their will during those elections and we have to admit that it shows a very important step towards democratic development of our neighbours. what is important now is the cooperation between political forces. it will require an extra effort from both sides. i hope that the new government and the opposition will concentrate on the further democratic development of their country. in this regard it is important to stress once again that the eu fully supports georgia’s territorial integrity and sovereignty. russia must withdraw its troops from the occupied georgian territories of south ossetia and abkhazia and this is what we, members of the european parliament, declare in our resolution.
in writing. − georgia has demonstrated once again that it is on the path to democracy by holding parliamentary elections in line with international standards. these elections, which were marred by irregularities, were characterised by intense party competition and active voter participation. the ruling party dominated the media, but the central election commission operated effectively. a large number of observers and an active civil society contributed to the transparent electoral process. i voted in favour of this resolution, which welcomes the action of president saakashvili, who led the party which lost the elections to join the opposition. the president's and the leader of the opposition coalition of political forces 'georgian dream', which won the elections, b. ivanishvili's desire to work together for the good of the country is particularly welcome.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution which signifies a breakthrough in an almost two-year negotiation on a new set of rules governing the jurisdiction of courts in civil and commercial matters. i support the rapporteur in believing that the new regulation will provide conditions for judgments to flow freely within the eu. the procedure will be quicker and simpler for the citizens, thus saving consumers and businesses more than eur 47 million per year. this report falls perfectly in line with the concept of the single market where free movement of goods and resources is already functioning. now it will be ensured that european citizens will have an easy and fast way of exercising their rights as the regulation introduces a number of changes designed to increase legal certainty and facilitate access to justice.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to recast the council regulation of 22 december 2001 on judicial cooperation in civil matters. although the regulation is working successfully, its application still presents certain difficulties (barriers to the free movement of judgments, complexity of international litigation, etc.) which need to be addressed. i support the proposals outlined above, such as the abolition of the procedure for recognition and enforcement of judgments (exequatur) in another member state, which impedes the free movement of judgments and is time-consuming and costly. the current regulation only applies to cases where the defendant is domiciled in the eu, in line with the proposal to extend the possibility for companies and citizens to sue defendants from third countries in the eu. i also support the provision that the courts of the member states are required to stay proceedings if another court has been seised of the case before it, in order to have it set aside, since it allows the parties to the dispute to refer the case first to a court which has no jurisdiction to hear the dispute and thus to delay the settlement of the dispute. i also agree with the other suggestions made in the report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to update the provisions of the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters. this regulation is widely recognised as one of the most successful pieces of eu legislation. this regulation aims to ensure that judgments are enforceable not only in the state of origin but also throughout the eu on presentation of an official, authentic copy thereof and a certificate in the prescribed form. this updated version the commission also proposes that the rules of the regulation on jurisdiction be made binding on third-country defendants, thus replacing the existing basis for determining the jurisdiction of the member states in such cases. it is important to note that the commission also proposes to lay down specific rules to avoid parallel proceedings and abuse of litigation tactics. arbitration should continue to be excluded from the scope of the regulation. the new wording of the regulation addresses some of the difficulties encountered in this area over the last decade and is a positive change.
in writing. - i voted for this document. regulation no 44/2001, the predecessor of the brussels convention, is one of the most successful pieces of eu legislation. it has laid the foundations for the european judicial area, has served citizens and businesses well by promoting legal certainty and predictability of decisions, and has been used as a tool for the development of other legislation. the new version of this regulation is therefore of great importance. the proposal does not introduce any substantive changes other than those explicitly identified as such in this proposal and, as regards the codification of the unchanged provisions of previous legislation and those amendments, the proposal seeks only to codify the existing legislation without changing its substance and with a view to ensuring more effective and faster recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters.
in writing. − the european union's integration has led it to gradually develop from an economic union of states to a political union with fiscal features. however, the creation of a single legal area is a long process, due to the differences in legal traditions. the adoption by the european parliament today of the regulation on the establishment of jurisdiction and the unification of the rules of judicial review in civil and commercial matters is therefore an important step towards ensuring that eu citizens, residents and businesses save both time and money in the preparation of procedural documents and the enforcement of judicial decisions.
in writing. − i believe that the abolition of the exequatur procedure for all judgments in civil and commercial matters is a very important step towards ensuring that citizens and businesses have the right to have recourse to the courts. in addition, the removal of the bureaucratic exchequer procedure will remove certain existing barriers to international transactions. it is important to note that the proper implementation of the provisions of this regulation will strengthen the single market and reduce the bureaucratic obstacles that cause additional costs and legal uncertainty for businesses.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to restrict the access of the general public to chemicals that can be used to make improvised explosive devices, thereby reducing the risk of attacks and increasing the safety of eu citizens. the eu has different legal and illegal measures for trade in such substances, so that access to them in one country may be controlled, but the same substances may be available in another. it is necessary to ensure uniform control of the acquisition of these substances across the eu and to reduce the possibility for terrorists to take advantage of the different security rules in different eu member states. moreover, the same rules across the eu would benefit both producers and retailers. i support the proposals that are being made to allow the purchase of substances in excess of the concentration limits to be restricted to consumers who obtain a licence to purchase the substance. i support the proposal to notify the single national contact centre of transactions relating to the sale of these substances which would be considered 'suspicious' for any reason.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the proposal aims to reduce the number of terrorist attacks and the possibility of legally acquiring substances (or mixtures thereof) which, in high concentrations, can be used to make explosives. it is important to note that the stricter rules on the acquisition of the relevant substances adopted by this regulation will not affect professionals or undertakings who supply these substances for legitimate purposes. it is also emphasised that the human right to privacy will be preserved by allowing the sale of high-concentration substances to the general public only under a lawful end-use licence. in short, the free movement of goods and the protection of human rights will continue to be ensured, while reducing the availability of high-concentration explosives to the general public.
in writing. - i voted for this motion. the proposal concerns a regulation aimed at restricting the access of members of the public to certain general-purpose materials which can also be used as precursors to explosives. this is intended to reduce the frequency and impact of terrorist attacks by restricting the access of the general public to widely and lawfully used substances (or mixtures thereof) which, as high-concentration substances, can also be used for the manufacture of explosives and to report suspicious transactions related thereto. the proposal is addressed to wholesalers, retailers and member states, as chemical manufacturers already have control measures and voluntary reporting codes for weapons and precursors of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in place and should not be particularly affected by these proposals. however, the very success of the proposal will depend on the actions of the competent authorities in collecting and sharing the relevant information.
in writing. − to protect against terrorist attacks, reduce their frequency and prevent fragmentation of the internal market, a sufficiently flexible regulatory mechanism must be established to respond to developments in an operational manner. it is noteworthy that terrorists are more likely to use improvised explosive devices, usually made from improvised explosive devices, the precursors of which are freely available in retail stores or online. in this context, i support the proposal to establish effective and proportionate control measures to ensure the safety of citizens. in particular, restrictions should be imposed on the acquisition of widely and lawfully used substances which can also be used as high-concentration substances in the manufacture of explosives. in addition, producers and retailers must take greater responsibility for the goods they trade and ensure that suspicious transactions involving these substances are promptly reported to the relevant authorities.

in writing. - i voted for this document. this document is intended for the accession of croatia to the european union in 2013. it contains a provision derogating from the general rules on the recruitment of staff of the european union. this was done in 2004 and 2007 with the accession of 12 new countries, one of which was lithuania, and it is now proposed to do the same for croatian citizens. the proposed regulation allows reserving certain recruitment competitions for croatian nationals until 2018. firstly, these calls will be mainly aimed at croatian language specialists (translators and interpreters, editors, proofreaders and press officers), as well as administrators and assistants in general areas.
