in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a protocol on the eu's accession to the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution caused by exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf and the seabed and subsoil (maritime protocol). the maritime protocol covers exploration and exploitation activities in the mediterranean, permits, requirements, dismantling of outdated installations, use of harmful substances, safety provisions, etc. in order to ensure the safety of operations in the mediterranean and to prevent accidents related to oil spills at sea, it is necessary to strengthen the policy for the sustainable management of oil and gas activities. the consequences of such accidents are not limited to one or two regions, and i therefore support the proposals set out for the european union to promote cooperation at international level in support of maritime safety and response capacities in all countries that have signed the protocol.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as on 27 october 2011 the commission published a proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of a protocol on the accession of the european union to the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution caused by exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf and the seabed and subsoil (maritime protocol). the need to enhance the safety of offshore oil and gas exploration has been particularly heightened by recent accidents, such as the 2010 deepwater horizon oil spill in the gulf of mexico. the planned eu response to the situation includes the commission proposal for a regulation on safety in offshore oil and gas exploration, exploitation and production currently under consideration.
in writing. − i have agreed to this proposal because on 27 october 2011 the commission published a proposal for a council decision on the approval of a protocol on the accession of the european union to the convention for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution from exploration and development (maritime protocol). the protocol for the sea, approved on 14 october 1994, is one of the protocols to the convention for the protection of the mediterranean environment and coastal zone (barcelona convention), signed on 16 february 1976 and amended on 10 june 1995. the eu and all eu mediterranean member states are contracting parties to the barcelona convention, along with 14 other mediterranean countries. the maritime protocol covers a wide range of exploration and exploitation activities in the mediterranean, permit requirements, dismantling of abandoned and unused installations, use and disposal of harmful substances, liability and compensation requirements, coordination of activities at regional level with other parties to the barcelona convention, and provisions on safety and contingency planning and monitoring. the protocol entered into force on 24 march 2011 after it had been ratified by the six contracting parties (albania, tunisia, morocco, libya, cyprus and syria), but the union has not yet signed or ratified it. in accordance with article 218 (6) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the union's accession to the protocol is subject to the consent of the european parliament.
in writing. − i support the proposal to call on the eu to join the protocol for the protection of the mediterranean sea against pollution resulting from exploration and exploitation of the continental shelf and the seabed and subsoil. we must make every effort to increase the safety of offshore oil and gas exploration. in view of the nature of this activity in the mediterranean and its potential negative consequences for the economy, the ecosystem and the environment, it is necessary to establish a sustainable management policy for this activity. moreover, international cooperation should be strengthened and the necessary safety and environmental standards established. only by acting together and by implementing the commitments made will the protection of the eu's marine environment in the event of major accidents be ensured.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a bilateral fisheries agreement with denmark and greenland. this agreement will cover the purchase of fishing rights for eu vessels and the promotion of a responsible and sustainable fisheries policy. the agreement will ensure that local stocks are not depleted or that greenlandic fishing communities, which will be supported by targeted support programmes, in particular through the creation of new jobs, are not harmed by eu financial compensation. this agreement is in line with the objectives of the eu common fisheries policy and will benefit both the eu and greenland. i agree with the proposals made to give the european parliament greater scrutiny of the implementation of the multiannual support programme for the fisheries sector. the commission should carry out a thorough assessment of the impact of the support measures for the sector on the local economy and coastal communities at the end of the new protocol.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as it gives parliament its consent to the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european community and the government of denmark and the home rule government of greenland. the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon has given parliament greater powers with regard to fisheries partnership agreements: under article 218 (6) (a) tfeu, parliament must now give its consent to the conclusion of any such agreement. the first fisheries partnership agreement with greenland was concluded in 1985, after greenland's withdrawal from the ec, to allow the community to retain its traditional fishing rights in exchange for an annual financial compensation. under the new protocol, the joint committee will decide on fishing opportunities for the following year, taking into account scientific advice, the precautionary principle, the needs of the fishing industry and, in particular, the minimum quantities to be caught in order to maintain fishing activities in greenland. the contribution from shipowners will be fixed at fixed prices per resource and will replace the previous licensing system. i believe that the positive impact of the sector support measures on the local economy and coastal communities, in particular on job creation in them, will be felt over time and should therefore be assessed in depth by the commission at the end of the new protocol. parliament should also be able to monitor more closely the whole process of implementation of the multiannual support programme for the sector.
in writing. - i voted for this deal. the first fisheries partnership agreement with greenland was concluded in 1985, after greenland's withdrawal from the ec, on the basis that the community could retain its traditional fishing rights in exchange for an annual financial compensation. fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the former home rule government of greenland, signed on 28 june 2007, with the current protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contributions for each year until 31 december 2012. as the current protocol expires on 31 december 2012, i have advocated the renewal of this agreement, as it will address fishing opportunities for subsequent years, taking into account scientific advice, the precautionary principle, the needs of the fishing industry and in particular the minimum quantities to be caught to maintain fishing activities in greenland.
in writing. − the new protocol will further strengthen the partnership between the two countries in the fisheries sector and ensure the implementation of a responsible and sustainable fisheries policy. it will also allow the eu fleet to continue and develop fishing activities in remote fishing areas outside eu waters and to better protect the interests of the european fisheries sector and consumers. attention should be drawn to the importance of ensuring that the fishing opportunities used are based on sound and reliable scientific data and knowledge. it would also create the conditions for a more rational use of fisheries resources from an economic, social and environmental perspective. in this context, it is necessary to monitor on a regular basis the proper use of the compensation paid by the eu and the promotion of sustainable exploitation of greenland's fisheries resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the right of eu citizens resident in a member state but not holding the nationality of that state to stand as candidates in elections to the european parliament. under eu law, any eu citizen residing in a member state of which he is not a national has the right to vote or stand as a candidate in european elections, subject to the same conditions as nationals of the member state concerned. it is necessary to ensure that citizens are not allowed to vote more than once in the european elections or to stand as candidates in two countries in the same election. i support the amendment of directive 93/109 which lays down measures to prohibit this practice. the proposal aims to change the obligation to exchange information between member states on citizens who have been entered on the electoral roll or who have been candidates by simplified means, introducing the necessary safeguards and deterrents. i support the proposal to require candidates to make a formal declaration that they are not denied the right to stand as a candidate.

in writing. - i voted for this document. on 12 september 2012, the council approved the text it would like to adopt as a directive amending directive 93/109/ec laying down detailed measures concerning the eligibility of union citizens who are resident in a member state but who are not nationals of that state to stand as candidates in elections to the european parliament. initially, parliament wanted to allow candidates to stand in more than one constituency in the same election. however, due to disagreements within the council on this issue and on the regulation of the right to vote in the member state of residence, no action was taken before the 2009 elections. this time, the council has refused to address the burdensome issue of voter rights and has focused only on reducing the burden on certain national authorities of checking whether a person has been banned from standing as a candidate in elections in their member state. while the new draft document does not meet the more ambitious objectives of the parliament, it does make some minor improvements in terms of administrative convenience for future candidates and the countries concerned.
in writing. - democracy without elections is unthinkable. the eu has a long history of supporting the right to vote and to stand for election, and the eu has a long history of supporting the right to vote and to stand for election. in particular, elections must be democratic and the right to vote and to stand as a candidate in elections must be adequately guaranteed, in particular as regards the right of eu citizens residing in the member state of which they are not nationals to stand as candidates in elections to the european parliament. it is welcome that the provisions of this directive will reduce the burden on national authorities and create more favourable administrative conditions for future candidates and the states concerned. however, we must make greater efforts to reach a compromise agreement on the reform of the mechanism to avoid double voting.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on strengthening the internal market for crossborder consumer credit and a high level of consumer protection. in order to develop the market for cross-border consumer credit, it is necessary to improve consumer information on the possibility of obtaining consumer credit in another member state and on their rights when concluding such a contract. i support calls for supervisors to require financial institutions to provide consumers with tailored, easily understandable explanations of the risks associated with borrowing foreign currency. it is necessary to monitor the advertising activities of financial institutions in order to avoid the dissemination of misleading information. i agree that the provisions on the calculation of the annual rate of the total cost of credit should be applied in the same way in all eu legal instruments. i agree that the commission should present an evaluation report on the implementation of this directive and its impact on consumer protection.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because this consumer credit directive has two objectives: a high level of consumer protection and the strengthening of the internal market for crossborder consumer credit. the current situation in europe with regard to core credit entitlements remains almost unchanged, as the use of consumer credit on the international market has actually decreased in recent years. the financial market crisis is thought to have played a role. it is also important to note that the language barrier or the lack of personal contact with financial institutions is more of a barrier to taking out consumer credit on the international market than a legal loophole. moreover, these procedures are most concerned with the legislators and financial institutions individually in the member states, and therefore, although the commission has also provided guidelines explaining the annual common credit rate, these guidelines do not have such binding legal effect.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the document has two objectives: to ensure a high level of consumer protection and to strengthen the internal market in crossborder consumer credit. the opening up of national markets in the important sector of the consumer credit economy, the strengthening of competition, the elimination of different levels of consumer protection and of possible distortions of competition between market participants and the improvement of the internal market are mandatory eu policy objectives and these actions are in the interests of consumers and creditors. improving the market for cross-border consumer credit would create european added value by promoting the internal market. this could therefore be achieved in order to better inform consumers about the possibility of obtaining consumer credit in another member state and about their rights when concluding such a contract.
in writing. - i voted for this document. inadequate pre-contractual information, advertising and mismanagement of contracts are of considerable concern to the member states. the provision of consumer credit to low-income persons in vulnerable groups further exacerbates the social exclusion of citizens or households. the commission also found that the information provided by the banks was not sufficient to ensure that the banks could effectively compete with other banks in the market. for this reason, the dissemination of information on consumer credit should be streamlined, highlighting possible tax changes or the consequences of impending insolvency. while quick credit for small amounts does not fall within the scope of this directive, i support the call for an enhanced level of consumer protection and for consumers of such credit. the irresponsible, mutual approach, the poor financial education of consumers can cause considerable problems for households that have borrowed even very small amounts of money.
in writing. −there is a need to extend the level of consumer protection at both eu and national level. effective consumer protection practices in the field of credit are one of the key conditions for financial stability. i think that special attention should be paid to short-term loans granted by means of various means of communication. in particular, excessive risks must be prevented. it is essential that the consumer is properly informed. he shall be given detailed and easily understandable information on the risks associated with the borrowing. furthermore, legal measures must be taken to ensure that he is not subject to any additional charges after exercising his right of withdrawal. it should be noted that all the objectives of the directive cannot be achieved if it is not properly transposed or implemented in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the social investment pact, which sets the objectives of social investment. targeted social investment would help individuals, families and society to adapt to changing economic conditions and labour market needs. i agree that the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework should provide for adequate budgetary resources to support social investment in the eu. i support calls on the commission to produce a compilation of the social investment indicators of the eu member states to assess the progress made by countries. i agree that social investment should also be supported by the structural funds. investments are needed in education, health and social protection, the labour market and so on.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the document because the current economic and financial crisis will undoubtedly have a strong long-term impact not only on the european economy, but also on employment indicators, public savings, social investment in europe. many of the recent and current crisis management measures are based on short-term objectives, mainly to restore the sustainability of public finances, which are vital to the eu economy. on the other hand, in these circumstances, we should not ignore the potential negative impact of these austerity measures on employment and competitiveness in europe and should therefore complement them with measures that are favourable to growth and employment, such as targeted social investment. europe faces very serious problems of unemployment, youth unemployment and increasingly difficult transitions from school to the labour market, which threaten to exclude young people from the labour market and, in the long term, to lose human capital. another issue that needs to be addressed urgently is the situation of low-skilled workers, who face a steadily declining demand for labour, and an increasing number of people living in poverty and at risk of social exclusion, due to sectoral changes, the shift to higher technology and high-skill activities. addressing the above challenges through targeted social investment to help individuals, families and society adapt to changing economic conditions and labour market needs is essential to restore sustainable growth. this is an important part of european economic and employment policy and the eu's response to the crisis.
in writing. − i believe that each member state should feel free to sign up to the social investment pact, as young people were the most affected by the economic crisis. in particular, young people must have free access to the labour market and decent working and living conditions. it is essential that the new multiannual financial framework allocates sufficient funds to promote and support social investment in europe. particular attention should be paid to the use of structural funds. in addition, it is necessary to facilitate access to finance for young people and to develop business support programmes for young people in cooperation with the business community.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that agricultural products, and in particular traditional european food products, need to be promoted more not only within the eu but also outside it. i agree with the rapporteur that attention should be paid to traditional european food products which are authentic, varied and delicious to the consumer. the european union must strive to export a sustainable agricultural model and its products. as the example of fairtrade products clearly shows, consumers also buy ideas when choosing what food to buy. i believe that in order to promote the competitiveness of eu agricultural products, ambitious measures must be taken to enhance the prestige of eu agricultural enterprises worldwide.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for an evaluation and review of the eu's agricultural promotion strategy. it is necessary to improve, simplify and make more consistent the existing measures for the promotion of european agricultural products, thereby increasing agricultural income in the eu, stimulating growth and creating new jobs. the promotion and information policy aims to take advantage of the prospects of global demand developments and to stimulate the interest of third-country consumers in eu products. an effective promotion policy is essential to promote eu agriculture by ensuring food security, sustainable use of natural resources and employment in rural areas. the wide variety of eu products meets very high standards and food safety standards, and it is necessary to improve their image inside and outside the eu and to increase exports. i support the proposal to define a more clear-cut promotion policy, to promote authentic, traditional products. i support the proposal to finance products that are compatible with a sustainable agricultural model and the proposal to withhold funding for measures to restore confidence following food scandals.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is a document which parliament proposes to clarify the policy on the promotion of agricultural products. historically, incentives were designed to combat agricultural surpluses and later food industry crises. the current annual budget for this measure is slightly over eur 50 million and its beneficiaries are trade and branch organisations. support for the fruit and vegetables and wine sectors is only one of the incentive measures and is recognised as one of the six possible programme objectives. these activities also aim to show pupils firsthand how food is produced and how life is lived in rural areas by inviting them to meet farmers. educational promotion should not only explain the benefits of eating products such as fresh fruit and vegetables, but also the eu's common agricultural policy itself.
in writing. − the common agricultural policy (cap) currently has a wide range of incentives, which have been designed for different reasons and for different beneficiaries. although incentives have historically been designed to combat agricultural surpluses and subsequently food industry crises, it is considered that it is time to define more clearly incentive policies that encourage and reward the production of certain products that are attracted to quality programmes and farming activities that reduce co2 emissions, protect biodiversity and are more conducive to maintaining the quality of soil and water resources. the incentive policy should focus as much as possible on funding projects that pursue both of these ambitious and, in many cases, mutually compatible objectives. the objective of increasing farmers' incomes by focusing on products eligible for supply management measures must be pursued as an intrinsic objective. the incentives should focus on traditional european food products that are authentic, varied and delicious to the consumer. vision is important for promoting products both inside and outside the eu. the european union must strive to export a sustainable agricultural model and its products. it is clear that individual projects are obliged to be financed under a rural development policy that can be adapted to specific local conditions, rather than under regulation (ec) no 3/2008, which provides for more complex rules for applicants. i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − i have repeatedly stressed that providing consumers with the right information is the first step towards ensuring the quality of food. on the other hand, it is also a step towards a more competitive eu agriculture and the products produced in this sector. i therefore support the provisions that it is necessary to increase the visibility of eu agricultural production and of the producers of this production, but only in a way that does not create the possibility of discriminating against eu producers on the basis of location (with certain exceptions for areas of lower productivity), size or other criteria.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because a dynamic and efficient agricultural sector is one of the key factors in increasing agricultural income, creating jobs and stimulating growth. i believe that more attention and resources should be devoted to products that can be subject to supply management measures, as well as to promoting entrepreneurship through the development of enabling strategies, training, and the development of skills, knowledge and abilities. only by working together will we create european added value in the food sector and increase farmers' incomes. it is therefore important that the funds and measures allocated are effective and serve the entrepreneurship of as many small businesses as possible, and in particular farmers.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a report on the implementation of the directive on the right of reselling. the purpose of the resale right is to ensure that authors of works of art receive a share of the economic success of their work. the directive aims to harmonise the application of the resale right in the eu. the directive has been promoted to harmonise the conditions for the application of the resale right, i.e. the categories of works of art, the rates of royalties, the maximum threshold for the minimum sale price of a work for the purposes of the resale right (eur 3 000), etc. the report concludes that the quality of administration of resale rights varies across the eu, with higher administrative costs for works of lower value sold. i support the proposals put forward to call on the commission to work more closely with stakeholders to address the administrative difficulties faced by smaller and specialised auctions and dealers and to strengthen the position of the european art market outside the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the commission's draft directive on resale has two objectives: firstly, to ensure that authors of graphic and visual artistic works can enjoy the economic success of their works and, secondly, to harmonise the application of resale law in the eu. while stressing the concern for existing art markets, it is recalled that art market research and statistics do not show that the resale right would have a negative impact on the position of the art market or its turnover. the report calls on the commission to work closely with stakeholders to strengthen the position of the european art market and to address certain problems, such as the so-called cascade effect.
in writing. − i voted in favour because it is known that the art market was valued at usd 10 billion in 2010 and almost usd 12 billion in 2012 and that the resale right represents only 0.03% of this amount. this is an important market from which artists and their heirs should receive a fair return. the directive on the resale right was drawn up with two objectives: firstly, to ensure that authors of graphic and visual artistic works enjoy the economic success of their works together, and secondly, to harmonise the application of the resale right in the eu. i think it is important to actively support local artists, including the youngest artists. the commission must work closely with stakeholders to strengthen the position of the european art market and address issues such as the so-called cascading effect and the administrative difficulties faced by smaller and specialised auctions and dealers.
in writing. − i agree with this report, as an efficient art market ensures that authors are properly valued as creative people, are financially successful and are adequately remunerated. it should be noted that the conditions for the application of the resale right should be uniform throughout the eu. this would effectively contribute to the creation of the common market and remove the existing barriers. i agree with the proposal that more attention should be paid to local artists, with particular attention to young artists. in addition, it is necessary to strengthen the european art market on a global scale and to address some of the challenges.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a recast of rule 70 of the rules of procedure on interinstitutional negotiations during legislative procedures, with a view to making the procedures more efficient, transparent and comprehensive. the proposal aims to incorporate some elements of the code of conduct for the ordinary legislative procedure for negotiations into the binding rules of procedure relating to participation in negotiations and the composition and mandate of the negotiating group. the application of binding rules in the negotiation of legislative procedures would encourage greater accountability and, at the same time, strengthen representative democracy in the eu. i agree with the proposals made on the procedure to be followed to ensure that all decisions to open negotiations at first reading are transparent and legal. a so-called emergency suspension procedure should also be established, under which a simple vote on whether to open negotiations could be held.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report as it aims to update the european parliament's rules of procedure. the inclusion of negotiating powers in the decision-making procedures is currently being considered. it could be argued that the adoption of the committee's negotiating mandate in plenary would give parliament's position more weight and, in theory, ensure the participation of all members in the decision-making on legislative proposals at an early stage. the general rule would therefore be that all draft decisions containing negotiating powers should be submitted to the plenary and that their adoption in plenary should be based on the pursuit of greater democratic legitimacy. however, there are a number of drawbacks. the choice of full automatic active participation of all members would risk making the procedure excessively complex and thus undermining the efficiency and relative speed associated with the adoption of agreements at first reading. the fact that this decision would increase the workload of the ep's linguists should also be taken into account. procedures should therefore be established which are not only flexible and pragmatic but also classified according to the importance of the legislative cases.
in writing. − in order to ensure that interinstitutional legislative procedures are more efficient, more detailed and function smoothly, i believe it is appropriate to include certain elements of a code of conduct in the binding rules of procedure. furthermore, in order to strengthen representative democracy at european level, it is necessary to implement the principles of openness and democratic accountability properly by laying down certain binding rules. it should be noted that the new rules should in all cases meet the requirements of efficiency and not complicate the process of adopting agreements at first reading.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the reduction of the volume of translations of transcripts of meetings (rule 181). article 181 requires that translations be made in writing into all the official languages of the eu, but this takes about 4 months and is expensive. the audio and video recordings of the meeting are published online in all the official languages immediately after the meeting and meps have the right to request an urgent translation of the extracts from the transcript. i think that in the current economic climate and the commitment of the eu institutions to save, it would be appropriate to abandon this expensive system of translation, which is both written and spoken. since all citizens can follow the meetings either live or from a recording in all eu languages, i believe that the current system of translations needs to be changed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the amendments to the article on the translation of minutes (french: compte rendu in extenso (cre)) included in the report by richard corbett had already been approved by the committee on constitutional affairs in 2007. in line with the commitments made by parliament in its 2012 budget, the transcripts would be prepared as a multilingual document, with the speeches recorded in the original language and translated into english only. it is understood that individual members will continue to have the possibility of requesting translation into the various languages of the parts of the text which interest them.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as the principle of multilingualism must be effectively implemented in the work of all eu institutions, and in particular the european parliament, and all existing obstacles must be removed. attention should be paid to the fact that europe is a place of cultural and linguistic diversity, and it is therefore necessary to ensure that all member states and all citizens of the union have equal opportunities to interact with the eu and equal rights of access to eu legislation. in view of this, i consider that the provision of translations of the transcripts into only one language would create a hierarchy between the official languages of the european union and would not ensure legal certainty.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution, which sets out new rules which will provide for stricter safety and pollution requirements for motorcycles. two- and three-wheelers currently account for about 2% of all road transport but account for about 16% of fatal accidents on european roads. the new rules will also reduce the administrative burden on motorcycle manufacturers, as the new regulation will replace as many as 15 (!) of the existing directives. i agree with the rapporteur that human behaviour and driving conditions have a great influence on safe driving, but it is important to make every effort to address the issue of safety in an appropriate way, taking into account the technical characteristics of the vehicle. we, the members of the european parliament, have therefore voted in favour of making anti-lock braking systems (abs) compulsory on all new motorcycles, except enduro and trials, and of improving the visibility of l-category vehicles by equipping them with automatic headlamp switching.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the harmonisation of the rules which will provide for stricter safety and pollution requirements for new bicycles and tricycles (category l). these vehicles account for 2% of all road transport in the eu, but account for as much as 16% of fatal accidents. the new regulation aims to replace 15 existing directives and will therefore significantly reduce the administrative burden on manufacturers of these devices. the proposals and requirements for these vehicles will contribute to more efficient, safer and cleaner urban mobility. i support the proposals made for the mandatory installation of anti-lock braking systems (abs) on all new motorcycles. i agree that automatic headlamp switching etc. should be fitted to improve the visibility of l-category vehicles.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it proposes a commission approval regulation on the market surveillance of bicycles, tricycles and quadricycles. some of the currently applicable legal provisions have been found to be too confusing and the aim is to simplify the existing legal framework and to introduce new administrative and technical requirements, such as those concerning environmental and safety aspects and market surveillance for dedicated vehicles. some of the key requirements also relate to reducing emissions, improving road safety, and taking greater account of new available technologies, such as hybrid l-category vehicles. i believe that the proposed requirements would help facilitate the transition of vehicles to more efficient, safer and cleaner urban mobility.
in writing. − in order to ensure the effective functioning of the internal market, i believe that uniform, harmonised rules should apply to two- and three-wheelers throughout the eu, in a way that provides legal certainty and clarity without adversely affecting businesses and, in particular, consumers. the establishment of transparent, simple and consistent rules would simplify legal regulation, close legal loopholes and ensure adequate market surveillance. it would also improve road safety and reduce emissions. however, in order to ensure the proper implementation of the provisions of this regulation, an effective coordination and monitoring mechanism should be established at both union and national level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for harmonised production rules for agricultural and forestry vehicles (tractors, trailers and towing equipment). the proposal aims to ensure road safety, occupational safety and environmental protection and to complete the internal market in agricultural and forestry vehicles. simplifying the existing legislation reduces the administrative burden and at the same time promotes the competitiveness of the agricultural and forestry vehicle industry. i support the proposals made on the mandatory installation of anti-lock braking systems in certain categories of vehicles, improved braking performance and compatibility of tractors with trailers and towing equipment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report, as the purpose of this proposal is to establish harmonised production rules for agricultural vehicles (tractors, trailers and towing equipment - category u). this is to ensure common rules for the functioning of the internal market and to reconcile them with a high level of road and occupational safety and environmental protection. i think the commission's proposal is important and right because it aims to simplify the existing type of regulation and helps to promote industrial competitiveness.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i welcomed the commission's proposal. since it simplifies the type-approval legislation and thus helps to promote industrial competitiveness. in my view, in order to ensure a high level of road safety, occupational safety and environmental protection and to complete the internal market for agricultural and forestry vehicles, a union-wide approval procedure for all categories of vehicles should be established, taking into account a balanced assessment of benefits and costs, with particular attention to small and medium-sized enterprises.
in writing. - i support the draft regulation submitted. in order to ensure the functioning of the internal market and to promote industrial competitiveness, harmonised rules for the production of agricultural and forestry vehicles should apply in the eu. the proper implementation of these rules will increase transparency, reduce administrative burden and eliminate the threat of market fragmentation. however, in all cases, the new rules must meet high road safety and environmental requirements.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on removing barriers to card, internet and mobile payments. payment instruments are becoming more diverse today, both in the eu and worldwide, but their effectiveness is not yet fully exploited. the markets for card, online and mobile payments in the eu are still fragmented and the methods of such payments vary considerably between member states. i agree with the need to create an eu-wide integrated payment environment to develop more efficient and secure payment instruments. i welcome the proposals made to ensure market access for new service providers, to strengthen payment security and data protection, to ensure transparent and effective pricing of payment services and to strengthen the interaction between service providers. the increased use of this type of payment would contribute to the growth and diversification of e-commerce in europe. i support the proposals listed above to achieve greater competition, more choice and safer payments.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the regulation aims to give consumers or businesses access to more convenient, faster, more flexible and more economical payment methods. the creation of a single payments area (sepa) has facilitated bank transfers in 32 european countries, but there are still a number of problems that have not been resolved. for example, surcharges, payment security, multilateral interbank charges (mits) threaten transparency, openness, competitiveness and costs for both traders and consumers. it is also important to note that despite the common standards applicable to member states, the markets for card, internet and mobile payments are still fragmented within the eu. the commission recognises the need to improve the overall level of infrastructure in the future and to seek a level playing field that encourages competitiveness and innovation rather than limiting the development of this area.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because the variety of payment instruments is constantly increasing, both in europe and worldwide. while new mobile and internet payment methods are rapidly emerging, of interest to both consumers and businesses, even the payment card market is still far from being fully exploited and its effectiveness is still far from being fully exploited. the commission published a green paper on the creation of an integrated european market for card, internet and mobile payments, in which it identifies a number of obstacles to the european payment market being as efficient and open as possible. the benefits of promoting and enhancing card, internet and mobile payments should be recognised in order to provide consumers and businesses with more convenient, secure, faster, more diverse, flexible and cost-effective payment methods. furthermore, the wider use of the payment methods listed is essential if e-commerce is to continue to expand rapidly and ensure its increasing contribution to the gdp of the member states. in this case, the differences between local and cross-border orders should be eliminated and, in the light of the aim of market integration with the payment card, cross-border payments should be as convenient as national payments. however, the market for mobile and online payments is still in its early stages of development and should not be over-regulated, as this could impede the natural development and innovation in this area.
in writing. - in support of the document adopted today, i would like to draw attention to one of its horizontal aspects. - the european parliament's observation that the charges levied on various services are often not justified by the cost of the services provided and are disproportionate. regardless of the nature of the payment, the weaker party (usually the consumer, who usually does not even have access to the standard terms of service) is forced to pay high fees, which can then be used by the service provider to cover losses on unprofitable services. i therefore support calls for the introduction of a requirement to determine the amount of such charges on the basis of the costs incurred alone and i believe that the consumer would only benefit from a cap on the amount of such a charge.
in writing. − i agree with the view expressed in this report, as it will create a secure, transparent and innovative payment environment, while enhancing the competitiveness of the european economy in the world. at present, the integrated european card, internet and mobile payments market is not a single market, but a separate system. a single eu-wide system is needed to protect consumers and traders from additional charges and other negative effects. it should be noted that standardisation and harmonisation of practices would benefit not only traders but also consumers, as they would be able to choose more cost-effective payment methods.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this draft resolution, which aims to ensure greater transparency and better regulation of the shadow banking sector. inadequate supervision of financial institutions that carry out activities similar to those of banks but fall outside the scope of regulation applicable to banks is detrimental to the stability of the eu financial system. the activities of such institutions could have a positive impact on the economy and stimulate growth (risk would be better distributed outside the traditional banking sector), but they must be carried out in full transparency. i therefore support the proposals put forward to improve the monitoring and regulation of this type of financial institution and to create a central repo database to enable supervisors to have a comprehensive view of the global repo market. i also support the establishment of a 25% equity exposure limit for all non-regulated entities and the establishment of a limit on the number of times a financial product can be securitised
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is necessary to monitor shadow banking more closely and to tighten its supervision. shadow banking is recognised as one of several important potential causes and factors that contribute to the financial crisis and can pose a threat to the integrity of the financial system. more and more robust data and analytical capabilities are urgently needed to build a comprehensive picture of shadow banking. the ecb and the esrb should also play an important role in combating shadow banking. given the highly innovative nature of the shadow banking system, its development may create systemic risks that need to be addressed. to do this properly, it is necessary to develop monitoring tools in the future to provide a concrete picture of the entire credit intermediation system.
in writing. − i voted in favour because, despite the changes to the new regulatory framework since the financial crisis, which would make the financial system safer and more sustainable, and perhaps because of them, a very large proportion of credit intermediation activities are still not sufficiently monitored and regulated. such activities include a shadow banking sector through a system of intermediaries, instruments, entities or financial arrangements that performs many functions similar to those performed by banks but which is not subject to their regulation or is subject to a less stringent regulatory regime or addresses issues not related to systemic risk and which does not have access to a central bank liquidity facility or public sector credit guarantees. i agree with the view that there is a need to increase transparency in the interrelationships and activities between traditional banks and non-consolidated institutions and to address these issues from a regulatory perspective. first, more and more robust data and analytical capacity is urgently needed to build a comprehensive picture of shadow banking. one of the key steps towards greater transparency could be the initiative on the repositories of repurchase transactions. second, the compilation of this data picture should make it easy to identify those aspects of the shadow banking system that benefit the real economy and those that pose a systemic risk or concern.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as it is only by limiting the growth of the shadow banking market that europe's financial stability will be ensured. therefore, a better and more stringent monitoring and regulatory framework is necessary to prevent potential systemic risk and other negative effects that shadow banking may have. it should be noted that shadow banking in the eu should act as a useful alternative source of financing. as it is an important instrument to help separate the risk from the banking sector and thus protect taxpayers or the system from potential impact.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution on the protection of children in the digital world. with the rise of social networking, children are spending more and more time online. according to statistics, young people in europe spend up to 40 hours a week watching television. they are online for 88 minutes a day (fifteen and sixteen year olds - 2 hours) and start using the internet at an average age of nine, and some children - much younger - before they go to school and learn to read. facebook is used by 77% of 15-16 year olds and 38% of 9-12 year olds, who are often not protected from the dangers of the virtual world. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament has adopted a resolution calling for a safe internet for children and for action to be taken against illegal and harmful content. we, the members of the european parliament, call on the eu member states and the european commission to present as soon as possible a common position and policy guidelines on the protection of children online and to come forward with a proposal for a single framework directive on children's rights in the digital world, which would include all the provisions of previously adopted eu legislation relating to children. it is particularly important that all eu member states take urgent action to ensure that our young people are protected in the digital world and that they are made aware of the limits of privacy and the dangers of misinterpretation and disclosure of personal data in the online space.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the safety of children on the internet, the fight against illegal and harmful content and the removal of such content. eu countries are not dealing with harmful content online in the same way and in an appropriate way, and there are differences in age rating systems and technical measures to ensure that websites are age-appropriate. i agree that dedicated hotlines should be set up to report harmful or malicious content online and that supporting infrastructure should be improved to remove illegal content more effectively. i agree that there should be more age-based classification systems for online games, codes of conduct and better awareness of this classification amongst retailers, so that children are not able to buy games that are not appropriate for their age. it is necessary to organise awareness campaigns for children on internet safety and to provide training in schools on internet safety.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because television and the internet occupy an increasingly large part of young people's lives and it is therefore necessary to ensure that quality standards and child protection are in place for content aimed at children. for example, it is estimated that young people between the ages of 9 and 16 use computers for schoolwork and play (100 percent), for watching videos (86 percent), for playing games with others, for downloading and exchanging videos and music (56 percent), and finally for sharing files and visiting virtual chat rooms (23 percent). there is a growing awareness among young people themselves, families, schools, researchers and the public of the quality standards that should be applied to content for children distributed in any form and by any medium (tv, computer, telephone, tablet). the eu's general funding has thus been used to develop appropriate measures, in particular the 'safer internet' programme, which has been successfully implemented in all eu member states and which provides for coordination by 2013, which was positively assessed in the interim report. the continuity of the 'safer internet' programme needs to be ensured and it is necessary to ensure that the responsibility for protecting children from cybercrime is shared by all member states. in order to be more effective, the fight against illegal content and the protection of privacy must be specifically addressed.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the issue of the protection of minors in the digital world must be addressed at the regulatory level, by using more effective measures, including self-regulation, i.e. encouraging industry to assume collective responsibility, and at the level of education and training, by training children, parents and teachers to prevent minors from accessing illegal content. one of the key objectives of an effective child protection strategy should be to ensure that all children, young people and parents/guardians have the information and skills to protect themselves using the internet. today, minors have a very free access to the internet and it is essential to help them use it wisely, responsibly and safely. i believe that minors should be protected from the dangers of the digital world in accordance with their age and developmental stage.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document and its provision for more regulation of the protection of minors in the digital world at two levels: through industry ownership and through education and training to ensure that minors are protected from harmful content. the information on the internet inevitably has a two-fold impact on minors. on the one hand, the internet as a source of knowledge has an educational function, while on the other hand harmful and inappropriate content can have serious consequences for the development of children and adolescents. the information on sexual content, which is encountered by a significant percentage of underage internet users by chance and accident, is of particular concern. the development of a knowledge-based society based on responsibility should be the guiding principle when it comes to the protection of children and adolescents in the virtual world. at the same time, particular attention should be paid to the child's immediate environment, the family, and its responsibility to develop fully responsible citizens. education and prevention should start in the family. therefore, by fully coordinating prevention, legal, technical and educational measures, member states must implement safer internet programmes, work with industry and civil society groups, ngos, educators, parents to protect children from the dangers of the digital world.
in writing. - i support this resolution. with the rapid development of technology, it is becoming increasingly difficult to adequately protect children in the digital world. this requires the use of self-regulatory and co-regulatory measures. however, it is essential that any measure adopted respects the principles of legal certainty of the rule of law and the rights and legitimate interests of consumers. in addition, prevention and intervention measures must address not only the fight against illegal content but also other issues related to the many threats faced by minors. i think child-safe sites should be labeled accordingly. it is very important that the commission pay more attention to the online marketing of products harmful to young people. i believe that campaigns should be implemented at both national and eu level to provide parents with the information they need to protect their children from illegal, inappropriate and dangerous material.
in writing. − the internet is increasingly penetrating our lives, becoming an integral part of our daily lives, even for minors. we must educate children to browse the digital world responsibly, and we must also strengthen online safety measures for minors. we need to do more to limit harmful content on the internet, advertising. after all, the younger generation is more vulnerable, more easily manipulated. i voted in favour of this report because it encourages greater involvement of parents, schools and the public in discussions on the protection of children's rights online. the communication sets the context for safe and responsible internet use by minors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on creating a favourable environment for social enterprises in the eu. social enterprises supply goods and services in the normal way for business, but use the surplus primarily for social purposes. since the primary objective of social enterprises is to have a social impact rather than to make a profit, the european commission and the member states should ensure that these enterprises are not placed at a disadvantage compared to other types of enterprises. social enterprises contribute to smart growth and promote social and economic transformation. i support the establishment of a regulatory framework for solidarity investment funds at eu level to facilitate access to financial markets for social enterprises. i also agree with the need to improve access to micro-credit for businesses and to facilitate access to start-up, growth and development finance for social enterprises. i support the proposals for the creation of a quality label for social enterprises to improve their visibility. i believe that there is a need to increase the awareness of social entrepreneurs of the eu programmes from which they can benefit.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because one of the key objectives for the future of the eu is a well-developed so-called social enterprise. i think there is a constant increase in the need for social services, for example in health care and nursing. europe is also pursuing economic growth to increase global competitiveness by unlocking the potential for new jobs, which are projected to be concentrated in the 'green' and 'white' economies. it is important to emphasise that, unlike many other sectors of the economy, social enterprises require additional funding instruments. in other words, i believe that in order to promote social enterprise in the eu, an environment must be created for innovation capacity and experimentation, the success or failure of which would be assessed by the eu institutions together with the member states over a given period of time. social entrepreneurship, understood as a common public interest or otherwise a benefit to society, is precisely the eu's flagship initiative that would enable new infrastructures to be created and new innovative ideas to emerge, and should therefore be strongly encouraged.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because, unlike many other sectors of the economy, social enterprises require additional funding. appropriate measures at national and regional level must be adopted as soon as possible following commission initiatives. in order to allow the rapid development of social enterprises, together with targeted support for individuals and organisations active in this field, this european parliament report aims to establish the general conditions for the new stage of the european social economy, as precise and clear as possible, while at the same time being open and providing new opportunities. the communication also takes the view that this new phase should be characterised by a high capacity for innovation, accompanied by experiments whose success or failure would be assessed by the eu institutions together with the member states within a given forecast period. concrete conclusions will then have to be drawn on the appropriate improvement actions and measures that will allow the social enterprise to continue to develop effectively in the long term. in short, the regulatory framework and action plans must preserve diversity and abundance where it exists and create it where it does not. the commission's proposed main instruments, such as the establishment of a panorama of social enterprises in europe, the creation of a certification database or a large-scale information platform for mutual learning, can provide a useful basis for this. the creation of a specific quality label for social enterprises should also be of great benefit for further development.
in writing. - i voted for the resolution. i agree with the position expressed in the document on support and promotion of social enterprises. companies that aim to have a positive social impact on different segments of society, by stripping away the social purpose and management of enterprises, should be encouraged through various support programmes. with particular attention to improving the fiscal and legal environment, ensuring support from eu funds at all levels from national to eu. on the other hand, i fully support the requirements for such companies to involve volunteers in activities, thus creating opportunities for young people to gain work experience at the beginning of their careers, to promote the implementation of the erasmus for young entrepreneurs programme and similar support and advisory programmes. the development of social enterprises in the member states, as in my country of lithuania, can make a significant contribution to the implementation of the eu's overall growth strategy, europe 2020, and to the inclusion of people at social risk.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because social enterprises play an important role in promoting social innovation and therefore need to create a favourable economic and regulatory environment in the social innovation economy. in order to increase the visibility of these enterprises, in particular, the financial needs of social enterprises must be properly assessed, access to financial markets facilitated and appropriate funding allocated at local, regional, national and eu level. they must also be properly integrated into action plans for employment and social inclusion. only the establishment of an appropriate support mechanism will ensure the growth and development of social enterprises. they will be able to become financially independent, engage in commercial activities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this important resolution. the european parliament stresses that to put the eu firmly on the road to financial stability and economic recovery, cosmetic touches are not sufficient. the european parliament wants a thorough overhaul of the economic and monetary union (emu) in all its aspects. i agree with the rapporteur that in order to achieve a stronger architecture, the so-called four pillars of the emu (its financial, budgetary, economic and democratic legs) must be reinforced. it is essential that democratic control matches the pace of reforms and, across the board, the european parliament, as the institution that represents all citizens, should play a key role. we, members of the european parliament, underlined that the goals of a stronger economic union should be sustainable economic growth, more jobs and greater social cohesion. completing the internal market, implementing existing internal market law, implementing the 2020 strategy for growth and jobs and a targeted use of european budgets are key issues which should be put in place without further delay.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on european economic and monetary union. in order to strengthen the eu's economic and monetary policy powers, it is important to increase the democratic accountability of the union and, if necessary, to amend the eu treaties, and to integrate the governance of the european monetary union into the eu institutional framework. i support the proposals put forward for the establishment of a european 'ministry of finance' headed by an eu finance minister, accountable to the european parliament, and for the right of the ep to approve the chairmen of the eu banking supervision mechanism and the european stability mechanism. it is also important to strengthen the role of the european commissioner responsible for economic and monetary affairs and his accountability to the ep. i support the call for member states to be given more responsibility for the preparation of national fiscal policy and economic reform plans. the commission should present legislation without delay on closer tax cooperation between eu member states, reform of the european social pact and the eu's own budgetary resources.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that economic and monetary union is a means of achieving the objectives of the union and its member states, in particular the objectives of balanced and sustainable growth and a high level of employment. indeed, it can be said that the past year has been a challenging one for the european union as a whole. i am referring to the economic, financial and banking crises that have occurred, which, together with macroeconomic imbalances, have had a rapid and direct negative impact on the social and economic development of the euro area and the union as a whole. this has affected all countries, with unemployment in the eu-27 rising from 7% to 10.4% between 2008 and mid-2012, with 25 million more unemployed, more than one in five young people out of work (22%) and youth unemployment rates now exceeding 50% in some member states. the eu is at a crossroads and a clear choice must be made either to combine the eu's existing strengths and ensure that the union remains strong and based on values and solidarity in a globalised world in the future, or to step back and allow itself to be passively adapted to globalisation. the response to the euro crisis is complex, but it requires continuous efforts. the need for closer european integration, based on accountability, democratic legitimacy and citizens' consent, is clearer than ever.
in writing. − effective economic and social cohesion is the basis for a strong and genuine economic and monetary union. this is a guarantee of balanced and sustainable growth and a high level of employment. however, it is essential to safeguard democracy and ensure proper citizen participation in order to achieve these objectives. national sovereignty must be protected and the rights of national parliaments strengthened, while preventing the transfer of powers from national institutions to eu supranational institutions. i support the proposal to preserve the right of peoples to express their will and to remove any restrictions on their right to decide on their own economic policies.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on the one hand we are told that shale gas can bring about an energy revolution because its resources are large enough and necessary for the needs of the economy. on the other hand, we are told that the effects of their extraction are poorly understood, that they pose a danger to public health, that they can harm both present and future generations. in fact, the information is too contradictory and to rely solely on the good or bad examples of the united states that reach us is too questionable. and until there is a firm belief that this technology is safe enough and will not cause a very large and painful environmental disaster, then to talk about extracting such gas in europe, in my opinion, is too bold. i would say that we should look for ways of extracting shale gas without harming the environment. this would be a first-rate challenge for european scientists, and i think they would be able to cope with it very well.
a few years ago, shale gas was still considered exotic in europe. today, shale gas is being talked about around the world as a technology that could change the global energy balance within a few years. today in the european parliament we are discussing two aspects of shale gas extraction: the economic and the environmental. my head, we need to weigh these sides responsibly. i think the present situation is unsatisfactory because, firstly, some countries are even banning the exploration of shale gas, which is not based on fear of possible ecological disasters. second, the activity is almost entirely unregulated. environmental regulation is certainly not enough. the very fact that the impact on europe has not been fully explored. i therefore support the european parliament's view that environmental impact must be assessed in as much detail as possible and that the european union must be prepared to respond as effectively as possible. such surveys should be carried out on a regular basis before, during and after extraction operations. the accumulated practice and research data shall be reviewed on a regular basis and action taken if it appears that the same or different legal safeguards are necessary. we also need to review the provisions governing public consultation. on the other hand, shale gas extraction must not become an industry with exclusive regulation. i am convinced that there is no need to create new administrative rules that burden businesses with disproportionate and unnecessary requirements and restrictions. there are many people in my country who say that even renewable energy is not environmentally friendly, that it poses certain problems, and i think there is no human activity that does not affect the environment in one way or another. but i think shale gas is the way to energy independence and diversification.
i would like to draw attention to two very important and specific aspects of the multiannual financial framework: financing the closure of the ignalina nuclear power plant and support for the baltic farmers. as we sit here today in strasbourg, the baltic farmers, who have gathered in brussels for a rally, say that enough is enough, enough is enough of making fools of us by giving us four times less pay. how long can this go on? all the resolutions and directives talk about a level playing field, so let's take it and get it done. lithuania committed to shut down the nuclear power plant and has done so. the european union has committed itself to financing its closure, but has not done so to the full. the commission notes that the measures in question are not imputable to the state, but to the state and the state-owned banks. i would like to emphasise that this is a clear departure from the provisions of the accession treaty and protocol 4 thereto. legally, this can be seen as a breach of the accession treaty.
in writing. as a member of parliament elected by the citizens of lithuania, i find it very difficult to take a positive view of the draft council conclusions presented by the president of the european council, mr van rompuy, last week and the proposed allocation of funds in the next financial perspective. the most painful and perhaps most damaging element of such a proposal is the reduction in the amount of funds for cohesion policy. such a proposal is totally unacceptable, since it would be particularly damaging to the european union as a family of states in the future. the essence of cohesion policy is to bring all the eu regions to the same level of development, and the council's proposal to reduce this funding, which would particularly affect the currently least developed regions, completely negates the essence of cohesion policy and would create the conditions for a so-called two-speed europe. the second proposal, which has been the subject of criticism, is the reduction in agricultural expenditure. the council's proposal to extend the transitional periods during which direct payments will have to be uniform across the eu is particularly difficult to accept. finally, the funds currently envisaged by the council for the closure of the three nuclear power plants and specifically the closure of the lithuanian npp. firstly, the funds available are totally insufficient to close the facility. second, the suspension of the aid in 2017 is totally unacceptable. the support must be provided for at least the entire duration of the new financial perspective. otherwise, lithuania would be placed under an unreasonably high burden that it would be unable to finance from its national budget and other vital areas of state administration would be affected.
in writing. − i congratulate the commissioner-designate on coming to work at a difficult time and on receiving a generous portfolio of unfinished work. i hope that the new commissioner for health will continue the work he has started and will be as principled as his predecessor on both food safety and public health. i hope that the promised legislation in these areas will also be presented soon (i am talking in particular about the regulation of novel foods and tobacco products).
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to allocate eur 670 million from the eu solidarity fund to the emilia-romagna region of italy. on 20 and 29 may 2012, two major earthquakes struck the region, killing 27 people and injuring 350 others, with another 45,000 people evacuated. this record-breaking allocation from the solidarity fund is intended to cover the costs of restoring critical infrastructure, restoring emergency services and protecting the cultural heritage of the region. the priority remains the housing of the thousands of people in the region who have been left homeless. the solidarity fund was set up in the wake of the 2002 floods in central europe. since then, the fund has been used to help victims of 49 natural disasters - floods, forest fires, earthquakes, storms and droughts. i support the calls made to all stakeholders in the member states to further improve the coordination of the use of the fund's resources in the future with a view to their early absorption.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the tariff quotas for timber exported from russia to the eu. under this agreement, the eu will reduce customs duties on timber from russia. this will help wood processing companies to obtain timber from russia, which is the largest exporter to the eu (timber imports from russia account for 60% of all imports to the eu), at a cheaper price. another important aspect of this agreement with russia is the protection of timber importers. the commission notes that the russian authorities have not provided any evidence that the export tax on wood is being increased. the eu is also committed to the development of a common defence policy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the tariff quotas for timber exported from russia to the eu. in recent decades, russia has supplied 60% of all timber imported into the eu. the new eu-russia agreement provides for significantly lower russian timber export duties to the eu, which will affect some russian timber (pine, fir). the eu has a strong interest in tariff quotas which give preference to russian timber exports, with much lower duties under the quota than at present. the agreement lays down rules for the management of export tariff quotas and provides for the cooperation between the competent authorities of the eu and the russian government necessary for the proper functioning of the system. i agree that this agreement should help to avoid a situation where russia unilaterally increases export duties, as this has a very negative impact on eu producers.
