in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii) not only provides for greater security and more advanced information use through interlinked alerts, but also for a new type of references and new functionalities. the transition from the currently applicable sis 1+ to sis ii is governed by two legal instruments council regulation (ec) no 1104/2008 established the former first pillar and council decision 2008/839/jha established the former third pillar. the current commission proposal is to reword these two acts into a single act to take account of the abolition of the pillars (com (2012) 81).
in writing. - i voted for this document. the schengen information system (sis) is undoubtedly the most important tool for ensuring the security of the schengen area, which is rightly regarded as the foundation of europe, i.e. an area without borders and an area of freedom, security and justice. the second generation of the schengen information system (sis ii) allows for the upload of new data (primarily biometric data), the use of new types of references and new functions. this will allow for increased security and a more advanced use of information through the use of interlinked alerts. the legal sis ii will apply from the moment the first member state completes the migration process. this will enhance legal certainty and prevent unnecessary expenditure in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the transition from the schengen information system (sis 1+) to the second generation system (sis ii). the sis was created to harmonise the abolition of border controls between the schengen states. its purpose is to maintain public order and public security, including national security. this system facilitates the exchange of information between member states and gives users (police departments, embassies and consulates, migration authorities, etc.) real-time access to the data they need to perform their functions. sis ii is a tool for enhancing the security of the schengen area, for more effective data protection and for ensuring fundamental human rights. the second generation of the schengen information system allows new data to be uploaded, new types of references to be used and new functions to be performed. i support the proposals to ensure effective oversight of the complex transition process and to encourage closer cooperation between the european data protection supervisor and the member states' authorities in implementing this transition.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a commission evaluation of the 28th report on the control of the application of eu law (2010). the proper application of eu law by the member states is a fundamental condition for the functioning of the european union, and i therefore support the aim of simplifying its implementation, application and enforcement in the member states. the eu pilot has played a key role in reducing the number of potential infringements of eu law. this system is designed to deal with requests and complaints from citizens and businesses that raise questions about the correct application of eu law. the eu pilot applies when member states need to explain their factual or legal position: they have to propose a solution to address breaches of eu law within a short timeframe. i agree with the suggestion that the system should indicate the rights or safeguards granted to the complainant. the commission should also be more effective in ensuring that member states transpose eu environmental legislation, which is the most infringing, into national law in a timely and appropriate manner. the training of national judges, lawyers, administrative officials and civil servants applying eu law needs to be improved and coordinated.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it aims to bring the 10 trade policy regulations into line with the new primary legislation under the treaty of lisbon. more specifically, it aims to align the regulations with the provisions of article 290 which transpose delegated acts into european union law for the first time. this article enables the legislator to delegate to the commission the power to adopt non-legislative acts of general application supplementing or amending non-essential elements of a legislative act. in this case, i consider it necessary to amend the recitals in the main acts in order to clarify the procedure for the application of delegated acts and to define precisely the purpose, content and scope of the delegation. it would also be appropriate to ensure that parliament's experts are able to attend expert meetings organised by the commission before the preparation and implementation of delegated acts.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal as parliament must stress the importance of respecting the rule of law, the principle of legal clarity, the requirements of transparency and openness and the principle of proportionality in order to ensure that union law is applied in a timely and appropriate manner. it is essential that the commission use all other available means to ensure that member states transpose union legislation, in particular environmental legislation, in a timely and appropriate manner, as this is one of the most affected areas. national courts in the member states play a crucial role in the application of eu law. the union's efforts to improve and coordinate the training of national judges, lawyers, national administrative officials and civil servants should therefore be fully supported, and more active action should be taken in this area in order to truly live the concept of a union based on the rule of law.
in writing. − i support this resolution, as more efforts are needed in the area of prevention of infringements to ensure more effective application of eu law. attention should be drawn to the fact that eu law can only be applied in a timely and appropriate manner in accordance with the principles of the rule of law, legal clarity, transparency, openness and proportionality. given that the infringement procedure consists of two stages, i believe that special attention should be paid to the administrative stage, in which citizens play a special role. it should be noted that the transposition of eu legislation into national law is the main source of infringements. the commission therefore needs to pay more attention to this process and to apply certain measures more effectively to the member states.
in writing. − the implementation of european union legislation depends not only on the eu member states but also on the eu institutions. the role of the member states in transposing eu legislation into national law is crucial to the quality of implementation of eu law. unfortunately, this process takes place at different rates in the member states and often leads to different legal practices. i voted in favour of this report because it introduces stronger controls on the application of eu law. it is also one of the main levers that the european parliament, the council and the commission can use to achieve a more transparent, high-quality and rapid transposition of eu law. without coordination and quality, there will be no legal order for the transfer of eu law.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it is the parliament's position on the environmental impact of shale gas and shale oil extraction. gas is and will remain an important source of energy throughout the eu at least until 2030 or 2035. although conventional gas production is declining, if the situation does not change, europe will still need to import significant amounts of gas for several decades. it is also being considered whether local shale gas resources could be tapped and whether the integration of the internal market could help to reduce the eu's dependence on gas imports. it is worth noting that global gas prices and trading patterns have been undergoing major changes in recent times, with clear implications for the eu. the 'shale gas revolution' is spreading relatively quickly around the world. although it is said that it is too early to draw conclusions about whether the eu could extract large quantities economically, several member states have granted permits for shale gas exploration and are preparing to extract it if possible. however, it should be stressed that all human activities involve a certain degree of risk. the aim of regulation should be to minimise the impact on the environment and to strike a reasonable balance between scientific, statistical and risk-benefit considerations (and the related alternatives).
in writing. - i voted for this document. europe will have to import a lot of gas, but at the same time natural gas is extracted in europe, and local shale gas reserves may be tapped, and the integration of the internal market may help reduce the eu's dependence on gas imports. the long-term effects of a gift can be varied. the different environmental impacts must take into account all the circumstances and comparable indicators. the friction is minimized when the production begins, the working equipment is on the surface for several square years and the production is silent. the commission notes that the uk authorities have not provided any evidence that the shale gas and shale oil extraction activities are carried out by an independent company. such potential interference must be brought to the attention of the competent national authorities in the course of their regulatory activities, in particular in the application of the environmental impact assessment directive. public participation should be ensured through information campaigns before the start of the exploration phase and through public consultation during the early stages of operation. more active communication and better public awareness of extraction of non-conventional fossil fuels is needed to enable the public to understand, accept and trust this activity. it is important to stress that extraction of non-conventional fossil fuels can also provide an excellent environment for economic strengthening, employment and development in certain eu regions.
in writing. − before starting to extract shale gas, a full assessment of the potential environmental and human health impacts is necessary. it is also necessary to ensure fair and equal conditions of operation throughout the union and strict implementation of the requirements of eu safety and environmental legislation. it should be noted that there is still no firm belief that the technology used to extract shale gas is sufficiently safe and will not cause major and painful environmental disasters related to the chemical pollution of drinking water, wastewater treatment, seismic effects and the possible emission of greenhouse gases.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out provisions for the responsible exploitation of shale gas deposits in europe. this report is the beginning of an eu dialogue on shale gas extraction, and we must seek a consensus based on scientific knowledge. the extraction of shale gas with the highest safety standards and the latest technology is our priority. before undertaking shale gas extraction, we must ensure that we are properly prepared: a detailed analysis of the work has been carried out, we are sure that the hydraulic fracturing will not affect the ecological balance (e.g. no contamination of groundwater, etc.), and we have checked whether the work complies with the legal standards. we should not blindly follow the lead of countries in shale gas extraction. each country has its own specificities. the polish example shows that seismic activity has started at the site where the hydraulic excavation was carried out.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's position on the industrial and other aspects of shale gas. it is essential to analyse the future prospects for the global and eu gas markets and to identify possible developments in the shale gas market and their impact on future security of gas supply and prices in the european union. the analysis provided shall reflect the state of play between the eu 2020 target and the co2 target. it is worth noting that global natural gas consumption is currently increasing and that europe remains one of the regions with the highest demand for gas imports. according to the international energy agency, by 2035 european domestic gas production is projected to decline and demand to increase, leading to an increase in imports of 450 billion cubic metres. it is therefore necessary to present, by the end of 2012, not only a planned energy action plan, but also an examination of the availability, scale and production of the eu's non-conventional gas resources.
in writing. − i abstained in this vote because the development of shale gas extraction is controversial in the eu and globally and requires a thorough assessment of all types of impacts (environment, public health and climate change) before further development of this technology. it should also be noted that public participation should be ensured through information campaigns before the start of the exploration phase and through public consultation during the early stages of operation. more active communication and better public awareness of extraction of non-conventional fossil fuels is needed to enable the public to understand, accept and trust this activity.
in writing. − today we have approved two important documents that open the way to greater exploitation of shale gas in the european union. however, these documents are only the first steps towards ensuring that this energy sector does not become a wild and unregulated business. i therefore urge both the commission and the member states to take note of parliament's recommendations on both licensing and land use, taxation and the environment. only then will shale gas become europe's energy future.
in writing. − it is important to note that exploration and extraction of shale gas is a complex, time-consuming and technologically expensive process. the question arises therefore whether the currently promising idea of shale gas extraction in europe cannot be compared with the vision of intensive agriculture on low yields and small land areas: a modest result achieved with a huge effort requiring a lot of time and investment. it is also very important to note that the development of shale gas extraction is subject to controversial assessments, which require a thorough assessment of all types of impacts (environment, public health and climate change) before further development of this technology. in this context, i believe that more investment in research and research and development programmes is needed to achieve better outcomes and a greater understanding of the safety and risks of intelligence and production operations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the environmental impact assessment of shale gas and shale oil extraction. the main benefits of shale gas for the european union would be greater energy independence from imports, increased competition and lower prices and job creation. however, shale gas production has a very negative impact on the environment, with large amounts of water used for its production, groundwater pollution and the risk of underground explosions. the extraction of such unconventional fossil fuels can boost the eu economy and increase employment, but a thorough assessment of all types of impacts (environment, public health and climate change) is necessary before the technology can be developed. i support the proposals that, despite the exclusive right of member states to exploit their energy resources, fossil fuel extraction should be carried out in a way that ensures a level playing field across the eu and that eu safety and environmental legislation is respected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to change the procedure for filing and examining petitions to make it more efficient, transparent and impartial. eu citizens can petition the european parliament on matters which fall within the eu's fields of activity and are of direct relevance to them. this gives parliament the opportunity to draw attention to infringements of citizens' rights by member states or local authorities. i support the proposals to improve the means of allowing eu citizens to raise important issues in plenary, and to give parliament more scope to call witnesses, conduct investigations and prepare for the on-the-spot discussions on the issues raised in petitions. this would improve the visibility, accountability and transparency of the committee on petitions. i welcome the cooperation between the committee on petitions and the european ombudsman's services.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the committee on petitions has a duty to constantly review and, where possible, strengthen its role, particularly in the area of promoting democratic principles, such as encouraging greater participation of citizens in the eu decision-making process and increasing transparency and accountability. in its normal course of action, the committee works closely with the member states, the commission, the european ombudsman and other bodies to ensure that the letter and spirit of eu law is respected. eu citizens and permanent residents have a legitimate expectation that the problems for which they turn to the committee on petitions will be resolved in a timely manner and in accordance with the legal framework of the european union, which they rely on to protect their rights as citizens of the union, in particular the right to the natural environment, health, freedom of movement, dignity and fundamental rights and freedoms.
in writing. - i support this resolution. i think that the usefulness of the committee on petitions is unquestionable, since it actively defends the fundamental rights and freedoms of citizens by using its political influence. it is to be welcomed that considerable progress has been made in developing and strengthening links with citizens. i believe that more attention should be paid to the implementation of eu legislation in the fields of the environment, justice and the internal market, where the level of infringements is not decreasing. attention should be drawn to the need for closer cooperation with national parliaments and governments in order to ensure more transparent transposition and application of eu legislation.
i congratulate the speakers who have done a great job, especially indrek taranda. four years ago, the european union declared climate change to be the greatest threat to humanity. we have only seven years left to prevent the irreversible damage of climate change. the crisis, unfortunately, has pushed this most pressing problem to the side. the impact of climate change on global security should be reflected in all key eu documents and an interinstitutional working group should be established to increase the capacity of the eu and its member states to anticipate and respond to natural disasters caused by climate change and their consequences. better coordination is needed between the eu countries, the european commission, the us, as well as china, india, russia and brazil. an early warning mechanism is needed, both at european and global level. the world's militaries, especially the largest, should make more efficient use of energy resources to help combat climate change.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. increasing the frequency of extreme weather events also means higher costs for the european economy, both for developing and so-called economically stable countries. the occurrence of natural disasters is a matter of course and requires a common approach from the member states of the european union to counteract the devastating effects of disasters. the union's priority in this regard should be to protect the population against loss of access to fresh water and food following a natural disaster. this requires the development of a forward-looking and integrated crisis management and response policy across the 27 countries. it is therefore necessary to examine which countries or regions are most exposed to the risk of natural disasters. a list of such countries or regions should then be drawn up and annual reports on possible risks and mitigation proposals should be made. the union must also, of course, cooperate with other regions of the world in this area in order to have a global picture of potential dangers. in addition, it is of great importance to continue and strengthen the union's humanitarian aid not only on the european continent but also beyond. the european commission should also include in its main development strategies the issue of effectively eliminating natural hazards linked to natural disasters, so that potentially affected areas and their authorities have a sense of security and certainty that they will receive assistance in the event of a natural disaster.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, i am pleased to have the opportunity today to brief you on behalf of high representative/vice-president ashton on the latest developments and the european union’s activities in kazakhstan. i would like to warmly thank mrs jaakonssaari for her excellent report. kazakhstan has been an important partner for the eu in central asia, not only on trade and economic exchanges, but as a stable country which has a proven track record of inter-ethnic and inter-religious harmony and tolerance. the eu has a strategic interest in further deepening our involvement with kazakhstan and in developing fully the potential for political cooperation; especially considering the rapidly evolving dynamics of regional integration. kazakhstan is a pragmatic partner, open to discussions and willing to explore opportunities. the european union, in return, is a very important trade and investment partner for kazakhstan: more than half of the total foreign and direct investment in the country comes from eu investors. over the past years, we have increased cooperation, have had frequent high-level meetings and launched negotiations for a new enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement. the negotiation of the new agreement proves the importance of kazakhstan for the eu, and is the recognition of our strong economic and strategic relations. however, as underlined by the vice president/high representative on many occasions before, the enhancement of eu-kazakhstan relations is not independent of the advancement of domestic political reforms and the protection and promotion of human rights in kazakhstan. this is a priority for the european parliament but also for the european union. the european union has been observing the political and human rights related developments in kazakhstan since the tragic events of zhanaozen in december 2011 with serious concern. this included the monitoring of the trials of the people accused of inciting or participating in the violent events of zhanaozen, by the eu delegation in astana, in line with the parliament’s appeals to do so in its resolution of 15 march 2012. we have seen several procedural shortcomings in the trial processes and fear that the verdicts given have been mainly based on political activism and the general involvement of the defendants in trade union or opposition movements. the high representative/vice-president ashton has encouraged, and will continue to encourage, the kazakh authorities to review the trial processes, in line with the international commitments and obligations of kazakhstan. the eu has also called for the right to a free, fair and transparent appeal process for mr kozlov and all other defendants. we fully support parliament when it calls on kazakhstan as a member of the venice commission, and also as a newly elected member of the un human rights council, to demonstrate its strong commitment to human rights, including the freedoms of speech, of assembly, of association and of religion and belief. the european union will continue to make this point in all bilateral contacts and cooperation fora, as we did just last week again during the eu-kazakhstan cooperation committee meeting and will do during upcoming negotiation rounds on the new pca. the respect for democracy, the principles of international law, fundamental freedoms and human rights is an essential component of the new eu-kazakhstan agreement. this means that, once the new agreement enters into force, the violation of this essential element could lead to the suspension of parts or all of the agreement. this is in line with the report where the honourable members of the parliament stress that, although used rarely, the suspension of the application of any pca is possible in the case of serious breaches of human rights. in this regard, the pca will strengthen the dialogue with kazakhstan on human rights through our regular dialogues. human rights will undoubtedly be raised by high representative/vice-president ashton during her upcoming visit to astana next week. as also called for by the report, the commission services and the eeas are doing their utmost to ensure that the new agreement is a comprehensive one, with emphasis on political, legal, economic and social reforms. in line with this, our aim is to broaden the scope of our cooperation with kazakhstan in a number of areas and also help the kazakh authorities’ reform and modernisation efforts. this includes encouraging kazakhstan’s efforts for legislative conformity with the eu acquis and wto rules. kazakhstan has the eu’s full support for wto accession, and in particular an early conclusion of the ongoing negotiations. it is likely that the negotiations on the new pca will be concluded following kazakhstan’s wto accession, so the negotiations of the pca are based on this assumption. in this regard, the european union expects that the customs union between kazakhstan, russia and belarus will not constitute a barrier for enhanced cooperation with the european union – as also stated in the european parliament report. the negotiation of a new pca is not a simple or short process. through this process, the european union is committed to standing alongside kazakhstan and its citizens, both as a friend and as a partner, on the path of political reform and economic development. in this endeavour, we will continue to provide full information to parliament, as we have been doing so far. we count on the support of parliament and we look forward to the resolution that you will adopt tomorrow.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a multiannual plan for the sustainable management of the baltic salmon stock. salmon stocks in some 30 baltic fisheries are threatened by a loss of genetic diversity. the baltic salmon stock should be exploited in accordance with the maximum allowable catch principle and in a way that is sustainable and that protects its diversity. i agree that in order to strengthen the control of salmon fishing, at least 50% of the fish landed in the member states should be inspected, that more attention should be paid to the declaration of catches and that more inspections in ports should be carried out. i support the proposal to introduce comprehensive controls and accountability for all types of recreational fishing. it is essential that the european fisheries fund (eff) provides financial support for the direct recovery of salmon stocks.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the context of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp), the multiannual plan for the conservation of the baltic salmon stock is a vital part of the management of marine resources. in order to adequately assess the extent of the baltic sea resources, a comprehensive consultation of stakeholders has been carried out. the information obtained during this process indicates that there is a lack of a large number of key data, which has made the preparation of this report more difficult. in the absence of adequate control and information, recreational fishing, not marked as 'service vessel', has led to an uncontrolled expansion of recreational fisheries, thus having a significant impact on the size of the baltic salmon stock. it is worth noting that the development of fisheries management plans for european union waters requires a comprehensive consultation of stakeholders in order to find compromise solutions that protect the environment and ensure the sustainable development of fisheries. i would therefore welcome stricter controls on catches and would consider it appropriate to control at least 50% of the fish landed in each member state to ensure that a sufficient level of control is in place, thus contributing to the recovery of salmon stocks.
