in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to amend the regulation on the conservation of fishery resources. the proposal aims to extend the rules on technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms until the adoption of a regional system of technical measures under the common fisheries policy. these measures lay down rules on minimum landing sizes, minimum mesh size, prohibited fishing periods, etc. although the temporary cessation of these measures would be detrimental to the conservation of fish stocks. i agree with the proposals made for the development of these measures in the light of scientific advice, in order to ensure the safety of fishermen and to prevent unfair fishing practices. i agree that these measures should be developed with a regional approach, i.e. they should be developed for specific cases and zones rather than set as general rules for all member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because technical measures for the conservation of fisheries resources play a central role in the annual decisions on fishing opportunities. more specifically, these conservation measures are the rules that fishermen have to follow on a daily basis when fishing. these measures concern the minimum landing size, the minimum mesh size, the zones and the closure periods, the limitation of the catch, the criteria for the use of fishing gear and the use of the means to ensure a wider choice of fishing gear and gear designed to protect the marine environment and to contribute to the objectives of the common fisheries policy (cfp). in addition to extending the validity of the current technical measures, the proposed text updates the existing measures in line with the recommendations of stecf and the ices and also refers to the measures to reduce discards in the north-east atlantic as agreed with norway and the faroe islands in 2010, but not yet transposed into eu legislation. it is disappointing that, instead of a permanent solution being found in time, parliament has received another proposal for transitional technical measures. european fishermen need legal clarity and the word 'temporarily' should not be taken too seriously.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because i support the provision that measures are needed to ensure that fish stocks are fished sustainably and that the ecosystems in which fish live are preserved. in addition, these measures need to be formulated and developed taking into account the variability of fisheries management and scientific advice. poor preparation or the setting of inadequate technical means may lead to the development of improper fishing practices and, in certain cases, to the risk to the life and safety of fishermen, which would be completely unacceptable.
in writing. - i support this resolution. it is essential to ensure that fish stocks are fished sustainably and that ecosystems are preserved. it should be noted that the cfp will not enter into force until next year. it is therefore appropriate to extend the validity of the rules on technical measures on the basis of the transitional regulation and in the interests of legal clarity. it should be noted that technical measures based on scientific research are a guarantee of sustainable fishing and the protection of the right fishermen and their continuous application must therefore be ensured. on the other hand, they cannot be regarded as rules of a general nature and must be limited to specific cases and defined areas on a regional basis.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal to ban the practice of shark finning on board ships. the practice of removing the fins of sharks, often while they are still alive, is intolerable, as it not only threatens the sustainability of some shark species, but also results in the loss of food components. regulation no 1185/2003 provides for an exemption from the prohibition on shark finning for vessels holding special fishing permits, which the commission is seeking to repeal. i agree that, in the absence of evidence that the practice of removing fins actually exists in eu waters and on board ships, this commission proposal is contrary to the principle that policy action should be based on scientific evidence. the aim is to obtain more accurate information on this matter and i therefore support the proposals set out here on the obligation for shipowners to report the total number and weight of shark species caught and on the obligation to always land fins and carcass together in the same port. i also agree that if the local authorities cannot ensure adequate control of fishing, the masters of the vessels should hire an independent body to carry out such control.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the practice of shark finning is environmentally unacceptable, because it threatens the sustainability of some species of sharks that are fished, and also socially and economically because it results in the loss of commercially valuable food components, and morally because it is a practice that is totally disregardful of animal life. it is therefore necessary to reject this practice unequivocally and to take appropriate measures to ensure that it is effectively prohibited in eu waters and on community vessels. in the absence of data to establish that shark finning is practised on eu vessels, the commission decided to propose the abolition of the exception to the prohibition of shark finning on community fishing vessels, which, as already mentioned, currently allows such practice with special fishing permits and subject to the provisions of this regulation. i believe that all the proposals in this draft report are useful in addressing two concerns of the commission: ensuring compliance with the ban on removing fins and collecting scientific data on good governance; concerns of the sector; ensuring legitimate economic and social interests; and concerns of ngos; protecting shark stocks.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the practice of deliberately removing fins, i.e. cutting off the fins of sharks on board ships and dumping their bodies at sea, has been officially banned in the european union since 2003 by a regulation. however, the regulation provides for the possibility of using exceptions to obtain 'special authorisations' and in two member states, spain and portugal, this exception has become the norm. such a complex system, which allows the removal of fins on board a vessel if the ratio of fins to carcass does not exceed 5% by weight, in principle prevents effective control. it is indeed difficult to verify that this requirement is met, especially if the landing of the fins and carcases takes place in different ports. i therefore supported this proposal, which is based on the method of requiring that the fins are not cut. this should be the only effective method to combat fin removal and to enable member states to comply with the regulation in a simple, effective and inexpensive manner.
in writing. - i support this resolution because the practice of removing the fins of sharks and dumping the remaining part of the shark into the sea is unjustified and should be banned. in this context, it is essential that a proper 'untrimmed feathers' policy is implemented at eu level to prevent such feather removal practices. in addition, a strict control mechanism should be established to close legal loopholes and to address problems related to the application of the fin-to-carcase ratio. in particular, the current derogation should be reduced and the obligation to land both fins and carcases in the same port should be respected. on the other hand, we must ensure that the prohibition on removing the fins will not have a significant impact on the profitability of the business and the safety of the crew.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the accession of eight third countries to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention establishes a framework for cooperation between states in cases of child abduction, provides for the jurisdiction of courts and the law applicable to the question of the child's place of residence, and provides for the prompt return of abducted children to their country of residence. for legal reasons, the council decided to postpone the consultation of parliament and the accession of these countries to the hague convention. i agree with the recommendations that the council should immediately resume the procedure for accession of the above countries to the hague convention and to that end consult the ep. i agree that in defending the interests of its citizens, the council should not prevent the eu from acting properly for alleged legal reasons.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is of the utmost importance to establish a framework within which participating states can cooperate in order to find solutions in cases of international child abduction. it is necessary to provide for the courts with jurisdiction and the law applicable to the decision on the child's place of residence. recommendations are now being made to the council that it should immediately continue the procedure for taking those decisions. in view of the interests of eu citizens who would benefit from these decisions being taken, it should not prevent the european union from acting properly for alleged legal reasons.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of the utmost importance, as it establishes a framework within which the participating states can cooperate to find solutions in cases of international child abduction, provides for the courts with jurisdiction and the law applicable to the decision on the child's place of residence. the convention also provides for the prompt return of abducted children to their country of residence. the convention shall apply only in relations between the parties which have ratified or acceded to it. accession of new countries requires the consent of the states which are already members in order for the convention to apply to their relations. the european union has already exercised its internal competence in the field of international child abduction, in particular by adopting council regulation (ec) no 2201/2003 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters and matters of parental responsibility. the council should continue the procedure for adopting those proposed decisions without delay. to this end, it should consult parliament on the eight proposed decisions. in view of the interests of eu citizens who would benefit from these decisions being taken, it should not prevent the european union from acting properly for alleged legal reasons.
in writing. - i support this resolution. it should be noted that the protection of children's rights is a matter of public interest and that it is therefore necessary to constantly seek the best solution in the child's best interests. very often, child disputes take on an international dimension and present the problem of illegal child removal. in this context, it is necessary to ensure the implementation of the provisions of this convention at international level. the accession process of new countries must not be delayed. we must protect children from the harmful effects of their illegal removal or retention. it is also necessary to ensure that the return of children to the state of their habitual residence is carried out expeditiously and that the right of parents to visit their child is properly enforced.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it confirms the european parliament's position that the internet must be a public space in which human rights and freedoms are respected. the internet must remain free and open and there can be no talk of any offers that could seriously threaten the open and competitive nature of the internet. the report calls on the european council to coordinate negotiations on the revision of international telecommunications regulations and to rely on information gathered from a wide range of actors. i believe that in the further development of telecommunications, the issues of internet governance and related regulation should continue to be defined in detail and at different levels.
in writing. - i support this resolution. in view of the importance of electronic communications policy, an open and robust legal framework should be established and a model based on consumer interests and multilateralism applied. any amendments to international telecommunications regulations should be compatible with eu law. it should be noted that greater attention should be paid to the preparation of the 2012 world conference on international telecommunications, given its importance for society. i believe that only by working together can we protect the openness of the internet, the rights of users and the proper implementation of the principles of the free market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution on the doha climate change conference at the end of november. the doha conference will negotiate a global, legally binding agreement on climate change, which should replace the kyoto protocol from 2020. i agree that the main objectives of the eu delegation to the negotiations should be to set a more ambitious greenhouse gas mitigation agenda and to move towards a global agreement on climate change. i support the proposals that the eu should reduce its carbon dioxide emissions by 30% by 2020 compared to 1990. i agree that the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol should start on 1 january 2013 and that the transition to the new international system should be completed by 2020. it is also necessary to seek to mobilise the green climate fund for developing countries.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the joint resolution recognises that climate change is an unavoidable and possibly irreversible threat to humanity and that this issue must be addressed at international level by all countries. as recent research shows that, for example, the effects of climate change in the arctic are more rapid and more pronounced than previously predicted, as investments in the energy sector very often take 30 years or more, and as new projects and policies take a long time to plan, this clearly demonstrates the need for new energy action worldwide. the eu should take a leadership role in the fight against climate change and reach a legally binding and binding agreement on a common long-term effort to mitigate climate change. it is important to note that after 2012 - the last financial year of the 'rapid start' (the commitment of usd 30 billion over three years made in copenhagen) - there is no certainty about climate finance. it is worth stressing that the current economic crisis cannot be the end of inaction or of the refusal to provide funds for adaptation measures in developing countries.
in writing. − the fight against climate change is a fairly new eu policy area. while we are considering a host of new legislation to reduce the climate impact of human economic activity, we have not made much progress in this area internationally. i agree with the vast majority of the provisions in the resolution, but i am convinced that they will remain mere words unless the european union is able to concentrate the efforts of all member states and finally speak with one voice in the international climate policy arena.
in writing. - i support this resolution. it is worth noting that doha will help lay the foundations for the global agreement on climate change in 2015. in this context, it is crucial that the eu succeeds in persuading its partners around the world to take more decisive action to join the international agreement. only by working together to reduce emissions will we preserve fair competition and avoid disastrous changes for all of humanity. in order to address the negative impacts of climate change, it is necessary to seek innovative and additional sources of financing. increased financial and technical support should be provided to developing countries and the poorest and most vulnerable countries. i think it is appropriate to include the cancún agreement provisions in the draft eu legislation under preparation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the definition of the strategic interests of eu enlargement policy. the eu's enlargement policy is one of the most important instruments for promoting democratic values, respect for human rights and freedoms, security and stability in the european region. at the same time, the eu must be able to integrate new member states financially, institutionally and politically, and the readiness assessments should remain objective, fair and based on the country's progress towards meeting the copenhagen criteria. the economic crisis has led to a decline in the popularity of eu enlargement, both in the member states and in the candidate countries. i agree with the suggestions that the eu needs a new communication strategy to spread information about eu enlargement policy through civil society, trade unions and ngos and bring it closer to eu citizens. the commission should carry out detailed impact assessments each time it considers a country's eu accession request. i agree that a strong focus should be placed on an effective and independent judiciary, which strengthens citizens' trust in the rule of law, the development of tolerance, the promotion of neighbourly relations and an atmosphere of regional cooperation, etc.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the enlargement process has a major impact on the eu itself, enabling it to better define its identity, objectives, values and policies and to better communicate these to its citizens. i believe it is important that the eu and the candidate countries uphold all their obligations, commitments and conditions to ensure the success of future enlargement, inter alia by providing assistance to the countries concerned to meet the eu membership criteria. i believe that enlargement policy is a sound policy and that compliance with the copenhagen criteria remains an essential basis for eu membership and that due account should be taken of the union's capacity for integration. i believe it is essential that the candidate countries make progress in the areas of democracy, human rights and reconciliation processes. these areas should be a constant focus of the enlargement process and should be reflected in the financial instruments.
in writing. - i voted for this document. i am a strong supporter of the enlargement process and believe that enlargement policy must remain a credible policy, supported by both the eu and the candidate and potential candidate countries. i would therefore stress the importance of the eu and the candidate and potential candidate countries fulfilling all their obligations, respecting all commitments and creating the conditions for the success of future enlargement, inter alia, by providing assistance to the countries concerned to meet the eu membership criteria. i also recognise the benefits of the enlargement and accession process for the citizens of the candidate and potential candidate countries and for the citizens of the eu.
in writing. - i voted yes. it is important that the european parliament has expressed its strong position in support of the continuity of the eu's enlargement policy. enlargement policy is one of the main and most effective tools of eu soft power. the eu's membership drive is a driving force for internal reforms, and contributes to the political, economic and even social transformation of those seeking eu membership. there is no doubt that enlargement opens up new opportunities for the eu as a whole and for its citizens. of course, this is not an easy process, and we often face some disappointment. however, it is not without reason that the text of the ep resolution begins with a reference to article 49 of the treaty on european union. i believe that the door of enlargement should not be closed to any european country which expresses its desire for european integration and shows concrete progress. there is another dimension to eu enlargement - a process that promotes peace and stability through deepening integration, democratisation - the ideas for which the eu was awarded the nobel peace prize.
in writing. − i support this resolution, since the benefits of enlargement policy are undeniable and it is therefore necessary to ensure the consistency and stability of this policy. it is vital that each country joining the eu has resolved its major bilateral issues and major disputes, including border disputes. given the complexity and nature of certain disputes, which sometimes cannot be resolved by the parties independently, constructively and peacefully, a special role is assigned to the commission and the council. i therefore support the proposal to call on these institutions to establish an arbitration mechanism to settle bilateral and multilateral disputes. however, the reform process should be given a new impetus, while maintaining a strict prohibition of discrimination in any form or nature.
in writing. − enlargement and cohesion have always served as a foundation for the future of the european union. the enlargement process has brought peace, stability and prosperity to many parts of europe and has allowed for the diffusion of norms such as human rights, environmental protection and liberal democracy. the eu should continue to support the accession process for candidate countries, provided said countries conform to eu standards on social, economic and political issues. despite the current european financial crisis, the eu should continue to support and fund the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa), as this mechanism helps to stabilise candidate countries and prepare them for their acceptance into the eu. i voted in favour of this report because it urges to take a focused approach to integration. the eu’s capacity to integrate and to incorporate each new candidate country should be closely monitored and evaluated by the commission to avoid impairing the ability of the eu to fulfil its economic, political and social objectives.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which expresses grave concerns over the situation in gaza and israel and commends the cessation of hostilities which cause unjustifiable suffering of innocent civilians. it is of utmost importance that an urgent de-escalation and cessation of hostilities takes place immediately. all sides must fully respect and abide by international humanitarian law. the situation in the region clearly shows that a two-state solution allowing both sides to live side-by-side in peace and security is the only solution in the current situation. the mediating efforts by egypt to achieve a ceasefire are very much welcome but it is necessary to address also the core of the problem in order to have the ceasefire which would be broad and sustainable as well as to ensure stability in the region.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution on the implementation of the common security and defence policy. the common security and defence policy is not a luxury or an anecdote. on the contrary, it is a strategic necessity for the european union. i support the rapporteur’s view that, even though nato still is a cornerstone of our continent’s common defence, even though the transatlantic partnership must be reaffirmed and is irreplaceable, there are cases of crises which affect our security, and in which nato cannot intervene (the georgian crisis for example, and african conflicts in general), or in which the united states deem that they do not have to intervene. we must admit that the strategic challenges which we are facing are huge and unprecedented: a structural and lasting decrease of defence budgets in the european countries, a reorientation of us priorities, and volatility and extreme diversity of threats. therefore, the european countries must make a following choice: either suffer a collective strategic drop, or pull themselves together and fully use the csdp’s potential, however modest it may be. i urge member states to choose the latter way.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the implementation of the common security and defence policy (csdp). the eu carries out operational missions in third countries on the basis of the csdp. the purpose of these missions is to maintain peace and strengthen international security, based on the civilian and military means provided by the member states. the civil and military capacity for conflict prevention and crisis management between states needs to be strengthened, and i therefore support the measures set out in the proposal. i support calls for the establishment of an eu operations headquarters to carry out civilian missions and military operations alongside the european external action service. i agree that public-private partnerships in the field of air transport should be strengthened to enable humanitarian relief in the event of disasters and the transport of materials and personnel through csdp missions. i believe that more support is needed for the european defence agency, the eu satellite centre and the eu security and defence college in order to implement the eu's security and defence policy more effectively.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the european union should be a full-fledged political actor at international level in order to promote peace and security at international level, to protect its interests in the world and to ensure the security of its citizens. particularly at a time of major geostrategic shifts in the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the common security and defence policy (csdp), in particular due to the major upheavals in the middle east and north africa, as well as the emergence of new international actors with ambitions at regional or even global level, and the shift of us defence policy priorities towards the asia-pacific region, it is important for the eu to consolidate its strategic autonomy in order to implement a robust and effective foreign, security and defence policy. strategic autonomy should be built through liaison with nato and other organisations and the development of a global common position among eu countries that ensures consistency, acts in solidarity and uses all available tools and mechanisms to ensure peace and the security of citizens.
in writing. - i voted yes. in the context of economic and financial difficulties, countries face challenges that limit eu member states' spending on defence. this is not just a matter of nato commitments, it primarily affects national capacities, loss of expertise, decline of industry, while negatively affecting the effectiveness of the eu csdp. the international context the emerging crisis in the eu's immediate neighbourhood, the arming of some third countries the inability to relax and rest on the laurels of relative security. given the limited resources, it is necessary to focus on capacity building and sharing. however, the eu csdp should not claim to duplicate any nato functions.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the development of an eu policy of mutual defence and solidarity. a stronger and more capable european defence is necessary to ensure the same security guarantees for all citizens of the union. the treaty of lisbon provided for a mutual defence and solidarity clause. under this provision, member states undertake to assist each other in the event of a terrorist attack or natural or man-made disaster. i support the proposal to establish a practical procedure and guidelines to ensure an effective response in the event of an attack by a member state and to provide for an analysis of the role of the eu institutions in this context. both the eu and the member states must carry out joint hazard and risk assessments on a regular basis, based on the analysis of intelligence data. in order to avoid duplication of effort and waste of resources, it is necessary to ensure closer political cooperation between the eu high representative and the nato secretary-general.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the eu recognises an international order based on effective multilateralism, which is based on international law; this is based on the european conviction that no country can face the new threats alone. it is important to note that the fight against international terrorism remains a priority for the eu in the areas of defence and security, and it is therefore necessary to ensure that all member states have a common strategy and response in place. while each member state has primary responsibility for crisis management in its own territory, this communication promotes and gradually shapes a common defence policy that would strengthen the european identity and the eu's strategic advantage. it is important to note that the security of the eu member states is indivisible and all eu citizens should have the same security guarantees and the same level of protection against traditional and non-traditional threats.
in writing. − i voted for this document because i support the idea that the security of eu member states is indivisible and that all eu citizens should have the same security guarantees and the same level of protection against traditional and non-traditional threats. i believe that the defence of peace, security, democracy, human rights, the rule of law and the freedoms that are essential to the well-being of our peoples in europe must remain the primary objective and duty of the european countries and the union. recently, security challenges have been confronted by a number of complex and evolving threats, such as international terrorism, proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, fragmentation of countries, frozen and unending conflicts, organised crime, the threat of cybercrime, energy scarcity, environmental degradation and related security risks, natural and man-made disasters, pandemics and many others. in addition, security and the fight against international terrorism are eu priorities and all member states should develop a common response and a common strategy.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which urges member states to complete without further delay their national cyber security and defence strategies and national contingency plans, and also to include cyber crisis management in crisis management plans and risk analyses. i support the rapporteur that the eu is currently missing an exhaustive overview of the existing cyber security challenges and is also lacking common definitions, standards and a united approach to these threats. politically-motivated cyber attacks are targeting not only the information systems but also critical infrastructures of the member states which are seeking to implement a crucial task in creating mutual trust between the state and private sector actors by developing frameworks for rapid information exchanges while guaranteeing anonymity of the private sector partners. one of ways to strengthen cyber security and defence is to enhance the role of the european defence agency and the european network and information security agency (enisa) in assisting member states, in helping to pool and share experience and in developing good practices.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on eu cybersecurity and defence. in today's globalised world, with the increase in cyber threats and attacks and the threat to the security and stability of states, it is essential that the european union develops a stronger policy for a high level of eu network and information security. a comprehensive eu cybersecurity strategy is needed, providing a definition of cybersecurity and defence, cyberattack. the strategy should take into account good practices in member states that already have national cybersecurity strategies. i support the proposal to strengthen the action of the eu computer emergency response teams (cert) and the national certs and to develop national contingency plans to be used in the event of a cyber attack. it is necessary to establish an eu cyber coordination office. i support calls for the european defence agency (eda) to strengthen cooperation with nato, the european cybercrime centre europol and the joint cyber defence training centre (ccdcoe) and to focus on capacity building, training and information exchange.
in writing. − i voted for this report because all countries, not only in the eu but also in the world, are heavily dependent on information and communication technologies. with almost two billion users worldwide, cyberspace has become a powerful tool for spreading democratic ideas, bringing together those seeking to realize the aspirations of freedom and fighting dictatorial regimes. it is worth noting that most high-profile cyber-attacks that threaten national or international security and defence are never identified and prosecuted. similarly, there is no international agreement on how to respond to state-sponsored cyberattacks against another state, nor has it been decided whether such actions could be considered a casus belli. given the recent dramatic increase in cyber problems, threats and attacks, it is necessary to adopt a resolution on a comprehensive protection system that would not, at the same time, undermine the open and free flow of cyber traffic.
in writing. - i spoke for this document. in today's globalised world, the eu and its member states have become highly dependent on a secure cyberspace, the secure use of information and digital technologies and flexible and reliable information services. the very rapid increase in cyber-related problems, threats and attacks poses a serious threat to the security, defence, stability and competitiveness of states and the private sector. since most of the most obvious and disruptive cyber incidents are now politically motivated, and the vast majority of cyber incidents are primitive, and the threat to critical infrastructure is becoming increasingly complex, this is precisely why a robust protection system is needed. however, the eu and its member states face numerous political, legislative and organisational obstacles to developing a comprehensive and unified approach to cyber defence and cyber security, as common definitions, standards and tools are lacking in the sensitive and vulnerable area of cyber security.
in writing. − i support this resolution as cybersecurity and defence is a highly topical security issue in both the national and eu minds. the latest information technology is both good and bad. in view of the growing threat of cyber threats and the increasing frequency of attacks, the eu needs to play a more active role in initiating initiatives to strengthen cyber security. in particular, a comprehensive eu cybersecurity strategy should be developed. this strategy should be flexible and easily adaptable to continuous developments in order to enhance cybersecurity. another important aspect is the need to pursue closer cooperation with all institutions, private business, society, and to maintain a clear direction, political will.
in writing. − cyber-security and defence is a pressing issue in today’s increasingly digital world; however, there is no international model for responding to cyber-attacks. i voted in favour of this report because recent cyber-attacks against governments and corporations have demonstrated the need to take steps to ensure that the eu and its member states possess sufficient security measures to defend against potential cyber-attacks. maximum protection and preservation of digital freedoms and privacy of eu citizens is vital, as online freedom is a core aspect of respect for human rights. additionally, the protection of both national and eu security and defence initiatives, such as the common security and defence policy (csdp), should remain a top priority. coordination and cooperation between eu member states (especially between those who already have national cyber-security strategies in place) will go a long way towards ensuring the digital safety of the eu and its citizens. all eu institutions and agencies must be on the same page in terms of cyber-security – horizontal cooperation is key in achieving a common eu approach to cyber-defence.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the role of the common security and defence policy (csdp) in the event of climate crises and natural disasters (csdp). the eu carries out operational missions in third countries on the basis of the csdp. the purpose of these missions is to maintain peace and strengthen international security, based on the civilian and military means provided by the member states. i support the proposals made to include the adverse impact of climate change and natural disasters on peace and security in all the strategic documents of the cfsp and csdp. i believe that the eu should develop its capacity to collect and analyse data, using the structures of the eu satellite centre and the eu intelligence analysis centre. i support calls on the commission to draw up contingency plans for the eu to respond to natural disasters outside the eu that affect eu security.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it expresses parliament's position on the impact of climate change on global security, peace and stability. it is worth noting that in recent years, the issue of climate change as the greatest threat to global security has been eclipsed in public debate and policy dialogue by the economic and financial crises. the increasing frequency of extreme weather events in recent years has been increasing the cost to the global economy, not only in developing countries but also globally. european countries are no exception. in this context, the eu should make every effort to reduce the importance of disaster risk, paying particular attention to women and children, who are the most vulnerable in crises. it is worth noting that complex crises can be foreseen and should be prevented by a comprehensive approach covering the policies under the common foreign and security policy (cfsp) and the common security and defence policy (csdp), as well as humanitarian and development assistance policies.
in writing. - i voted for this document. it is recognised that climate change has implications for global security, peace and stability. the increasing frequency of extreme weather events in recent years has led to an increasing cost to the global economy, not only in developing countries but also worldwide, both in terms of direct recovery and aid costs and in terms of indirect costs associated with increases in insurance, product and service prices. these events also pose a growing threat to international peace and human security. the fight against climate change through security measures can therefore be a positive one, but it is only one component of the eu's climate action, which aims to use political and economic means to mitigate and adapt to climate change.
in writing. − climate change has a clear impact on security, and while no conflict has been identified to date as being caused by climate change alone, the implications of natural disasters and climate change for international security must be taken into account. i therefore support the inclusion of the negative impacts of climate change and natural disasters on peace, security and stability in the strategic planning of the cfsp and the csdp, in order to strengthen the capacity for rapid response and coordination of action, to develop the military sector's expertise, analysis and planning and knowledge sharing in this area, and to assess the negative environmental impacts of industry and activities with a view to reducing them.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report on the state of play of the negotiations on the eu-kazakhstan enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement. the new agreement aims to lay down detailed provisions for the further development of eu-kazakhstan relations in areas such as human rights, good governance and democratisation, economic development, trade and investment, energy and transport. i support the proposal to support the implementation of political reforms and institutional capacity building, as well as the call for kazakhstan to remove tariff and non-tariff barriers in order to expand trade, in particular trade in services, and foreign investment. it is also necessary to increase technical assistance to kazakhstan in the field of water resources management. i agree that an effective dispute settlement procedure should be introduced to ensure that the agreement reached is respected.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the eu and kazakhstan seek to deepen and expand their relations and closer cooperation is mutually beneficial. it is worth noting that kazakhstan is one of the key countries that has played a positive role in central asia, as it has made efforts to develop good neighbourly relations, to renew regional cooperation and to resolve bilateral issues through peaceful means. in this way, in pursuit of better democratic rights and principles of equality, kazakhstan is admitted to the venice commission of the council of europe. the kazakh authorities, in cooperation with ngos, have also taken important steps in western kazakhstan to improve the situation of the population in the region, especially the striking workers. this initiative by kazakhstan in the central asian region is not only commendable but also deserves further close cooperation and support from the eu. it is also important to note that the eu is kazakhstan's main trading partner and largest investor in the country. by clearly expressing its desire to move towards eu standards and its social and economic model, which will require comprehensive reform of the kazakh state and public administration, kazakhstan has already demonstrated its ability to achieve important results in poverty reduction, public health and education. it is expected that this positive initiative and influence of kazakhstan will not diminish in the future.
in writing. − i abstained in the vote on the resolution on the negotiation of a more comprehensive eu-kazakhstan partnership and cooperation agreement, because i am confident that the kazakh regime will see this resolution as a moral and political compromise of the eu, which in no way obliges it to respect human rights and to stop persecuting critics and dissidents of the regime, but rather allows it to subtly violate human rights and to explain this by the difficulties of its transition democracy. this resolution is out of date, it sends the wrong signal to kazakhstan and it is an ep mistake. i therefore abstained and would have supported the postponement of the adoption of this document.
in writing. − i voted for this document because the eu and kazakhstan are seeking to deepen and broaden their relations. closer cooperation should benefit both the eu and the people of kazakhstan. the negotiations for a new partnership and cooperation agreement should provide for detailed provisions on the scope for cooperation and socio-economic development, as well as the necessary political and economic reforms, given the close links between development in the social and economic spheres. kazakhstan has played a positive role in central asia by making efforts to develop good neighbourly relations with neighbouring countries, to renew regional cooperation and to resolve bilateral issues through peaceful means. negotiating position ensure that the new partnership and cooperation agreement sets out detailed provisions for the further development of relations in all priority areas, including human rights, the rule of law, good governance and democratisation, youth and education, economic development, trade and investment, energy and transport, environmental sustainability and water, and tackling common threats and challenges.
in writing. − kazakhstan is a growing economic and political regional power in central asia. the country possesses vast mineral reserves and deposits of fossil fuels, but is also looking to diversify and modernise its economy. i voted in favour of this report because it argues that the eu would be well advised to deepen relations with kazakhstan in the form of an enhanced partnership and cooperation agreement (pca). such an initiative would bring significant economic benefits (reduced tariffs, foreign investment, energy cooperation, economic and development assistance) to both partners as well as increased socio-political stability in central asia. however, to achieve success in such a pca, kazakhstan must improve its standing on many critical issues. prior to the establishment of a pca, kazakhstan must reform its standards on human rights, democracy, and transparency of governance. on the economic side, kazakhstan must comply with all wto regulations and procedures to facilitate trade with the eu. additionally, increased environmental regulation and protection (especially in the realm of water conservation) is a must – the eu can provide technical assistance on this issue. more importantly, kazakhstan must strengthen its respect for rule of law and freedom of the press. the eu supports the country’s on-going efforts to strengthen workers’ rights and fight corruption.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the development of small-scale and traditional fisheries. in the context of the reform of the eu's common fisheries policy, it is necessary to establish rules for small-scale fisheries taking into account the specific characteristics and problems of such fisheries. small-scale fishing has a significant territorial, social and cultural impact on the mainland and islands. i support the proposals set out below to establish a community programme to support small-scale fisheries, to allocate an appropriate amount of the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) to this fisheries, and to give priority to projects that benefit all coastal communities. it is necessary to encourage the participation of young fishermen in the sector and to provide assistance in the field of vocational training. it is also important to establish support mechanisms to be used in case of emergency situations, such as natural disasters, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i believe that small-scale fisheries should be given greater consideration in the reform of the cfp. the challenges and opportunities of the cap need to be taken into account more fully and all three pillars of the reform - the basic regulation, the cfp regulation and the financial instrument implementing the cap (currently the emff) - need to be amended. small-scale fisheries are usually characterised by certain features, among others: close links with the economy, social structure, culture and traditions of coastal areas and communities, fishing relatively close to the shore and short sea stays, a greater direct role of manual labour, etc. the current view is that the european commission is proposing to continue the centralised management of the cap, which often results in out-of-date guidelines that are poorly understood by the sector (they are not involved in the discussion or drafting of the guidelines), are difficult to implement and often have the opposite results. moreover, the proposal to introduce a compulsory common system of exploitation of resources does not take account of the very different real situation of fisheries in the european union. the proposed application of this system could have a very negative impact on certain small-scale fisheries, as the concept of 'small-scale fisheries' is narrow and does not reflect the real situation. it is therefore necessary to ensure a programme to encourage the participation of young fishermen and women in the sector and to create mechanisms that benefit all coastal communities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this document because i agree that different rules for small-scale fishing should be established. small-scale fishing not only promotes social and economic cohesion and provides a source of livelihood for a large number of families, but is also a factor in the preservation of fishing communities in all coastal zones. i believe that in the fisheries sector it is important to adopt an approach that takes account of the biological, ecological and social levels in order to achieve a sustainable balance between the situation of existing resources in the various marine areas and the social and economic structure of coastal communities whose employment and well-being depend on fishing along the coast.
in writing. − small-scale and small-scale fisheries have been particularly badly affected by the economic and social crisis. however, in coastal regions it has remained a key factor in creating and maintaining jobs. in this context, i believe that the european maritime and fisheries fund should pay greater attention to small-scale fisheries. first, there is a need to focus more on social and economic objectives. it is necessary to ensure stability of markets and to create favourable conditions for the generation of higher incomes from small-scale fisheries. flexible and specific support mechanisms should be established to take account of the specific problems and needs of the sector.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for a new policy guideline for the common external fisheries policy. the external policy of the cap is very broad and covers fish caught outside the eu and imported into the eu for food, fish caught in eu waters and exported, and fish caught in eu waters that have been processed in a third country before being consumed in the eu. the proposal aims to promote the sustainability of eu fisheries beyond eu waters, including the outermost regions. i agree that in order to ensure sustainable fisheries, it is necessary to improve the availability of data on the catches of fish stocks caught in the eu or destined for the eu market and to ensure that information on the catches of local fleets and those of third countries is available. i support the proposal to ensure that vessel owners contribute more to the cost of fishing rights. it is also necessary to ensure the effective financial management of the support to the sector provided for in the agreements and to provide for the suspension of payments in the event of failure to achieve results.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important that the eu's fishing interests are properly and lawfully pursued. the eu is still the world's largest market, has one of the largest fleets flying its flag and is often ranked among the top three fishing regions. nevertheless, new emerging markets are developing rapidly, especially in asia. many of them seem to be failing in their duty as flag, port and market states or even in their fundamental human rights, creating unfair, even unbridled competition. it is worth noting that the basic principle should be implemented outside the eu in accordance with the same standards as those applied to operators operating in the european union. similarly, if an rfmo applies a higher standard to eu vessels operating in its territory than the cfp, then the higher standards should be included in the cfp as a whole. new systems for the fair and equitable allocation of resources among rfmo members, based on transparent ecological and social allocation criteria, while ensuring that management and safeguard measures are effectively implemented and enforced by all market participants, need to be adopted as a matter of urgency.
in writing. - i voted for this document. i welcomed the commission's communication and the many positive proposals it contained to promote the sustainability of eu fisheries and related activities outside eu waters, including in the outermost regions. i believe that it is essential to coordinate foreign and cooperation policies in order to establish sustainable fisheries agreements and to create the necessary synergies to contribute more effectively to the development of the third countries concerned, since the maintenance of fisheries agreements and the search for new fishing opportunities in third countries should be a priority objective of the external fisheries policy.
in writing. - recognising that the external aspects of the eu's fisheries policy are most closely linked to fishing areas outside the european continent, i would like to draw attention to the ticking bomb in our own pockets. the baltic sea has become virtually an internal sea of the eu. there are a number of bilateral, multilateral agreements and eu legislation regulating this area. but the baltic coast is also scaling the russian coast. unfortunately, it cannot be said that this country has yet achieved an equivalent level of environmental protection and conservation of fisheries resources. this issue could become particularly relevant if russia decides to build a third nord stream gas pipeline to the kaliningrad region. i therefore urge the commission to be vigilant and to respond not only to developments off the coasts of other continents but also to look in its own pocket more often.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to increase the participation of eu citizens in the 2014 european parliament elections. the resolution calls on european political parties to propose candidates for the post of president of the commission before the european elections. the debate on these candidates is intended to be a major focus of the 2014 european parliament election campaign, thereby encouraging citizens to take a more active part in the elections and to vote. the aim is also to select a number of future european commissioners from among the newly elected members of the european parliament, thus more effectively representing eu citizens. the resolution also calls for a greater gender balance in the commission. i support the proposals set out here and the proposal to hold the 2014 european elections at the end of may instead of june, in order to give the european parliament more time to prepare for the next elections for the president of the european commission.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, in the light of the commission's 2012 statement on the 2014 european elections, i believe it is important to encourage european political parties to nominate candidates for the post of president of the commission and to encourage member states to nominate both a male and a female candidate for this position. it is also important to further strengthen the political legitimacy of the parliament and the commission, taking into account their respective elections and the choice of their voters.

i want to point out a few potential problems. the european patent office is concentrating on improving machine translation in the main european patent languages (german, english, french), but much less attention is paid to improving machine translation in the languages of smaller countries, so that a good quality translation, for example, into lithuanian, which is a particularly difficult language, may have to wait for many years. i would therefore think that countries like lithuania need to provide for a sufficient transition period to allow patent applicants and industry to move smoothly from human to machine translation. it is also necessary to take into account that the translation of a patent is published in the public domain, informing the public of the exclusive rights of the patent proprietor, and that an incorrect translation may mislead industrial undertakings and lead to undesirable distortions.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to align the implementation of the energy star programme with the new us-eu agreement on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for stationery. under the new agreement, the programme will be operated under two separate product registration systems: products placed on the eu market will have to be registered by the european commission, while products placed on the us market will be registered by accredited third parties. energy star is an energy efficiency programme, and products qualifying for this programme use less energy and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. it has reduced the electricity consumption of eu stationery products (computers, printers, copiers, scanners, etc.) sold in the last three years by 16% and saved around eur 1.8 billion in taxes. i believe that 'energy star' is a dynamic policy tool that is well suited to the ever-changing ict products.

in writing. - i voted for this motion. pursuant to the agreement between the government of the united states of america and the european community on the harmonisation of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for stationary equipment, regulation (ec) no 106/2008 of the european parliament and of the council implements the energy star programme in the union. this regulation establishes union energy-efficiency labelling programmes for stationary equipment. i have agreed to the amendments to this regulation as the support from the energy star programme contributes to the achievement of the energy efficiency objectives of the member states and the union

in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the creation of a digital single market. e-commerce is now becoming an essential part of commerce and a key driver of competitiveness and technological innovation, creating many highly skilled jobs and enabling the eu to become a dynamic knowledge-based economy. the internet services could soon account for up to 20% of employment and economic growth in the eu, and i therefore agree with the need to rapidly remove obstacles to development in this area. it is necessary to facilitate cross-border access to products offered online, to address payment and delivery issues, and to protect and inform consumers. i agree with the need to facilitate dispute resolution procedures, to make the internet safer and to encourage investment in wireless connectivity, and i support the proposals set out in this paper for a pan-european system with harmonised data protection rules, a secure online payment system and an eu strategy on intellectual property rights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the impact of the internet economy has grown tremendously in recent years. this is clearly shown by the figures: in some g8 countries, the internet has created 20% of economic growth and 25% of new jobs over the last five years. however, the eu digital single market has not developed as fast as it could have, and we have not exploited all the opportunities offered by the digital economy. the current legal uncertainty is holding consumers and businesses back from trading across borders. as indicated in the latest consumer performance index on e-commerce, consumers can save in 13 out of 15 product categories for which price data have been collected. the study also showed that consumers have at least twice as much choice when shopping online as when shopping offline. european consumers already earn around eur 11.7 billion a year from online shopping for goods alone (equivalent to 0.12% of eu gdp). if e-commerce were to grow to 15% of total retail trade and if barriers to the digital single market were to be removed, the overall benefit to consumer welfare would be €204 billion (equivalent to 1.7% of eu gdp). currently, about 35% of internet users avoid shopping online because of concerns about payment security, lack of legal certainty, etc. the creation of an eu trustmark online would be another step to further strengthen the foundations already laid by the above-mentioned measures.
in writing. - i spoke for this document. we live in a time of great economic and technological change. the so-called digital revolution has undoubtedly changed our lives in many ways. the new ways of doing business, of interacting with other people, of finding information, of comparing products and prices, of learning, and many other things have changed dramatically. the digital revolution has also changed the way businesses operate, and the impact of the internet economy in recent years has been enormous. economic growth, job creation, consumer opportunities, product diversity, affordability and business opportunities are simply not covered. however, the digital single market in the european union has not developed as fast as it could have without taking full advantage of the digital economy. the current legal uncertainty is holding consumers and businesses back from trading across borders. a well-functioning digital economy is, of course, essential for the overall functioning of the eu economy. however, the free movement of digital services is currently seriously hampered by the existence of uneven rules at national level, with businesses in the european union facing numerous barriers to cross-border trade, mainly due to the different rules applied in the member states in areas such as consumer protection, vat, regulation of specific products and payment transactions, and this document will aim to remove these barriers.
in writing. − the document adopted today rightly calls for more active action by both the eu institutions and the member states to improve the shared use of the digital space. this approach is indeed necessary, especially given that the digital space is borderless, but the rules applied by the member states often differ. we must therefore harmonise them as soon as possible. at the same time, i would like to draw attention to another problem which has been less emphasized in this report. this is the protection of consumers in the digital space. although we have discussed the various aspects of such protection on many occasions - the protection of children, the protection of the networks themselves, secure purchases, etc. - i am convinced that it is now necessary to start discussions on the protection of consumers in a single and integrated digital market.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to improve access to credit for smes in support of internationalisation. smes in the eu create 75% of private sector jobs and have created as much as 80% of all new jobs in the last few years. however, only 25% of smes operate outside the member state in which they are established. the main reasons for this situation are the difficulty smes have in accessing information on foreign markets and on trade and investment opportunities abroad, and the lack of capital for most companies to start cross-border business. i support the proposals set out to allow smes to receive funding directly without using financial intermediaries and to allow these companies to benefit from simplified application procedures. i agree with the proposal to develop an eu export and import facility, under which additional support should be provided to smes seed capital, loans for new businesses, loan guarantees, export guarantees, etc. it is also necessary to encourage the private sector to be more active in financing smes. in order to improve the general awareness of the needs of smes, the collection of statistical data on the difficulties of these enterprises should be improved.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it sets out parliament's recommendations on improving access to investment finance for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). in the european union, smes account for 75% of private sector jobs and have created around 80% of all new jobs in the last five years. it is therefore surprising that only 25% of smes operate outside the member state in which they are established and less than 13% of them export to markets outside the eu. smes contributing to foreign direct investment are also few. several factors can be cited to explain the lack of internationalisation of smes. first, it is difficult for smes in the eu to obtain information on foreign markets and trade and investment opportunities abroad. second, many smes lack the capital to start operating globally, including financing cross-border business activities. in view of the above problems, i welcome the recent decision of the european commission to help small businesses to improve their market access opportunities in 2014-2020 through the enterprise competitiveness and smes programme. the new programme is expected to cost eur 2.5 billion. the programme could support around 40 000 enterprises and contribute to their internationalisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it is essential for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises wishing to engage in active export and import activities to have access to capital and to appropriate trade-related financing support. this is also essential for investing in third country markets and for increasing the ability of these companies to compete internationally. this document aims to improve the quality of information provided to smes and microenterprises on financing opportunities and trade financing instruments at national and eu level. the support provided to smes and microenterprises is expected to overcome the trade barriers that prevent eu companies from entering third country markets. in addition, the additional tailored import and export facility is expected to provide them with the opportunity to take advantage of all the growth and job creation opportunities associated with their internationalisation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for the establishment of the first eu strategy on digital freedom in external action, which aims to protect human rights in the digital space. communication online is intensifying both in the eu and globally, and new electronic social media can help to develop values such as access to information, freedom of expression, and encouraging people to engage in the development of democracy and human rights. digital freedoms are inherent in traditional human rights such as freedom of expression and assembly and therefore need to be protected. i support the proposals made to the commission to ensure that legal digital expression on the internet is not criminalised and that legislation is adopted to restrict such activity. i agree that the promotion and protection of digital freedoms must be integrated into all eu external action, funding and assistance policies.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the internet and new technologies are playing an increasingly important role in all our lives. in this digital world, there are several areas where the eu must act as a global player and exert its economic and political influence. given the potential of the open internet, while overly strict regulation would do more harm than good, it is necessary to update some rules to keep pace with technological developments and ensure democratic oversight. for example, ad hoc telephone and internet connections should be provided for the first critical hours following natural disasters or humanitarian crises. ict is also crucial for effective election monitoring. it is also important to note that the eu cannot credibly promote and defend digital freedoms in the world if they are not defended within the eu itself. although the eu is the world's most important market, the majority of internet companies are based in the us, forcing eu citizens to accept us consumer terms. the united states has a wide range of jurisdictions, including the united states, which are the largest providers of digital services in the world. this extraterritorial effect of us law should not limit the eu's ability to protect citizens' fundamental rights.
in writing. − several eu member states now consider internet access to be a fundamental human right. in this increasingly globalised world, access to the internet and digital freedom are vital tools that can facilitate everything from large-scale economic transactions to personal blog posts. the significance in foreign affairs of the internet and rapidly-developing digital technologies is becoming apparent quickly. many pressing developments regarding digital security exist. cyber-security and defence have become relevant issues, as online hackers have demonstrated their ability to threaten vital government and corporate structures. oppressive regimes have also harnessed digital technologies to monitor and control their populations. when guaranteeing the openness of the internet and the privacy of its users, we must ensure that cyber-security is not compromised and continue to condemn the use of digital technologies as a means of oppressing societies. i support the first eu digital freedom strategy because it will allow the eu to remain relevant and vigilant in the face of the digital security challenges of the 21st century.
