in writing. − as in the first reading in 2011, i am in favour of the proposal for an additional eur 46 million in macro-financial assistance to georgia under the commitment of the georgian donors' conference. it is a much-needed support to help mitigate the dual negative impact of the military conflict with russia and the global economic and financial crisis on the georgian economy. it is important that the commission actively support the appropriate absorption of this aid through economic convergence instruments with the eu in order to make it more sustainable. i hope that the remaining procedural issues between the council and the european parliament will be resolved as soon as possible and that the financial package will reach its addressee soon. at the same time, i hope that the new georgian government will continue to implement the necessary reforms, including the fight against corruption and fraud.
in writing. − the question of macro-financial assistance to georgia is very important for the concerned country itself and for its supporters. let me emphasise and remind you that georgia is developing its relations with the eu within the framework of the european neighbourhood policy. georgia is also a member state of the eastern partnership. taking into account the substance of the revised neighbourhood policy and its ‘more-for-more’ principle, i believe that the eu should support georgia’s economic stabilisation. furthermore, macro-financial assistance for georgia will stimulate modernisation and reform efforts in this eastern neighbour and will help this country to achieve eu standards. this assistance is particularly vital for georgia in view of georgia’s deteriorating economic situation and with regard to the ongoing negotiations of the association agreement and the deep and comprehensive free trade agreement with the eu. lithuania as the member state of the eu that will organise the eastern partnership summit in vilnius during its eu presidency in the second half of 2013 is actively seeking closer cooperation with its eastern neighbours. lithuania shares the european aspirations of these eastern partners and supports these neighbourhood countries on their way to the eu.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to extend the mandate of the european maritime safety agency (emsa). the purpose of the agency is to prevent pollution from ships, to ensure safe navigation and to monitor and evaluate eu legislation in this area. the revised regulation will extend the mandate of the emsa to prevent and respond to environmental disasters such as oil and gas spills. it is also planned that emsa will contribute to the fight against piracy at sea and improve training for seafarers. the cost to european taxpayers would be much lower if safe navigation were ensured by emsa rather than by each national authority on its own. the use of emsa's marine observation systems to provide the necessary information to other policy specialists would be much more cost-effective than the development of separate systems. i agree that it is necessary to ensure that the additional mandate of emsa is commensurate with its budget and staffing levels.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it expresses parliament's position on the proposed update of the regulation establishing the european maritime safety agency (emsa). since the establishment of the agency in 2003, the eu has been actively responding to oil pollution and is preparing to do so in the future. emsa contributes to the safety of shipping and the prevention of pollution from ships at sea, including the monitoring and evaluation of relevant eu legislation. much of its work consists of recommendations to the commission and/or the member states. it is generally recognised that it is an efficient, well-functioning organisation that can save member states a lot of money by acting at european level and thus ensuring economies of scale. emsa also provides better opportunities for cooperation with neighbouring countries. we therefore voted in favour of the amendments to the regulation which will soon extend the remit of the european maritime safety agency (emsa). the agency will now have to help eu countries combat pollution at sea following an accident on oil and gas platforms, as well as fighting piracy and cutting red tape. in addition, emsa's activities aim to ensure safe shipping between all eu countries, and i therefore believe it is important to continue to ensure that the agency's tasks continue to be fully reflected in its budget and staff numbers.
in writing. − as we emphasised in the first reading, in the current state of the marine environment, with the increasing economic activity at sea and the resulting new threats, emsa can and must be the body that coordinates actions to protect the marine environment, prevent environmental disasters and take preventive measures and measures in the event of such disasters. i also continue to believe that emsa could be the organisation to coordinate actions with relevant third country bodies in similar areas.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution which gives green light to a competitive european system and reduces costs for a european patent. also it is important to have a european patent with unitary effect, i.e. wide legal patent protection in the eu as patents for inventions with high market value are frequently subject to litigation; the lack of a single litigation system causes additional costs for the patent proprietor. i welcome this unanimous agreement between member states on the european patent after years of failed attempts for such an agreement. i agree that the european patent with unitary effect will broaden patent protection to all participating member states. this will increase business opportunities while opening up markets and contributing to the fulfilment of a true single market, which is necessary for the eu to get out of the recent economic crisis. moreover, the new system will help make the union a more attractive place to create and innovate, for both european and non-european inventors.
in writing. − i voted for this report because the eu has been working for more than a decade to create a common european patent system. the creation of a common patent system will in particular provide for much-needed simplification of the current system. this will reduce administrative barriers in europe and reduce the cost of patenting by up to 80%, thereby improving and protecting the free movement of goods in the internal market and facilitating innovation and entrepreneurship in europe. the high cost of granting european patents in some member states and the complexity of the process are the main reasons why patent holders are reluctant to apply for an eu patent. for example, the total cost of obtaining a european patent for a standard volume valid throughout the eu (including translation costs and the approximate costs for the patent agent and publication) is eur 22 000 26 000. the figures show that companies across the eu spend between €205 million and €230 million each year on translation, proofreading and professional expenses. the eu patent will not only reduce these costs to eur 680 per unit patent, but will also facilitate investment in research and development.
in writing. - i voted for this document. i believe that the creation of a common patent system will indeed, in particular, provide a much-needed simplification of the current system. secondly, it will reduce administrative burdens and patent costs in europe by up to 80%. this will enhance and protect the free movement of goods in the internal market and facilitate innovation and entrepreneurship in europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it expresses parliament's position on the commission's proposal for closer cooperation in the creation of a common patent system in the eu. a well-functioning patent system contributes to the development of a comprehensive economy. for several decades, member states have been working towards a common eu patent protection. in this context, it should be noted that the eu patent system is highly fragmented and not sufficiently competitive internationally. a european patent, which has been approved by 13 countries, is 13 times more expensive than in the united states and 11 times more expensive than in japan. therefore, during the consultation on the future patent system in europe, smes themselves drew attention to the need for specific support, in particular in relation to translation costs, patent research and legal protection. while this proposal is based on the working languages of the european patent office and has been developed after a considerable effort to reach a political compromise, it stresses the need to protect and promote as far as possible the english language, which is the most widely used in international trade relations. it is important that this regulation enters into force once the system of jurisdiction has been ratified by at least nine member states, including the three which have filed the most patent applications.
in writing. − i voted for this document because for almost half a century the member states have been working towards a common eu patent protection. the failure to reach an agreement on the community patent led to the so-called munich convention in 1973, which was subsequently signed by all the current eu member states. however, the centralised procedure provided for in the convention does not provide for the removal of the main obstacles to the improvement of the european patent system. in particular, it does not contribute to reducing the high level of legal uncertainty and the high costs associated with the granting and enforcement of patents. in view of these limitations, the patent system is highly fragmented and not sufficiently competitive internationally. it is sufficient to point out that a european patent, which has been approved by 13 countries, is 13 times more expensive than in the united states and 11 times more expensive than in japan. a well-functioning patent system, tailored to the real needs of users, is essential to boost the eu's economic growth and competitiveness. i also agree that specific measures should be put in place to help smes to access the european patent market and to benefit from innovation. legal instruments relating to generic patent protection therefore offer an excellent opportunity to meet the requirements of smes, especially in terms of costs and legal support.
in writing. − to ensure the competitiveness of eu industry and science, it is essential to ensure the best possible conditions for unitary patent protection throughout the european union. however, i cannot support this document because it does not take proper account of the specific features of the use of the less popular official eu languages. lithuanian, one of the oldest languages in use in the world, is sufficiently complex to allow the use of machine translation equipment to render accurately and clearly complex technical terms such as those used in patents. the use of such translation will undoubtedly cause additional hassle and costs for persons translating patents into lithuanian. i therefore abstained.
in writing. − i voted in favour of a unified eu patent litigation system. under the system in place today, national patents are granted by the patent offices of the member states or european patents are granted by the european patent office (epo). once a european patent has been granted, it is broken down into a strand of national patents governed by national law. the system is considered to be very expensive and complex, involving disputes in more than one country and often leading to conflicting decisions. the proposal aims to harmonise the system of settling disputes and to establish a unified patent court for this purpose. such a court would help reduce the cost of litigation, save eu businesses considerable money and ensure legal certainty by interpreting the law in the same way. i support calls for member states to conclude negotiations and ratify as soon as possible the international agreement establishing a common patent court.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is parliament's own-initiative report on the possible dispute over the patent jurisdiction system. an efficient european patent system can make a significant contribution to economic growth through innovation. european businesses, especially smes, need such a tool to respond to the current economic crisis and remain competitive on a global scale. the european parliament and the council are now in agreement on the need to abandon the current fragmented patent system. to this end, the possibility of establishing a general patent court is being considered. the creation of a unified patent court would greatly reduce the cost of litigation, as parties would no longer have to be involved in litigation in different countries at the same time. the studies show that the proposed dispute settlement system would save european businesses a lot of money. a functioning common patent court could ensure legal certainty by providing a uniform interpretation of the applicable law. it is of particular importance for smes that the judicial system to be established is effective and at the same time ensures high-quality decisions. i believe that parliament should continue to support efforts to create a single patent market that would ensure legal certainty and strengthen the competitiveness of businesses internationally.
in writing. - i voted for this document. i believe that the creation of a court is an appropriate and successful way of creating a coherent system for the settlement of patent disputes. the unified patent court will help to reduce the cost of litigation by eliminating the need for parties to litigate in different countries at the same time. the studies also show that the proposed dispute settlement system would save european companies a lot of money. finally, a functioning common patent court will provide legal certainty by ensuring a uniform interpretation of the applicable law.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal for enhanced cooperation between eu member states (un) in the creation of common patent protection. today, such protection in the eu can be granted by the national patent offices of the member states that issue national patents or by the european patent office (epo). however, patents issued by the office must be accompanied by a translation and certified in each of the vcs where protection is sought. the cost of accreditation in the eu is about eur 193 million per year, which makes the system very expensive and complex. the current proposal aims to enable eu patent holders to apply to the epo for joint protection in the territory of 25 member states. such a patent will ensure the same level of protection for their inventions in all 25 member states, and applications will be possible in any eu language. the translation costs of the single european patent would eventually amount to only eur 680. i fully support the new arrangements proposed, which will not only save money and reduce administrative burdens, but also stimulate innovation in the eu. i support the proposals for lower patent registration fees for european smes and the creation of a common patent court. i also believe that full compensation for translation costs should be ensured. in order to protect against fraud, it is necessary to set a maximum permitted price for translation per page.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to include in eu law the safeguard clause and the stabilisation measure provided for in the association agreement with central america (ca). the safeguard clause in the agreement will allow the rate of the duty to be changed if, following the liberalisation of trade, imports are increased in such quantities that they cause significant injury to the eu industry producing the same product. the stabilisation measure for imports of bananas will allow the suspension of the preferential tariff until 1 january 2020 if the volume of exports from latin american countries to the eu market exceeds the set volume. the agreement will open up the eu market to imports, in particular of bananas, sugar and beef, and will increase the eu's export opportunities for dairy products, cereals, pigmeat and spirits. i agree with the need to fully respect the main international labour and environmental conventions in the process of liberalisation and to involve the european parliament and all stakeholders in the process. i support the proposal to include specific provisions on reporting, impact on employment, working conditions, fair trade and analysis of the impact on the outermost regions.
in writing. − i voted for this report because in 2007 the council authorised the commission to open negotiations between the eu and the latin american countries. negotiations were opened in order to effectively facilitate the gradual opening-up and expansion of markets so that all the sectors concerned could gradually adapt to the new trading situation. it is important to note that the agreement includes a bilateral safeguard clause which provides for the possibility of re-establishing the rate of duty applicable under the most favourable treatment (mfn) if, following the liberalisation of trade under the agreement, imports are introduced in such increased quantities and under such conditions as to cause (or threaten to cause) serious injury to union producers of the like or directly competing product. the agreement provides for a stabilisation measure for imports of bananas which may suspend the application of the preferential rate of duty until 1 january 2020. given the provisions and the purpose of the agreement, it is important that this liberalisation process be conducted in full compliance with the main international labour and environmental conventions, that the regulation be implemented in the most transparent way possible and that all stakeholders, including industry, civil society organisations, non-governmental organisations, trade unions and other actors, be involved.
in writing. - i voted for this document. on 22 march 2011, the european commission signed an association agreement with six central american countries (costa rica, el salvador, guatemala, honduras, nicaragua and panama). the agreement provides for eu preferences for these countries under the new generalised scheme of preferences (gsp+). trade in certain agricultural products has also been fully or partially liberalised by the contracting parties. the provisions of the agreement mean that the eu market will be more open to imports, in particular of bananas, sugar and beef, and the eu will have more scope to export other agricultural products to these countries, such as dairy products, cereals, pigmeat and spirits.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution as i believe that this first region-to-region agreement building an association between the european union and central america will contribute decisively to the integration of central america and strengthening the dialogue between both regions. i would like to underline that the trade part of the agreement plays a very important role for the further development of the central america region as it enhances economic relations between the two parts, considerably stressing that the current system of generalised preferences will be replaced by a reciprocal and gradual trade liberalisation system. i agree with the rapporteur that this agreement is not only the first one of its kind, but it accomplishes the objective of creating an appropriate context to provide social integration, cohesion and sustainable development, which are key elements to achieving economic consolidation, growth and social and democratic stability.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of the agreement establishing an association between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and central america, on the other. the main objective of this association agreement (apa) is to contribute to the enhancement of regional integration and stability in central america, and to its economic, political and social development by promoting trade and investment. i support the aim of creating an eu-central america free trade area with a stable and predictable regime that encourages investment, greater participation of central america in world trade, efficient management of resources, environmental protection and increased competitiveness. at the same time, it is necessary to develop and strengthen human rights and democracy in the region. it is important to open a dialogue on the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime. i support calls on the commission to draw up an annual report on the aspects of the association agreement relating to the safeguarding of the principles of democracy and human rights. i agree that a general evaluation of this association agreement should be carried out over a period of five years.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because regional, social, economic and cultural integration between the eu and central america (ca) is not only beneficial to both countries economically, but also promotes a political dialogue that determines whether democracy, the rule of law and respect for the human rights of citizens are respected. the eu and central america, as equal partners, must work together to combat inequality, poverty, promote inclusive development and address outstanding social, economic and political challenges. it is important to note that the new interregional dialogue opens up the possibility of dialogue on the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime. although social inequalities have been reduced in the countries of central america in recent years, full social cohesion will only be possible if education is ensured and levels of poverty, inequality and social exclusion are reduced. therefore, contributing to the revival of economic and social relations between the two regions and the integration of extractive structures is one of the main objectives of the agreement.
in writing. − i voted for this document because the eu-central america (ca) association agreement (aea) is an important precedent, since it is the first eu-ca signed by two regions since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. regional, social, economic and cultural integration through bilateral and subregional association agreements are the main objectives of the strategic partnership between the eu and the two latin american regions. in order to develop eu-latin america relations in a mutually beneficial way and to benefit all, it is essential that the respect for democracy, the rule of law and the human rights of all citizens be at the heart of the political dialogue. the madrid summit of may 2010 allowed the resumption of all negotiations with latin america, which had been frozen in recent years, and thus concluded the negotiations on this association agreement. the development of relations with latin america is mutually beneficial and has advantages for all eu member states.
in writing. − the eu is the primary investor, second largest trading partner, and primary development aid donor in central america. further development of relations with this region is mutually beneficial and can help states in both parties. the recently concluded association agreement (aa) of may 2010 serves as a trade, political dialogue, and cooperation agreement. it represents a step in the right direction towards the reduction of economic barriers and facilitation of trade between the eu and central america – it will further stimulate the flow of services, goods, and investments. the aa stipulates that the safeguarding of human rights, democracy, and rule of law as well as increased socio-economic cohesion are necessary prerequisites for economic cooperation. additionally, environmental protection must be guaranteed in the face of increasing economic cooperation. finally, the aa allows for increased eu aid and assistance in reducing inequality, poverty, discrimination, corruption, and social exclusion. these efforts, coupled with an intensified focus on streamlining education, modernising infrastructure, and strengthening the justice system, will result in a more stable and prosperous central america with a stronger relationship with the european union. i voted in favour of this report for these reasons.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal to include in eu law the safeguard clause and the stabilisation measure provided for in the association agreement with colombia and peru. the safeguard clause in the agreement will allow the rate of duty to be changed if, following the liberalisation of trade, imports are increased in such quantities that they cause significant injury to a competing eu industry producing the product. the stabilisation measure for imports of bananas will allow the suspension of the preferential tariff until 1 january 2020 if the volume of exports from latin american countries to the eu market exceeds the threshold. i agree that the liberalisation process must fully respect the main international labour and environmental conventions and involve the european parliament more in the negotiations on the trade agreements themselves. i support the proposal to include specific provisions on reporting, impact on employment, working conditions, fair trade and analysis of the impact on the outermost regions. it is also necessary to assess the compliance of colombia and peru with social and environmental standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because developing relations with latin america is mutually beneficial and brings benefits to all eu member states. on 19 january 2009, the council authorised the commission to open trade negotiations with the andean community member states, which led to the conclusion of the trade agreement with colombia and peru. this agreement provides, inter alia, for the reduction and eventual abolition of customs duties in the trade of bilateral partners. it also provides for a safeguard clause under which preferential tariffs may be suspended or abolished if such trade liberalisation results in an unexpected increase in imports which would worsen the situation of european industry. these bilateral safeguards were adopted in order to ensure security where market liberalisation requires time for the industry to adapt to new conditions. in particular, these conditions are granted a validity period of 10 years. the implementation of this agreement requires full respect for international labour and environmental conventions, with emphasis on the role of trade unions, ngos and civil society organisations.
in writing. - i voted for this document. on 23 march 2011, the european commission signed a trade agreement with colombia and peru. this agreement has a significant impact on the agricultural sector, in particular the corresponding impact on banana exports to the european market. the safeguard clause provided for in the agreement should be transposed into european union law in order to avoid serious disturbances on the markets concerned. the agreement also provides for even lower customs duties for the european union on imports of bananas from these countries, thus making the contractual conditions for latin american exports to the european market even more favourable.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the conclusion of a trade agreement between the eu, its member states and colombia and peru. this agreement is part of the process of strengthening the relations between the european union and the countries of the latin american and caribbean region and of building a stronger partnership between these regions. during the negotiations, which began as early as 2007, the eu achieved many of its objectives, including the abolition of high tariffs, the removal of technical barriers to trade, the liberalisation of services markets, the opening of public procurement markets and commitments to implement labour and environmental standards. the agreement will give european union companies the same operating conditions as other competitors in the region, such as the us, colombia and peru, and will allow them to gain greater access to the eu market, especially for the export of agricultural products such as bananas, sugar and rum. the newly established bilateral dispute settlement mechanism will ensure a transparent and predictable environment for eu operators and investors operating in the region. i agree that it is necessary to ensure that all signatories to the agreement carry out appropriate monitoring of the respect for human rights and democratic values.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because long-term cooperation between the eu and the andean countries is an important factor in contributing to the strengthening of europe's role in the world. the agreement gives eu companies access to relatively small but growing markets. between 2006 and 2010, eu trade with colombia and peru increased by 10%. the agreement can also be seen as a means of establishing closer relations with the countries of central and latin america, particularly in trade. it is also important to note that the sectors that will benefit most from increased access to the colombian and peruvian markets, namely machinery, transport equipment (including certain cars), chemicals and, above all, services, are the classic eu export sectors. the three sectors account for more than 80% of current eu exports. in the services sector, the telecommunications, construction, distribution and financial services sectors will benefit the most. while the nature of the agreement is primarily economic, human rights provisions, which cover the core labour standards set by the ilo and the multilateral environmental agreements, must also play an important role. it is therefore essential that the parties ensure sufficient technical and financial capacity to help ensure full compliance with the sustainability standards set out in the trade agreement and that human rights review, monitoring and evaluation are carried out.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the prevention of age-related diseases in women. the proposal aims to ensure a healthy ageing of the eu population through the provision of quality healthcare and preventive measures to encourage older people to remain independent for as long as possible. older women are much more likely than men of the same age to suffer disabling illnesses, such as fractures, rheumatoid arthritis, cancer, and diabetes. i agree that prevention and information on risk factors must be key aspects of the strategy. the promotion of healthy eating, the importance of physical activity and the fight against smoking and alcohol abuse are key objectives in reducing the number of age-related diseases. i also support the proposals for promoting the activities of retired elderly people in order to encourage them to be active and not feel excluded from social and professional life. it is also important to improve the structure of sports or public transport to adapt it to the needs of older people and to encourage them to use the internet and thus continue to participate in social life.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the active ageing of the european population makes it important to apply preventive measures. despite a higher rate of longevity, older women are much more likely than their male counterparts to suffer from disabling diseases: fractures due to osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, stroke, urinary incontinence, cancer. the same is true of disability, which is caused by the progressive decline of psychomotor responses, thinking disorders and dementias (e.g. alzheimer' s disease). the number of such cases has been increasing over the years. the main risk factors to be considered in terms of interdependence are hypertension, hyperglycaemia, sedentary lifestyle, smoking, overweight and obesity, excessive cholesterol and hormonal changes in women due to menopause. it is therefore essential to promote healthy lifestyles. the eu institutions need to work with national and local partners to bring prevention strategies to the wider public that aim to encourage good behaviours that contribute to healthy and active ageing. in addition, clinical trials should take greater account of gender, not only by highlighting the predominance of certain female-specific pathologies, but also, in particular, the factors that cause and affect them. statistics show that many factors, both physical and psychological, are involved in age-related diseases in women, and the current situation clearly needs to be improved at both local and national level.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal because the population of the european union is gradually ageing due to low fertility rates and increasing life expectancy. the fact that 2012 has been declared the european year of active ageing and solidarity between generations shows that this area is increasingly being integrated into european policies. the aim is to promote healthy ageing for all by providing quality healthcare and preventive measures to help older people to remain independent for as long as possible. the results of the eurobarometer survey 'active ageing' (2012) show that the definition of 'young person' and 'older person' varies between countries. the average european is considered 'old' at the age of 64, and 'not older' at 41.8. despite their longer life spans, older women are much more likely than their male counterparts to suffer from disabling illnesses, such as fractures due to osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, stroke, cancer, and so on. the same is true of disability, which is caused by the progressive decline of psychomotor responses, thinking disorders and dementias (e.g. alzheimer' s disease). the number of such cases has been increasing over the years. we must therefore pay more attention to older women.
in writing. - the document i supported was adopted at the right time. the eu has declared this year as the year of active ageing and solidarity between generations, as it is projected that by 2060 almost a third of the eu population will be over 65 years old. as a result, as living conditions improve and life expectancy increases, older people become more socially active. statistics show that women live longer, which may lead to higher health costs. there is also a trend towards women being more affected by chronic and disabling diseases. these factors severely limit the active social life of older women. i therefore fully support the need to provide more intensive health care for older women, who are more likely to be lonely, especially in the regions of the member states. also take the necessary early prevention measures increase investment in research, disease prevention, education, psychological support and the full integration of women, especially single women, into social life. in addition, it is necessary to ensure equal pay for women and men at working age, which does not create the conditions for unequal benefits in old age.
in writing. − older women are particularly vulnerable to gender stereotypes and therefore face more difficulties in reaching middle age, when their physical activity declines. i congratulate the rapporteur, mr angelilli, on his excellent work, and i think it is very important to draw attention in a timely manner to the problems of an ageing society and to address the problems of older women in particular. i think it's imperative that we take gender into account in health care. research has shown that older women after menopause are more likely than men to develop disabling conditions such as osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, stroke, urinary incontinence, and cancer. it is very important to note that the symptomatology of some chronic diseases (e. g. cardiovascular diseases) is quite different in women and men. older women must have access to cancer prevention programmes (e.g. breast cancer, colon cancer) which are implemented in the member states. research shows that older women are less likely to use secondary prevention programmes because of lack of awareness of the severity of the problem and less access to services. all of these factors are often linked to women's education and lower incomes. older women should therefore be given all the necessary information on preventive measures by their family doctor and should be given the practical opportunity to undergo preventive examinations in good time, avoiding long queues. chronic diseases in women are not inevitable, but they can be significantly reduced by taking preventive measures.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal because of the ambition to limit antimicrobial resistance and to develop new antimicrobial therapies. antibiotic resistance is on the rise in the eu, causing around 25 000 deaths and €1.5 billion in healthcare costs each year. i support the 12 specific action plans submitted by the commission to promote the prudent use of these medicines in medicine and veterinary medicine. it is important that member states not only develop coordinated strategic action plans for the prudent use of such substances, but also provide patients with new antimicrobials. i agree that it is important to improve the eu legislation on veterinary medicines and to develop an eu animal health act. i also support the proposal to have a monitoring system at european level in the medical and veterinary sectors in order to obtain comprehensive, reliable and comparable data on the effects of these substances. it is necessary to promote the exchange of best practice, closer communication between doctors and training in the veterinary and medical sectors.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because the transnational nature of infectious diseases makes the growing problem of drug-resistant microbes a global one and one that must also be tackled on a global scale. it is also essential that the eu takes concerted action to tackle this problem. over the past decade, the european council conclusions and european parliament resolutions have repeatedly called for the prudent use of existing antimicrobials and for initiatives to develop new antimicrobials. however, there is no single solution to the aml (antimicrobial resistant material) problem and a diversified approach and better tools are needed. these measures should include improved monitoring and information on drug resistance, as well as more effective infection control measures, including the use of vaccines, the promotion of research and the development of new antimicrobials without compromising patient safety. the work of the transatlantic task force on antimicrobial resistance (tatfar) is an excellent model for international cooperation in the field of amr and i believe that similar multilateral and bilateral commitments should be encouraged.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the increasing antimicrobial resistance (amr) is a serious problem caused by a number of interrelated factors. amm has effects on both humans and animals and its effects are dangerous for human and animal health. i therefore advocated this document because the main objective of the amr strategy is to maintain the efficacy of existing antimicrobials by using them responsibly, only in the right therapeutic doses when really necessary and for the specific time, and by reducing the use of antimicrobials in general, and particularly the use of antimicrobials of critical importance in medicine and veterinary medicine. in addition, it is recommended to strengthen the monitoring of antimicrobials for use in infants and children and in clinical practice where this is necessary to monitor and evaluate the use of antimicrobials.
in writing. - i voted for this document without hesitation, because the increase in bacterial resistance to antimicrobials is a serious and threatening problem that can only be tackled by a complex of measures. for more than eight decades, antibiotics have been used and applied in medicine, veterinary medicine, animal husbandry, agriculture, and horticulture. this seems to have been done rather carelessly, without anticipating the possible consequences of changing the resistance of the bacteria. so the result today is a lot of death and damage to health systems, and an ongoing situation where disease-causing microbes are evolving and adapting, many of the antimicrobials that have been used are no longer effective, and relatively few new ones are being developed. i therefore strongly support the need, as expressed in the resolution, to maintain the effectiveness of existing antimicrobials and to introduce more effective educational programmes that will change the attitudes and use practices of patients, farmers and doctors. i also hope that the european commission will take measures to encourage research and interinstitutional cooperation in this area.
in writing. − resistance to antimicrobials produces undesirable effects. more and more people in europe and beyond are recovering from serious illnesses, and additional treatment is costly. consumers are unaware that they are creating the conditions for resistance by taking antibiotics when other treatments are available. the responsible use of antibiotics in animal husbandry is equally important. there are still cases where animals raised for meat are given antibiotics for preventive purposes. this creates antibiotic-resistant strains of bacteria that could be very deadly in the future. i voted for this report because it covers all the main aspects of this issue. first, it promotes the responsible use of antimicrobials and the prevention of the spread of infections. second, the development of new antimicrobial drug elements that will help reduce the resistance of infectious agents to drugs. the third element of particular importance is the exchange of examples of work practice at both national and international levels.
in writing. − the use of antimicrobials in excess of their intended use increases the resistance of microorganisms to these medicines. the increasing resistance to antimicrobials is a major public health problem worldwide. the results of the lithuanian study suggest that only 9.5% of the time a family doctor makes a rational choice of antibiotics for infectious diseases. in less than half of the cases, only 42.9%, antibiotics were prescribed for the appropriate indications. i think the situation is quite similar in all the new member states. antibiotic resistance is a natural phenomenon caused by bacterial gene mutations, and overuse and misuse of antibiotics accelerates the emergence and spread of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. resistant bacteria can spread and cause infections in people who do not take antibiotics. as a result, diseases that were once easily controlled become more difficult and take longer to treat, and in some cases, are even incurable (for example, drug-resistant tuberculosis). responsible use of antibiotics can help prevent the development of resistant bacteria and preserve the effectiveness of antibiotics for future generations. the increased use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine is a cause for concern. member states should implement educational programmes for family doctors, veterinarians and the general public on the use of antibiotics and on when to use antibiotics and when not to use them. i support this initiative.
in writing. mr president, i would like to thank you for your kind words. as a member of the european parliament's committee on agriculture, i wish to speak on a report on the protection of animals during transport which is important for farmers. since 1977, the european union has had rules on animal welfare during transport designed to eliminate technical barriers to trade and to ensure a high level of community agriculture. for this reason, animals from third countries should be subject to strict controls and supervision in order to ensure that european producers are in a stable competitive position vis-à-vis them. but what can help more rural areas to achieve sustainable development, especially in new member states like lithuania, is to slaughter animals and process meat as close as possible to where they are raised. the transport of meat and other animal products is a technically easier and more economically rational solution than the transport of live animals. and if so, then measures should be taken to promote local sales and shorten the food delivery process. union policy in this area should aim at supporting local processing, small local slaughterhouses and local meat processing. this will allow the delivery of animals for slaughter to be carried out over short distances. this in turn will help to stimulate small farms and, as one of the objectives of the report, will significantly reduce the transport time of animals below the expected eight hours, including loading and unloading.
when we adopted the 2012 budget a year ago, we knew we were adopting a deficit budget. at the end of the year, the european commission had only to find that nine billion euros were still outstanding. the european parliament wants the eu to honour its financial commitments in full. however, member states have only agreed to collect €6 billion, so not all the bills will be paid this year. the remaining financial commitments of the european union will be discharged as soon as possible, early next year, as part of the agreement between the three institutions, parliament, the commission and the council. our experience with the 2012 budget is a serious signal to everyone. the excuse is the well-known financial crisis. but if this practice continues and people lose confidence in the european union, the crisis will only worsen.
today we approved a new draft budget for 2013. this is again a deficit budget, as the european union's commitments are higher than the budget's revenue. moreover, the 2013 budget is smaller than this year's budget, amounting to only 0.99% of eu member states' gnp. the 2012 budget, including the additions approved today, is 0.6% higher in terms of gnp. it is, however, welcome that the appropriations for some headings in the 2013 budget are higher than in this year's budget. overall, the allocation for competitiveness is 4.8% higher, and specifically, for example, for the seventh framework programme (fp7) 6.4% higher, for the trans-european networks 6.3% higher than in 2012. the european commission has warned us that the budget will again be short of funds, and that we will have to monitor the budget during the year and be prepared to review it.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because ground services at airports are essential to ensure the smooth operation of an airport. ground service personnel shall be responsible for flight safety, technical flight safety and counter-terrorism. according to the commission, the turnover of the ground handling sector worldwide is around eur 50 billion. the number of people employed in this sector in europe is estimated to be at least 60 000. on 1 december 2012, the european commission presented a proposal for a regulation on groundhandling services which should replace directive 96/67/ec. the aim of the regulation is to prevent flight delays and to improve the quality of passenger services. the legislative proposal aims to prevent wage cuts in the ground handling sector and to encourage the conversion of temporary jobs into permanent jobs, to prevent wage dumping, which threatens flight safety standards, the smooth operation of airports and, ultimately, the safety of flights.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the allocation of slots at european union airports. currently, about 70% of flight delays are caused by problems at airports with preparing aircraft for a regular flight; airports are no longer able to serve passengers properly. if current trends continue, air traffic in the eu will almost double by 2030, with 19 major eu airports overcrowded and up to 50% of all passenger and cargo flights delayed. action is needed today to increase the capacity of eu airports, reduce delays and improve the quality of services provided to passengers. the proposal aims to ensure optimal time allocation at congested eu airports (airport time allocation access to runways and terminals on a specific day, at a specific time, for flights to or from a congested airport). it will also be possible to trade in secondary time slots allowing airlines to buy and sell them throughout the eu. the proposed measure would increase the capacity of eu airports to handle an additional 24 million passengers by 2025. this would generate €5 billion in additional revenue for the eu economy over the period to 2025 and create almost 62 000 jobs.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because one of the major problems facing europe today is overcrowding at airports, and this proposal for a regulation on the allocation of slots at eu airports proposes a way of tackling this problem. according to the long-term forecasts published by eurocontrol in december 2012, even taking into account the infrastructure improvements currently planned, almost 10% of air transport needs will not be met in 2030 due to insufficient capacity. i would therefore support the view that the time-series regulation should be reviewed and that it should be improved as much as possible to ensure that capacity meets the needs of air transport in all sectors (long-haul, regional, cargo, etc.). for example, some of these airports - london heathrow and paris orly - are heavily overcapacitated throughout the year; others have limited capacity during certain peak periods. these examples only demonstrate the need to strengthen the mechanisms for the allocation and use of slots at airports and to ensure their effective application.
in writing. - i voted for this document. the time-limits are allocated to air carriers in accordance with the administrative procedure laid down in council regulation (eec) no 95/93 of 18 january 1993 in accordance with the legislation in force. however, this system of allocating slots has proved to be inefficient and does not ensure that the airport's capacity is fully utilised. it was therefore decided to review the time-frames regulation and to identify the best possible way to improve it in order to meet the capacity needs of air transport in all sectors. i have supported this proposal because i believe it is a good starting point for improving the efficiency of airports, as many of the amendments proposed aim to strengthen the content of certain provisions in order to make them more effective and clearer.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this document because it is a proposal for a council directive on a common system of financial transaction tax (ftt) amending directive 2008/7/ec. i have endorsed this document as several member states have indicated their willingness to consider the possibility of establishing a common system of financial transaction tax (ftt) in the context of enhanced cooperation.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this proposal on the protection of animals during transport. the proposal aims to remove barriers to trade in live animals, while ensuring an adequate level of protection for such animals. the commission has submitted a report on the impact of regulation no 1/2005 on the protection of animals during transport on animal welfare and trade flows. the report shows a sharp increase in such animals between 2005 and 2009: cattle by 8%, pigs by 70%, sheep by 3%, and only horses by 17%. as the objective of the regulation to reduce the number of animals transported has not been achieved, i support the proposal to review eu policy in this area. i support the proposals to support local slaughterhouses and meat processing plants where animals are slaughtered for short distances and to set a maximum journey time of 8 hours for animals to be slaughtered in the eu. the fact that the correctness of the data reported by the member states cannot be verified due to the different control methods in this area threatens to undermine the establishment of the true situation. it is therefore necessary to ensure uniform controls on the observance of the conditions of carriage in the eu and to consider the establishment of specific control bodies in the member states.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important to ensure animal welfare and a uniform, effective framework of eu legislation governing the movement of animals in all member states. at present, the implementation of the provisions on the transport of animals varies widely between member states. parliament criticised the commission's report for not fully assessing the cost of transporting all animals, limiting itself to analysing the impact on intra-eu trade, regional, social and economic consequences. the methods and means of transport of animals should be clearly defined both within and outside the eu. the introduction of strict inspections and monitoring of animals from third countries is necessary to ensure competitiveness for european union livestock farmers and to encourage the improvement of standards for the transport of animals in third countries. i believe that the commission must take measures to strengthen cooperation and control between the competent authorities of the different member states in this area.
in writing. - i voted for this document. because eu legislation requires that the welfare of animals be ensured during transport. i think it's important to consider the economic costs, and at the same time try not to harm the animals or cause them stress. i supported the need for member states to ensure the implementation of the existing minimum standards for transport checks, as well as the application of effective and proportionate penalties and dissuasive measures. particular attention shall be paid to checking the journey times and rest periods, feeding and watering intervals, the space allocated to the animal in the vehicle, the ventilation of the vehicles and the effective operation of the animal irrigation systems. it is also important to encourage cooperation and exchange of information between border control authorities of each member state on cross-border movements of animals.
in writing. − i agree that the issue of safe and animal-friendly transport must be addressed both within and outside the eu. animals transported from third countries should be monitored with particular care, as transport over very long distances, in unhygienic or unfavourable conditions, may result in the risk of communicable diseases and other related consequences. i therefore welcome the resolution's provision for slaughtering animals as close as possible to their place of production, thereby reducing the potential for animal welfare violations and promoting sustainable regional growth and development and the development of small businesses in rural areas.
in writing. − statistics show that the number of animals transported for commercial purposes has been increasing over the last decade. for some animal species, this increase is particularly high, for example, the number of pigs transported increased by as much as 70% between 2005 and 2009. i voted in favour of this report because i agree that the transport of animals should be more regulated. the economic operators should not only be concerned with maximising profits. they must ensure that the animals are provided with acceptable conditions during transport; during long journeys, the animals should be able to eat and drink. i agree with the view expressed in the report that 8 hours should be the maximum duration of a journey without a break. this was the position of over a million eu citizens. undertakings should endeavour to ensure that meat and animal products are transported over long distances instead of live animals. promoting local sales, reducing food supply chains would give work to smaller local slaughterhouses, boosting the local economy. this would not only be more cost-effective but would also protect animal rights.
in writing. − millions of animals are transported on europe's motorways every year, and often in totally unacceptable conditions. the transport of animals to the slaughterhouse has recently increased as the transport distances increase, so it is very important to set maximum transport times. it is essential that the stressed animal does not travel more than 8 hours to the slaughterhouse and that the travel conditions meet or exceed international animal welfare guidelines. more than one third of these journeys take longer than this, causing stress for the animals. we all know that stress is toxic to meat. for example, a trawler with 31 pigs recently left latvia for iran and was stranded for four days on the bulgarian-turkish border because it was not allowed to cross. it is difficult to predict how many live calves will reach iran and what quality meat will be produced. and there are many, many cases of this. more than a million people have signed a petition to reduce the transport time of animals to 8 hours. we cannot ignore this fact. i agree that special attention should be paid during transport to the duration of the journey and to the periods of rest, feeding and watering intervals, space for the animal in the vehicle, ventilation of the vehicles, etc.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because respect for human rights is one of the most important values of the european union. i would urge the commission to better inform citizens not only about their rights but also about their implementation in practice, by maintaining a constant dialogue with the relevant non-governmental organisations. i believe that it is necessary to support the eradication of all stereotypes and the fight against discrimination through specific programmes, actions and campaigns involving the member states, the social partners, non-governmental organisations, institutions and members of national parliaments. it is equally important to consider the situation of stateless people. in view of the declaration of 2013 as the european year of citizens, i would urge the commission and the member states to ensure that effective information campaigns are organised on eu citizenship and related rights. i would also urge all member states to establish appropriate legal frameworks and to define the concept of trafficking in human beings in a uniform way, to protect and defend children's rights and to combat discrimination.
the notifier. − the preparation of this document and the related discussions in the various political groups of the european parliament demonstrate the importance to the european parliament and the european union of a human rights policy and commitment to the defence of human rights as an opportunity to consolidate peace in the world through dialogue and dialogue, rather than force and fist. as the author and rapporteur of this document, i am deeply grateful to my alde colleagues, shadow rapporteurs and colleagues from other groups for the valuable comments, insights, advice, recommendations, criticism and collegiality that have accompanied all my work. this collegial spirit and our concerted efforts and dialogue is one of the most essential and positive experiences i have had in my work on the report. we wanted to produce a coherent, coherent, coherent, logical report that not only reflected the past and identified and registered problems, but also provided guidelines and orientations, thus becoming a strategically important document for the european union. that is why the main emphases of this document include: the european union's responsibility for human rights defenders and dissidents in third countries and around the world (because they, not institutions that are hostile to democracy and human rights, are our essential partners); the human rights clauses in the eu's international trade agreements with third countries (because we are concerned about the poorly prepared, unbalanced, unambitious and inadequate human rights monitoring mechanisms in these agreements, especially with regard to the central asian countries); special attention to the drama of the situation in tibet, which is only concerned with preserving its faith, culture and historical identity, and the consequent need to establish a special representative of the european union for tibet - this is particularly evident in the context of systematic human rights violations in china and russia. this year, the focus is on freedom of expression and new media - experiences that can no longer be ignored after the arab spring we witnessed. at the same time, we cannot avoid and remain silent about what we would lose the right to call the human rights institution lgbt, the caste system of discrimination, the problems of women and children's rights in the world. and there is no way to ignore the fact that people are being killed for their sexual orientation in the 21st century, that so-called honour killings are still punishable, that female genital mutilation is still legal, and that it is still possible to stone unfaithful women. i would like to thank my colleagues once again from the bottom of my heart for their extraordinary support, understanding and collegiality, while believing that we have done the work together that this document has enshrined. i am therefore confident that we will complete this work in the same spirit and with the same degree of collegiality in the votes tomorrow.
first of all, i would like to thank my colleague mr donsky, who is the lead author of the annual report under discussion. the most important human rights issues are reflected in the report we will be voting on tomorrow, and which i will certainly support. i would like to mention two issues today: the human rights situation in occupied tibet and freedom of religion and belief. 2011 and 2012 will go down in history as the year of burning tibet. in protesting against the intolerable repression and violations of human rights and freedoms, tibetans are taking extreme forms of protest, becoming living torches, and almost a hundred tibetan men and mothers of young children, monks, young people have already given their lives. and we, the great and powerful european union, are watching. we are watching, not trying to achieve at least the minimum that the conflicting parties seek solutions through dialogue, at the negotiating table. freedom of religion. interestingly, in the postmodern world, religious freedom is gaining importance all over the arab world, europe, russia, china and elsewhere. i am grateful to mr donsky for accepting most of my amendments on this subject. we know that the european union's guidelines on freedom of religion or belief are currently being discussed, and i think that the european parliament should also have a say on this important subject.
president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank all of you for this very important debate. this house has for years been a champion of human rights and your active involvement in our broad activities on human rights continues to guide us throughout the process. the important reports of the two rapporteurs will undoubtedly further nourish our reflexion on how to better ensure consistency in eu policy by working closely with the european external action service, the commission and this house. let me now turn to some specific points that have been raised by the honourable members. definitely i cannot answer every question or every very important remark that has been made, but i will try to answer or to comment on some of those issues that have been raised. let me first of all express on behalf of the high representative/vice-president how much she regrets that she cannot be here with you today. as you all know, she has committed herself to making human rights an integral part of our eu external relations and she would have been delighted to discuss with you the great achievements we have seen this year, which i have briefly elaborated on in my introduction. this week cathy chaired the foreign affairs council, where tangible improvements on human rights issues in the serbia-kosovo dialogue have been achieved. she participated in the general affairs council, where discussions went on late into the night last night to come to an agreement to advance the stabilisation and association process for the western balkans, and of course this week the friends of syria meeting as well as the situation in egypt are particularly high on her agenda. we must do our utmost to end the terrible bloodshed in syria and to ensure that the recent advances in egypt’s democratic transition do not unravel in the light of recent events. regarding women, peace and security, which has been mentioned, i would like to say that the european union is active on the issue of women, peace and security in more than 70 countries. its support amounts to about eur 200 million a year for the development and the implementation of national action plans, funding for non-governmental organisations and training for governmental agencies. the european union has included specific attention to women, peace and security in its political and human rights dialogues and consultations with countries such as canada, ethiopia, the us, nepal, pakistan, papua new guinea, south africa, somalia, sudan and uganda, to name but a few. we also want to ensure that the political commitment to gender equality is translated into concrete cooperation activities and feeds into the programming of eu assistance. the second implementation report on the eu plan of action on gender equality and women’s empowerment in development has been prepared. the report includes concrete examples of mainstreaming of gender in our geographical instruments. on gender-based violence, including female genital mutilation: this is one of the most prevalent and pervasive forms of human rights violations and it is deeply rooted in gender inequality between men and women. the european external action service and the commission are therefore committed to strengthening its actions both internally and externally. the high representative/vice-president ashton and vice-president reding made a statement on the international day against female genital mutilation on 6 february 2012 and a declaration on ending fgm at the european parliament on 13 june 2012. the european parliament unanimously adopted the joint resolution on ending female genital mutilation in june 2012. the european external action service is currently preparing a campaign to be launched in spring 2013 under the eu human rights guidelines on violence against women and girls to draw attention to the need to step up efforts to eradicate this practice, particularly on the african continent. on the death penalty: consistent with its strong and principled policy against the death penalty, the european union is undoubtedly one of the most prominent international players and lead donors in the abolitionist cause worldwide. the fight against the death penalty is at the heart of the eu’s human rights policy and a personal priority for the high representative/vice-president. the eu uses all tools available in order to promote its abolitionist policy according to the 11 eu guidelines. mention was made of kazakhstan. the lack of substantial progress in advancing human rights in kazakhstan is certainly a matter of concern which we have conveyed to president nazarbayev. when the high representative/vice-president met with the president during a visit to astana in november, they had an intensive exchange of views. on that occasion she expressed to him her firm belief that, as a member of the council of europe’s venice commission and also a newly elected member of the un human rights council, kazakhstan should demonstrate its strong commitment to human rights, including the freedoms of speech, of assembly and association and of religion and belief. the respect for common values of democracy, the rule of law and human rights is also the basis for deepening our relations through the new pca. on freedom of religion and belief: as a universal human right, freedom of religion and belief is a priority under the eu human rights policy. the european union has to promote it for everyone outside and within the european union. the european union and member states have been very active on freedom of religion and belief over the last two years. the eu is active in putting together action lines, specific council conclusions 2009-2011, an internal action plan in 2010, a request made to all eu delegations in 2011 to follow the situation and report on issues and actions taken, focus on freedom of religion and belief in the eu annual human rights reports of 2010-2011, and proposals for new guidelines on the freedom of religion and belief agreed in the foreign affairs council in june to be adopted by the beginning of 2013. the european parliament of course will be informed and comments will be very welcome. on the question raised by graf lambsdorff, i agree that there will be a need for coordination between the existing instrument and the new european endowment for democracy. as you know, a great part of the existing european instrument for democracy and human rights is dedicated to election observations where parliament has a great role to play. our intention is that the european endowment for democracy will be complementary to that. to conclude, let me once again pay tribute to this year’s sakharov prize winners – nasrin sotoudeh and jafar panahi – for the courage they showed in the struggle against repression and once again assure this house of the central place of human rights and democracy in the external action of the eu, as demonstrated by our strong commitment and continuous work in this field throughout 2012. a lot of work lies ahead. i am not here to say that we are perfect but that we want to achieve that goal. i can assure you that the high representative, the eu special representative mr lambrinidis and all the member states will redouble our efforts until human rights are not only volumes of conventions and resolutions, but are translated into reality for every human being on this planet irrespective of colour, ethnic origin, religion, gender or sexual orientation. if we want to have a better world, human rights should remain at the heart of our domestic and our foreign policy.
the notifier. - the russian writer and dissident alexander solzhenitsyn has said the crucial phrase that in modern times, states have no longer really their internal affairs, because all these affairs have already become international and common human affairs. this means that no citizen or resident is the property or internal affair of his or her state. the national state cannot claim to be the arbiter of universal human affairs and problems, of which human life and its value, the incomparable value and dignity of the person, fundamental rights and civil liberties are essential. like the chinese democracy wall activists in beijing in 1978, russian dissidents, who in their desperate struggle inspired the west and created the entire human rights discourse of today, are the best counterargument to the belief that human rights have become a new secular and political religion of the west, having nothing to do with the rest of humanity. the european union cannot fail to speak with one voice when it comes to human rights as the essential criterion for assessing the civility of the policies of states, their democratic credentials and their credibility in the face of modern forms of sensitivity. i therefore hope that this report will become one of the european union's policy instruments for achieving these objectives and for harmonising our discourse and making our actions more effective.
mr president, there are many cases in which russia deserves critical remarks as a systematic violator of human rights and international commitments. unfortunately, we deserve criticism as well for avoiding even talking with our partner about some particularities of our common, better future. such a long-prepared resolution on the agreement could be seen as an effort towards dialogue on relations, including what is at least an abnormal lack of a mutually-recognised legal border between the eu and russia. that gap remains at the estonian eastern border when russia refuses to ratify an agreement properly worked through and signed by both negotiators several years before. the resolution was an opportunity to remind our russian colleagues of that particular unfinished issue, but that opportunity was not taken. the level of our appeasing instincts is tremendously unrealistic. it is much worse when something similar occurs about human lives and losses. there was another chance to encourage russia to join the international community in its efforts to stop the destruction and bloodshed of civilians in syria. we missed it. the suggestion was deleted. as now there are signs already that russia may drop its unconditional support for mr assad, we see that we could step forward and show ourselves being less afraid to say in a resolution a european word to russia. but we have not helped russia as an illusionary world peace maker in the case of syria either.
mr president, over the years i have followed not only the tragic events on the spot but also the debates of politicians – debates conducted at a distance, and often in rather abstract terms – and the formulas and wording used concern me. i wish to ask, since there is so much talk about palestinians and palestine: what palestine, and what palestinians, are we talking about? geographically there are at least two palestines now, with two ruling representative forces or personalities. if they are legitimately authorised to represent sections of the palestinian people, who represents palestinian refugees? maybe it is time to sit round the table and get an evaluation rather than play with words along the lines of ‘palestine is recognised, palestine is this or that’. which palestine? hamas’ palestine? abbas’ palestine? does hamas’ palestine recognise abbas as a legitimate president? let us consider the issue in a realistic light.
the parliamentary elections in ukraine have unfortunately not turned into a boost for the european option, democracy and human rights in that country. they were not transparent, some opposition leaders met them in prison, much of it due to so-called 'government resources'. however, it should be stressed that the main political forces there are in favour of strengthening cooperation with the european union. the majority of ukrainian citizens support the european direction. it is important to send them a strong signal that the european union really values this. public voice and pressure should lead the parliament and the government to focus more on human rights and to implement reforms that would enable, as commissioner štefan fule has said, the signing of an eu-ukraine association agreement at the vilnius summit, and perhaps even earlier.
mr president, as usual, we like to strongly criticise ukraine about its elections and the stage of democracy there. it is worth comparing our valuation of the same matters in two of the largest post-soviet states: russia and ukraine. in the case of ukraine, real elections were held but nevertheless failed to meet all international standards. in russia, however, in the case of both parliamentary and presidential elections, the very elections were pre-empted by the selection of candidates, as in the good old days; those with the potential to debate with the power-holders were put aside, simply not registered. the two ukrainian opposition leaders sentenced for misuse of powers and kept in jail there should not be compared with the two extremely dangerous singing girls imprisoned in russia. in ukraine the new political forces were allowed to participate and pass the electoral threshold, thus building a real parliamentary opposition. that is not the case in russia, where the highest power is guaranteed personally for a lifelong term, as in central asia, and only selected, largely ornamental groups are permitted to enter the lower house as ‘his majesty’s loyal opposition’. in ukraine, the existing democratic institutions must be further improved; as there are no democratic institutions involved in the governance of russia, only imitations of them, no such improvements can be made until fundamental changes come. to sum up, ukraine is better, and must be encouraged not to lose its european links and aspirations. the power of encouragement remains in our hands; let us not delete any positive advances, as happened in the case of the recent resolution.
for the efd group indeed, austerity measures have pushed the economy into a dangerous downturn. to save money, you have to earn it first. and the institutions of the european union have hardly done enough to make it easier and simpler for society to do so. mr president, we are desperately late and are hastily borrowing new funds with the hope of increasing gdp by a few tenths of a percent, and when it falls, we are borrowing again in order to at least bring gdp back to its previous level and try to convince everyone that there is no crisis or problem. we must admit that such austerity policies have not improved but worsened the economic and social situation. what do you do? i think we need to go three ways. first, the promotion of production and consumption appropriate to it. secondly, saving not at the expense of public revenues, but at the expense of the bureaucratic machinery of the states and the expenditure of the state banking sector. thirdly, the efficient use of european union funds, including those for the most necessary social reforms.
