in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because, despite the promotion and justification of human rights, discrimination on grounds of race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic characteristics, language, religion or belief, political or other opinion still exists in the eu. on 28 february 2008, the council therefore adopted decision 2008/203/ec implementing the provisions of regulation (ec) no 168/2007 as regards the adoption of the multiannual programme of the european union agency for fundamental rights for the period 2007 to 2012. the eu's activities in this agency aim to provide compensation for victims, asylum for immigrants, protection for children and access to justice for all union citizens or to inform them of access to justice. it is important to note that many organisations support the work of the agency in the relevant areas and would like it to continue its work, in particular in the areas of discrimination (72%), asylum and migration (43%), racism and xenophobia (38%) and the right to a fair trial (31%). in view of the indivisible and interrelated nature of human rights as enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the eu and in un human rights instruments, the scope of the agency should clearly cover a wide range of economic, social and cultural rights in the member states.
in writing. − the report mentions the procedural changes for the written declarations that, from my point of view, are really necessary now. at the heart of the increase of the european parliament’s legislative role, these procedural changes can be very efficient. first of all, procedural rules of written declarations need to be changed because nowadays written declarations only have a limited impact on the decision-making process of the eu. their importance is more punctual; they raise awareness on issues of public concern but do not influence the union’s legislation. and taking into account the parliament’s increased policy prerogatives, the relevance of some written declarations to these prerogatives sometimes is very small. furthermore, under the current procedure only a small percentage of written declarations obtain the required support of a majority of members of the european parliament. that is why, taking into consideration all mentioned points, i welcome these structural changes to the follow-up rules and the signature process of the written declarations. and i consider all these procedural changes important as they will not only reduce the costs for the eu but will also bring more coherence into the legislative procedure of the eu.

in writing. − this comprehensive report documenting the situation of human rights around the globe demonstrates that, although significant progress has been made, much work remains to be done. the eu has noted and protested against the imprisonment, torture, and execution of countless dissidents, journalists, whistle-blowers, activists, and criminals across the globe, in countries ranging from syria to ukraine to the united states. the eu has been a major player in working with the un and international criminal court (icc) to ensure fair and open trials for accused persons. democracy clauses in eu agreements with third countries have helped to diffuse democratic norms – by requiring respect for human rights as a prerequisite for trade agreements with the eu; these clauses have provided a motivator for third countries to improve their human rights records. the eu has also been a major voice speaking out against the use of the death penalty, discrimination on any basis, and racism and xenophobia. it has also consistently supported women’s rights, voting rights, and the right to the freedoms of assembly, religion, press, and speech. i support this report because the eu serves as the world’s major promoter of human rights, and should continue to do so in the future.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because one of the eu's main objectives is to protect and promote human rights. the recent unrest in the eastern partnership has shown the particular importance of ensuring political dialogue between public authorities, trade unions, universities and civil society in order to protect fundamental freedoms (during the transition processes). the european democracy fund (edf) is therefore one of the most realistic ways of responding adequately to the potential challenges of democratisation in the member states and beyond. it is of the utmost importance to mention that the eu supports the universal human rights and freedoms enshrined in the universal declaration of human rights, which states that equal opportunities must be guaranteed to everyone, regardless of religion or belief, gender, racial or ethnic origin, age, disability, sexual orientation and gender identity. the strategic programme and action plan is the minimum, not the maximum, of the eu's human rights policy. the eu institutions and member states will need to take a firm and consistent approach to human rights violations worldwide and act in a transparent and accountable manner to ensure that no human rights are violated in the implementation of eu policies. these mandates and tasks are not easily and quickly achieved, but must be continuously improved and regularly evaluated.
in writing. − the eu was founded on the principle of respect for human rights and has a legal obligation to place human rights at the centre of all eu policies, member state agreements and international agreements. eu institutions and member states must develop a common response to human rights abuses, both at home and abroad. policy regarding human rights must be consistent across all eu member states – coordination with the eu institutions is vital in this regard. after all, the eu cannot act as a credible defender of human rights abroad if serious human rights deficiencies occur within its own borders. the recently established post of special representative of the european union for human rights should aid greatly in streamlining human rights standards throughout the eu and should reinforce the eu human rights agenda in eu external policy. policy coordination and coherence with other international organisations, such as the un and council of europe, can also go a long way towards establishing a more globalised approach to human rights. i support this report because i believe that if the eu is and should remain the global leader in protecting human rights.
in writing. − it is regrettable that the trends in russia, especially in the field of human rights, are not positive, but it is most regrettable that human rights violations are not recognised and that instead, arguments about 'foreign powers' are often used to justify restrictions in domestic politics or attempts to divide the unity of the eu by accusing several eu member states of some kind of violation. therefore, the eu-russia human rights dialogues at this stage appear to be little more than meetings to exchange differing views. russia shares moral and political responsibility for the deaths of 20 000 syrian civilians, the deepening civil conflict and the humanitarian crisis, as a result of its unconstructive stance in the un security council. there is concern for the survival of a regime that is killing its own people in the name of national interests. this is why statements are made that ignore the fate of current victims but care about future victims of the collapse of the assad regime. all this is the result of a lack of understanding of the benefits of democratic processes, of listening to the expectations of citizens. it is important to continue to make human rights conditionalities in the negotiations for the new agreement. i also welcome the expectations of the ep in the field of energy, in particular the call for russia to join the espo convention and the need to ensure that new and existing nuclear infrastructure fully complies with international safety standards.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because i agree that both the european union and russia need a new and good treaty. the criticism of some of russia's actions in the report is not 'schadenfreude', on the contrary. it is a desire to remove obstacles to our cooperation, while recognising that, even in difficult times, the eu is not perfect. russia, for geopolitical, historical and other reasons, will never be like, say, portugal, germany, or poland. russia, by virtue of its sheer size, spanning two continents, has a choice in which path to take. the most mutually beneficial path, i would say, would be to move closer to the european union. such a line would be supported by a large proportion of russian citizens, according to polls. i see this report as a support to them, as an invitation to an even more open, more substantive dialogue and to a strengthening of the strategic partnership.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution even though my original proposal was to postpone the adoption of such a resolution until after the newly elected ukrainian parliament starts its work. in this case the european parliament would be able to express its concerns and expectations to the new parliament of ukraine. today i would like to stress that it is of utmost importance that the ukrainian government seriously addresses the inconclusive results in some electoral districts and the shortcomings of the electoral law. i regret that the 2012 parliamentary elections, which were to be ‘a key test’ for ukraine’s development into a fully-fledged democracy, failed to meet international standards and were ‘a step backward’ compared to previous elections. but even in those conditions the eu must remain supportive of the ukrainian people as a protection against attempts to isolate ukraine, which could lead to ‘favourable conditions for undemocratic regimes’. moreover, we observe worrying tendencies regarding rising nationalistic sentiment in ukraine which led to the election of the ‘svoboda’ party to the parliament of ukraine. we must recall that racist, anti-semitic and xenophobic views go against the eu’s fundamental values and principles and might undermine eu readiness to cooperate with ukraine.
in writing. - i voted yes. the resolution identifies problem areas where ukraine should make progress in the near future. i believe that the eu should continue to work actively with its partners in ukraine to help make that progress. i hope that at the eastern partnership leaders' meeting in vilnius in 2013, we will witness the beginning of a qualitatively new phase of eu-ukraine cooperation and rapprochement.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it is important for the european union to maintain and develop a strong steel industry. the steel industry in europe plays a key role in the economy and is a key part of the development and creation of many industrial sectors that are essential for economic and social well-being. the commission considers that appropriate measures should be taken to enable all member states to effectively request and receive funding for research in the coal and steel sectors. in short, it is essential to financially support and develop research and to increase the efficiency and sustainability of production in this sector. the europe 2020 strategy, which aims to increase the share of this industry in the european union's gross domestic product from 16% to 20% by 2020, is the only hope for overcoming the economic and social crisis. the preservation and strengthening of a robust steel sector is the economic foundation of the european union, which will provide opportunities for the future development of other infrastructure areas.
